articles.headline: Update: Shenzhen "Declaration toward Peace": Trump, Xi and Putin agree on the UN, the ICC, oil products and nuclear risk, with Europe absent from the table
articles.summary:
**The first-ever meeting of the leaders of the United States, China and Russia ended in Shenzhen on Thursday with a joint "Heads of State Declaration toward Peace" (full text published by the Russian Foreign Ministry, Russian state source).**

Its four points: (1) as permanent members of the UN Security Council, the three "committed to reform the U.N." so it can respond more effectively to global challenges; (2) they "plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products" and "reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows"; (3) they recognised "the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials" as "of paramount importance" and agreed that "the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction"; (4) they reaffirmed that "a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought" and will hold a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing proliferation. Before the declaration, Trump told Xi and Putin that he would suggest ways to protect their countries from the ICC (clip via @Acyn). Putin said the three are "united by our status as victorious powers in the Second World War" and that, at Trump's initiative, much of the US–Russia bilateral was devoted to Ukraine. Xi called the meeting "positive, constructive and fruitful" and said "positive interaction between major countries is not optional, but a must" (Chinese MFA spokesperson; Global Times, Chinese state media). Trump left China shortly afterwards (Anadolu, Turkish state agency).

**Context:** This closes the story that opened the 07:30 edition (Putin–Trump bilateral). As we noted then, Europe is not at the table, and it still cannot agree on who speaks for it: the Dublin formula of 13 November gave the talks to "the EU institutions and the E5" rather than to the High Representative, Kaja Kallas, whose own words on Russia ("if you would have more like small nations it's not a bad thing if the big power is actually much smaller", Lennart Meri Conference, 18 May 2024) have weighed against her as a negotiator (07:30 edition, story 2).

**European reactions in this window:** Former Commissioner Michel Barnier: "En Chine aujourd'hui il manque un drapeau, un continent: l'Union européenne" ("In China today one flag, one continent is missing: the European Union"). Former Commissioner Thierry Breton: "Seuls, face aux empires" ("Alone, facing the empires"). Polish Foreign Minister Radosław Sikorski, in Budapest: "We will not accept any new spheres of influence in Europe", and on Shenzhen: "What is this supposed to be, another Yalta?" (clip via Clash Report). Germany's Minister of State for Europe, Gunther Krichbaum, at the General Affairs Council: "Nothing about Ukraine without Ukraine, nothing about Europe without Europe."

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123372469461328015), [t.me](https://t.me/MFARussia/33494), [t.me](https://t.me/MFARussia/33490), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123351927945634175), [China Military Bugle](https://x.com/i/status/2123382291363971240), [Chinese MFA spokesperson](https://x.com/i/status/2123354920699191354), [Global Times](https://x.com/i/status/2123377920182026430), [@RapidResponse47](https://x.com/i/status/2123359138617172080), [@RapidResponse47](https://x.com/i/status/2123357612280328697), [@Acyn](https://x.com/i/status/2123358513850155283), [Anadolu](https://x.com/i/status/2123371188147622122), [Anadolu](https://x.com/i/status/2123308738043949119), [Anadolu](https://x.com/i/status/2123376434542416321), [Michel Barnier](https://x.com/i/status/2123321849245565393), [Thierry Breton](https://x.com/i/status/2123310308294812085), [Polish MFA](https://x.com/i/status/2123351790766965043), [Clash Report](https://x.com/i/status/2123329229643268420), [Germany in the EU](https://x.com/i/status/2123383156879294510), [Diplomacy page](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy), [Euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2123369338979971373)
articles.why: Three powers have just signed, without any European present, a text on UN reform, international justice and nuclear risk — subjects that the EU and its member states treat as their own. Point 3 directly undercuts the ICC, which the EU supports as a matter of policy and which has had an arrest warrant out against Putin since March 2023; point 2 commits Washington, Moscow and Beijing to more oil-product supply at a time when the EU is still trying to cut Russian energy revenue. No EU member state alone has the weight to be invited to such a table; that is CEAFE's case for a single European voice instead of E3/E5 formats and competing envoys.
articles.watch: Whether the "dialogue on reducing nuclear risks" gets a date and format; EU and ICC reactions to point 3; what Witkoff and Kushner tell the Coalition of the Willing in Berlin this afternoon.

articles.headline: Berlin: Coalition of the Willing meets with Witkoff and Kushner as Shenzhen ends
articles.summary:
**Chancellor Friedrich Merz is hosting the Coalition of the Willing at the Federal Chancellery under the motto "United for Peace in Ukraine and European Security", co-chaired with France and the United Kingdom (E3), with heads of state or government from 37 countries plus António Costa, Ursula von der Leyen, Kaja Kallas and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte (Bundesregierung).**

President Zelensky arrived with his team: "More than 40 partners will be represented, including the team of the American President. Ukraine's priorities are strengthening our air defense, energy and financial support, the diplomatic track…" US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff said they were heading to Berlin "to consult with President Zelenskyy and European leaders"; they are expected to brief on Trump's talks in China (Interfax-Ukraine, Kyiv Post). The agenda covers security guarantees in three parts: support for Ukraine's armed forces, a Multinational Force for Ukraine, and legal and political guarantees (Interfax-Ukraine).

**Sources:** [@ZelenskyyUa](https://x.com/i/status/2123377054158643397), [@jaredkushner](https://x.com/i/status/2123319813883748586), [Bundesregierung](https://www.bundeskanzler.de/bk-de/aktuelles/koalition-der-willigen-in-berlin-2461162), [Kyiv Post](https://www.kyivpost.com/post/90536), [Interfax-Ukraine](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1239165.html), [DW live](https://www.dw.com/en/ukraines-allies-gather-in-berlin-for-coalition-of-the-willing-summit/live-79986520)
articles.why: On the same day, Europe's leaders meet in Berlin and learn second-hand, from US envoys, what was agreed in Shenzhen. The E3 co-chairs the format while the EU's institutions attend as guests: another sign of the fragmented European representation that story 1 describes.
articles.watch: Final statement and any figures on the multinational force; the US envoys' read-out of Shenzhen.

articles.headline: EU institutions: Commission hit by a large AI-assisted cyberattack; Swedish diplomat Lars Danielsson named sanctions envoy
articles.summary:
**The European Commission was hit by a cyberattack on its internal HR and medical-reimbursement systems (Sysper, MyPMO, JSIS), first reported by Politico Europe on Thursday.**

Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier said the attack used "a publicly available AI tool", was first detected on 22 October, involved no ransom demand and that there is no "evidence of a data breach affecting Commission staff as a whole"; he did not attribute it (Euronews). Politico reported that CERT-EU identified the tool as ARTEX, that the top crisis-management body met and that Tech Commissioner Henna Virkkunen briefed the College on Wednesday. Separately, the Commission has created an EU Sanctions Office under Commissioner Maria Luís Albuquerque (operational 16 January 2027) and appointed Lars Danielsson, Sweden's former permanent representative to the EU (2016–2023), as International Special Envoy for the Implementation of EU Sanctions from 6 February 2027, succeeding David O'Sullivan (Commission decision of 18 Nov reported by Brussels Times, Kyiv Post; congratulated by Sweden's prime minister).

**Sources:** [Politico Europe](https://www.politico.eu/newsletter/brussels-playbook/cyberattack-hits-the-commission/), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/19/eu-commission-hit-by-large-scale-cyberattack-with-data-leakage-unknown), [Reuters via GMA](https://www.gmanetwork.com/news/topstories/world/1010091/european-commission-targeted-in-cyberattack-politico-reports/story/), [@SouveraineTech](https://x.com/i/status/2123348325961240987), [Swedish PM via @SweMFA](https://x.com/i/status/2123295237754048568), [Brussels Times](https://www.brusselstimes.com/2412656/eu-revamps-sanctions-strategy-with-new-office-and-envoy-for-enforcement), [Kyiv Post](https://www.kyivpost.com/post/90535)
articles.why: The Commission has been breached three times this year (January mobile-device infrastructure, March Europa.eu cloud, now HR systems, per Euronews). HR data (names, grades, home addresses) can feed targeted campaigns against EU staff: digital sovereignty and the EU's own cyber-defence are security matters, not IT matters. The sanctions envoy update continues the 20:30 story on the new Sanctions Office.
articles.watch: Attribution of the attack; whether personal data was taken; the 22nd sanctions package against Russia (Kyiv Post).

articles.headline: Indo-Pacific: Japan–India "2+2" in Tokyo, Russian bombers near Taiwan, Germany–Japan military talks
articles.summary:
**Japan and India held their 4th Foreign and Defence Ministers' Meeting ("2+2") in Tokyo (Motegi, Koizumi, Jaishankar, Rajnath Singh) and issued a joint statement on a Free and Open Indo-Pacific and defence cooperation including maritime security, followed by the 19th Japan–India Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue.**

Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense reported two sorties of Russian Tu-95 bombers entering its ADIZ from the south and exiting north-east of Keelung on Thursday morning, during the Shenzhen summit. Japan and Germany held their 18th military-to-military dialogue in Tokyo. Japan also reported that the Canadian frigate HMCS Regina completed Canada's 16th mission monitoring illicit ship-to-ship transfers with North Korean vessels.

**Sources:** [@MofaJapan_en](https://x.com/i/status/2123362045945090055), [@MofaJapan_en](https://x.com/i/status/2123384371898130480), [@MofaJapan_en](https://x.com/i/status/2123369979856953726), [@SpokespersonMoD](https://x.com/i/status/2123356253460238657), [@ModJapan_en](https://x.com/i/status/2123309207638413732), [@MoNDefense](https://x.com/i/status/2123305270394994777)
articles.why: Asia's middle powers deepen defence ties among themselves while the great powers meet; Germany's dialogue with Japan is a national track where a common EU security policy towards the Indo-Pacific is still thin.

articles.headline: WTO: record stockpile of trade restrictions in 2026
articles.summary:
**The WTO Director-General's annual trade-monitoring overview says the pace of new tariffs and other non-facilitating measures "rose sharply in the first half of 2026" and the stockpile reached a record level.**

Members introduced 333 new restrictive measures in H1 2026 alone, more than the 300 in all of 2025, but also 466 trade-facilitating measures (391 in 2025); export-facilitating measures covered a record USD 570 billion (2.3%) of world exports, much of it temporary action linked to disruption in the Strait of Hormuz.

**Sources:** [WTO](https://www.wto.org/english/news_e/news26_e/tmwto_17nov26_552_e.htm), [@wto](https://x.com/i/status/2123380117111980526)
articles.why: The EU, the world's largest trading bloc, depends on open rules; a rise in restrictions and the use of trade as a weapon reward scale and collective bargaining power, which only the Union as a whole has.

articles.headline: Update: Shenzhen: Trump and Putin open their bilateral as the first US–China–Russia leaders' meeting nears
articles.summary:
**Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump began a bilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen on Thursday morning; the press was allowed in for about one minute before the talks continued behind closed doors (TASS, Russian state agency).**

Trump said at the start that he has an excellent relationship with Putin and that "great results" could be achieved (TASS). Earlier, Trump said: "I look forward to a historic trilateral meeting with President Xi and President Putin later today" (Clash Report clip). In a Fox News interview before the talks he called China and Russia "natural enemies" whose partnership "should never have been allowed to happen" (South China Morning Post), and said on the war in Ukraine: "It doesn't affect us. In fact, I guess you could say, we make a lot of money" (Aaron Rupar clip). At the APEC plenary, Xi Jinping called for removing barriers to trade and investment and announced $20 million for APEC practical cooperation (Xinhua, Chinese state media); Putin said Russia supports the draft final declaration of the summit (TASS).

**Sources:** [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99144), [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99145), [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99137), [Kremlin](https://t.me/news_kremlin_eng/8449), [@mfa_russia](https://x.com/i/status/2123275940205850837), [Clash Report](https://x.com/i/status/2123261832278520318), [Clash Report](https://x.com/i/status/2123261130596311226), [Aaron Rupar](https://x.com/i/status/2123215452604182532), [Aaron Rupar](https://x.com/i/status/2123213787427639558), [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3374980/natural-enemies-trump-china-russia-ties-he-plays-down-nvidia-tragedy), [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/military/article/3374979/us-launched-unarmed-icbm-test-hours-trumps-air-force-one-landed-china), [Xinhua](https://x.com/i/status/2123244396951040157), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2123279575132131466), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2123277624667447752)
articles.why: The future of a war on the European continent is being discussed by three leaders, none of them European. Trump's line that the war "doesn't affect us" shows that Washington sees it as someone else's problem, while it sells the weapons.
articles.watch: Readouts of the bilateral from the Kremlin and the White House; the trilateral itself and any joint text; Ukraine's reaction. Note: the South China Morning Post is owned by Alibaba; its China reporting is cited here for factual items only.

articles.headline: Europe absent from the Shenzhen table, and still divided over who speaks for it
articles.summary:
**On the day three leaders meet in Shenzhen to try to end the Ukraine war, neither the EU nor any EU member state is in the room: individually none of them has the global weight to sit there.**

Europeans also cannot agree on who represents them. At the informal European Council in Dublin on 13 November, leaders declined to name a single envoy; António Costa said: "The leaders agreed that our European team for the negotiations on peace in Ukraine is the European Union institutions and the E5 of the Coalition of the Willing" (France, Germany, the United Kingdom, Italy and Poland) (Euronews). Friedrich Merz defended the old format: "The E3 format has proven very effective. Incidentally, we always include Italy and Poland." High Representative Kaja Kallas argued the envoy role was part of her mandate and admitted that "Russians do not want me"; Ursula von der Leyen declined to back her: "We have taken our decision" (Euronews). Names floated this year as possible European envoys or representatives include Kallas, Costa, von der Leyen, Finland's President Alexander Stubb ("If I'm asked, that's probably a question that can't be answered in the negative"), Mario Draghi and Angela Merkel (Irish Times, 29 May 2026), as well as Sauli Niinistö and Jean-Claude Juncker (Politico, via Kyiv Post).

**Sources:** [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/13/eu-leaders-bring-italy-and-poland-into-ukraine-peace-talks-team-as-kallas-fights-for-spot), [European Council](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/european-council/2026/11/13/), [Politico](https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-kaja-kallas-fights-to-find-a-role-in-ukraine-peace-talks/), [Politico](https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-deal-on-ukraine-talks-overshadows-ai-focused-summit-in-dublin/), [Irish Times](https://www.irishtimes.com/world/europe/2026/05/29/its-like-trying-to-grasp-a-wet-bar-of-soap-eu-prepares-for-potential-talks-with-slippery-putin/), [Kyiv Post](https://www.kyivpost.com/post/76888), [EUobserver](https://euobserver.com/248871/eu-leaders-hand-ukraine-peace-talks-to-france-germany-uk-italy-poland-plus-brussels-instead-of-a-single-envoy/), [Lennart Meri Conference](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PcFUnybWftM), [@ThierryBreton](https://x.com/i/status/2123144301719007421), [@ZelenskyyUa](https://x.com/i/status/2123133098627928241), [DW](https://www.dw.com/en/ukraines-allies-gather-in-berlin-for-coalition-of-the-willing-summit/live-79986520), [German Chancellery](https://www.bundeskanzler.de/bk-de/aktuelles/treffen-der-koalition-der-willigen-2460904)
articles.why: Formats such as the E3 or the E5, and a roster of competing names, weaken the idea of European construction: the Union already has a High Representative for foreign policy. But Kallas's limited room for manoeuvre and her anti-Russian statements have disqualified her as a negotiator in Moscow's eyes. At the Lennart Meri Conference in Tallinn on 18 May 2024 she said: "Russia's defeat is not a bad thing because then you know there could be really a change in the society and you know there are many different nations right now part of Russia as well. I think if you would have more like small nations it's not a bad thing if the big power is actually much smaller." Former Commissioner Thierry Breton wrote overnight: "Face à Trump, Poutine et Xi Jinping, il est absolument indispensable que les Européens soient unis. Je ne vois pas beaucoup d'avenir à un pays isolé dans ce monde brutal." We Europeans either act together or we stay outside the room where our own continent's future is discussed.
articles.watch: Whether the US envoys' Berlin debrief changes the European team's role; any Russian acceptance of direct talks with the Europeans.

articles.headline: Update: Trump on Fox: "We sell equipment to the European Union… we make a lot of money"
articles.summary:
Asked about the war in Ukraine in a Fox News interview in Shenzhen, Trump said: "We sell equipment to the European Union. They do with it what they want. I guess they give it for the most part to Ukraine, but we sell it… I guess you could say we get full price. We don't give discounts. So you could say we make a lot of money with that" (quoted by TASS, Russian state agency; also reported by The Mirror and The Guardian live blog). The remark came hours after the Pentagon's Elbridge Colby left a Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting at NATO after criticising Ukraine's deep strikes into Russia (The Independent, The Hill; first reported by The Telegraph). Portugal's foreign minister Paulo Rangel told his Ukrainian counterpart in Kyiv that Lisbon cannot hand over more F-16s, which it needs for its own airspace and maritime territory, but is open to training Ukrainian pilots (Ukrinform, Kyiv Post).

**Sources:** [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99130), [The Mirror](https://www.themirror.com/news/us-news/donald-trump-declares-we-make-2115479), [The Guardian](https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/live/2026/nov/18/donald-trump-mary-peltola-alaska-hakeem-jeffries-democrats-republicans-congress-house-senate-midterms-latest-news-updates), [The Independent](https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/europe/pentagon-elbridge-colby-walks-out-nato-talks-ukraine-b3087554.html), [The Hill](https://thehill.com/policy/international/6229395-colby-criticizes-ukraine-long-range-strikes/), [Clash Report](https://x.com/i/status/2123169448593097071), [Ukrinform](https://www.ukrinform.net/rubric-polytics/4186065-portugal-unable-to-provide-ukraine-with-additional-f16s-but-open-to-discussing-pilot-training-foreign-minister.html), [Kyiv Post](https://www.kyivpost.com/post/90515), [@MFA_Ukraine](https://x.com/i/status/2123152336130658716)
articles.why: The US president himself says European money for Ukraine's war ends up as full-price revenue for US industry. CEAFE wants a pan-European peace with Ukraine, Russia and the EU at the table; every euro spent on US weapons also means jobs and R&D that do not stay in Europe.
articles.watch: European reactions to Trump's remark in Berlin today; the Commission's line on "buy European" in the €45 billion instrument.

articles.headline: Hegseth in Caracas: US and Venezuela restore military ties suspended since 2005
articles.summary:
**US Secretary of War Pete Hegseth made an unannounced visit to Caracas on Wednesday and signed a technical-military cooperation agreement with Venezuela's defence minister Gustavo González López, in the presence of acting President Delcy Rodríguez (Venezuelan National Radio; AP).**

The deal covers joint training, intelligence sharing, equipment and access to technology, and the fight against drug-trafficking networks; Hegseth said Venezuela "has gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner" (AP). He also said the oil deal with Venezuela "makes the Strait of Hormuz a nonfactor for the Western Hemisphere". Hegseth then travelled on to Colombia and backed its president against a New York Times report ("Totally false").

**Sources:** [AP](https://apnews.com/article/hegseth-venezuela-maduro-trump-e02dd6173e575c644a37dd417d84296d), [Venezuelan National Radio](https://rnv.gob.ve/venezuela-y-ee-uu-acuerdo-cooperacion-tecnico-militar/), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/11/18/latam-venezuela-us-military-cooperation/5731795032282/), [AFP](https://www.afp.com/en/hegseth-makes-surprise-trip-venezuela-inks-defense-pact), [@DeptofWar](https://x.com/i/status/2123171948872040559), [@PeteHegseth](https://x.com/i/status/2123238686510776325)
articles.why: It is the highest-level US visit since US forces captured Nicolás Maduro on 3 January. Washington grounds its security in control of the Western Hemisphere, energy included, while asking Europe to buy its weapons and energy. Europe has no comparable presence in a country whose oil reserves matter to its own supply.
articles.watch: Publication of the agreement's terms; Colombian leg of the trip.

articles.headline: EU postpones methane rules on oil, gas and coal imports by two years
articles.summary:
**The Council and the European Parliament reached a provisional agreement overnight to postpone by two years the methane monitoring, reporting and verification obligations for importers of crude oil, natural gas and coal, from 1 January 2027 to 1 January 2029; methane-intensity reporting moves from 5 August 2028 to 5 August 2030 (Council).**

The Commission had proposed one year; the delay was longer after pressure from governments including France and from the United States, Reuters reported (via ETLegalWorld). The Commission must review implementation by 1 January 2028.

**Sources:** [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/19/methane-regulation-eu-agrees-targeted-amendment-to-safeguard-security-of-supply/), [@EUCouncilPress](https://x.com/i/status/2123247536366592162), [legal.economictimes.indiatimes.com](https://legal.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/international/eu-parliament-agree-to-delay-methane-regulation-by-two-years/135976321), [European Parliament](https://www.europarl.europa.eu/news/en/press-room/20261021IPR48321/methane-rules-parliament-backs-longer-delay-for-energy-importers-and-producers)
articles.why: The postponement is justified by the disruption caused by the US–Israeli war with Iran. It eases rules that weighed on US LNG exporters at a time when the EU buys more and more US energy: one supplier replaced another.
articles.watch: Formal endorsement by Council and Parliament.

articles.headline: Friends of Cohesion: 17 EU member states reject cuts to national allocations in the next EU budget
articles.summary:
**The ministers for European affairs of the 17 "Friends of Cohesion" EU member states adopted a joint declaration on the 2028–2034 Multiannual Financial Framework ahead of the General Affairs Council, rejecting any reduction of national allocations under the National and Regional Partnership Plans in the next "negotiating box" (Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs; EFE via Infobae).**

Spain hosted the meeting.

**Sources:** [Spanish Ministry of Foreign Affairs](https://www.exteriores.gob.es/es/Comunicacion/Comunicados/Paginas/2026_COMUNICADOS/Declaracion-conjunta-sobre-el-Marco-Financiero-Plurianual-2028-2034.aspx), [@MAECgob](https://x.com/i/status/2123195661294391772), [infobae.com](https://www.infobae.com/america/agencias/2026/11/18/paises-amigos-de-la-cohesion-refirman-su-oposicion-a-recortes-en-financiacion-de-la-ue/)
articles.why: The fight over the next budget decides how much the Union can pay for common defence and industrial policy. Cohesion countries defend their share while the Union also needs common funds for defence (SAFE, EDF, EDIP).
articles.watch: Next "negotiating box" from the Council presidency.

articles.headline: Update: Shenzhen eve: one hour for the Trump–Xi–Putin meeting, and a US "last chance" warning to Moscow
articles.summary:
On the eve of Thursday's first US–China–Russia leaders' meeting, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said "one hour is allotted" for the trilateral and that no full-fledged Putin–Trump negotiations are planned for 19 November; Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said a Putin–Trump meeting is planned after the APEC plenary (TASS, Russian state agency). US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner have warned Russia that this round may be its last chance for a favourable deal, according to journalist Tim Zadorozhnyy, shared by the Kyiv Independent. The New York Times reports that Western intelligence expects Putin to keep fighting through the winter. Putin's military aide confirmed that the "nuclear briefcase" travelled with him to China (as relayed by @DD_Geopolitics). Putin stood centre-stage beside Xi and Trump in the APEC "family photo", his first in nine years, which Bloomberg called "a powerful rebuff of western efforts to isolate" him.

Middle powers worked the margins. Canada's Mark Carney met Trump on a trade agreement and said Canada had restored market access for "more than 90 per cent" of the trade previously hit by Chinese tariffs; he also accused Putin of "lying" when Putin said Western sanctions were "a thing of the past" (Al Jazeera). Japan's Sanae Takaichi met Putin for about 30 minutes, the first face-to-face meeting of the two countries' leaders since 2019 (South China Morning Post).

No member state, on its own, has the scale of the powers it hopes to sit beside at the same table.

**Sources:** TASS, Kremlin, Kyiv Independent ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123103040878297295)), NYT via Clash Report ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123036161140805969)), @DD_Geopolitics ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123061715323490376)), Bloomberg ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123085109825823189)), @MarkJCarney ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123045894790459874)), Al Jazeera ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123107718793703910)), [South China Morning Post](https://www.scmp.com/news/china/diplomacy/article/3374961/japans-takaichi-meets-putin-rare-talks-amid-strained-ties-russia), [TASS on Telegram](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99076).
articles.why: This continues the 13:30 story on Trump's arrival. Canada, Japan and South Korea are using Shenzhen to secure their own deals, while no European leader sits at the table where Ukraine will be discussed. CEAFE wants a pan-European peace involving Ukraine, Russia and the EU, without outside powers deciding for them. The nuclear briefcase is a reminder of the nuclear dimension many European leaders play down.
articles.watch: The trilateral on 19 November and any joint text; whether Ukraine and the Abu Dhabi track feature in it; any one-on-one Putin–Trump meeting.

articles.headline: Europe's own track: the Coalition of the Willing meets in Berlin on Thursday
articles.summary:
NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte will travel to Berlin on 19 November for a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing co-hosted by Chancellor Friedrich Merz, President Emmanuel Macron and UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham (NATO press office); Finland's President Alexander Stubb will also attend. The meeting falls on the same day as the Shenzhen trilateral. Rutte said NATO is "doing our part to ensure peace talks will be successful" and welcomed "hundreds of millions of dollars" of new pledges to the PURL scheme. President Zelensky thanked Ursula von der Leyen for the proposed Instrument for Coordinated Support to Ukraine (up to €45 billion for 2027, of which up to €25 billion for defence) and asked Parliament and Council for "swift adoption". In Paris, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot accused Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon of the same line: "capitulation of Ukraine and complacency with the Kremlin". In Washington, House Republicans threatened to strip Ukraine-related provisions, including intelligence sharing, from a major defence bill (Clash Report).

**Sources:** NATO press office ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123027373608026541)), [NATO media advisory](https://www.nato.int/en/news-and-events/events/media-advisories/2026/11/18/participation-by-the-nato-secretary-general-in-a-meeting-of-leaders-on-ukraine), [Finnish Presidency](https://www.presidentti.fi/en/president-stubb-to-attend-meeting-of-the-leaders-of-the-coalition-of-the-willing-in-berlin/), @ZelenskyyUa ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123033090452795604)), Ukrainian MoD ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123059097780076896)), @jnbarrot ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123069600241783248)), Clash Report ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123068381066645995)), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/13/eu-leaders-bring-italy-and-poland-into-ukraine-peace-talks-team-as-kallas-fights-for-spot).
articles.why: The European negotiating team agreed in Dublin on 13 November (EU institutions plus France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK) meets in Berlin while the decisive meeting happens in Shenzhen. A seven-member team without a single European voice carries less weight than a Union speaking as one. CEAFE's line is that more money for weapons prolongs the war; what matters here is whether Europe secures a seat in the peace talks.
articles.watch: Outcome of the Berlin meeting (security guarantees, ceasefire sequencing); the €45 billion instrument in Parliament and Council.

articles.headline: Update: Washington presses Europe to buy American: Colby's F-35 remarks published and a forum for 80+ US firms
articles.summary:
The Department of War has published Under Secretary Elbridge Colby's remarks to the EU Foreign Affairs Council (Defence) of 17 November, as prepared: "we strongly oppose measures to exclude American firms from competition in European markets", extended to "other non-EU NATO allies". On fighters he said "there is no way that a gathering of disparate so-called middle powers would ever be able to build a competitor to the F-35 in a timely fashion" and that the effort "would almost certainly result in the waste of European and Canadian money, with an inferior result". After a meeting at NATO headquarters he told Reuters that "if you're going to have a secure Europe in NATO 3.0, you need things like the (US fighter jet) F-35", while saying the US does not insist on American-only production and proposing joint ventures and licensed co-production. The same day the US ambassador to NATO said he led a "Transatlantic Defense Industry Access Forum" connecting "80+ U.S. companies with European partners", adding: "bolstered by NATO Allies' 5% defense spending commitment, we are cutting red tape, fueling American jobs". The State Department discussed "burden sharing" and Lithuania's 5% of GDP plan with Vilnius. EU Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius told the European Business Summit that Europe must "outspend Russia and outproduce it", and that European air-defence firms can deliver to Ukraine "only in 2028 or 2029".

The EU as a whole can bear comparison; each capital on its own cannot. That is the difference that matters.

**Sources:** [U.S. Department of War (Colby remarks)](https://www.war.gov/News/Speeches/Speech/Article/4649777/remarks-by-under-secretary-of-war-for-policy-elbridge-colby-at-the-european-uni/), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/pentagons-colby-warns-nato-allies-against-shutting-us-firms-out-of-arms-deals-5033782), @USAmbNATO ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123065147266568514)), @StateDeptPM ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123102591483568266)), [European Commission (Kubilius speech)](https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/speech_26_2506), [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/defense/budget-policy-operations/italy-ramp-gcap-spending-2030s).
articles.why: This updates the 07:30 story on Colby in Brussels: the warning is now on the official record. Washington is openly using Europe's 5% pledge as a market for US industry and jobs, and argues that Europe should not build its own fighter, although it already does (GCAP: Italy, UK, Japan; and FCAS). A fighter whose software, spares and upgrades depend on US approval is the clearest case for European preference.
articles.watch: The US force-posture review due by 1 December (about 80,000 US troops in Europe, per Reuters); "European preference" rules in EDIP and SAFE.

articles.headline: Russia asks whether the Netherlands is "openly joining the conflict" over the Crimean Bridge strike
articles.summary:
The Russian embassy in The Hague posted: "Moscow has been duly informed of the NL involvement. The confession has been well noted. Is The Hague openly joining the conflict?" It responded to a statement by Destinus, the Netherlands-headquartered company, that its missiles were the only foreign-made weapons used in Ukraine's 17 November attack on the Crimean Bridge (Reuters via The Moscow Times). Destinus president Oleksandr Danyliuk said nine Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles were launched and seven hit the bridge (Clash Report). Dutch Foreign Minister Tom Berendsen told lawmakers that such embassy messages aim to divide Western countries and that Dutch companies exporting to Ukraine does not mean the Netherlands is at war with Russia. Separately, France's Minister Delegate for the Armed Forces Alice Rufo told RMC that a defence mission attached to the French embassy works in Ukraine, including specialists who maintain Mirage aircraft and Caesar howitzers (TASS, citing RMC).

**Sources:** @rusembassynl ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2122976975320990148)), [The Moscow Times (Reuters)](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/18/russia-asks-if-netherlands-is-joining-ukraine-war-after-dutch-companys-missiles-used-in-bridge-attack-a94298), [DutchNews.nl](https://www.dutchnews.nl/2026/11/russian-embassy-responds-to-nl-role-in-crimea-bridge-attack/), [Clash Report](https://clashreport.com/defense/articles/russia-asks-netherlands-joining-war-j3w4df768t), [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99092).
articles.why: Moscow is singling out an EU member state and a European manufacturer; in April Russia's defence ministry had already listed European firms, including Destinus sites in Hengelo. Russia's warnings target European states rather than the US, which is why CEAFE takes its nuclear signals seriously. Weapons as reported: Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles and Da Vinci (LORD) deep-strike drones by Destinus (Netherlands), and the FP-5 Flamingo by Fire Point (Ukraine). Destinus's account has not been independently verified.
articles.watch: Any formal Russian démarche to The Hague; a Dutch government statement; Moscow's reaction to the French mission.

articles.headline: EU sets up a Sanctions Office under Commissioner Albuquerque, outside Kallas's remit
articles.summary:
The European Commission created an EU Sanctions Office in its Secretariat-General, overseen by Commissioner Maria Luís Albuquerque, to cover the whole sanctions cycle from design to enforcement and anti-circumvention, mainly for the Russia and Belarus regimes; the changes take effect on 16 January 2027 (Brussels Times; Sofia Globe). TASS noted that the office is not under the High Representative, Kaja Kallas. The Council also authorised the signature of the EU–Indonesia trade and investment agreements, which it says "will boost EU competitiveness, diversify trade". EU and UK leaders meet in Brussels on Friday 20 November for the second EU–UK summit, on "strategic partnership" and "security in Europe and beyond". Six EU countries (Austria, Croatia, Germany, Lithuania, Slovakia and Slovenia) will explore joint procurement of CBRN surveillance equipment through the European Defence Agency.

**Sources:** [Brussels Times](https://www.brusselstimes.com/eu-affairs/2412656/eu-revamps-sanctions-strategy-with-new-office-and-envoy-for-enforcement/), [Sofia Globe](https://sofiaglobe.com/2026/11/18/european-commission-sets-up-new-eu-sanctions-office-appoints-new-eu-sanctions-envoy/), [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99089), Council of the EU ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123093508643021034)), European Council ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123109187085590736)), @EUDefenceAgency ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123012350001234073)).
articles.why: Sanctions and trade are where the Union already acts with one voice and real weight; centralising enforcement strengthens a tool only the EU as a whole can wield. The Indonesia deal diversifies supply chains away from dependence on the US and China, and the joint CBRN purchase is the kind of intra-European procurement CEAFE welcomes.
articles.watch: Name and mandate of the new EU Sanctions Envoy; the EU–UK summit's security deliverables; Montenegro's accession conference on 19 November.

articles.headline: Estonia moves to close its border with Russia indefinitely
articles.summary:
Estonia's Prime Minister Kristen Michal called for closing the Estonian–Russian border indefinitely and said the border guard is ready for a possible "migration attack" (TASS, citing Delfi). Defense News reports that Estonia plans to close its road crossings after an attempted arson attack on the drone maker Threod Systems. Narva's mayor criticised the proposal to close the Narva crossing, saying it would also affect Latvian and Finnish citizens (TASS, citing ERR).

**Sources:** [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99082), [Defense News](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/).
articles.why: Sabotage against a European drone maker on the eastern flank is a hybrid threat to the EU's own defence industrial base, and a closed external border is a matter for the whole Schengen area, not only Tallinn.
articles.watch: The formal government decision and the closure date; Russia's response.

articles.headline: Update: Trump lands in Shenzhen as Xi and Putin close ranks against "coercion" before Thursday's three-way summit
articles.summary:
US President Donald Trump arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday for the APEC summit and was greeted on the tarmac by Xi Jinping, with a flypast by Chinese fighter jets (Anadolu; Global Times/CCTV video). The first-ever trilateral meeting of the US, Chinese and Russian presidents is scheduled for Thursday 19 November, after the leaders address the APEC forum and a Trump–Xi bilateral; Beijing says they will discuss "issues concerning global peace", and Anadolu reports nuclear disarmament, the Russia-Ukraine war, Iran and trade on the agenda. Earlier on Wednesday Xi and Putin held talks lasting over two hours, continued over a working breakfast with Lavrov and Ushakov (Kremlin; TASS). Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said work on "the text of a statement" following the trilateral meeting "is proceeding intensively" and that Putin and Trump will have "a full-fledged conversation" regardless of format, possibly first at Wednesday evening's reception (TASS, Russian state agency). On Truth Social Trump wrote that he was "heading to China, from the Philippines", announcing "a new and completely different Trade Deal with the Philippines" that would be "great for our Farmers and those in the business of 'Energy'".

**Key facts.**

- Xi to Putin (TASS summary): China and Russia "should take responsibility as major powers and contribute to building a multipolar world order" and "boost exchanges between government bodies and armed forces"; Xinhua: China-Russia relations "have brought greater stability and certainty to a world of turbulence".

- Putin at the APEC CEO Summit: "the old instruments of economic dominance and de facto coercion have outlived their usefulness"; sanctions "can still slow growth" but no longer halt it (Russian MFA; Anadolu). He also said "the EU has been unable to adapt to the consequences of its own sanctions. Debt burdens are growing & inflation is rising" (Russian MFA, official Russian source). Eurostat on the same morning put euro-area annual inflation at 4.0% in October 2026.

- Putin to Xi: Russia-China trade "has stood well above $200 billion" for several years (Russian MFA transcript).

- Canada's Mark Carney, asked about Putin's claim that sanctions are "a thing of the past": "I think you'll find out that they're very real" (Clash Report video); Anadolu: Canada says sanctions will keep increasing while the war continues. Carney said he would meet Trump later on Wednesday (Anadolu).

- Trump said he "may" meet Kim Jong Un during the tour; Pyongyang has not confirmed (Anadolu).

**Sources:** [Anadolu (Turkish state agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/trump-in-china-for-apec-summit-global-peace-meeting-with-xi-putin/4128576) ([2](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/politics/economic-coercion-thing-of-past-putin-tells-apec-business-leaders-as-russian-president-meets-chinas-xi/4128504)), [Russian MFA](https://t.me/MFARussia/33422) ([2](https://t.me/MFARussia/33426), [3](https://x.com/i/status/2122973081345872354)), [Kremlin](https://t.me/news_kremlin_eng/8428), [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99043) ([2](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99048), [3](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99054), [4](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99055)), [Xinhua](https://x.com/i/status/2122976121562234923), [@ChinaMilBugle](https://x.com/i/status/2123005692047143369), [Global Times (Chinese state media](https://x.com/i/status/2123007111840031143), [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2122986954186744166), [Clash Report (Carney](https://x.com/i/status/2123004151307084090), [Eurostat](https://x.com/i/status/2122993215775371336), [Truth Social](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/117636323928351024)
articles.why: The three powers are preparing a joint text on "global peace", including the war in Ukraine, at a meeting where no European state or the EU is present. Bloomberg notes the summit has drawn comparisons with Yalta; Finland's president had warned on 17 November of a Yalta-style division if Europe relies on US-led talks. CEAFE's reading: a settlement of the war on the European continent should be pan-European, with Ukraine, Russia and the EU at the table, and only a Union acting as one has the weight to claim that seat. Putin's attack on the EU's economy in Shenzhen (below) shows how Europe's divisions and dependence are framed from outside.
articles.watch: The trilateral meeting and any joint statement on Thursday 19 November; a Putin–Trump encounter on Wednesday evening; whether the text mentions Ukraine and a European role. Earlier coverage: Xi–Putin and Xi's free-trade speech.

articles.headline: Update: Commission proposes a €45 billion Ukraine loan for 2027, financed by joint EU debt
articles.summary:
The European Commission on 18 November adopted legislative proposals for an "Instrument for Coordinated Support to Ukraine": a limited-recourse loan of up to €45 billion for 2027, financed by EU borrowing on capital markets and guaranteed by EU budget headroom (Commission release via Mirage News; Euronews). Up to €25 billion would go to military assistance and up to €20 billion to budget support conditional on reforms, covering about two thirds of an estimated €70 billion financing gap; Ukraine would repay the principal only after receiving Russian reparations, and "the Union reserves its right to make use of the Russian assets immobilised in the Union" if Moscow refuses (Politico, quoting the document). Ursula von der Leyen said the aim is to "give Ukraine a strong hand at the negotiating table" and that the proposal will be presented at Thursday's Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin and at the European Council in two weeks (Interfax-Ukraine). The same morning the 37th Ukraine Defense Contact Group meeting in Brussels ended with 15 countries announcing new packages, led by air defence for the winter (interceptors, radars, IRIS-T systems, drones), according to Ukraine's defence ministry; Sweden, Ukraine and the UK signed a Letter of Intent on ammunition and materiel for Ukraine's JAS aircraft (Swedish NATO delegation).

**Key facts.**

- Package: the new instrument; an amendment to the MFF Regulation so the EU budget guarantees the loan; up to €5 billion more in EU loans backed by AAA/Aaa-rated third countries via the Ukraine Facility; windfall profits from immobilised Russian assets could help repay the €45 billion and the existing €90 billion Ukraine Support Loan (Commission release).

- The EU and its member states have provided "nearly €238 billion" in overall support to Ukraine since 2022 (Commission). Russia's immobilised assets in the EU are worth €210 billion (Euronews).

- Kubilius: €25 billion "will go for defence in 2027"; the Commission says the loan will also support closer integration of Ukraine's and Europe's defence industries.

- The proposals go to the European Parliament and the Council; EU leaders discuss them at their summit at the end of next week (Politico).

**Sources:** [European Commission (via Mirage News](https://www.miragenews.com/eu-proposes-e45-billion-in-ukraine-aid-for-2027-1779492/), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/18/von-der-leyen-proposes-45bn-loan-to-ukraine-backed-by-joint-debt) ([2](https://x.com/i/status/2123005221399846971)), [Politico](https://www.politico.eu/article/russian-assets-in-play-to-repay-e45b-loan-to-ukraine/), [Interfax-Ukraine](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1238445.html), [@vonderleyen](https://x.com/i/status/2122994833836953756), [@KubiliusA](https://x.com/i/status/2122994136437682642), [France 24](https://x.com/i/status/2123005380254970198), [@DefenceU](https://x.com/i/status/2122973462079611299), [@SwedenNato (via @SweMFA](https://x.com/i/status/2122961284299715058)
articles.why: Joint borrowing ("Eurobonds", in Euronews' words) shows what the Union can do when it acts as one; but CEAFE's line is that more money for weapons prolongs and escalates the war, weakening and impoverishing Ukraine, Russia and the EU alike and raising the nuclear risk on the continent. Euronews notes soaring borrowing costs will make the credit costly, with member states paying the annual interest. The diplomatic step CEAFE highlights is the one missing from the package: a European mandate to negotiate a pan-European peace, rather than financing a "strong hand" for talks led by others.
articles.watch: Berlin Coalition of the Willing meeting (19 Nov), where US and European officials are expected to discuss security guarantees (Izvestia, via TASS); the European Council; positions of member states opposed to military aid such as Slovakia (Euronews on Fico).

articles.headline: Abu Dhabi talks: EU security institute calls Russia's demands on Europe's security order "preposterous"
articles.summary:
A commentary published by the EU Institute for Security Studies (EUISS, the EU's agency for security analysis) says the talks in Abu Dhabi "produced no diplomatic breakthrough", and that Russia "succeeded in placing a future European security architecture on the table", listing its demands as no further NATO enlargement, restrictions on allied forces in Eastern Europe and "a weakened, neutralised Ukraine". The author argues the EU should see this as "an attempt to sow discord" and warns that Europeans "may fear that, unless they get involved, the basic contours of a new architecture may be negotiated over their heads". Finland's President Alexander Stubb dismissed a Bild report that Russian proposals in Abu Dhabi included a demand that Finland leave NATO, saying he "has never once heard" such statements from Russians (TASS, Russian state agency). In Brussels, the US Ambassador to NATO wrote that the Alliance is being transformed so that "Allies take primary responsibility for Europe's conventional defense".

**Key facts.**

- EUISS: Russia seeks to use the months before winter "both to weaken Ukraine and to raise the cost of supporting Kyiv for its partners"; it describes "increasingly impatient US negotiators" and Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev's business offers.

- The Schuman Security and Defence Forum continued in Brussels (600 participants, 85+ partner countries and organisations, per the EEAS), with EEAS Secretary-General Kajsa Ollongren opening on behalf of Kaja Kallas; NATO's representative at the forum (@NATORomeroC) said "the EU is an essential partner for the Alliance".

- The EUISS also opened the EU-MED Peace & Security Forum (regional security, maritime security, counterterrorism).

**Sources:** [EUISS](https://www.iss.europa.eu/publications/commentary/putins-preposterous-proposals-are-no-path-peace) ([2](https://x.com/i/status/2122981292296048724)), [TASS](https://t.me/tassagency_en/99040), [@USAmbNATO](https://x.com/i/status/2122955466984894526), [@EUSec_Defence](https://x.com/i/status/2122925267198918828), [@eu_eeas](https://x.com/i/status/2122995611133698514), [@NATORomeroC](https://x.com/i/status/2122999399169380649), [@EU_ISS](https://x.com/i/status/2122997339187208324)
articles.why: Whether one reads Russia's proposals as a manoeuvre (EUISS) or as an opening, the European security order is being discussed in formats where the EU is not a party, while Washington tells Europeans to take "primary responsibility" for their conventional defence. CEAFE's conclusion is the same from both directions: Europe needs its own mandate to negotiate and its own capabilities (ultimately a European army) so that its security is not settled over its head.
articles.watch: Whether Russia's proposals are confirmed by an official source; the Berlin meeting on 19 November; Norway's call for a European mandate.

articles.headline: France's National Assembly writes protection from extraterritorial laws into its NIS2 cybersecurity law
articles.summary:
On 17 November the French National Assembly adopted at first reading the bill on the resilience of critical infrastructure and cybersecurity, which transposes the EU's NIS2 and critical-entities directives and the DORA regulation, by 464 votes to 64 (Assemblée nationale, scrutin 9916). Against the government's advice, deputies adopted amendment 40 (36 votes to 29), requiring the entities concerned to use technical solutions protected from foreign extraterritorial laws; the Journal du Net reports further amendments giving preference to providers qualified by ANSSI and subject to French law, sovereignty criteria in the procurement of operators of vital importance, and the option, modelled on Germany's transposition, of banning components controlled by a third state from the most sensitive systems. About 15,000 entities, including 1,500 local authorities, will be covered (Assembly debate). The vote comes as the US Commerce Department's BIS extends licensing requirements to computing capacity supplied from data centres outside the United States (Souveraine Tech; see 07:30, story on the BIS "remote access" rule).

**Key facts.**

- Amendment 40 passed with cross-party majorities against the government's advice (Journal du Net); it does not itself fix where data must be hosted (Polidix summary). The text now goes to a joint committee (commission mixte paritaire) with the Senate (Souveraine Tech).

- MEP Aurore Lalucq (S&D) called Mistral "one of our flagships" facing American dominance.

**Sources:** [Assemblée nationale](https://www.assemblee-nationale.fr/dyn/17/scrutins/9916), [Journal du Net](https://www.journaldunet.com/cybersecurite/1557881-nis2-l-assemblee-adopte-enfin-la-transposition-et-la-reecrit-contre-l-avis-du-gouvernement/), [Polidix](https://polidix.fr/votes/9787), [@SouveraineTech](https://x.com/i/status/2122976329595306255) ([2](https://x.com/i/status/2122976867179261954)), [@AuroreLalucq](https://x.com/i/status/2122965435553628556)
articles.why: It is a direct response to the kill-switch and data-sovereignty risk CEAFE flags: US laws can reach data held by US providers even in Europe, and US export controls now reach data centres abroad. A national safeguard is a start, but 27 different transpositions fragment the market; the logic CEAFE defends is a common European rule, equivalent to what Washington applies to itself, so that sensitive European data and systems rely on European providers.
articles.watch: The joint committee with the Senate; the European Commission's reaction (single-market compatibility); whether other member states follow.

articles.headline: European armaments cooperation: OCCAR turns 25 and the EATC grows to 16 nations
articles.summary:
France's procurement agency DGA marked 25 years of OCCAR, the Organisation for Joint Armament Co-operation, which runs 28 programmes in the land, air, naval, space and cyber domains, from the A400M, FREMM frigates and Tiger helicopter to the COBRA radar and the ASTER systems (SAMP/T and PAAMS); the DGA says these programmes strengthen the European defence technological and industrial base (BITDE), its competitiveness and interoperability. OCCAR celebrated the anniversary in Petersberg in October with German State Secretary Jens Plötner and director Joachim Sucker. The European Air Transport Command (EATC) marked 10 years of tactical airlift cooperation at the ETAC in Spain and announced that Denmark and Poland are joining, bringing membership to 16 nations. Spain's defence ministry marked "25 years" of the Airbus C295 in its service, from the veteran transport aircraft to the new search-and-rescue variant.

**Key facts.**

- OCCAR: 28 programmes; Stéphane Kammerer named as future director (DGA).

- EATC: 16 member nations after Denmark and Poland join (EATC).

**Sources:** [@DGA](https://x.com/i/status/2122991698779517140) ([2](https://x.com/i/status/2122991702038503614), [3](https://x.com/i/status/2122991703741051064)), [@EATC_](https://x.com/i/status/2122947920538268087), [@Defensagob](https://x.com/i/status/2122962900226568203)
articles.why: These are the examples CEAFE presents as positive: weapons and enablers designed, built and operated together by Europeans, with jobs and R&D kept in Europe and no external permission needed to use them. The contrast with purchases of US systems, which bring ITAR controls and kill-switch risks, is the case for scaling OCCAR-type programmes and joint commands up to a European army.
articles.watch: Which new programmes OCCAR takes on under SAFE/EDIP; Poland's EATC membership versus its US purchases.

articles.headline: APEC in Shenzhen: Xi defends free trade and meets Putin before Thursday's meeting with Trump
articles.summary:
**Xi Jinping opened the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen on 18 November, warning against "rampant" protectionism and unilateralism and calling for free and open trade and global cooperation on AI (Bloomberg, Reuters, France 24).**

He then met Vladimir Putin, who arrived on 17 November for the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting (18–19 Nov) (Xinhua, Russian MFA), and South Korea's Lee Jae Myung (Xinhua). Bloomberg reported that Putin will meet Xi and Trump on Thursday; Trump lands in China after Manila and plans to meet Mexico's Claudia Sheinbaum there (White House, via Bloomberg). China said it would take countermeasures if the US imposed new chip curbs (Reuters headline), and Global Times quoted Chinese experts criticising reported EU plans to expand the Foreign Subsidies Regulation. Taiwan's APEC envoy said he would speak with other members (Reuters).

**Sources:** [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2122885616534745133), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122895210489233534), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122896126579810495), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122904599724265520), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122890046009483533), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122796194049016104), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122912728880697432), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122809550214418836), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122904848081502244), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122892621165027796)
articles.why: The three nuclear powers that matter most for Ukraine and for the global economy meet in Shenzhen, and the EU is not in the room (it is not an APEC member). Decisions on chips, trade and possibly the war may be shaped there. At the same time Beijing is warning Brussels over the FSR. Europe can only bargain on equal terms with both the US and China as one bloc.
articles.watch: The US-China-Russia meeting on 19 November; any Ukraine language; Chinese countermeasures on chips.

articles.headline: Quad summit in Manila: "grave concerns" about economic coercion and export restrictions
articles.summary:
**The Japan–Australia–India–US (Quad) Leaders' Summit was held in Manila on 17 November for about 90 minutes with Sanae Takaichi, Anthony Albanese, Narendra Modi and Donald Trump, and issued a joint press release (Japan PMO).**

According to Japan's summary, the four leaders "expressed strong opposition to any unilateral attempts to change the status quo by force or coercion" in the East and South China Seas, and "grave concerns about economic coercion, including through arbitrary export restrictions", pledging to secure critical supply chains; they also discussed the Middle East, including Iran. Takaichi and Trump had a brief separate talk at President Marcos's dinner. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Trump is "serious" about engaging Kim Jong Un but no meeting is scheduled for the China trip (Yonhap, AP). ASEAN's Secretary-General briefed on the outcomes of the 49th ASEAN Summit (15–17 Nov). In Manila, police blocked protesters marching against the US-led "Pax Silica" tech initiative and the cost of living, which they blamed on the war with Iran (Anadolu).

**Sources:** [Japan PMO](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/105/diplomatic/202611/1117quad.html), [and](https://japan.kantei.go.jp/105/diplomatic/202611/1117us.html), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122851037925273705), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122885846382883019), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122865116492279814), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122903132166623576), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122800711968649603)
articles.why: Export restrictions and supply-chain security are now the language of Indo-Pacific summits. Europe depends on the same critical inputs but negotiates them country by country.

articles.headline: Norway asks for "a clear European mandate" to talk to Russia, as the Commission proposes new Ukraine funding today
articles.summary:
**The European Commission will propose on Wednesday 18 November a new loan package for Ukraine backed by all member states, "as some capitals continue to balk" at the funding (Bloomberg).**

Defence Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said the Commission has disbursed €1.71 billion under the defence component of the Ukraine Support Loan (UASL). Zelensky asked the EU to deliver the "additional 8 billion euros for Ukraine this year" in the Ankara Summit declaration and to focus SAFE on what "has already been tested" in war. Norway's foreign minister Espen Barth Eide called on Euronews for a clear European mandate for Europe to talk to Russia: "This war has been going on longer than the First World War, and wars end", and "if anybody is going to talk about European security order, Europe has to be there". He also said Moscow must not be allowed to dictate Europe's security arrangements and warned against a return to spheres of influence; Euronews reported that the next phase of the peace talks remains uncertain as Russia plays down face-to-face talks with Europeans. Economy Commissioner Valdis Dombrovskis said "the stronger pressure we put on Russia, the faster we can arrive at a real peace process". Zelensky said there are "21 billion euros in unused SAFE funds" that should go to joint projects with Ukraine (via Clash Report). after the EEA Council in Brussels he spoke of "economic security, competitiveness and strategic autonomy". Kremlin envoy Kirill Dmitriev wrote that "Europe should focus on funding Ukraine's reconstruction, not on prolonging the war". The EU's Schuman Security and Defence Forum runs on 17–18 November (EEAS).

**Sources:** [Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2122777086926770364), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122765186826215702), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122787033731276989), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122825121500893446), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122781103547392287), [and](https://x.com/i/status/2122779699294220622), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122758467580776674), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122777493811745114), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122758802575597933), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122766376729473335), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122774142349152429), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122766723501748719)
articles.why: CEAFE's line is that funding more weapons prolongs and escalates the war; the money Europe raises should serve a negotiated, pan-European peace and reconstruction. Barth Eide's call for a European mandate to talk to Moscow is the kind of diplomatic step CEAFE highlights: a peace among Europeans, Ukraine and Russia, negotiated with Europe present rather than settled over its head.
articles.watch: The Commission proposal's size and conditions; Berlin meeting on 19 November.

articles.headline: Iran-linked assassination plot in North Macedonia and Greece
articles.summary:
**North Macedonia and Greece said they had uncovered and foiled an Iran-linked assassination plot (Reuters, Haaretz headlines; articles not readable).**

CNN, cited by The Times of Israel, reported US intelligence suggesting Iran was working on plans to target senior Trump administration figures with a "dirty bomb" or chemical weapon in Washington; Trump said Washington takes the reports "very seriously" (Anadolu); Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi and deputy foreign minister Kazem Gharibabadi denied them (Anadolu, Al Jazeera), and Rubio later said Iran poses no "imminent threat" (Al Jazeera). Rubio also said there is "zero" evidence that the recent US technology outages (flights, banks, email, the NSA's classified network) are linked to each other or to a hostile actor (AP, State Dept). Clash Report, citing a report, said Tehran has hardened its negotiating position after the Republican midterm losses.

**Sources:** [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2122807041659916530), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122838497715204106), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122813325968904412), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122767134941946074), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122827135207280900), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122792144507228650), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122892640869871910), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122866764165910764), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122827840584380447)
articles.why: The US-Iran war is reaching European soil through covert operations in the Balkans, while the Gulf exchanges (see Early warning) keep energy prices and shipping at risk. Europe pays the costs of a war it did not decide.

articles.headline: Israel: an Eisenkot ally becomes Knesset speaker as the Gaza ceasefire is called "at risk of collapse"
articles.summary:
**Matan Kahana of Gadi Eisenkot's Yashar party was elected Speaker of the Knesset with 66 votes, defeating Likud's Ofir Katz, with support from Arab parties (Clash Report, Al Jazeera, France 24); CNN called it "a critical blow" to Netanyahu's grip on power.**

Netanyahu said "the results of these elections are not what I wanted" and that today's threats are "no less serious than they were before the 1967 Six-Day War"; Likud called it a "low point" (Netanyahu's account). The US-backed Board of Peace warned the UN Security Council that the year-old Gaza ceasefire is at risk of collapse without immediate steps (Al Jazeera). After the UK's sanctions on eight Israeli companies supporting West Bank settlements (20:30 edition), Australia imposed new sanctions on settlement expansion (Haaretz). Opposition leaders warned that Netanyahu could reignite an all-out war with Iran to stay in office (Washington Post).

**Sources:** [Clash Report](https://x.com/i/status/2122803089170223462), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122811446274793491), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122809950217089371), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122815241348153505), [and](https://x.com/i/status/2122814753143927114), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122877451328168105), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122868691175960581), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122791684085817618)
articles.why: A weaker Netanyahu and a fragile Gaza truce change the regional equation. The UK and Australia are acting on settlements while the EU, Israel's largest trading partner, has still not used its collective weight.

articles.headline: Ukraine Defence Contact Group: Europe pays, but part of the money still buys American
articles.summary:
**The 37th Ukraine Defence Contact Group met at NATO headquarters in Brussels, co-chaired by UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting, with about 50 nations.**

The UK announced a £240 million package of more than 1,000 short-range air-defence missiles and launchers, effective against Russia's jet-powered Shahed drones, plus more than a dozen radars; the missiles come from Thales Belfast and the radars from the UK and Europe, with deliveries from mid-December (UK MoD). Germany's Boris Pistorius said Germany and Norway will jointly buy another package of US weapons for Ukraine through NATO's PURL mechanism, focused on air defence, with a German contribution of about €273 million. Ukraine signed a memorandum on joint defence production with Finland and a letter of intent with Sweden and the UK on arming the Gripen jets it has procured (munitions, equipment, spare parts). Minister Khmara told the EU ministers that Ukraine plans to double drone supplies in 2027, when drones will be more than half of its weapons needs, and proposed joint production in Europe.
articles.why: Two models were on show on the same day. The British package, the Finnish memorandum and the Swedish Gripen deal keep money, jobs and know-how in European industry. PURL does the opposite: European taxpayers fund US production lines, and Europe stays dependent on American export permission for the air defence that protects Ukraine and, tomorrow, itself. Ukraine's call for joint drone production in Europe points to the better path.
articles.watch: The UK prime minister will set out the rest of the winter support at the Coalition of the Willing meeting on Thursday 19 November (UK MoD).

articles.headline: Poland says Washington gave the "green light" for a US base, and claims a leading role in Europe's security architecture
articles.summary:
**Poland's deputy defence minister Paweł Zalewski said in Brussels: "We have received confirmation that Washington gives the green light for a US military base in Poland.**

We are now awaiting the announcement of further details." Deputy Prime Minister and Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz, after meeting Elbridge Colby, whom he called deputy head of the Pentagon, wrote that "a week after the visit to Washington we returned to talks on a permanent US troop base in Poland. The matter is going in a good direction and is a priority for us." At the same doorstep he said: "There can be no European security architecture without Poland playing a leading role." The Polish foreign ministry separately met the US-Poland Business Council on American investment.
articles.why: Warsaw wants to lead European security while negotiating its core security bilaterally with Washington. A permanent US base deepens the "special relationship" bet that CEAFE questions: it ties Poland's defence to decisions taken in Washington. A leading role in European security would mean investing in European capabilities and a common army, not in a separate deal with Washington.
articles.watch: Any Pentagon or White House confirmation; cost-sharing terms; how this fits the EU's CARD findings.

articles.headline: Update: The EU prepares its 22nd sanctions package as Moscow puts "European security architecture" on the table
articles.summary:
**The European Commission began consulting member states on 17 November on a new sanctions package against Russia, the 22nd since February 2022, expected to target banks, crypto channels and the "shadow fleet", to be presented before the end of the month and agreed in December (Euronews).**

High Representative Kaja Kallas called the Kremlin's demands to redesign Europe's security architecture "absurd" (Euronews). The EEAS said new sanctions target international shipping and fleet-management firms helping Russia move oil, and that EU money flowing into Russia's energy sector is down 85% since 2021. The EU Institute for Security Studies wrote that the Abu Dhabi talks produced no breakthrough and that Russia's "interest" in a new European security architecture is "an attempt to sow discord", meant to keep the Americans talking and confront Europeans with the fear that a new order could be negotiated "over their heads". Zelensky said a prisoner exchange, one of the main agreements reached at the trilateral meeting in Abu Dhabi, is being prepared.
articles.why: Sanctions are one of the few tools the EU wields as a bloc, and the last package was watered down by national vetoes (Euronews). Russia's line on a "new security architecture" is aimed at precisely that weakness. Euronews also notes that Moscow could use the package as a pretext to keep refusing talks with the European delegation, so Europe needs both unity on sanctions and a single negotiating voice.
articles.watch: Formal Commission proposal before end-November; whether any member state blocks; Russia's reaction.

articles.headline: Update: Quad summit in Manila and a US-Thailand trade deal, as Lavrov attacks NATO's "presence" in Asia
articles.summary:
**On the sidelines of the ASEAN summits in Manila, Donald Trump held the first leader-level Quad summit in two years with Narendra Modi, Sanae Takaichi and Anthony Albanese; the group launched a new initiative on AI and deals to secure critical-mineral supply chains, plus maritime-security cooperation (The Japan Times, Al Jazeera).**

Trump and Thai PM Anutin Charnvirakul signed a joint trade statement: according to Trump, Thailand will eliminate all tariffs on US exports and remove "substantial non-tariff barriers" on US vehicles, medical devices, pharmaceuticals, ethanol and poultry, with the deal to be finalised in the coming weeks (Anadolu, Bloomberg). Asked about a separate meeting with Vladimir Putin, Trump said: "If it's available, I would do that" (Euronews). At the East Asia Summit, Sergey Lavrov said NATO members are "expanding their presence in the Asia-Pacific, openly seeking to contain China", and called the coming US-China-Russia trilateral "useful under any circumstances, because these are three nuclear powers". In Shenzhen, Xi Jinping received the leaders of Chile, Peru, Mexico, Vietnam and Papua New Guinea before APEC; PNG's prime minister told Xi it "wasn't easy" to close his country's Taiwan office (Reuters).
articles.why: The Quad is one of the US-led blocs CEAFE tracks: Washington now ties AI and critical minerals to it, two areas where Europe has no seat. The Thai deal shows the US method: bilateral, tariff-free access for American goods in exchange for relief, the same template Washington wants with each EU state. And on 19 November the three nuclear powers will meet in Shenzhen while Europe meets in Berlin: as Lavrov says, they have never met in this format, and Europe is not in the room.
articles.watch: APEC and the Shenzhen trilateral on 19 November; India-Japan 2+2 on 18–19 November (Indian MoD).

articles.headline: The UK sanctions Israeli settlement builders; Israel calls it a "hostile act"
articles.summary:
**The UK sanctioned eight Israeli construction companies involved in building settlements in the occupied West Bank and the activist group Tzav 9, which blocks humanitarian aid into Gaza (Anadolu, Al Jazeera).**

Ed Miliband said: "We will not be bystanders in the destruction of the two-state solution." Israel's foreign minister Gideon Sa'ar said Israel "views with the utmost gravity" the sanctions, called them "a hostile act targeting private, law-abiding companies" and said Israel "will not yield and will not change its policy under external pressure". On the same day Benjamin Netanyahu addressed Europe directly: "EUROPE, WAKE UP! … Europe is not a spectator. Europe is the target", referring to Iran's missiles and nuclear programme.
articles.why: London acted alone; the EU as a bloc still has no agreed measures of this kind. Israel answers European criticism by casting Europe as Iran's next target, which also feeds Israeli arms sales such as the Arrow 3 that Czechia is studying (07:30 edition). European policy on the Middle East is credible only if it is common.
articles.watch: EU reaction; whether other member states follow the UK.

articles.headline: EU defence ministers approve the 2026 defence review: "cooperate earlier", from the planning stage
articles.summary:
**EU defence ministers met in Brussels on 17 November at the Foreign Affairs Council (Defence) and the European Defence Agency (EDA) Steering Board.**

According to the EDA, ministers approved the 2026 Coordinated Annual Review on Defence (CARD), whose core message is to cooperate earlier, from the capability planning stage, and endorsed eight collaborative opportunities "from cruise missiles to a secure defence cloud". They also endorsed a joint statement on security of supply, to keep defence supply chains secure and resilient, and approved the Agency's 2027 budget of €78 million (+8.7%). At the same Council, Germany's defence minister Boris Pistorius announced $300 million for another PURL air-defence package for Ukraine, and Spain's minister Margarita Robles called for an EU Special Representative for Women, Peace and Security. The Council also highlighted Ukraine's battlefield expertise in defence technology as a potential boost to Europe's capabilities.

If Europe wants to sit as an equal, it has to pool what is today fragmented.
articles.why: The CARD diagnosis repeats what CEAFE has long argued: fragmented national planning is the root of Europe's capability gaps. At the same time, the German contribution goes through PURL, the NATO mechanism that pays for US-made weapons for Ukraine, so European money keeps feeding the US industrial base. An EDA budget of €78 million is tiny next to national defence budgets.
articles.watch: Whether the eight CARD opportunities turn into funded joint programmes, and how much of Europe's Ukraine aid keeps flowing to US suppliers rather than European ones.

articles.headline: Update: East Asia Summit in Manila; Trump meets the Quad and ASEAN adopts a critical-minerals statement
articles.summary:
**The 21st East Asia Summit took place in Manila on 17 November, as President Trump arrived for the ASEAN meetings and met the Quad leaders (US, Japan, India, Australia).**

ASEAN published a leaders' statement on critical minerals, which stresses the region's "significant critical mineral endowment" and its growing role as a producer, refiner and consumer of minerals. Russia's foreign minister Sergey Lavrov also attended the East Asia Summit and gave a press conference afterwards. Japan's foreign minister Motegi briefed on the Japan–India "2+2" meeting and the Quad leaders' meeting. The 07:30 edition covered the ASEAN–UN summit and Trump's arrival.
articles.why: Southeast Asia's minerals are a key prize in the US-led critical-minerals coalitions, and the Quad is one of the US-led blocs that group allies under Washington's leadership. Europe is not at the table in Manila. Its own access to these minerals depends on bilateral deals such as France–Malaysia rather than on a single EU voice.
articles.watch: The text of the Quad leaders' statement, and whether ASEAN's minerals statement favours any one bloc or keeps the region open to all partners.

articles.headline: Xi receives Vietnam's To Lam and Mexico's Sheinbaum in Shenzhen before APEC
articles.summary:
**China's leader Xi Jinping held a summit with Vietnam's party general secretary and president To Lam in Shenzhen on 17 November, ahead of APEC Economic Leaders' Week.**

According to Bloomberg, Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum also reached out to Xi during a meeting in Shenzhen, seeking to overcome a recent trade spat. These meetings follow the Carney–Xi meeting covered in the 07:30 edition: Canada, Mexico and Vietnam, all deeply tied to the US economy, are each negotiating their own terms with Beijing.
articles.why: While US neighbours and partners rebalance their ties with China, the EU is absent from APEC and has no comparable channel at this summit. CEAFE's view is that Europeans should cooperate with all global actors on their own terms, and do it as a bloc.
articles.watch: Any tariff or investment announcements from the Sheinbaum–Xi meeting, and the APEC leaders' meeting later this week.

articles.headline: UK sanctions those blocking Gaza aid and companies backing West Bank settlement expansion
articles.summary:
**The UK announced on 17 November sanctions on those blocking aid from entering Gaza and on companies supporting illegal settlement expansion in the West Bank, the Foreign Office reported, sharing a post by minister Ed Miliband.**

"We will not be bystanders in the destruction of the two-state solution," the post says. Separately, Al Jazeera reported that Israeli settlers opened fire in the village of al-Duyuk near Jericho, killing a woman.
articles.why: London acts on its own, outside the EU, while the Twenty-Seven remain divided on measures against settlement expansion. Each European capital acting alone carries less weight than a common EU position would.
articles.watch: The names on the UK list, and whether EU member states follow with national or EU-level measures.
