articles.headline: Auterion and Ukraine's SkyFall plan a drone joint venture producing in Germany
articles.summary:
**Auterion and SkyFall announced on 20 November that they intend to form a joint venture, "Skyfall x Auterion", to build drones at high volume in a new factory in Germany, with German funding and a path to supplying the German armed forces.**

The partners say they have already delivered more than 50,000 Shrike strike drones to Ukraine together. Production starts with SkyFall's Shrike FPV airframes running Auterion's avionics and AuterionOS; interceptors and deeper-strike drones may follow (Auterion; Breaking Defense).

**Sources:** [auterion.com](https://auterion.com/auterion-and-skyfall-intend-to-form-a-joint-venture-to-build-drones-for-ukraine-in-germany/), [·](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/autonomy-firm-auterion-to-launch-joint-venture-with-ukrainian-drone-maker-skyfall/)
articles.why: European money and a German site, but the autonomy software layer comes from Auterion, which operates from the US. Europe gains production capacity and Ukrainian combat experience. The question is who controls the software and its export licences.
articles.watch: The JV's ownership split, where the IP sits, and whether the Bundeswehr orders.

articles.headline: Morocco commits €366m to build a national defence industry by 2035
articles.summary:
**Morocco has allocated 4 billion dirhams (about €366 million) from the Hassan II Fund to its "Morocco Offer" defence and security industry roadmap (Royal Office statement; Euronews, 20 Nov).**

By 2035 it aims to create about 50,000 jobs, produce 40% of its military and security equipment at home and earn over 65% of sector revenue from exports. Priorities are drones and autonomous systems, land and naval systems, defence electronics, cyber defence and AI, with industrial zones in Benguerir and Benslimane.

**Sources:** [maroc.ma](https://maroc.ma/en/news/statement-royal-office-12), [·](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/20/morocco-commits-366-million-to-build-a-national-defence-industry-by-2035)
articles.why: It is a market and a partner on Europe's southern flank. European firms (French, Spanish) compete there with US, Israeli and Turkish suppliers for joint ventures.
articles.watch: The first foreign industrial partners named for the Benguerir and Benslimane zones.

articles.headline: USAF opens a $16.1bn propulsion contract to 58 companies, Rolls-Royce and Safran included
articles.summary:
**The Air Force named 58 companies on a multiple-award contract for "advanced propulsion enterprise work" with a ceiling of $16.1 billion through 2041 (Breaking Defense, 20 Nov; DoD contracts).**

Awardees include Boeing, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, RTX, Rolls-Royce, Safran, Williams International and Hermeus. The ceiling is not guaranteed spending: only small initial amounts were obligated. The owner reposted the story.

**Sources:** [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/air-force-issues-massive-16b-contract-for-engine-work-to-dozens-of-companies/)
articles.why: European engine makers get access to the US market through their US subsidiaries, under US control rules (FOCI, ITAR). European firms have no reciprocal multi-billion European propulsion framework.
articles.watch: Task orders, and whether the European firms' share goes through US subsidiaries.

articles.headline: EU defence ministers endorse a joint statement on defence security of supply
articles.summary:
**At the EDA Steering Board, EU defence ministers endorsed a Joint Statement on strengthening defence security of supply for Defence Readiness 2030 (EDA, 21 Nov).**

The EDA says it helps member states identify strategic dependencies and assess supply-chain weaknesses in the European Defence Technological and Industrial Base.

**Sources:** [eda.europa.eu](https://www.eda.europa.eu/what-we-do/all-activities/activities-search/security-of-supply), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124050186439643403)
articles.why: Security of supply is where dependence on non-European components (chips, raw materials, propulsion) turns into an operational risk. Joint European action is the only scale that works.
articles.watch: Whether the statement leads to joint stockpiles or binding priority-order rules.

articles.headline: Danish GomSpace wins €8m to build lunar prospecting satellites for Blue Origin
articles.summary:
**GomSpace has secured an €8 million phase-two contract to keep developing two spacecraft for a lunar resource-prospecting mission.**

GomSpace called the customer only "a leading North American space company"; European Spaceflight identifies it as Blue Origin from the company's earnings calls. An initial €2.9 million contract was awarded in January 2026.

**Sources:** [europeanspaceflight.com](https://europeanspaceflight.com/denmarks-gomspace-secures-e8m-contract-for-blue-origin-moon-mission/), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124065966812184678)
articles.why: European satellite know-how is going into a US lunar resource programme. Europe still has no comparable lunar programme of its own to keep it at home. SpaceNews meanwhile reports that Europe's space community is again making the case for a European human spaceflight programme.

articles.headline: Space: USSF-317 launched, Ariane 6 VA271 set for Monday
articles.summary:
**SpaceX launched the USSF-317 mission for the US Space Force on a Falcon 9 from California at about 04:22 UTC on 21 Nov; the first stage landed on the droneship (SpaceX).

- Arianespace completed the launch readiness review for Ariane 6 flight VA271; liftoff is planned for Monday 23 November between 11:09 and 11:38 UTC (Arianespace).

- Breaking Defense / SpaceNews: China has left 52 rocket bodies in orbit while building its satellite networks.**

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123995383625924847), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123864721862406579), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123909158529270042)

items.title: Defence Industry — 2026-11-20 20:30
headlines: France orders 50,000 155 mm shells from KNDS and triples a production site
BAE Systems opens the UK's first fully automated large-calibre ammunition factory
Two German one-way attack drones pass live-fire tests; first deliveries this year
Sweden's Nordic Air Defence launches the K200 interceptor against Geran-3a jet drones
Update: Baykar begins Kizilelma deliveries to the Turkish military
France's third Suffren-class SSN, De Grasse, enters active service

articles.headline: France orders 50,000 155 mm shells from KNDS and triples a production site
articles.summary:
**The DGA has ordered 50,000 155 mm shells from KNDS, with deliveries planned for 2029 and 2030.**

The order comes with a joint state–KNDS France investment to triple the capacity of the La Chapelle-Saint-Ursin (Cher) site through three new production units (KNDS, 20 Nov). The DGA says French output has risen from 30,000 to 60,000 shells a year since 2022 and will gradually increase to 150,000 a year by 2029 (DGA on X, 20 Nov).

**Sources:** [press release, 20 Nov, via](https://knds.com), [press release, 20 Nov, via](https://urlr.me/4GPYvx)
articles.why: This is European demand going to a Franco-German group. Sovereign ammunition supply is the clearest lesson of the Ukraine war. The scale only adds up if European orders are pooled, so that each national line does not stay subscale next to US production.

articles.headline: BAE Systems opens the UK's first fully automated large-calibre ammunition factory
articles.summary:
**BAE Systems says it has opened the UK's first fully automated large-calibre ammunition factory at Glascoed, South Wales.**

It says the £180m investment in robotics and autonomous vehicles enables a 16-fold increase in 155 mm shell capacity for the UK and NATO allies (BAE Systems on X, 20 Nov; the press release link was unreachable).

**Sources:** [baes.co](https://baes.co/NRVc5108qlh)
articles.why: Together with the French order, this shows European capacity being rebuilt at home rather than bought abroad. The UK is outside the EU, so whether it can take part in SAFE-funded demand is the test of a wider European munitions base.

articles.headline: Two German one-way attack drones pass live-fire tests; first deliveries this year
articles.summary:
**Two German one-way attack drone variants passed live-fire trials this month, according to Germany's military procurement office.**

This clears the way for initial deliveries and troop training before the end of the year (Defense News, 20 Nov; headline and summary only).

**Sources:** [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/)
articles.why: Loitering munitions from German suppliers instead of US systems such as Switchblade. It is a national step, and the gain comes if these programmes open to other European buyers.

articles.headline: Sweden's Nordic Air Defence launches the K200 interceptor against Geran-3a jet drones
articles.summary:
**Swedish start-up Nordic Air Defence unveiled the K200 autonomous drone interceptor, successor to the Kreuger 100XR, designed to intercept jet-powered one-way drones including Russia's Geran-3a.**

The firm has opened a staffed office in Ukraine, where testing will shape further development (Breaking Defense, 20 Nov).

**Sources:** [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/swedens-nordic-air-defence-launches-k200-drone-interceptor-pushes-toward-ukraine-tests/)
articles.why: Cheap European interceptors are the answer to firing expensive missiles at cheap drones, and testing in Ukraine speeds up the learning cycle. This comes on the day Poland reported that two Russian missiles and a drone violated its airspace overnight (Reuters, 20 Nov).

articles.headline: Update: Baykar begins Kizilelma deliveries to the Turkish military
articles.summary:
**Baykar has begun delivering its jet-powered Kizilelma drones to the Turkish military, letting the NATO member start using unmanned aircraft in air-to-air combat (Bloomberg, 20 Nov; Baykar on X, "from the first design to the first delivery").**

This follows the 19 Nov 20:30 item on Kizilelma entering service.
articles.why: Turkey fields a combat drone ahead of any European unmanned fighter. Baykar already owns Piaggio Aerospace in Italy, so it is also a player inside the European industrial base.

articles.headline: France's third Suffren-class SSN, De Grasse, enters active service
articles.summary: **The French Navy's chief, Admiral Cluzel, declared the nuclear attack submarine De Grasse, built by Naval Group, admitted to active service on 20 November (Marine Nationale, reposted by Naval Group).**
articles.why: It shows a fully sovereign European nuclear submarine capability. Only France has one in the EU, and the UK has the other in Europe.

headlines: MBDA Deutschland and ATMOS to study precision strike from space
UK minister: the US should build a British frigate design in America
Netherlands targets 40% defence-industry growth and €15bn revenue by 2030
Europe still seeks an "indispensable" role in the revised Artemis programme
ESA selects Plasma Observatory; Kongsberg wins LISA transponders
FNSS–CSG Karpat medium tank fires in Slovakia
China delivers a Y-9E military transport aircraft to Kazakhstan

articles.headline: MBDA Deutschland and ATMOS to study precision strike from space
articles.summary:
**German in-space logistics start-up ATMOS Space Cargo has signed a cooperation agreement with MBDA Deutschland to explore a capability for precision strikes against ground targets from space, using reentry vehicles (SpaceNews, 19 Nov; Defense News).**

According to SpaceNews' Andrew Parsonson, it is an industry-led initiative, not a response to an existing government programme, betting that nations will seek such capabilities in the coming years.

**Sources:** [spacenews.com](https://spacenews.com/atmos-and-mbda-to-explore-space-based-precision-strike-system/), [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/)
articles.why: A European-owned missile maker and a European start-up are moving into a capability until recently seen as taboo, without waiting for a US-led framework. It is an intra-European initiative; whether governments fund it will show if Europe wants sovereign options in space-based strike or leaves the field to the US and China.

articles.headline: UK minister: the US should build a British frigate design in America
articles.summary:
**In an op-ed in Breaking Defense (18 Nov), Luke Pollard, the UK's Minister for Defence Readiness and Industry, argues that the US Navy should procure a UK frigate design and produce it in the United States, as Washington rebuilds its shipbuilding base.**

The British Embassy's defence account in Washington pushed the piece on the US list today.

**Sources:** [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/britain-has-the-frigate-the-us-needs-and-americans-should-build-it-uk-minister/)
articles.why: Linked to the 08:30 item on the US Navy nominee's idea of a foreign-built shipyard on US soil: European designs are welcome in the US only if the work, jobs and yards move to America, while Washington opposes any European preference in Europe's own market. The asymmetry (US content rules, ITAR) runs one way.

articles.headline: Netherlands targets 40% defence-industry growth and €15bn revenue by 2030
articles.summary:
**Defense News reports (20 Nov) a Dutch defence-industry plan targeting 40% growth and €15bn in revenue by 2030, noting that the country of 18 million "punches above its weight" in several defence technology areas.**

(Headline and summary only; full article not read before deadline.)

**Sources:** [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/)
articles.why: National industrial plans add capacity, but no member state alone has the scale of US primes; the value comes if Dutch growth plugs into joint European programmes (the Netherlands joined the CAVS armoured-vehicle programme this week).

articles.headline: Europe still seeks an "indispensable" role in the revised Artemis programme
articles.summary:
**Nearly eight months after NASA made major changes to Artemis, Europe is still working out how to adapt and remain "indispensable", SpaceNews reports from Bremen (20 Nov).**

ESA is considering upgrading or augmenting the European Service Module so Orion can enter low lunar orbit.

**Sources:** [spacenews.com](https://spacenews.com/europe-seeks-indispensable-new-roles-in-artemis/)
articles.why: Europe's place in lunar exploration depends on US programme decisions it does not control. Artemis is a US-led bloc; CEAFE's line is that Europe should keep options open with other partners rather than tie its space future to one ally's changing plans.

articles.headline: ESA selects Plasma Observatory; Kongsberg wins LISA transponders
articles.summary:
**ESA member states selected Plasma Observatory, seven coordinated spacecraft to track how solar energy moves through Earth's magnetic shield, as the agency's next medium-class mission (ESA, 19 Nov).**

Separately, Kongsberg (Norway) signed a contract with Antwerp Space (Belgium) to deliver X-band deep-space transponders for ESA's LISA gravitational-wave mission, ESA's third Large-class mission; value undisclosed (Kongsberg, 19 Nov).

**Sources:** [esa.int](https://esa.int/articles/seven-spacecraft-observatory-to-study-plasma-universe), [kongsberg.com](https://www.kongsberg.com/news/news-archive/2026/kongsberg-awarded-contract-to-support-esas-lisa-mission-with-deep-space-transponders/)
articles.why: Intra-European space supply chains (Norwegian and Belgian suppliers on an ESA mission) — the cooperative model that gives Europe scale.

articles.headline: FNSS–CSG Karpat medium tank fires in Slovakia
articles.summary:
**Turkey's FNSS and the Czechoslovak Group (CSG) say their CFL-120 KARPAT medium tank completed its first live-fire demonstration in Slovakia (FNSS posts on X, 20 Nov; FNSS page unreachable).**

**Sources:** [fnss.com.tr](https://www.fnss.com.tr/en/fnsscsg-cfl-120-karpat-medium-tank-completes-first-live-fire-demonstration-slovakia)
articles.why: A European group (CSG) teaming with a Turkish maker for a Central European market; a European–partner product rather than a US purchase.

articles.headline: China delivers a Y-9E military transport aircraft to Kazakhstan
articles.summary:
**Kazakhstan's Defence Ministry announced on Thursday that a Chinese Y-9E military transport aircraft has arrived in Almaty and joined the fleet of the Kazakh Armed Forces' military transport aviation (Global Times, Chinese state media).**

Global Times stressed the aircraft's "mature technology". The post was reposted by @F_CEAFE. Kazakhstan is a member of the Russian-led Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO).

**Sources:** [@globaltimesnews](https://x.com/i/status/2123752270487810472)
articles.why: China is no longer only a buyer of Western and Russian technology: it is becoming an arms exporter and security provider in Central Asia, Russia's traditional backyard, and across the markets where European industry competes. The same day, US lawmakers pushed to deny certification to Chinese-made aircraft (see Economy).
articles.watch: Further Chinese deliveries to Central Asian armed forces; Russia's reaction.

Leonardo DRS wins THAAD seeker work and plans to quadruple seeker output
Navy under-secretary nominee proposes a foreign-built shipyard in the US for frigates

articles.headline: US lawmakers want Airbus to lose US defence contracts over its China investments
articles.summary:
**The House Select Committee on China released a report on 19 November recommending that the US government refuse FAA certification of Chinese-made aircraft and pull government contracts from aerospace firms, Airbus included, that do not halt investments in China's aerospace industrial base (Reuters; committee).**

The committee says Western firms "inadvertently participated" in China's military-civil fusion strategy and calls for tighter export controls and investment restrictions in the sector. It singles out Airbus's Tianjin A320 final assembly lines, whose wings come from Xi'an Aircraft Industry Group, which also builds Chinese military aircraft; chairman John Moolenaar has also accused the French government of controlling what Airbus may disclose (AeroTime). The report also names US firms — Honeywell, GE Aerospace and Collins — as having obtained licences for controlled transfers involving Chinese military end users (committee). These are recommendations, not law.

**Sources:** [chinaselectcommittee.house.gov](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/reports/investigation-details-how-western-government-policy-enabled-china-s-rise-in-the-skies), [·](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exclusiveus-should-not-certify-chinese-aircraft-restrict-investments-in-chinas-aerospace-sector-lawmakers-say-5039601), [·](https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/us-lawmakers-airbus-contracts-china-ties), [· @Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123660108504994077)
articles.why: This is extraterritorial pressure on Europe's flagship aerospace group: a US congressional body proposing to use US defence contracts as leverage over a European company's commercial strategy, while US suppliers named in the same report obtained US licences for their own China transfers. It is a reminder that Europe has no equivalent leverage over US firms, and that dependence on the US defence market exposes European primes to US policy. Watch for a European (Commission/French government) response.
articles.watch: Whether any recommendation moves into the NDAA or executive action; Airbus and Paris reactions.

articles.headline: Spain approves over €6.4bn in zero-interest loans for defence modernisation programmes
articles.summary:
**Spain's Council of Ministers approved a royal decree regulating zero-interest, multi-year loans from the Ministry of Industry to finance the armed forces' Special Modernisation Programmes (PEM).**

Spanish press reports the package at more than €6.4bn (Europa Press, Infodefensa, El Español, elEconomista); one outlet and a secondary brief give €6.9bn, so the total is unconfirmed. Beneficiaries named include Indra, GMV, Airbus, EM&E (Escribano) and the Spanish Eurofighter consortium, for programmes including PNT/Galileo systems, helicopters, digitalisation of the UME, counter-drone systems and air-platform upgrades.

**Sources:** [europapress.es](https://www.europapress.es/economia/noticia-gobierno-financiara-6400-millones-indra-gmv-airbus-eme-consorcio-espanol-eurofighter-20261118124816.html), [·](https://www.infodefensa.com/texto-diario/mostrar/6095764/gobierno-moviliza-6400-millones-prestamos-financiar-programas-defensa-indra-airbus-gmv-escribano), [·](https://www.elespanol.com/observatorio-defensa/20261117/gobierno-aprueba-millones-prestamos-desarrollo-programas-especiales-modernizacion/1003744462301_0.html), [·](https://www.elconciso.es/empresas/gobierno-aprueba-nuevos-prestamos-programas-defensa-pem_0_2008534062.html)
articles.why: Positive: national money flowing to European-built programmes (Eurofighter, Galileo-based PNT, Airbus helicopters) rather than off-the-shelf non-European purchases.
articles.watch: The BOE text and the per-programme breakdown.

articles.headline: Leonardo DRS wins THAAD seeker work and plans to quadruple seeker output
articles.summary:
**Leonardo DRS, the US subsidiary majority-owned by Italy's Leonardo, said on 19 November it has a contract from BAE Systems to develop a next-generation infrared focal plane array for the THAAD interceptor.**

Work is under way at its 200,000 sq ft Dallas foundry, which DRS is expanding to support the programme's aim of raising seeker production to about four times historical levels. No value was given.

**Sources:** [leonardodrs.com](https://www.leonardodrs.com/news/press-releases/leonardo-drs-awarded-contract-to-develop-advanced-next-generation-sensor-for-thaad/), [· @LeonardoDRSnews](https://x.com/i/status/2123525990093615152)
articles.why: A European group growing inside the US missile-defence supply chain — but through a US-listed subsidiary operating under US control rules, so the technology stays American. Europe has no comparable domestic demand pull for its own interceptor seekers.
articles.watch: Contract value; THAAD production ramp after the Iran war drawdown.

articles.headline: Navy under-secretary nominee proposes a foreign-built shipyard in the US for frigates
articles.summary:
**At his Senate confirmation hearing on 19 November, William Toti, nominee for Under Secretary of the Navy, proposed setting up a new "world-class" shipyard in the US, built by a foreign shipbuilder, focused on frigates and large surface combatants (Breaking Defense).**

Foreign shipbuilding is a sticking point between the administration, which wants some Navy vessels built overseas (the "Finland model"), and Congress, which wants to limit that.

**Sources:** [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/toti-pushes-new-foreign-built-shipyard-in-the-us-to-focus-on-frigates-large-surface-combatants/), [· @BreakingDefense](https://x.com/i/status/2123524406949372274)
articles.why: European yards (Fincantieri already owns Marinette Marine) and Asian ones are the candidates; the US model is to bring foreign capacity onshore under US control, the reverse of Europe's habit of buying finished platforms abroad.

articles.headline: Senate Republicans shelve a $350bn defence top-up as Iran-war costs and munitions gaps grow
articles.summary:
**Senate Republicans are suspending their effort to pass $350bn in additional military spending, as momentum fades to pay for the Iran war and other priorities before the GOP loses control of Congress in January (WSJ).**

The same night, Al Jazeera reported that the GAO found the Pentagon lacks an overarching plan for persistent munitions shortages, and Xinhua reported a Pentagon official telling lawmakers the Iran war had cost $48.3bn as of 13 November, up about 27% from $38bn.

**Sources:** [@WSJ](https://x.com/i/status/2123582713298817127), [· @AJEnglish](https://x.com/i/status/2123608705459712098), [· @XHNews](https://x.com/i/status/2123641295411548261)
articles.why: US munitions shortages and a stalled top-up mean slower deliveries to European FMS customers (Patriot, THAAD, GMLRS) — an argument for European production capacity.

articles.headline: Update: Vulcan's failure tightens the Space Force launch bottleneck
articles.summary:
**Air & Space Forces Magazine reports that ULA's 15 November Vulcan Centaur failure, which destroyed 40 Amazon Leo satellites, tightens the Space Force's launch bottleneck; ULA blamed "inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines".**

Blue Origin's New Glenn has not flown since May after a pad explosion, leaving SpaceX with a near monopoly on heavy lift. SpaceX separately said Starship Flight 15's Super Heavy booster performed a safe abort and splashed down off Starbase instead of being caught.

**Sources:** [airandspaceforces.com](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/ula-launch-failure-trouble-space-force/), [· @SpaceX](https://x.com/i/status/2123516375805379040)
articles.why: US launch concentration on one private supplier contrasts with Europe's need to keep Ariane 6 and Vega C flying; Ariane 6 carries Amazon Leo satellites on 23 Nov.

items.title: Defence Industry — 2026-11-19 20:30
headlines: Poland and Greece will buy radar satellites together with EU SAFE loans
The Netherlands and Germany order HENSOLDT's Knifefish jammer in series production
Kongsberg joins Ukraine's Brave Prime industry programme
France orders 72,000 HK416F rifles and receives its third Albatros patrol aircraft
European exports: Argentina eyes Fincantieri corvettes, Malaysia KNDS light guns
GKN Aerospace and MBDA explore cooperation on missile and launcher structures

articles.headline: Poland and Greece will buy radar satellites together with EU SAFE loans
articles.summary:
**On 19 November in Warsaw, the defence ministries of Poland and Greece signed a Memorandum of Understanding.**

It sets up a framework to buy SAR (synthetic aperture radar) Earth-observation satellites together, using part of each country's loan under the EU's SAFE instrument, the Polish ministry says. The memorandum lets Poland's Armament Agency add Greece to the MikroSAR contract it signed in May 2025 with a consortium of ICEYE Polska and the state-owned Wojskowe Zakłady Łączności Nr 1 (WZŁ-1). The ministry notes that it does not yet oblige either side to sign a framework or delivery contract. A Polish–Greek Defence Industry Day held alongside it brought together 84 companies (53 Polish, 31 Greek). Deputy Defence Minister Magdalena Sobkowiak-Czarnecka wrote: "This time the Greeks are buying our satellite system. Within SAFE, of course."

**Sources:** [gov.pl](https://www.gov.pl/web/obrona-narodowa/polska-i-grecja-zaciesniaja-wspolprace-w-obszarze-satelitarnej-obserwacji-ziemi), [·](https://www.onalert.gr/eksoplismoi/ellada-kai-polonia-ypegrapsan-mnimonio-synergasias-gia-tin-koini-apoktisi-doryforon-sar-meso-safe/834784/), [·](https://www.money.pl/gospodarka/co-sie-dzieje-z-safe-grecy-kupuja-polski-system-satelitarny-7352728539252736a.html), [· @iceye_global](https://x.com/i/status/2123400620929397023)
articles.why: This is the kind of joint purchase SAFE was designed for: two member states pooling demand for a European product instead of buying national systems or US imagery. It also shows that European space capacity can be built inside the EU, at a time when ICEYE itself is bidding €2.05bn for Avio S.p.A., the Vega maker. Joint orders like this one, not 27 separate national ones, give European space firms the scale to compete with US providers. Here, once again, Europeans buying together make a stronger market than any one of them alone.
articles.watch: Whether Greece signs on to the MikroSAR contract itself, and how many satellites it would order.

articles.headline: The Netherlands and Germany order HENSOLDT's Knifefish jammer in series production
articles.summary:
**HENSOLDT will supply its Knifefish electromagnetic-warfare system in series production to the armed forces of the Netherlands and Germany.**

The Dutch materiel command COMMIT, also signing for Germany, and HENSOLDT Netherlands signed the call-off on 19 November at the NEDS fair in Rotterdam. It is the first option under a framework agreement concluded in June. Knifefish jams enemy radio links, including drone control and command radio. It will be fitted to GDELS's Piranha 5 wheeled vehicle and works with HENSOLDT's Sawfish reconnaissance system. On the same day, HENSOLDT signed an industrial participation agreement with the Dutch Ministry of Economic Affairs for the programme. No contract value was given.

**Sources:** [hensoldt.net](https://www.hensoldt.net/news/hensoldt-awarded-dutch-german-contract-for-knifefish-radio-jamming-system), [·](https://www.hensoldt.net/news/hensoldt-agrees-industrial-cooperation-in-the-netherlands), [· @hensoldt](https://x.com/i/status/2123396590216056999), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123426179298304428)
articles.why: One country buying for two, from a European supplier, for a European vehicle, is the common procurement Europe needs. Electronic warfare against drones is now a frontline need, and here it is met by a European product rather than a US one.
articles.watch: NEDS also brought a Rheinmetall–Netherlands agreement on military vehicle technology (@RheinmetallAG https://x.com/i/status/2123428081478119539; the press-release link returned 404 when checked).

articles.headline: Kongsberg joins Ukraine's Brave Prime industry programme
articles.summary:
**Norway's Kongsberg signed a Memorandum of Understanding with Brave1, Ukraine's government-backed defence-technology cluster, in Kyiv.**

That makes it the third foreign defence company in Brave1's Brave Prime initiative. The partnership will look at Kongsberg technologies that meet Ukraine's needs and test them under Brave1's "Test in Ukraine" framework. It will also match Kongsberg with Ukrainian firms to integrate their technologies and components, and identify areas for joint research and development. Kongsberg's NASAMS air defence has been in use in Ukraine since 2022, and the company opened a permanent office in Kyiv in 2025.

**Sources:** [kongsberg.com](https://www.kongsberg.com/news/news-archive/2026/kongsberg-joins-brave-prime-to-strengthen-collaboration-with-ukrainian-industry/), [· @kongsbergasa](https://x.com/i/status/2123476582295593414)
articles.why: Bringing Ukraine's fast, battle-tested defence-tech sector together with European primes builds a European supply base, and keeps it from becoming a showroom for US firms.

articles.headline: France orders 72,000 HK416F rifles and receives its third Albatros patrol aircraft
articles.summary:
**France's procurement agency DGA has placed a ten-year order with Heckler & Koch France for 72,000 HK416F rifles, notified on 2 November 2026.**

The rifle is the core of France's AIF individual weapons programme. The order also includes silencers and optical sights. More than 100,000 rifles have been delivered since 2017 to replace the FAMAS. Separately, the DGA delivered the third Falcon 2000 Albatros maritime surveillance aircraft from Dassault Aviation to the French Navy on 16 November. This meets the target of three deliveries in 2026, and two more will follow each year. The AVSIMAR programme covers 12 aircraft, which will replace eight Falcon 50M and five Falcon 200 Gardian.

**Sources:** [@DGA](https://x.com/i/status/2123466669242650689), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123421556781285477)
articles.why: Both are European supply chains: a German rifle design made by H&K's French subsidiary, and a French business jet adapted for maritime patrol.

articles.headline: European exports: Argentina eyes Fincantieri corvettes, Malaysia KNDS light guns
articles.summary:
**Argentina's defence minister signed a Letter of Intent in Rome to acquire up to three Fincantieri FCX20 corvettes, in full configuration with an integrated logistic support package, Fincantieri says.**

Malaysia handed KNDS a letter of intent to buy 105LG light artillery systems, KNDS France reports. Neither statement gives a value or quantity beyond these details.

**Sources:** [@Fincantieri](https://x.com/i/status/2123442435585966257), [· @KNDS_France](https://x.com/i/status/2123463875698045432)
articles.why: Exports spread the cost of European production lines. In both markets, Europeans compete with US, Turkish and Asian suppliers.

articles.headline: GKN Aerospace and MBDA explore cooperation on missile and launcher structures
articles.summary:
**GKN Aerospace and MBDA have signed a Letter of Intent to explore working together on missile and launcher systems.**

It combines MBDA's missile-system expertise with GKN's lightweight composite canisters and structures. GKN Aerospace is British (owned by Melrose), and MBDA is jointly owned by Airbus, BAE Systems and Leonardo.

**Sources:** [@GKNAero](https://x.com/i/status/2123423457350189535)
articles.why: Europe's missile production is short of capacity, and canisters and structures are a bottleneck. Keeping that supply chain European keeps it free of ITAR.

articles.headline: BAE Systems plans to cut up to 1,070 UK jobs while its order book hits £33 billion
articles.summary:
**BAE Systems told staff on 18 November that it is consulting on cutting up to 1,070 roles, about 940 of them in its air business in north-west England (Warton and Samlesbury in Lancashire) and the rest at its head office, Aviation Week and local media report.**

The company says it wants to be "efficient, agile and affordable" and aims to make the cuts through voluntary redundancies; shop-floor manufacturing, aircraft maintenance at RAF bases and early-career trainees are excluded. The move comes six days after a market update citing £33 billion of orders so far in 2026 and an expected 10–12% rise in underlying operating profit. The Unite union, which first disclosed the plan, blamed the government for "not making critical decisions" and called for new Eurofighter Typhoon and Collaborative Combat Aircraft contracts. The Ministry of Defence pointed to a £708 million GCAP contract extension for BAE and the £8 billion Typhoon sale to Turkey.

**Sources:** [@AviationWeek](https://x.com/i/status/2123362650704756975), [18 Nov 2026](https://aviationweek.com/defense/budget-policy-operations/bae-systems-eyes-more-1000-job-cuts), [ITV News Granada](https://www.itv.com/news/granada/2026-11-18/bae-systems-set-to-cut-around-900-jobs-across-sites-in-north-west), [Lancashire Post](https://www.lep.co.uk/news/almost-1000-jobs-to-go-at-bae-systems-in-warton-and-samlesbury-9359654), [TheBusinessDesk](https://www.thebusinessdesk.com/northwest/news/2183065-more-than-1000-jobs-set-to-be-axed-at-bae-systems-aircraft-plants/), [Business Live](https://www.business-live.co.uk/manufacturing/bae-systems-cut-up-1070-34934625)
articles.why: BAE's air sector builds Eurofighter Typhoon, assembles the GCAP demonstrator and makes parts for the US F-35. Cutting engineering and support staff at the heart of Europe's combat-air base, while governments say they are rearming, shows that budgets alone do not keep capacity: firm, multi-year orders do. Every European order for a US fighter is an order not placed for Typhoon, Rafale, Gripen or, later, GCAP and FCAS. Without common European demand, Europe's own industrial base will keep shrinking even in a boom.
articles.watch: UK decisions on new Typhoon orders and a UK collaborative combat aircraft; GCAP funding.

articles.headline: The Netherlands joins the European CAVS armoured-vehicle programme
articles.summary:
**The Netherlands signed the Technical Arrangement of the Common Armoured Vehicle System (CAVS) programme on 19 November at the NEDS 2026 defence fair in Rotterdam, with State Secretary for Defence Derk Boswijk signing.**

It is the first step towards becoming the eighth participating nation, after Finland, Latvia, Sweden, Germany, Denmark, Norway and the United Kingdom. Finland's Patria leads development of the 6x6 vehicle; within CAVS it has orders for nearly 2,000 vehicles including options and has delivered nearly 500, with much of the production done by participating nations' own industries. The programme received €60 million from the EU's EDIRPA joint-procurement instrument. Dutch parliamentary answers name the Patria 6x6 as a possible candidate to replace CBRN reconnaissance vehicles; numbers and costs are not yet set.

Background: CEAFE has followed CAVS since it began in 2020 as a Finnish-led programme around the Patria 6x6; Sweden joined in 2021, Germany became a full member in January 2025 and Denmark became the fifth nation in April 2025, ordering 129 vehicles through it. #BuyEuropean in practice.

**Sources:** [@group_patria](https://x.com/i/status/2123368930546790482), [19 Nov 2026](https://news.cision.com/patria-group/r/the-netherlands-joins-the-cavs-programme), [EDR Magazine](https://www.edrmagazine.eu/the-netherlands-joins-the-cavs-programme), [Nordic Defence Sector](https://nordicdefencesector.com/en/article/netherlands-joins-the-cavs-programme), [Defence24](https://defence24.com/armed-forces/talks-with-several-countries-the-netherlands-is-interested-in-finlands-export-hit), [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/1470802036715409409), [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/1944726802351403368)
articles.why: This is the model CEAFE supports: European states buying one European vehicle together, sharing requirements, spreading production across national industries and securing supply. CAVS, with EU co-funding, now spans the Nordic and Baltic states, Germany, the UK and soon the Netherlands. No EU member state is big enough alone; pooled demand is how Europe gets scale.
articles.watch: The Dutch order (numbers, CBRN variant) and whether other states join.

articles.headline: ESA signs €102 million with OHB for the ClearSpace-1 debris-removal mission
articles.summary:
**ESA awarded the German satellite maker OHB a €102 million contract to build ClearSpace-1, a spacecraft that will capture and de-orbit ESA's Proba-1 satellite after it retires, European Spaceflight reports.**

The contract was signed on 17 November at Space Tech Expo Europe in Bremen and opens the implementation phase; launch is planned for 2030. OHB took over as prime in 2024, with the Swiss start-up ClearSpace keeping close-proximity and capture operations, after the original target, a Vega adapter, was hit by debris in 2023. The launch, first booked on Vega C, is now planned on a dedicated microlauncher; an OHB slide from July appears to show RFA ONE, built by Rocket Factory Augsburg, in which OHB holds 56.8%, though neither ESA nor OHB has confirmed it.

Background: ESA picked the Swiss start-up ClearSpace for the first debris-removal mission in 2020 and, as CEAFE noted in April 2024, handed mission leadership to Germany's OHB.

**Sources:** [@AndrewParsonson](https://x.com/i/status/2123312062151467300), [19 Nov 2026](https://europeanspaceflight.com/esa-awards-ohb-e102m-contract-for-clearspace-1-debris-removal-mission/), [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/1784224485693899049)
articles.why: Active debris removal and in-orbit servicing are part of space security, and the same capture technology underpins rendezvous and inspection in orbit. Keeping it in a European industrial chain, possibly launched by a European microlauncher, builds sovereign know-how in a field the US and China are moving fast in.
articles.watch: Confirmation of the launcher; Space Tech Expo Bremen coverage ([2026-11-17_0730.md](2026-11-17_0730.md)).

articles.headline: Ariane 6 to launch 36 Amazon Leo satellites on 23 November
articles.summary:
**ESA announced that Ariane 6 will lift off from Europe's Spaceport in Kourou on 23 November carrying 36 Amazon Leo satellites, with the broadcast from 12:39 CET.**

ESA also said its member states will meet in Rome on 15 December "to shape Europe's future in space exploration"; Director General Josef Aschbacher wrote that "the world is not waiting for Europe" and that Europe has "a choice to make".

**Sources:** [@esa](https://x.com/i/status/2123360778350977184), [livestream](https://youtube.com/live/k2adMyxSoJE), [@esa](https://x.com/i/status/2123357437956940275), [quoting @AschbacherJosef](https://x.com/i/status/2123354957164208591)
articles.why: A European heavy launcher earning money from a US mega-constellation helps Ariane 6's cadence and finances. But it also means Europe's rocket is helping a US competitor deploy its broadband network while the EU's own sovereign constellation, IRIS², is still years from service. The 15 December meeting in Rome is where member states decide how ambitious Europe will be in exploration.
articles.watch: Launch outcome (to be logged in the launches tracker); ESA meeting in Rome.

articles.headline: European Parliament's industry committee adopts its position on the EU Space Act
articles.summary:
**Defence and Space Commissioner Andrius Kubilius congratulated the European Parliament's industry committee (ITRE) on adopting its position on the EU Space Act, thanking rapporteur Elena Donazzan.**

He wrote that as the EU scales up its ambitions in space "it needs to have a functional space single market" and that he looks forward to the Council's position and the start of trilogues. The committee text itself was not checked in this run.

**Sources:** [@KubiliusA](https://x.com/i/status/2123381079130485148)
articles.why: A single set of EU rules on safety, resilience and sustainability for space activities would replace 27 national regimes, a precondition for European firms to scale. It also matters for non-EU operators serving the EU market, including US constellations.
articles.watch: Plenary vote and Council general approach.

articles.headline: EDF-funded Euroguard semi-autonomous vessel launched in Estonia
articles.summary:
**Commission official Florian Arbault (DG DEFIS) said he represented the Commission, alongside Estonia's President Ülle Madise, at the launch of the Euroguard ship.**

Euroguard, a European Defence Fund project, brings together 29 partners from 10 countries to develop a versatile semi-autonomous vessel. Further details were not checked in this run.

**Sources:** [@ArbaultF](https://x.com/i/status/2123335389221970006)
articles.why: A multinational, EU-funded naval drone is the kind of joint programme that can give Europe its own answer to US uncrewed-vessel offers.

articles.headline: Helsing scales back its Plymouth drone plant after losing the Royal Navy's Atlantic Net to a British rival
articles.summary:
**Helsing, the German defence start-up described by Bloomberg as Europe's most valuable, is retreating from its flagship UK project to build underwater naval drones, Bloomberg reported on 18 November, citing people familiar with the matter.**

Navy Lookout reports that Helsing has made 10 staff redundant in Plymouth and is moving research and development closer to its London software hub, while keeping some presence in the city. The trigger was the Royal Navy's choice, on 10 November, of Hampshire-based Ocean Infinity Solutions as commercial mission partner for Atlantic Net, a £90 million framework of uncrewed vehicles, sensors and AI for North Atlantic anti-submarine surveillance; Helsing had bid in a consortium with QinetiQ. Helsing says it remains on course to invest £350 million in the UK, the pledge it made under the 2024 Anglo-German Trinity House agreement. The US firm Anduril, which also pitched for Atlantic Bastion, posted overnight test footage of its Seabed Sentry sensor on the floor of a Scottish loch; the UK has said no Seabed Sentry contract has been placed.

**Sources:** [Bloomberg via @business](https://x.com/i/status/2123115303949185314), [summary](https://www.briefs.co/news/helsing-scales-back-uk-drone-push-after-missing-90-million-r/), [navylookout.com](https://www.navylookout.com/helsing-cuts-plymouth-workforce-after-royal-navy-selects-ocean-infinity-for-atlantic-net/), [royalnavy.mod.uk](https://www.royalnavy.mod.uk/news/2026/november/10/20261110-90-million-investment-for-new-drones-and-sensors), [Ocean Infinity](https://oceaninfinity.com/news/ocean-infinity-selected-as-commercial-mission-partner-for-royal-navy-atlantic-net-programme/), [UK Defence Journal](https://ukdefencejournal.org.uk/26-proposals-assessed-in-atlantic-net-undersea-programme/), [@anduriltech](https://x.com/i/status/2123188410487894153), [@PalmerLuckey](https://x.com/i/status/2123190774045319201)
articles.why: London chose a domestic supplier over both a German and a US bidder, which keeps the capability, jobs and data in the UK. But the case also shows how fragmented Europe's defence market remains: a European champion that opened a factory with ministerial fanfare a year ago gets no order, and its capacity moves elsewhere. A European market with common demand (EDIP, SAFE, joint naval programmes) would let firms like Helsing and Ocean Infinity scale on European orders instead of winning or losing national contests one by one. If Europe wants to compete on equal terms, it has to pool what is today fragmented.
articles.watch: Further Atlantic Bastion tenders; whether Helsing's maritime work (naval HX-2, Contra) wins UK or German orders; Helsing's role in the Palantir-alternatives debate.

articles.headline: Update: NATO's space-data marketplace runs on a US Space Force platform
articles.summary:
**NATO and the US Space Force launched NATO's Global Data Marketplace on 17 November at NATO EDGE 26 in İzmir, to buy commercial space data, products and services, starting with space domain awareness.**

New details published overnight show the procurement platform is the US Space Force Joint Commercial Operations solution from Bluestaq, a Colorado-based company that the Space Force has used since 2020. NATO says 222 companies from 17 Allied nations have already joined through its SPACENET industry group, and first orders, for the Space Theatre Component at Allied Air Command in Ramstein, are expected before the end of 2026. Purchased data goes into a NATO Unified Data Library; UK Defence Journal reports that both are hosted on Amazon Web Services' European sovereign cloud and that NATO keeps ownership of the data it buys.

**Sources:** [nato.int](https://www.nato.int/en/news-and-events/articles/news/2026/11/17/nato-launches-its-global-data-marketplace-for-space), [NCIA](https://www.ncia.nato.int/newsroom/news/nato-launches-global-data-marketplace-for-space), [spacenews.com](https://spacenews.com/nato-creates-marketplace-to-buy-satellite-data-and-services/), [@SpaceNews_Inc](https://x.com/i/status/2123204988394422407), [Defense One](https://www.defenseone.com/threats/2026/11/nato-aims-spur-space-industry-help-militaries-new-data-marketplace/417283/), [UK Defence Journal](https://ukdefencejournal.org.uk/nato-opens-space-data-marketplace-to-over-220-firms/)
articles.why: The marketplace opens a door for European space start-ups to sell to the Alliance, which is welcome. But the front door itself is a US platform, the cloud is a US hyperscaler's "sovereign" offer, and the model is copied from the Space Force. Europe already funds its own space-surveillance capacity (EU SST) and a sovereign constellation (IRIS²); without a European procurement layer and European infrastructure, European firms' data reaches commanders through American systems. Without a common industrial, technological and defence base, Europe will keep depending on decisions taken in Washington.
articles.watch: The first orders and which countries' firms win them; earlier coverage: HawkEye 360's GDM role via Luxembourg; NATO Starlift launch programme; also in today's Conflictos brief).

articles.headline: MaiaSpace signs its first commercial customer: Luxembourg's Space Cargo Unlimited
articles.summary:
**MaiaSpace, the ArianeGroup subsidiary developing Maia, a small launcher with a reusable first stage, announced on 18 November that Space Cargo Unlimited has bought launch capacity on its first commercial mission.**

Space Cargo Unlimited, headquartered in Luxembourg, will fly its BentoBox in-space manufacturing platform. Aviation Week, interviewing the customer at Space Tech Expo Europe in Bremen, puts the launch "likely in 2028", after Maia's demonstration flights; the inaugural mission is due in 2027. Maia, launched from the Guiana Space Centre, is designed for up to 4 tonnes to low Earth orbit depending on version and kick stage. Space Cargo Unlimited is co-developing its own REV1 return vehicle with Thales Alenia Space for 2030, but has also booked flights on ATMOS Phoenix 2.1 (2027) and SpaceX's Starfall (no earlier than 2028).

**Sources:** [maia-space.com](https://www.maia-space.com/news/space-cargo-unlimited-selects-maia-to-support-its-space-manufacturing-ambition/), [SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/maiaspace-signs-space-cargo-unlimited-as-customer-for-first-commercial-launch/), [@SpaceNews_Inc](https://x.com/i/status/2123276482944307219), [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/space/commercial-space/space-cargo-unlimited-places-order-maiaspace-launch), [space-cu.com](https://space-cu.com/blog-posts/space-cargo-unlimited-reveals-commercial-space-factory-rev1-as-the-vehicle-enters-production-targeting-flight-readiness-in-2030), [@AviationWeek](https://x.com/i/status/2123117034716221690)
articles.why: A European customer buying a European launch, on a European reusable rocket, is exactly the value chain Europe needs if it wants independent access to space. The customer's parallel SpaceX booking is a reminder that European demand will go to US providers unless European launchers fly soon and reliably. Europe has the resources; what it lacks, time and again, is the scale that only joint action can provide, here meaning firm European institutional launch demand.
articles.watch: Prometheus engine tests at Vernon (H1 2027); European launcher challenge; PLD Space's first commercial customer (same brief).

articles.headline: US charges a Russian national with spying on Palantir employees
articles.summary:
**A US federal grand jury has indicted Igor D'iu, a Russian national, on charges of conspiring to act and acting as an agent of a foreign government, interstate stalking and identity-document fraud, the Justice Department said on 18 November.**

Prosecutors say Telegram handlers told him his work was for "the Motherland" and directed him to gather information on a Palo Alto technology and defence company because it supplied weapons used against Russia in Ukraine. The indictment does not name the company; NBC News, citing three people familiar with the investigation, and Reuters identify it as Palantir. According to the affidavit, D'iu entered the US from Mexico in mid-2026, photographed employees' laptop screens, positioned laptops for remote access and followed one employee for nearly 30 miles. NBC reports no Palantir systems were breached.

**Sources:** [U.S. Department of Justice](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/russian-national-indicted-acting-foreign-agent-russia-target-silicon-valley-technology-and), [NBC News](https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/justice-department/russian-national-igor-diu-targeted-palantir-workers-sources-say-rcna610112), [CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/russia-agent-charges-spying-silicon-valley/), [Reuters via @Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123258718435369338), [Euronews via @euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2123243859106795648)
articles.why: European defence firms face the same threat, as the attempted arson at Estonia's Threod Systems showed. Industrial security of the defence supply chain (staff, sites, data) should be part of a common European approach, not left to each capital. The case also underlines how central US software firms have become to Ukraine's war, a dependence Europe is only starting to address with its own alternatives.
articles.watch: 24 Nov hearing; any Russian official response; European parallels (Threod Systems, earlier sabotage cases).

articles.headline: Senate's 2027 bill: a much bigger Space Force budget and more national-security launches
articles.summary:
**The Senate Appropriations Committee's draft 2027 defence bill would give the Space Force $54.7 billion, up 73% from $31.6 billion this year (Air & Space Forces Magazine's framing; its table shows $26.1 billion enacted for 2026 excluding reconciliation), though below the Pentagon's $59.1 billion base request.**

National Security Space Launch would get $7.08 billion against a $4.12 billion request, raising planned launches from 31 to 54. Golden Dome gets $9.4 billion, about half the $17.5 billion requested; the Space Development Agency's missile-tracking satellites are cut from $2.73 billion to $833 million, while Next-Gen OPIR Polar, which the Pentagon wanted to cancel, gets $520 million. Breaking Defense quotes the House Armed Services Committee chair saying the $350 billion reconciliation bill is "not going to happen".

**Sources:** [Air & Space Forces Magazine](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/senate-backs-bigger-space-force-but-trims-pentagon-plans/), [@ASForcesMag](https://x.com/i/status/2123125773036896352), [Breaking Defense via @BreakingDefense](https://x.com/i/status/2123174417987514596), [@BreakingDefense](https://x.com/i/status/2123195808707207259)
articles.why: One US committee adds more money to military launch in a single year than many European space budgets hold in total, and 54 national-security launches is a demand base that no European launcher has. Appropriators also told the Space Force to keep "multiple vendors" instead of sole-source awards: a reminder that the US funds competition inside its own industry while it asks Europe to open its market to US suppliers.
articles.watch: Earlier Senate cuts to fighters; Vulcan return to flight.

articles.headline: Avio's American arm wins Tomahawk motor work through a US-governed subsidiary
articles.summary:
Raytheon (RTX) has awarded Ursa Major and Avio USA a joint contract to design, develop and qualify a new solid rocket motor booster for the US Navy's Tomahawk cruise missile, both companies said on 18 November, so that Raytheon can dual-source the booster. Avio USA (Arlington, Virginia) is a subsidiary of Avio S.p.A. (Colleferro, Italy; Vega launcher and solid motors), not of Avio Aero (GE Aerospace's engine business). Its press note says it is "structured to operate in compliance with U.S. security and export-control regulations" and is "governed by a U.S.-based board of directors"; its CEO is James Syring, a retired US Navy vice admiral and former director of the Missile Defense Agency. The company broke ground in September on a solid rocket motor plant in southern Virginia. No contract value was disclosed.

**Sources:** [Ursa Major press release](https://ursamajor.com/media/press-release/raytheon-awards-ursa-major-and-avio-usa-a-joint-contract-to-develop-solid-rocket-motors-for-the-u-s-navys-tactical-tomahawk-m/), @ursamajortech ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123106798878265480)).
articles.why: This is the other side of ICEYE's bid for Avio S.p.A. (13:30 edition). An Italian propulsion firm can work on a core US weapon only through a US-governed subsidiary, the foreign-ownership ring-fence Washington demands, which is why the ICEYE offer needs CFIUS clearance and a DCSA notification. Europe has no equivalent rule forcing US-owned defence units in Europe under a European board, and European know-how here adds to US production capacity.
articles.watch: Whether the Tomahawk work weighs in Rome's golden-power review and CFIUS's review of the ICEYE bid; Leonardo's decision on its 18.04%.

articles.headline: Patriot's French bottleneck: the PAC-3 MSE ramp-up depends on an ArianeGroup fabric
articles.summary:
According to a Wall Street Journal investigation, Raycarb C2B is the only carbonised rayon approved for the nozzle of the PAC-3 MSE interceptor's rocket motor. ArianeGroup, the Airbus–Safran joint venture, makes it near Bordeaux. The fibre comes from a Czech factory owned by a Thailand-based group, is woven in France and carbonised by ArianeGroup, then sold to Park Aerospace in Kansas and passed to L3Harris for the motors that go to Lockheed Martin's Patriot line. A new ArianeGroup line is due in 2028 but will not meet US demand; a preliminary deal of 18 July 2026 foresees an ArianeGroup plant in the United States, with $25 million in advance payments from Park, unlikely before 2030 (Aerotime; Interfax-Ukraine). More fabric for the US would mean less for other priority clients, including the French armed forces (Interfax-Ukraine, citing the WSJ). The target is about 2,000 PAC-3 MSE a year, up from 620 delivered in 2025.

Technological and defence dependence is not abstract: it shows up in the number of companies, in spending and in the presence on the ground.

**Sources:** WSJ ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123092871225999487)), [Aerotime](https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/french-fabric-bottleneck-patriot-missile-production-wsj), [Interfax-Ukraine](https://en.interfax.com.ua/news/general/1238753.html), [Hindustan Times (WSJ reprint)](https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/the-pentagon-urgently-needs-more-patriot-missiles-it-s-running-into-a-rayon-problem-101794970704060.html).
articles.why: The best-known symbol of Europe's dependence on US air defence runs on a European chokepoint, which gives Europe leverage just as the Pentagon insists that European markets stay open to US firms. A US plant would move that capability across the Atlantic. The European alternative to Patriot exists: SAMP/T NG by Eurosam (MBDA and Thales).
articles.watch: Whether France sets conditions on the US plant; L3Harris's qualification of a second rayon source.

articles.headline: MBDA Deutschland and ATMOS Space Cargo study "Precision Orbital Deep Strike"
articles.summary:
ATMOS Space Cargo (Lichtenau, Germany; sites in Strasbourg and Kraków) and MBDA Deutschland signed a cooperation agreement on 18 November to design, develop and demonstrate a "Precision Orbital Deep Strike" (PODS) capability, combining military payloads with ATMOS's orbital transport and re-entry technology. The initial scope covers architecture, feasibility, payload integration and possible demonstrations; no budget, timetable or specifications were disclosed. ATMOS says PODS is separate from its civilian PHOENIX capsules and that deployment would depend on government decisions and applicable law. Opex360 notes the vulnerabilities: a predictable low-orbit trajectory, exposure to anti-satellite weapons and escalation risk.

**Sources:** [ATMOS Space Cargo](https://atmos-space-cargo.com/milestones/atmos-x-mbda-cooperation-agreement-signed/), @MBDADeutschland ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123088080999776621)), [Resilience Media](https://resiliencemedia.co/atmos-mbda-europe-militray-precision-space/), [hartpunkt](https://www.hartpunkt.de/atmos-mbda-deutschland-und-kooperieren-bei-faehigkeit-zum-precision-orbital-deep-strike/), [Opex360](https://www.opex360.com/2026/11/18/mbda-deutschland-et-atmos-space-cargo-veulent-developper-une-capacite-de-frappe-orbitale-de-precision/).
articles.why: A German start-up and a European champion are entering a field shaped so far by the US and China, in principle a sovereign capability. But conventional strike from orbit raises arms-control questions Europe has not debated: anything that shortens warning times between NATO and Russia increases the risk of miscalculation, including nuclear.
articles.watch: Whether the Bundeswehr or the European Defence Fund funds a demonstrator; reactions under the Outer Space Treaty.

articles.headline: HENSOLDT hands Spexer radar series production to car-parts maker ZF
articles.summary:
HENSOLDT and ZF Friedrichshafen signed a cooperation agreement on 18 November at Germany's Economy Ministry, with Minister Katherina Reiche present. ZF will set up scalable series production of Spexer counter-drone radars and an automated test system, making the radars and delivering them directly to customers, while all intellectual property stays with HENSOLDT. The Spexer 2000 is part of Rheinmetall's Skyranger 30 and of the Bundeswehr's short-range air defence programme (NNbS). CEO Oliver Dörre called it "a key element in reliably meeting the structurally rising demand in the long term".

**Sources:** [HENSOLDT](https://www.hensoldt.net/news/hensoldt-expands-production-capacity-partnership-with-zf), @hensoldt ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123091323272233426)).
articles.why: A European car supplier (about 153,000 staff, €38.8 billion in 2025 sales) moves into defence electronics, keeping industrial jobs and adding capacity with IP kept in Europe: a model for a car sector under pressure from energy costs.
articles.watch: Volumes and site; other automotive conversions.

articles.headline: Dutch marines' "Kaaiman": a US JLTV chosen over a European bid
articles.summary:
Oshkosh Defense said it hosted the Netherlands Ministry of Defence this week to view the prototype of the Dutch Expeditionary Patrol Vehicle (DXPV) "Kaaiman", built on its JLTV line. The Netherlands ordered 150 vehicles for the Korps Mariniers in June 2025, with deliveries from 2028. Defensie's own magazine says the tender ended with one European and one American finalist, and that the European bid "was not sufficient on a number of critical points".

**Sources:** @OshkoshDefense ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123092630620012932)), [Oshkosh Defense](https://oshkoshdefense.com/oshkosh-defense-begins-production-of-first-dxpv-prototype-for-netherlands-ministry-of-defence/), [Defensie](https://www.defensie.nl/nieuws/20250424-mariniers-krijgen-nieuwe-patrouillevoertuigen), [Defense News](https://www.defensenews.com/land/2026/10/14/oshkosh-adapts-jltv-for-dutch-military-patrol-vehicle/).
articles.why: Another European fleet goes to a US platform. European light tactical vehicles exist, such as the Rheinmetall/Mercedes-Benz Caracal already in Dutch and German service; the requirement gap cited (fording to 1.5 m, salt-water corrosion) is one European industry could close through joint EDF/EDIP-funded development. Each such purchase means lost jobs and R&D and dependence on US export permission.
articles.watch: Prototype trials in 2027 and deliveries from 2028.

articles.headline: Round-up: TEKEVER's French factory, a US radar order and Vulcan's failure cause
articles.summary:
**TEKEVER (Portugal) in France:** the DGA recapped the new TEKEVER factory at Fontanes near Cahors, inaugurated on 13 November: a €100 million plant and a €43 million contract for 15 AR3 tactical drone systems, first deliveries by year-end; TEKEVER is in exclusive negotiations for deep-support drones. A European supplier building in another EU state, with French payloads. **Navantia** (Spain) held an industry day in Copenhagen with more than 40 Danish companies. **Leidos** won a $40.8 million US Marine Corps award for 14 Medium Range Air Defense Radars. **Shield AI** plans a 420,000 sq ft factory in Des Moines. **ULA** says its first data review points to "inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines" as the cause of low booster thrust on the 15 November Vulcan launch. No new US arms-sale notification since Albania's HIMARS (17 November); next launches: Falcon 9 USSF-317 (19 November) and Ariane 64 VA271 (23 November).

**Sources:** @DGA ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123100777795268950)), [TEKEVER](https://www.tekever.com/news/tekever-inaugurates-cahors-factory-and-unveils-the-first-system-to-be-delivered-to-the-french-armed-forces/), @NavantiaOficial ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123039508174110748)), @LeidosInc ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123051104745263326)), @shieldaitech ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123082758369264083)), [ULA](https://blog.ulalaunch.com/blog/vulcan-leo-1-updates), [US State Department](https://www.state.gov/arms-sales-congressional-notifications/).

articles.headline: Update: ICEYE–Avio — Brussels applauds, Rome hesitates, and Washington must also approve
articles.summary:
New facts since the 20:30 edition of 17 November and the 07:30 edition of 18 November. The bid concerns Avio S.p.A. (Colleferro, Italy: Vega launcher, solid rocket motors), not Avio Aero (GE Aerospace's engine business). Andrius Kubilius, EU Commissioner for Defence and Space, wrote on X that satellite production and launch capability "unites in one company", that this "can have a major impact on the future of 🇪🇺 space activities" and that such consolidation "is exactly what M. Draghi suggested in his famous report". Defence Minister Guido Crosetto told Reuters: "If I were Leonardo, I would think carefully before exiting Avio" (Teleborsa/ANSA). Leonardo holds 18.04% and is 30% owned by Italy's Economy Ministry; without it, ICEYE would need more than 80% of the remaining shares to reach its 66.67% threshold. Government sources told Reuters that Rome had received no notification and that any assessment was "premature". ICEYE's CEO Rafal Modrzewski said he was open to talks, including a possible public partner. Mediobanca Research expects "significant" political and regulatory obstacles and a possible counter-bid by Italian or European investors (MilanoFinanza).

**Key facts.** €41 per share, up to about €2.05bn, cash; 20% premium; commitments of €1bn of investment over five years and 400 jobs in Italy; combined revenue about €0.8bn (MilanoFinanza). Conditions: 66.67% threshold; Italian golden power; FDI in France and the UK; EU FSR; CFIUS; DCSA notification.

**Sources:** @KubiliusA ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123004235688403143)), [Iris 2 S.p.A. offer notice (ICEYE, PDF)](https://www.iceye.com/hubfs/102%20Notice%20%2817.11.2026%29%20%5BENG%5D.pdf?hsLang=en), [Teleborsa/ANSA (Crosetto)](https://teleborsa.ansa.it/notiziario/finanza/opa-iceye-su-avio-crosetto-se-fossi-leonardo-rifletterei-prima-di-uscire/), [MarketScreener/Reuters (no notification)](https://it.marketscreener.com/notizie/avio-al-governo-nessuna-notifica-da-iceye-prematura-ogni-valutazione-fonti-ce785edcda8bff21), [MilanoFinanza](https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/avio-iceye-faro-golden-power-2724557), [Defense News](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/).
articles.why: This is an intra-European merger (Finland–Italy) that would join SAR satellites and a European launcher with solid-propulsion know-how that also feeds MBDA. On CEAFE's line that is positive: fewer, larger European champions. Yet the offer notice shows how far US jurisdiction reaches into a deal between two EU firms. Besides Italy's golden power, French and UK FDI clearance and EU foreign-subsidies review, the offer requires approval by the US Committee on Foreign Investment (CFIUS) "without conditions" and a notification to the Pentagon's Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA), because of the groups' US operations. No EU authority can block a US merger in the same way. Rome's reluctance is the other risk: a national veto on a European consolidation would cut against the EU-scale industry that Kubilius is calling for.
articles.watch: Leonardo's decision (with the government), Avio's board opinion, the golden-power filing and any counter-bid. Next Vega C (VA-series, IRIDE satellites) is slipping toward Christmas (the 07:30 edition of 16 November).

articles.headline: Switzerland votes on 29 November on easing its arms-export law: polls at a dead heat
articles.summary:
Two final polls published on 18 November show the reform of the Swiss War Materiel Act just ahead but without a majority: 49% yes and 48% no (Tamedia/20 Minuten, LeeWas, 11–12 Nov, >12,000 respondents) and 49% yes, 46% no, 5% undecided (SRG SSR, gfs.bern, 4–11 Nov, 13,527 respondents, ±2.8 points). The law passed by parliament in December 2025 would allow exports to 25 mostly Western countries even when they are in a conflict, while giving the government a veto on neutrality grounds (Bloomberg via swissinfo). Swiss manufacturers say neutrality-based restrictions have pushed them to move capacity abroad; they lost business after Russia's invasion of Ukraine and face a further drop after the Iran war triggered a ban on shipments to the US. The divide is political (FDP 75–79% yes, Greens and SP reject it), by gender (59% of men in favour, 38% of women in Tamedia's poll) and by age.

**Sources:** [swissinfo (Bloomberg)](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/swiss-face-nail-biter-vote-on-allowing-more-weapon-exports/92397966), [swissinfo (SRG poll)](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/votes/november-29-votes-opposition-to-pension-financing-plan-edging-ahead/92396495), [SRF](https://www.srf.ch/news/zweite-srg-umfrage-kriegsmaterialgesetz-pattsituation-mit-leichtem-ja-vorteil), [20 Minutes](https://www.20min.ch/fr/story/sondage-20-mintamedia-tva-et-initiative-du-centre-rejetes-materiel-de-guerre-incertain-103669075), Bloomberg ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2122958029075128749)).
articles.why: Swiss firms are part of European supply chains, and Swiss refusals to let European buyers pass on Swiss-made ammunition and equipment have been a recurring problem for European armies since 2022. A "yes" would make Swiss suppliers more predictable for the 25 listed partners. It is also a European parallel to the ITAR debate (the 07:30 edition of 18 November): whoever controls re-export rules controls the use of the product.
articles.watch: Result on 29 November; which 25 countries are on the list; reactions from German and Danish buyers.

articles.headline: PLD Space signs its first commercial launch: Mitsubishi Electric on MIURA 5's second flight
articles.summary:
Spanish launcher start-up PLD Space announced on 18 November its first commercial launch contract: a Mitsubishi Electric demonstration satellite for the Japanese group's planned mega-constellation will fly on the second test flight of MIURA 5. Mitsubishi Electric is also an investor: it put €50m into PLD Space in March 2026, leading the €180m Series C, and led a €108m extension on 1 September, with "priority access" to MIURA 5 launches. No date is set; the maiden flight from the Guiana Space Centre slipped in October to the first half of 2027 (European Spaceflight).

**Sources:** @PLD_Space ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2122977305106567566)), [European Spaceflight](https://europeanspaceflight.com/pld-space-investor-selects-miura-5-to-launch-demo-mission/), SpaceNews ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2122932907744317744)).
articles.why: A second European commercial launcher (after Isar's Spectrum, which reached orbit from Andøya) is part of the answer to the launch squeeze left by Vega C delays and the Vulcan failure (the 07:30 edition of 17 November). The anchor customer and lead investor is Japanese, not European. European institutional customers (ESA's European Launcher Challenge, national governments) would give such firms a domestic market.
articles.watch: MIURA 5 qualification and the first-flight date; ESA Launcher Challenge contracts.

articles.headline: DLR chief: Europe needs a heavy-lift launcher competition and a German sea-launch trial
articles.summary:
At Space Tech Expo Europe in Bremen, Walther Pelzer, head of the German Space Agency at DLR, said Europe relies only on Ariane 6 for heavy lift and should extend the European Launcher Challenge model to larger rockets. He said Germany could trial a sea-launch capability next year with a sounding rocket fired from a vessel, an offshore option that could later be placed near the equator. He also said the EU should treat UK and Norwegian launch sites as European, and that Germany is working with Canada and Spain on launch infrastructure. Trying to calm fears that Berlin is going it alone in security space, he said Germany had invited the EU and ESA to join its "Protocol Stack for Space" (European Architecture for Space Interoperability) (Aviation Week).

**Sources:** [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/space/launch-vehicles-propulsion/dlr-boss-wants-european-heavy-lift-rocket-challenge), [DLR](https://www.dlr.de/en/latest/news/2026/space-tech-expo-2026-dlr-showcases-technologies-for-the-future-of-spaceflight), Aviation Week ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2122973838270976034)).
articles.why: Independent access to space is a precondition of a European defence capability (reconnaissance, communications, navigation). A heavy-lift competition would avoid relying on one launcher, while the UK/Norway point raises the question of how far "European" preference extends. The interoperability offer responds to the France–Germany friction reported in the 07:30 edition of 18 November.
articles.watch: ESA ministerial decisions on launchers; any German sea-launch test date.

articles.headline: European space round-up from Bremen: Estonia's Space Cyber Range, Dcubed's €27.2m round, ICEYE processing
articles.summary:
**Estonia** is offering a Space Cyber Range to countries and companies for testing satellites, ground stations and operations against cyber attacks, fully operational in 2027 (Minister of Economy and Industry Liina Vahtras, Aviation Week). It is being developed under ESA's ARTES 4S programme by Spaceit, CybExer Technologies, CGI Estonia and the CR14 foundation (a NATO DIANA test centre), with the University of Tartu. Context: Russia's 2022 cyberattack on Viasat. [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/defense/sensors-electronic-warfare/estonia-offers-satellite-cybersecurity-test-range), [Spaceit](https://spaceit.eu/services/space-cyber-range/).

**Dcubed** (Germany; release actuators, deployable structures, solar arrays) closed a €27.2m Series A+ (about $30m) led by Poland's Warsaw Equity Group with the EU's EIC Fund and HTGF. It will quadruple production in Germany and the United States and fly its ARAQYS solar array in 2027; it has 87 staff and more than 500 products in space. An EU-funded company is scaling up partly in the US, which fits CEAFE's watch on EU-funded technology moving to the US. [HTGF](https://www.htgf.de/en/dcubed-raises-oversubscribed-27-2-million-round/), [SpaceNews](https://spacenews.com/dcubed-raises-30-million/).

**ICEYE** says processing of its Spot Fine SAR image has fallen from about 35 to about 6 minutes in a year (@iceye_global, [post](https://x.com/i/status/2122963040786075743)).
