articles.headline: Lutnick demanded a 51% US government stake in battery start-up Pure Lithium, using $1 billion of Japan’s investment pledge
articles.summary:
**US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick asked battery start-up Pure Lithium in July to give Washington a 51% controlling stake in exchange for funds to build a manufacturing plant that the company would neither own nor control, Reuters reported on 20 November from documents and a source.**

The plant would have been owned by a special-purpose vehicle controlled by Tokyo and Washington and financed with $1 billion from Japan’s $550 billion investment pledge under its tariff deal; Pure Lithium would only have operated it and received a share of revenue after debt service. Lutnick said the US government needed to control the company so its lithium-metal battery could be used by the US military and other agencies. The company refused (“51% is far outside precedent and invites scrutiny”, its counsel Skadden Arps wrote on 22 August) and Commerce rejected its 9.9% counter-offer. @F_CEAFE reposted the Reuters exclusive at 09:23 and a reply noting that Pure Lithium works with Canada’s E3 Lithium on batteries using Canadian lithium (09:24).

**Takeover ALERT check:** no new acquisition of a European strategic company by a US firm or fund in this window. @F_CEAFE has already posted the Pure Lithium story, so no ALERT. Other deals: KKR (US) negotiating a majority stake in EdgeCore Digital Infrastructure (US data centres) (Bloomberg https://x.com/i/status/2123864009396940978); early takeover interest in UK lender Metro Bank (Bloomberg Deals https://x.com/i/status/2123916845665120457).

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2124056146403016808), [original @Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123992347717329173), [original @Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124056255429849544), [· Reuters via US News](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-20/exclusive-lutnick-asked-battery-startup-pure-lithium-to-accept-us-takeover-documents-and-source-say), [· Investing.com reprint](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exclusivelutnick-asked-battery-startup-pure-lithium-to-accept-us-takeover-documents-and-source-say-5042851)
articles.why: This is US industrial policy by equity: Washington takes control of strategic technology, and an ally (Japan) pays for the factory through a tariff-linked investment pledge. The EU signed its own tariff deal with a US investment pledge. Europe should expect the same leverage on its pledged money, and should note the model: a state that secures control of critical battery technology for its military. The EU has no equivalent instrument at Union level.
articles.watch: Commerce reply; congressional oversight of equity stakes (Intel, MP Materials precedent); use of Japan’s and the EU’s pledges.

articles.headline: Trump threatens a “tremendous tax” on US firms that build AI data centres abroad; “only older chips” for China
articles.summary:
**At his White House press conference on 20 November, President Trump said US companies would not be allowed to build data centres in other countries and that those that do would face “a tremendous tax”.**

He gave no rate, legal basis or date and said he had not yet told his own officials (AP, CNBC, Axios). “Whoever wins SI [super intelligence] wins… We’re not allowing data centers to go into other countries — because China will take…”, he said. On chips for China: “We want only older chips — and we don’t mind if none go”. @F_CEAFE reposted these remarks between 19:32 and 20:48 on Friday, and Al Jazeera and Bloomberg on Saturday framed them together with this week’s chip curbs, which hit data-centre hubs in Malaysia, Singapore and Thailand.

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123847020427284662), [@RapidResponse47](https://x.com/i/status/2123836545346285698), [@RapidResponse47](https://x.com/i/status/2123865998780432419), [@CBSNews](https://x.com/i/status/2123858517777928355), [@CBSNews](https://x.com/i/status/2123863207047578023), [@RapidResponse47](https://x.com/i/status/2123845477829673077), [· @AJEnglish](https://x.com/i/status/2124015156795699309), [· @business](https://x.com/i/status/2124108094783287541), [· @euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2123945122857361820), [· AP](https://apnews.com/article/trump-artificial-intelligence-data-centers-f1ac03b73d13445400eeed8631d9d879), [· CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/20/trump-data-centers-ai-companies-tax.html), [· Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/20/us-ai-trump-data-centers-overseas), [· IBTimes UK](https://www.ibtimes.co.uk/trump-tax-ai-data-centres-abroad-legal-questions-1833720), [· Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/artificial-intelligence/asias-data-center-hotbed-hit-by-us-chip-curbs-as-trump-visits), [· MOFCOM 17 Nov](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/syxwfb/art/2026/art_3a69f2058b724dd39cd8ecddcaa4ab87.html)
articles.why: Microsoft, Amazon, Google, Meta and Oracle are building much of the EU’s AI and cloud capacity. A US penalty on investing abroad, on top of the 16 November BIS remote-access rule that already covers EU data centres, would make Europe’s computing capacity dependent on Washington’s permission and taxes. It is the US double standard: “America First” for its own infrastructure, open markets demanded of others. The lesson is sovereign European compute and cloud, as Spain’s new data-centre rules on digital sovereignty begin to signal.
articles.watch: Any executive order or bill; reactions from Brussels and EU capitals hosting US hyperscaler projects; MOFCOM countermeasures.

articles.headline: OFAC’s “Operation Economic Outcast” targets Iran’s “oil trustees”; Treasury presses Singapore and Malaysia; Tehran speaks of a “silent economic war”
articles.summary:
**On 20 November OFAC designated four Iranians: Mohammad Javad Bavand, a former IRGC intelligence officer, and Majid Taj, accused of recovering Iran’s oil revenue held in third countries (E.O.**

13902), and Mohammadhossein Servati and Mojtaba Arabnejad, linked to the front company Sepehr Energy Jahan Nama Pars and to Mahan Air (E.O. 13224). Treasury says there is “no oil on the water outside of the U.S. military blockade” and that the regime “may never see the revenue from the oil it has already sold” (Bessent). The same day Treasury officials met regulators in Singapore and Malaysia to warn them of the risks of not enforcing US sanctions on Iran; Singapore said it was strengthening safeguards, Malaysia did not respond (Reuters). Reaction: President Pezeshkian said Iran faces a “silent economic war” that is “tougher than a war with missiles” (Al Jazeera, citing Iranian state media). @F_CEAFE reposted the Treasury and Bessent posts (00:18–01:55 Saturday).

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123918858167742844), [@USTreasury](https://x.com/i/status/2123885407938998420), [@USTreasury](https://x.com/i/status/2123920605322121330), [@SecScottBessent](https://x.com/i/status/2123885854716252526), [@SecScottBessent](https://x.com/i/status/2123943226113499252), [@USTreasury](https://x.com/i/status/2123916878296895695), [· @Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123854076022575489), [· @AJEnglish](https://x.com/i/status/2124065050000519666), [· @AJEnglish](https://x.com/i/status/2123950026418475324), [· @AJEnglish](https://x.com/i/status/2124085991480955377), [· Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/news/press-releases/sb0697), [· OFAC](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261120), [· Reuters via FMT](https://www.freemalaysiatoday.com/category/highlight/2026/11/20/us-treasury-presses-singapore-malaysia-on-iran-sanctions-compliance)
articles.why: Treasury states that it works “with partners across the U.S. government, the European Union, United Kingdom, Gulf partners” and has “expanded sanctions exposure for non-U.S. persons”. European banks, shippers and insurers are bound by US secondary sanctions whether or not the EU agrees, the core of the extraterritoriality problem. Bessent also cited a “consensus between the U.S., Russia, and China in Shenzhen” on oil supply, a sign that the great powers are settling energy markets among themselves, with Europe as a price-taker.
articles.watch: Chinese response on teapot refineries; EU position on Iranian oil enforcement; oil prices.

articles.headline: EU finalising “ReadyEU”, a tool to block market access quickly; Beijing warns of “institutionalized protectionism”
articles.summary:
**The EU is finalising a new instrument, working name “ReadyEU”, that would let the European Commission rapidly block selected goods and services from the 450-million-consumer single market, Bloomberg reported on 20 November.**

It could be triggered if a country interferes in EU trade decisions, breaks WTO or trade-agreement rules and refuses to settle, or poses an immediate and serious economic threat. It is part of a package to address the EU’s €360 billion trade deficit with China (2025), including more flexible trade-defence tools and a diversification mechanism for strategic sectors, to be presented on 9 December before the 17–18 December European Council. Reaction: Global Times (Chinese state media), quoting Chinese analysts, says “institutionalized protectionism” will raise costs for European businesses without restoring industrial strength.

**Sources:** [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123926903140602034), [· @globaltimesnews](https://x.com/i/status/2124069971353583774), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123860618583110114), [· Bloomberg via Bloomberg TV Bulgaria](https://www.bloombergtv.bg/a/2-novini/167227-es-e-blizo-do-nov-instrument-za-blokirane-na-dostapa-do-edinniya-pazar), [· Global Times](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202611/1374757.shtml), [· Politico](https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-commission-eyes-rule-change-to-retaliate-faster-against-china/)
articles.why: It answers the CEAFE complaint about Europe’s lack of reciprocity under economic coercion. Politico reports that a qualified majority of EU member states would be needed to block its use, a far lower hurdle than for the never-used Anti-Coercion Instrument. The tool is not country-specific, so it could also apply to US coercion (Greenland threats in January).
articles.watch: 9 December package; MOFCOM reaction; EU–China talks on chemicals and machinery (January, March).

articles.headline: Europe’s second energy crisis reaches the power market: steel mills stop at peak hours
articles.summary:
**Bloomberg (21 November) reports that Europe’s second major energy crisis in under five years is taking hold in wholesale electricity: power for each of the next three months trades around €200/MWh, roughly double last winter, because European gas prices have tripled year-on-year as the Middle East war tightened global supply.**

A German steel mill owned by Italy’s Feralpi halts production at expensive hours despite full order books. Two German suppliers, Grüüün and Stromee, stopped delivering power; Austria’s Verbund took a €120 million hit and Spain’s Acerinox €16 million in one quarter. In a severe scenario monthly contracts could reach €300/MWh (BB Energy).

**Sources:** [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2124067828487598317), [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123949571457888570), [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123845110869700796), [· @euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2123911510884041197), [· Bloomberg via Energy Connects](https://www.energyconnects.com/news/utilities/2026/november/europe-s-power-market-is-flashing-a-warning-to-its-economy/)
articles.why: The CEAFE energy line: high gas prices are pushing energy-intensive industry towards stoppages and relocation, while Europe has swapped dependence on Russian gas for dependence on US LNG (P-TEC, 18 Nov). Germany is preparing to bring coal and oil plants back from reserve.
articles.watch: TTF and power forwards next week; German grid-reserve law; ECB 17 December meeting.

articles.headline: Mercedes-Benz nearly caught by a US ban on Chinese cars because of its Chinese shareholders
articles.summary:
**US lawmakers are close to a deal on a bill to ban Chinese cars from the US market, after last-minute talks aimed partly at sparing Mercedes-Benz, which is nearly 20% owned by Chinese entities, above a proposed 15% threshold (Bloomberg Law, WSJ).**

The fix under negotiation exempts passive Chinese stakes without voting power. Sponsors from auto-producing states want a bill on Trump’s desk by year-end.

**Sources:** [@WSJ](https://x.com/i/status/2123940249432739868), [· Bloomberg Law](https://news.bloomberglaw.com/international-trade/us-lawmakers-near-deal-to-ban-chinese-cars-in-lame-duck-session)
articles.why: A European champion’s access to the US market depends on Congress drafting a carve-out, showing how US–China rivalry is turned into rules on European companies’ shareholder registers. It also shows the risk of Chinese stakes in strategic European firms.
articles.watch: Final text; Daimler Truck, BMW and supplier exposure; German government reaction.

articles.headline: US trade deals tied to energy purchases: Thailand, the Philippines, Mexico
articles.summary:
**Trump announced trade deals with Thailand (eliminating tariffs on 99% of US exports and buying an additional $2.6 billion of US farm goods) and the Philippines, and said a deal with Mexico is close while talks with Canada lag (Bloomberg).**

Recounting his talk with Philippine President Marcos: “Where do you buy your energy?” “From the Middle East.” “Not anymore, you don’t. You’re going to buy 100% of your energy…” from the US. @F_CEAFE reposted both clips (20:38–20:45 Friday).

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123863584178622840), [@RapidResponse47](https://x.com/i/status/2123837956054261930), [@RapidResponse47](https://x.com/i/status/2123865421493207425), [@clashreport](https://x.com/i/status/2123836288260268278), [· @business](https://x.com/i/status/2123892929643094283)
articles.why: The same pattern as P-TEC in Warsaw: US trade deals packaged with energy purchases, making allies dependent on a single supplier. US double standard: demands open markets and energy purchases while restricting its own firms’ investment abroad (topic 2).
articles.watch: Published texts of the agreements; Mexico deal and USMCA review.

SK hynix (South Korea) becomes the top shareholder of Japan’s Kioxia (NAND memory) as US fund Bain exits

Markets and war risk: Warsaw falls 4.5%, Europe’s worst session, after Russian missiles and a drone enter Polish airspace

articles.headline: Update: Senator Cotton says Commerce Secretary Lutnick repeatedly ignored warnings that Nvidia AI chips were being smuggled to China
articles.summary:
**Republican Senator Tom Cotton told the Wall Street Journal (20 November) that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick repeatedly ignored warnings that US AI chips were being smuggled to China before the recent Nvidia scandal became public.**

Cotton stopped short of calling for his resignation but withheld his support: “If Howard Lutnick wanted my support, maybe he should have answered my many letters warning about these Chinese Communist Party shell companies…” (WSJ via Reuters). Cotton’s published letters to Lutnick (13 October 2025 and 20 March 2026) flagged Megaspeed, a Singapore-based spin-off of Chinese state-owned cloud firm 7Road, which imported over $4.6 billion of Nvidia hardware routed through Malaysia and Singapore, and the Super Micro smuggling indictment.

**Sources:** [@WSJ](https://x.com/i/status/2123838285248164000), [@WSJ](https://www.boursorama.com/bourse/actualites/le-senateur-republicain-tom-cotton-affirme-que-lutnick-a-ignore-ses-mises-en-garde-concernant-les-puces-destinees-a-la-chine-rapporte-le-wsj-67fb2ff5f64847590588820091e40e43), [· Cotton letters](https://www.cotton.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/media/doc/101325lutnickletter.pdf), [· Cotton letters](https://www.cotton.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/media/doc/32026chipsletter.pdf), [· Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/11/11/trump-lutnick-nvidia-china-chip-export-controls), [· CBS News](https://www.cbsnews.com/news/lutnick-nvidia-ai-chips-china/)
articles.why: The same Commerce Department that this week extended US licensing to data centres in third countries, the EU included (BIS remote-access rule, 16 Nov), is accused at home of not enforcing the rules against diversion through US firms’ own channels. Europe’s cloud operators bear the compliance burden of an extraterritorial regime that Washington applies selectively. This is the double standard of the editorial line. Any enforcement shake-up at Commerce (Lutnick, Under Secretary Kessler) will decide how hard the rules bite on allies.
articles.watch: Commerce/BIS reply; whether the long-delayed Megaspeed controls are published; Chip Security Act.

articles.headline: Update: China answers the House aerospace report: “politicising normal business”
articles.summary:
**Reaction to the House Select Committee report “China’s wingmen” (topic 1 at 14:30).**

Global Times (Chinese state media), quoting Chinese experts, says the calls to deny FAA certification to Chinese-built aircraft and to pull contracts from foreign defence contractors that keep investing in China’s aerospace sector “reflect a growing trend toward politicizing normal business”. It says the proposals stretch national-security claims, disrupt global aviation supply chains and reflect a Cold War mindset, and that Boeing and Airbus investments in China involve non-critical civil technology. @F_CEAFE reposted the Global Times post at 13:48.

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123760310716973464), [original @globaltimesnews](https://x.com/i/status/2123704916145500419), [· Global Times](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202611/1374718.shtml), [· AeroTime](https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/us-lawmakers-airbus-contracts-china-ties), [· MFA briefing 20 Nov](https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/mfa_eng/xw/fyrbt/202611/t20261120_12064156.html)
articles.why: Airbus, with its Tianjin final assembly line, and French suppliers sit between the two. Washington threatens US contracts and a presumption of denial for French takeovers, while Beijing frames any withdrawal as politicisation. So far the only official-sounding reply is Chinese state media; no MOFCOM or MFA statement was found (MFA briefing of 20 Nov did not address it), and no response from Paris, Brussels or Airbus.
articles.watch: MOFCOM/MFA response next week; Airbus and French government position.

articles.headline: SK hynix (South Korea) becomes the top shareholder of Japan’s Kioxia (NAND memory) as US fund Bain exits
articles.summary:
**On 20 November SK hynix disclosed that it will convert ¥129 billion (about $810 million) of convertible bonds issued by BCPE Pangea Cayman2 (SPC2), the Bain-led vehicle created in 2018 to buy Toshiba’s memory business, into 129,000 common shares, and buy the remaining 1,001 SPC2 shares from a Bain Capital affiliate for ¥100 million.**

After completion, scheduled for 4 December, SK hynix will own 100% of SPC2 and an indirect stake of about 14.1% in Kioxia Holdings, ahead of Toshiba (10.46%). SK hynix says it has no plan to buy more Kioxia shares or to expand its role in management.

**Sources:** [@ReutersTech](https://x.com/i/status/2123765854210805825), [@ReutersTech](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2120882/000119312526469266/d79768d6k.htm), [· Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261120005051320), [· Reuters via CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/business/sk-hynix-become-top-shareholder-in-rival-kioxia-after-bond-conversion-6569061), [· Nikkei Asia](https://asia.nikkei.com/business/markets/bonds/sk-hynix-to-become-kioxia-s-top-shareholder-with-bond-conversion)
articles.why: NAND flash is a core input for AI data centres, and its ownership is consolidating among Asian producers: SK hynix is No. 2 in NAND (19% share), Kioxia No. 4 (14%) (Counterpoint, via Reuters). Europe has no memory-chip maker of its own, so it depends on Korea, Japan, the US (Micron) and increasingly China for a strategic input. Not an ALERT case (no European target, no US buyer); the US element is Bain Capital’s exit.
articles.watch: Japanese government (METI) view of a Korean rival as top shareholder; closing on 4 December.

articles.headline: Takeovers, the other direction: Italy’s Bending Spoons buys Mailchimp from Intuit for $3.68 billion
articles.summary:
**Intuit (US) agreed on 19–20 November to sell its email-marketing platform Mailchimp to Bending Spoons (Milan) for an enterprise value of $3.68 billion: $3.31 billion in cash plus $368 million that Intuit will reinvest in newly issued Bending Spoons shares.**

Closing is expected in early 2027, subject to regulatory approval. Bending Spoons, owner of WeTransfer, Vimeo, Evernote and Eventbrite, keeps buying US consumer software.

**Sources:** [Intuit](https://investors.intuit.com/news-events/press-releases/detail/1331/intuit-reports-first-quarter-results-and-enters-agreement-to-sell-mailchimp-to-bending-spoons), [· Bending Spoons](https://investors.bendingspoons.com/newsroom/bending-spoons-to-acquire-mailchimp), [· SEC 6-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/2004711/000200471126000026/bsp-20261119x6k.htm), [· TechCrunch](https://techcrunch.com/2026/11/20/bending-spoons-buys-mailchimp-for-3-68-billion/), [· TechCrunch](https://x.com/i/status/2123826239521587396)
articles.why: It is a rare case of a European buyer of a US tech asset, the reverse of the usual flow in which US groups buy European firms. It is not strategic infrastructure (cloud, chips, defence), so it does little to reduce Europe’s dependence on US digital platforms. Also in the window: Bloomberg on Sanofi’s pursuit of US-based Insmed, the biggest pharma takeover in years (thread from 17 Nov), another French buyer of a US company.

articles.headline: Energy security — Update: Brussels puts military fuel needs into the EU emergency oil-stock rules
articles.summary:
**Update to the oil-stocks overhaul (08:30 topic 4).**

A draft Commission document seen by Euronews (20 November) would require member states to factor armed-forces demand, including sudden surges and simultaneous civilian and military pressure, into national oil-security risk assessments. They would also have to check whether refineries, ports, pipelines and distribution networks could withstand major disruptions, and report refinery closures and investments. Armed forces could tap emergency stocks temporarily in exceptional cases, and stock composition would have to reflect national use of diesel, jet fuel and other products (Bloomberg via Quartz). The Commission aims to adopt it in early December.

**Sources:** [@euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2123770300555010093), [· Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/20/brussels-puts-military-fuel-needs-at-heart-of-new-oil-security-strategy), [· Euronews](https://qz.com/eu-oil-reserve-rules-emergency-stocks-fuel-use-111926), [· Yahoo Finance](https://finance.yahoo.com/energy/articles/eu-moves-overhaul-emergency-oil-193000476.html)
articles.why: In a 2025 Commission impact assessment, 61.54% of EU countries reported trouble securing fuel for armed forces moving across the continent, a major hurdle for the 2030 military-readiness goal (Euronews). Europe imports most of its crude and, increasingly, refined diesel and jet fuel, while refinery closures continue; military mobility depends on that supply chain. It links the energy-dependence and defence-readiness threads.
articles.watch: Formal proposal in early December; position of refining countries.

articles.headline: Markets and war risk: Warsaw falls 4.5%, Europe’s worst session, after Russian missiles and a drone enter Polish airspace
articles.summary:
**Poland’s WIG20 fell 4.48% to 4,016.30 on 20 November, the worst performance among Europe’s markets, after Russian missiles and a jet-powered drone entered Polish airspace and crashed in the east of the country.**

Banks and insurer PZU led the fall (PKO BP about -6.4% intraday). The zloty weakened, with the Swiss franc above 4.83 zł and the dollar at 4.06 zł (Bloomberg; mybank.pl; TVP Info).

**Sources:** [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123833795321155808), [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123785723786498254), [@business](https://mybank.pl/news/35907-wig20-traci-4-48-frank-przebija-4-83-zl-dolar-po-4-06-zl-skad-ta-wyprzedaz.html), [@business](https://www.tvp.info/96589772/gpw-inwestorzy-masowo-wyprzedaja-akcje-wig20-znizkuje-o-ponad-4-proc-najslabsze-banki-pko-bp-znizkuje-o-64-proc)
articles.why: The war risk is now priced in on the eastern flank. Poland, NATO’s biggest defence spender relative to GDP, sees capital leave on each incursion, and its banks and insurers bear the brunt. Investor confidence in the EU’s frontline economies depends on a credible common European defence and air-defence umbrella, which no single member state can provide alone. Bloomberg also notes that the AI-driven sell-off (14:30 topic 4) is following patterns seen before the dotcom crash.
articles.watch: Polish market on Monday; NATO and EU response.

The AI sell-off spreads: global stocks post their longest losing run since September 2023

Energy dependence: Russian LNG still reaches the EU while Türkiye signs a new Novatek supply contract

articles.headline: US House China Committee: no FAA certification for Chinese aircraft, curbs on investment in Chinese aerospace, and “heightened scrutiny” of French takeovers of US aerospace firms
articles.summary:
**The House Select Committee on the CCP (chair John Moolenaar) published on 19 November a year-long investigation, “China’s wingmen: How Western government policy enabled China’s rise in the skies”.**

It says American and European aerospace contractors transferred technology and know-how to Chinese aerospace firms through joint ventures and licences that ended up helping China’s military air power. It recommends that the Treasury restrict outbound investment in China’s aerospace sector (and that Congress write this into the COINS Act), that the FAA refuse to certify Chinese-built aircraft, that federal contracts be pulled from contractors (Reuters names Airbus) that keep investing in China’s aerospace base, and that acquisitions of US aerospace companies by French firms face “heightened scrutiny and a presumption of denial” until they unwind ties with China’s civil-military ecosystem. @F_CEAFE posted the story at 08:10.

**Sources:** [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/2123675385913319706), [· House Select Committee on China](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/reports/investigation-details-how-western-government-policy-enabled-china-s-rise-in-the-skies), [· House Select Committee on China](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exclusiveus-should-not-certify-chinese-aircraft-restrict-investments-in-chinas-aerospace-sector-lawmakers-say-5039601), [· The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/world/united-states/us-should-not-certify-chinese-aircraft-restrict-investments-in-chinas-aerospace-sector-lawmakers-say), [· The Straits Times](https://insidetrade.com/daily-news/house-panel-calls-extensive-restrictions-chinas-aerospace-sector)
articles.why: This is an explicit proposal to use US contracts, investment screening (CFIUS) and certification as levers over a European company and a European state. Airbus, Europe’s main aerospace champion, competes with Boeing in China (COMAC is the future third competitor), and the report singles out France: French aerospace firms are said to have “much stronger ties to the Chinese aerospace industrial base than American companies”, and to market themselves as “beyond the reach of US restrictions” (e.g. Airbus selling satellite imagery without US restrictions). If adopted, French buyers of US aerospace assets would face a presumption of denial, while US buyers of European firms face no such test in Europe. It fits the US double standard and Europe’s lack of reciprocity described in the editorial line. Once again, a single European state (France) is singled out alone, and only a common EU response on investment screening would carry comparable weight.
articles.watch: Airbus and French government reaction; whether the Treasury extends the Outbound Investment Security Program to aerospace; China’s MOFCOM/MFA response (none found in the 20 November MFA briefing).

articles.headline: Update: US chip curbs bite in China: Alibaba may cut its 20 GW computing goal, Chinese AI start-ups slump, TSMC suspends some Chinese orders
articles.summary:
**Reuters (20 November) reports that the series of US measures this week, including the BIS remote-access rule, Nvidia’s halt of some shipments to China and a US proposal requiring American companies to disclose use of Chinese AI models, “further pummelled” Chinese tech stocks.**

Alibaba CEO Eddie Wu said the rule will affect its products next year, could force it to lower its long-term target of 20 gigawatts of computing capacity, and that cloud revenue growth may slow to 30–45% next year from 53%. Tencent President Martin Lau said the curbs will slow its next-generation model and accelerate the shift to domestic chips. Z.AI has fallen 22% and MiniMax 34% in two weeks; Iluvatar CoreX (ByteDance supplier) fell 17%. TSMC suspended some previously permitted advanced orders from Chinese customers after the new licensing requirement on overseas data centres.

**Sources:** [@Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123743208446267802), [@Reuters](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-20/us-ai-chip-curbs-hit-china-tech-stocks-spur-self-sufficiency-push), [@Reuters](https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/stocks-suffer-worst-run-since-2023%2C-havens-gain%3A-markets-wrap/92410554), [· MFA press conference 20 Nov](https://www.fmprc.gov.cn/mfa_eng/xw/fyrbt/202611/t20261120_12064156.html)
articles.why: The rule covers data centres in third countries, including the EU, so European cloud operators serving Chinese clients are now inside a US licensing regime. The fact that a US rule decides what a Taiwanese foundry and a European data centre may do is the core of the extraterritorial-controls thread. China’s answer is to speed up self-sufficiency, which over time shrinks the market for European chip-tool makers such as ASML. Europe pays the cost of a contest between two powers in which it has neither a seat nor a vote.
articles.watch: MOFCOM response; whether EU data-centre operators seek licences.

articles.headline: Export controls, the other way: China’s licence requirement for drone engines and parts is now in force; Kyiv welcomes it, Russia’s Shahed supply chain is the target
articles.summary:
**Since 18 November Chinese exporters need a MOFCOM dual-use licence for a list of drone items: autopilots, drones with 30+ minutes’ endurance, engines above 16 kW, turbojets with thrust of 400 N or more, high-power radio modules, heavy brushless motors (≥48 V, ≥3 kW), speed controllers, large carbon-fibre propeller blades and related software and technology (MOFCOM, MAC and CMC Equipment Development Department Announcement No.**

49 of 2026, issued 19 October). Some of the engines covered are used in the Shahed/Geran drones Russia assembles at Alabuga. Ukraine’s sanctions commissioner Vladyslav Vlasiuk thanked China but said anti-jamming antennas, navigation modules, gimbal cameras and servos remain outside the controls (“only part of what matters… but it is a start”). @F_CEAFE reposted the Kyiv Independent report at 08:34.

**Sources:** [of @KyivIndependent](https://x.com/i/status/2123681258433622481), [original](https://x.com/i/status/2123502594156871891), [original](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/zcfb/blgg/art/2026/art_0d3312d7762d486bb4a7626e85b9dbed.html), [original](https://english.mofcom.gov.cn/News/SpokesmansRemarks/art/2026/art_3522f2c8fa074f34a6644192642228b9.html), [· Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/china-tightens-export-controls-on-components-for-russian-drones/), [· The Moscow Times](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/19/china-tightens-export-controls-on-drone-parts-used-by-russia-a94318)
articles.why: The measure took effect the day Putin arrived in Shenzhen for the trilateral meeting with Trump and Xi; Beijing used its own export-control law, not a Western sanctions regime. Europe, which sanctions Chinese firms for supplying Russia, now depends on a decision in Beijing for the volume of drones hitting Ukraine’s (and Europe’s largest) energy infrastructure. MOFCOM frames it as non-proliferation and “dynamic adjustment”, and says compliant licence applications will be approved. A reminder that the levers over the war’s supply chains are in Washington and Beijing, not in Brussels.
articles.watch: Licence approval data; whether the EU adjusts its listings of Chinese suppliers.

articles.headline: The AI sell-off spreads: global stocks post their longest losing run since September 2023
articles.summary:
**The MSCI All Country World Index fell 0.7% on 20 November, its seventh straight drop and the longest run since September 2023, as the AI trade unwinds (Bloomberg).**

Anthropic fell nearly 6% in early trading, partly reversing its 17% first-day gain. The Stoxx Europe 600 fell 1.1% by late morning (more than 430 members down, technology leading), a fifth daily fall; MSCI Asia Pacific -3.3%, heading for its worst week since the start of the pandemic; Australian equities had their worst week in more than four years. Investors bought bonds: the German 10-year yield fell 8 bp to 3.33%, the US 10-year 6 bp to 4.99%. The dollar is near a 19-month high, set for a fourth weekly gain; the yen led G10 currencies.

articles.why: The AI sell-off is being imported into Europe through tech stocks, while the financing side shows the asymmetry: SpaceX sold $32 billion of debt in a day to buy AI chips (part at yields above 8%), whereas Europe’s annual bond sales, above €2 trillion for the first time this year (2026), are driven mainly by government borrowing. A strong dollar and a near-certain Fed hike in December (two more priced for 2027) tighten conditions for European importers of US energy and arms paid in dollars.
articles.watch: US close tonight; Fed 9 December; ECB December meeting.

articles.headline: Update: Commerzbank raises its profit outlook as UniCredit’s takeover nears
articles.summary:
**Commerzbank CEO Bettina Orlopp said on 20 November the bank now “clearly” expects €3.5 billion of net profit in 2026, above the previous “at least €3.4 billion”.**

In her first remarks since this week’s agreement between Berlin and UniCredit, she welcomed the clarity on the Frankfurt headquarters and the stock-market listing; UniCredit CEO Andrea Orcel had given Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil eight binding commitments (listing kept in Frankfurt, key decisions taken in Germany, expansion of the Mittelstand business) (Reuters; Reuters German service via onvista).

**Sources:** [@ReutersBiz](https://x.com/i/status/2123744471443509459), [@ReutersBiz](https://money.usnews.com/investing/news/articles/2026-11-20/commerzbank-ceo-raises-2026-profit-outlook-as-unicredit-takeover-nears), [· RTÉ](https://www.rte.ie/news/business/2026/1120/1600004-commerzbank-ceo-on-unicredit-deal/), [· RTÉ](https://www.onvista.de/news/2026/11-20-commerzbank-chefin-sieht-klarheit-fuer-ihr-institut-bei-unicredit-0-20-26578823), [· Mr Price](https://x.com/i/status/2123685308201898407), [· Mr Price](https://x.com/i/status/2123738181723902050)
articles.why: An Italian–German bank merger is the kind of intra-European consolidation the editorial line sees as positive: scale in banking union rather than US banks or funds taking European lenders. The open question is UniCredit’s plan to cut Commerzbank’s international network, which serves German exporters.

articles.headline: Energy dependence: Russian LNG still reaches the EU while Türkiye signs a new Novatek supply contract
articles.summary:
**Bloomberg (20 November) notes that, despite the EU’s drive to wean itself off Russian energy since 2022, Russian LNG is still entering the bloc ahead of a full ban.**

Russia’s Novatek said on 18 November it had signed an LNG supply contract with Türkiye and is discussing larger volumes and gas investments; buyer, volume, price and start date were not disclosed (TASS, RIA, Anadolu — Russian state media, attributed). @F_CEAFE reposted Turkish analyst Gizem Özpinar’s comparison: non-EU Türkiye signs with Novatek for its own energy security while EU member Greece is criticised for its choices (her framing).

**Sources:** [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123682794853319005), [· @euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2123735639749239291), [· of @zgizemozpinar](https://x.com/i/status/2123695400133722410), [original](https://x.com/i/status/2123507335314198542), [original](https://www.aa.com.tr/tr/enerjiterminali/lng-lpg/rus-enerji-sirketi-novatek-turkiyede-dogal-gaz-yatirimlarini-gorusuyor/61097), [original](https://tass.com/economy/2220487), [original](https://x.com/i/status/2123724947524608144)
articles.why: Europe is replacing Russian gas with US LNG at prices well above US levels (the 11x gap covered on 18 November), while neighbours such as Türkiye keep buying Russian supply and can resell energy and industrial goods into the EU. Iran is also readying a tanker convoy at Kharg Island to test the US oil blockade (Euronews); any incident there would hit Brent, still near $90. Dependence has changed supplier, not nature.
articles.watch: EU timetable for the full Russian LNG ban; Kharg convoy.

articles.headline: Update: Anthropic touches $2 trillion on its Nasdaq debut, closes at about $1.75 trillion, and Wall Street falls more than 2%
articles.summary:
**Anthropic, the US developer of the Claude models, began trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT on 19 November.**

The shares opened at $111.50, 34% above the $83 offer price, and rose as high as $115 (+38.6%), which briefly gave the company a fully diluted market value of about $2 trillion (PitchBook, AP, The National; Reuters via Investing.com). The rally faded: the stock closed at $97.17, up 17.1%, which values Anthropic at about $1.75 trillion on a fully diluted basis (The National, citing PitchBook) or about $1.27 trillion on the shares now outstanding (Yahoo Finance); the BBC gives about $1.76 trillion. **Verified figure: the $2 trillion valuation was reached intraday, at the open, not at the close.** The IPO raised $81.3 billion (980 million shares at $83), plus a $26 billion private placement, for a total of $107.3 billion, the largest offering on record, ahead of SpaceX’s $86 billion in June. The debut did not lift the market: all three US indices fell more than 2%, the S&P 500 lost for a sixth straight session and chip stocks fell, led by AMD (-7.7%) after a short seller alleged China export-control exposure.

The US is expected to put $450 billion into start-ups this year; Europe hosts 7% of world computing capacity against 72% in the US, and only seven European tech companies listed in 2026 up to 20 October (Atomico). US capital markets, not European ones, set the price of frontier AI, and European savings ($50 trillion, of which about 0.01% goes to European venture capital, Atomico) flow to it. Dependence on US AI models is now also dependence on a $1.75 trillion listed company subject to US law.
articles.watch: Second-day trading and the 30-day over-allotment option (147 million shares); lock-up expiries around the first earnings reports (PitchBook expects 2027 to test the price); whether the AI sell-off spreads to European chip and AI stocks (ASML, Infineon, STMicro) at today’s open. Earlier coverage: 2026-11-19_0730 topic 3 (pricing), 2026-11-19_2030 “Briefly noted”.

articles.headline: Washington licensed 879,868 Nvidia and AMD AI chips for Chinese firms, including Pentagon-listed “Chinese military companies”
articles.summary:
**House Foreign Affairs Committee chairman Brian Mast used his powers under the Export Control Reform Act on 19 November to publish BIS licence data for Nvidia H200 and AMD MI325X chips to China.**

As of 11 May 2026 the Commerce Department’s Bureau of Industry and Security had received applications for 3,444,160 chips for Chinese companies and approved 879,868 across 21 applications (about 579,868 Nvidia and 300,000 AMD), including 75,000 for Alibaba, 150,000 for Tencent and its subsidiaries, 43,000 for Baidu and 4,000 for BYD, all on the Pentagon’s 1260H list of Chinese military companies (committee summary). All approved rows are marked “Approved, not shipped”, so the data do not show deliveries (Edit USA analysis of the tables). The committee says Nvidia named possible diversion fronts as installers and that every application rated diversion risk “low”; Nvidia’s Jensen Huang will be interviewed on 1–2 December. Bloomberg reports California has opened an investigation into whether Nvidia chips or confidential information were improperly obtained by China.

**Sources:** [@ReutersTech](https://x.com/i/status/2123598901319962651), [· @Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123575840797524453), [· @ReutersBiz](https://x.com/i/status/2123598881455841571), [· @AJEnglish](https://x.com/i/status/2123597199095529605), [· @FT](https://x.com/i/status/2123581451853549724), [· @FT](https://x.com/i/status/2123616719381930080), [· @business](https://x.com/i/status/2123583386753122669), [· @business](https://x.com/i/status/2123593470073856009), [· HFAC press release](https://foreignaffairs.house.gov/news/press-releases/chairman-brian-mast-exercises-legislative-authority-to-publicly-release-ai-chip-license-information-for-china), [· HFAC press release](https://democrats-foreignaffairs.house.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/11.19.26-ECRA-Information-Disclosure-HFAC-Summary.pdf), [· HFAC press release](https://democrats-foreignaffairs.house.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/11.19.26-ECRA-Information-Disclosure-of-BIS-License-Decisions.pdf), [· CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/amp/2026/11/19/nvidia-amd-china-chip-sales-congress.html), [· Edit USA](https://www.editusa.com/intelligence/house-releases-879-868-ai-chip-approvals-for-china-what-the-records-show)
articles.why: This is the other face of the rule that took effect on 19 November (topic 1 of the 20:30 edition): Washington forces TSMC, Samsung and European intermediaries to cut Chinese designers off while licensing its own champions’ sales to Chinese firms it itself labels military companies. US export controls are an industrial policy that protects US market share, not only a security tool; Europe aligns (ASML’s China sales, the data-centre due diligence) without getting comparable exemptions. Equivalent European rules and a common EU export-control voice remain absent.
articles.watch: MFA/MOFCOM reaction; Huang interviews 1–2 December; whether Commerce revokes approvals for 1260H firms; link to AMD’s Hunterbrook allegations (topic 1).

articles.headline: Update: Methane rules delayed two years after US pressure; US LNG exporters restart long-term deals with Europe
articles.summary:
**The Council and the European Parliament agreed on 19 November to postpone the methane regulation’s monitoring, reporting and verification obligations for imported gas, oil and coal from 1 January 2027 to 1 January 2029, and methane-intensity reporting from August 2028 to August 2030 (Council of the EU; covered as a provisional deal in the 14:30 edition).**

Politico reports the delay followed months of lobbying by Washington and fossil-fuel companies, and that an amendment to keep the rules for Russian imports was dropped. US exporters had told their commercial teams to pause long-term contracts with European buyers for fear of a 20% non-compliance penalty; the Center for LNG’s Charlie Riedl told Reuters at P-TEC in Warsaw that the delay “helps make the case” to sign. At P-TEC US firms signed agreements or memoranda with Montenegro, Albania, Hungary’s 4iG and Poland’s Orlen, and are finalising a long-term deal to supply 20% of the Czech Republic’s LNG consumption (Reuters).

**Sources:** [@Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123559501945065628), [@Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123496624617836885), [· Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/19/methane-regulation-eu-agrees-targeted-amendment-to-safeguard-security-of-supply/), [· Council of the EU](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/us-gas-exporters-more-comfortable-144449548.html), [· Politico Europe](https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-extends-delay-of-key-methane-rules-to-two-years-after-us-pressure/)
articles.why: An EU environmental rule was softened under pressure from the supplier that now dominates EU LNG imports, which then rewards Europe with long-term contracts that lock in dependence. Russia has been replaced by a single new supplier, at gas prices about 11 times higher than in the US (Burgum chart, 18 November LEAD).
articles.watch: Signature of the Czech long-term LNG contract; Parliament plenary vote; whether TTF stays near €90/MWh.

articles.headline: EU to overhaul emergency oil stocks after the Hormuz shock; tanker attacks intensify
articles.summary:
**Bloomberg reports the European Commission plans to revise the Oil Stocks Directive to avoid shortages of diesel and kerosene, after the Middle East war exposed the bloc’s dependence on imported refined products.**

According to reports of the draft, emergency reserves would be tied to each member state’s actual fuel use and refining capacity, at least one third would have to be held as refined products rather than crude, and armed forces could get limited, temporary access in exceptional cases; approval is expected in early December (Quartz; OilPrice). The Japan Times reports Iran’s attacks on tankers crossing the Strait of Hormuz are intensifying even as oil prices fall, and Euronews quotes the IEA warning that the longer the disruption lasts the harder recovery will be for global energy markets.

**Sources:** [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123536926661632279), [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123554458307055651), [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123502873493258289), [· @japantimes](https://x.com/i/status/2123624252024734092), [· @euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2123553892160122950), [· Quartz](https://qz.com/eu-oil-reserve-rules-emergency-stocks-fuel-use-111926), [· OilPrice](https://oilprice.com/Latest-Energy-News/World-News/EU-Moves-to-Overhaul-Emergency-Oil-Stockpiles.html)
articles.why: Europe imports most of its diesel and jet fuel; holding stocks in crude does not help when refining capacity has closed. Military access to fuel stocks links energy policy to defence readiness, a European competence still being built.
articles.watch: Commission proposal in early December; Hormuz shipping incidents (Conflicts section).

articles.headline: BP weighs selling its 56% stake in the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim LNG plant off Senegal and Mauritania
articles.summary:
**Bloomberg reports BP is considering divesting its majority stake and operatorship of the Greater Tortue Ahmeyim (GTA) floating LNG project on the Senegal–Mauritania maritime border, as chief executive Meg O’Neill streamlines the portfolio.**

The $4.8 billion plant needs more investment to expand; a sale is uncertain given limited buyers and cross-border political sensitivities (Bloomberg, via Investing.com and TipRanks). No buyer or price has been reported.

**Sources:** [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123519226497364068), [· Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/bp-weighs-divesting-west-africa-lng-stake-to-streamline-portfolio-bloomberg-says-5039717), [· TipRanks](https://www.tipranks.com/news/the-fly/bp-considers-selling-majority-stake-in-west-africa-lng-facility-bloomberg-says-thefly-news)
articles.why: GTA is one of the few non-US, non-Russian LNG sources close to Europe. If a European major exits, the buyer’s nationality (US, Gulf or Chinese) will decide who controls Atlantic LNG that could reduce Europe’s single-supplier dependence on the US.
articles.watch: Bidders; any CFIUS-style screening angle if a non-European buyer emerges.

articles.headline: Rates turn hawkish worldwide as the AI trade unwinds
articles.summary:
**Overnight, Japan’s core inflation accelerated in October, cementing expectations of a Bank of Japan rate rise (Reuters).**

J.P. Morgan now expects the Federal Reserve to raise rates at each of its next three meetings as inflation persists (Reuters), and Chicago Fed president Austan Goolsbee warned the AI investment surge could strain US capacity and overheat the economy (Reuters). In Europe, ECB Governing Council member Fabio Panetta said inflation must not become entrenched without undue harm to growth, and Bank of England policymaker Megan Greene said rates have not done enough to curb inflation (Bloomberg). The FT reports oil is losing its grip on bond markets as inflation spreads more broadly; gold is heading for its biggest weekly fall since March and Seoul faces record foreign outflows despite record profits (“Sell Korea”, Reuters).

**Sources:** [@ReutersBiz](https://x.com/i/status/2123638771132297289), [· @Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123549420205605302), [· @Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123597386190586253), [· @business](https://x.com/i/status/2123549415134597388), [· @business](https://x.com/i/status/2123573320046010465), [· @business](https://x.com/i/status/2123617371269074995), [· @FT](https://x.com/i/status/2123647848163992001), [· @ReutersTech](https://x.com/i/status/2123584664254271699), [image](https://pbs.twimg.com/news_img/2123584666644979713/aO0ucfBa?format=jpg&name=orig)
articles.why: Higher US rates with an AI sell-off pull capital back to the dollar and raise borrowing costs for European defence and energy investment just as Europe needs to finance both.
articles.watch: ECB and Fed December meetings; euro-dollar.

France’s Sanofi weighs a takeover of US drugmaker Insmed worth more than $30 billion

articles.headline: Update: the US chip rule takes effect and TSMC and Samsung cut off Chinese chip designers
articles.summary:
**The Commerce Department’s interim final rule on remote access to advanced semiconductors was published in the Federal Register and took effect on 19 November.**

Reuters reports, citing two people familiar with the matter, that TSMC has told staff to halt affected orders from Chinese chip designers on processes of 16 nanometres and below unless the customer obtains a US export licence, generally limiting them to 28 nm and 40 nm chips without high-bandwidth memory or advanced packaging. The Financial Times reports (via StockAnalysis) that TSMC and Samsung have also paused some shipments to Chinese customers, including smartphone-chip clients, while licence applications are pending. The rule removes the verification route that let foundries and packagers ship Chinese-designed chips judged to fall outside US controls; now any advanced chip designed by a company headquartered in China is presumed controlled unless the designer is on a US-approved list, which includes Nvidia, AMD, Apple, MediaTek and Realtek but no mainland Chinese firm. TSMC’s guidance also requires checks on ownership, packaging providers and shipping routes, extending to orders placed through subsidiaries or intermediaries in Taiwan, the US, Europe, Japan and Southeast Asia.

**Sources:** [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123439953979830412), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123441680552428011), [·](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/19/2026-23529/addressing-remote-access-to-advanced-semiconductors), [·](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/tsmc-tightens-china-ai-chip-curbs-as-new-us-rules-close-manufacturing-loophole-sources-say-5038806), [·](https://stockanalysis.com/news/tsmc-samsung-suspend-chip-shipments-china/), [·](https://www.bis.gov/press-release/bis-issues-rule-addressing-remote-access-american-super-intelligence-technology), [·](https://www.mofcom.gov.cn/syxwfb/art/2026/art_3a69f2058b724dd39cd8ecddcaa4ab87.html)
articles.why: A US national rule now decides what a Taiwanese and a Korean foundry may make for Chinese customers anywhere, including orders routed through European subsidiaries. European data centres and chip intermediaries must run the same due diligence on Chinese ownership. The rule also adds licence requirements for Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Thailand and Brazil and threatens “import restrictions” and a downgraded export-control status for countries that “tolerate evasion”. The EU had no say in it and will have to comply. China has already said it will take countermeasures (MOFCOM, 17–18 November, covered on 17 November).
articles.watch: Licence decisions for Chinese designers; whether MOFCOM announces concrete countermeasures; ASML and other European suppliers’ guidance; the EU’s reaction (if any) to the extraterritorial reach of the rule.

articles.headline: Two investigations show US chips still reaching blacklisted Chinese buyers, and AMD shares fall
articles.summary:
**Short-seller-affiliated Hunterbrook Media published “AMD Has Its Own China Problem” on 19 November, disclosing that Hunterbrook Capital is short AMD.**

It reports that Chinese server maker IEIT Systems, placed on the US Entity List in March 2025, has since incorporated at least six newer versions of AMD firmware into its products, and that three IEIT-linked companies (Maginfra in China, Kaytus in Singapore and Aivres in California) offer nearly identical firmware. AMD said the claims misrepresent its practices; no export-control violation has been established, and Hunterbrook could not say how IEIT obtained the firmware. AMD shares fell about 7% (CNBC), with @F_CEAFE reposting a report of a 13% intraday drop. Separately, a CNN review of nearly 300 Chinese procurement records found at least six US-blacklisted Chinese universities, including the military-linked Harbin Institute of Technology and Northwestern Polytechnical University, reported buying restricted Nvidia chips (A100 to H200), mostly in small quantities through little-known suppliers; CNN could not verify delivery.

**Sources:** [newsletter.hntrbrk.com](https://newsletter.hntrbrk.com/p/amd-has-its-own-china-problem), [·](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/19/amd-falls-on-short-seller-report-of-alleged-china-exposure.html), [·](https://www.roic.ai/news/hunterbrook-report-alleges-blacklisted-chinese-server-maker-continued-receiving-amd-firmware-raising-export-control-questions-11-19-2026), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123460609538768924), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123439006578798636), [·](https://qz.com/chinese-universities-blacklist-nvidia-chips-purchases-111926)
articles.why: The enforcement net is widening from Nvidia to AMD, and with it the pressure on every company in the chain, including European distributors, server integrators and cloud operators, to prove that no US chip or code reaches a listed Chinese entity. The more porous the controls appear, the stronger Washington’s case for tighter extraterritorial rules that Europeans must apply.
articles.watch: Any BIS inquiry or congressional letter on AMD; the 10 January 2027 expiry of the affiliates-rule suspension.

articles.headline: France’s Sanofi weighs a takeover of US drugmaker Insmed worth more than $30 billion
articles.summary:
**Paris-based Sanofi is working with advisers on a possible acquisition of Insmed, a New Jersey biopharma company specialised in lung and respiratory treatments, Bloomberg reported on 19 November.**

Talks are ongoing and a deal could be weeks away; Sanofi does not comment on rumours. Insmed shares rose as much as 24%, valuing it at about $30 billion, while Sanofi fell about 3–4% in Paris. Sanofi, led since early 2026 by Belén Garijo, has said it will use acquisitions to offset the coming patent expiry of Dupixent, and has about €10 billion from the sale of control of Opella to Clayton, Dubilier & Rice.

**Sources:** [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123473940475457743), [·](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/sanofi-weighs-takeover-of-us-drugmaker-insmed-bloomberg-news-reports-5039450), [·](https://www.handelsblatt.com/unternehmen/industrie/pharma-sanofi-erwaegt-uebernahme-des-us-pharmakonzerns-insmed/100271371.html), [·](https://www.ilsole24ore.com/art/sanofi-valuta-l-acquisizione-insmed-oltre-30-miliardi-dollari-AJqwJGMC)
articles.why: This is the opposite of the flow CEAFE usually flags: a European buyer of a US firm, as with EQT–Flatiron (18 November). It would be among the largest biopharma deals in years, but it also shows where European capital goes to find innovation: the pipeline Sanofi needs was built in the US. **Takeover alert check:** no new purchase of a European strategic company by a US buyer was found in this window.
articles.watch: A formal offer; rival bidders; US review (CFIUS rarely blocks pharma deals by allied buyers).

articles.headline: EU countries paid Russia as much for energy as they gave Ukraine in aid, 2022 to mid-October 2026
articles.summary:
**In a written answer to German liberal MEP Moritz Körner, EU Enlargement Commissioner Marta Kos stated that, since the start of Russia's war of aggression against Ukraine, from 2022 to mid-October 2026, the EU and its member states mobilised €231.5 billion in support for Ukraine, while €232.05 billion left the EU for Russia over the same period, mainly as payment for energy imports such as gas (Der Spiegel).**

Körner called it “a confession of European inconsistency”. An earlier Kos answer put EU payments for Russian fossil fuels at €213 billion for January 2022 to December 2025, falling to €17 billion in 2025 (5% of EU fossil-fuel imports) from €144 billion in 2022; the EU aims to end Russian energy imports by September 2027. @F_CEAFE posted the figures. In Warsaw the same day, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said he has “not heard a single European nation interested in reengaging in energy imports from Russia”, and declined to confirm reports of talks on bringing a US investor into Nord Stream.

**Sources:** [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/2123436933116211380), [·](https://www.spiegel.de/politik/deutschland/eu-mitglieder-zahlten-weiter-milliarden-fuer-gas-aus-russland-a-721c0e79-f355-4e2e-bf0f-e4297580e9f4), [·](https://www.eunews.it/en/2026/11/06/eu-paid-russia-213-billion-euros-for-energy-since-the-start-of-the-war-in-ukraine/), [·](https://boereport.com/2026/11/19/us-energy-chief-wright-sees-no-sign-europe-wants-return-to-russia-energy/)
articles.why: The two figures measure different flows (public aid against company and consumer energy bills), but together they show how slowly Europe freed itself from a single supplier, and that it did so by shifting to another one: the US now supplies most of the EU’s LNG. Meanwhile Washington keeps open its own options with Moscow (a diesel deal, Nord Stream ownership talk) while asking Europeans to buy American.
articles.watch: The EU’s end-2026 LNG and late-2027 pipeline phase-out; any US move on Nord Stream sanctions.

articles.headline: OFAC extends the window to negotiate a sale of Lukoil’s international assets
articles.summary:
**On 19 November the US Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control issued Russia-related General License 131L, replacing 131K, with updated FAQs 1224 and 1225.**

It authorises negotiations and contingent contracts for the sale of Lukoil International GmbH or its majority-owned subsidiaries until 19 December 2026, but not the completion of a sale without separate OFAC authorisation, and allows maintenance and wind-down activities until 20 February 2027, with no transfers to Russia. The same day OFAC also designated cyber-scam operators and armed-group facilitators in Southeast Asia and counter-narcotics targets.

Background: OFAC designated Lukoil on 22 October 2025. Since then CEAFE has tracked the race for its foreign assets: Carlyle and Chevron in November 2025, Kazakhstan's formal bid in January 2026 and a Todd Boehly-led consortium in November 2026.

**Sources:** [ofac.treasury.gov](https://ofac.treasury.gov/recent-actions/20261119), [·](https://ofac.treasury.gov/media/937386/download), [·](https://ofac.treasury.gov/faqs/updated/2026-11-19), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123466757318848592), [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/1989099688885354892), [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/2117741726509199821)
articles.why: Lukoil International holds refining and retail assets inside the EU. Who may buy them, on what timetable, is being decided by a US licence, not by EU authorities, a clear case of extraterritorial sanctions shaping ownership of European energy infrastructure.
articles.watch: Named bidders for Lukoil’s European assets; whether any EU government seeks control of the refineries.

articles.headline: Critical minerals: Kenya picks a US consortium for the Mrima Hill rare-earths project after Chinese bidders withdraw
articles.summary:
**Kenya’s mining ministry issued a notice of intention to award the Mrima Hill niobium and rare-earths project in Kwale County to the Frontier Minerals consortium (Frontier Minerals LLC, Bunker Hill Mining, ReElement Technologies and American Resources), stressing the notice is not a licence.**

US officials had named Mrima Hill as a key target of the Trump administration’s critical-minerals drive. The two Chinese firms among seven shortlisted bidders withdrew without giving a reason. Losing bidders, Australia’s RareX (with Iluka) and Mrima Earth (including Critical Metals Corp. and European Lithium), say they will challenge the award; RareX alleges Frontier missed the expression-of-interest deadline.

**Sources:** [apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/kenya-mrima-hills-minerals-510f8850db4308eefdfac88996f6116b), [·](https://www.mining.com/web/kenya-picks-us-consortium-to-develop-mrima-hill-critical-minerals-project/), [·](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cm9q84gp0gr3o), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123434500793475084)
articles.why: The US is locking up African critical-mineral deposits for its own supply chain while Europe’s Critical Raw Materials Act strategic projects advance slowly. A European-linked bid lost here; Europe risks depending on US-controlled supply instead of Chinese.
articles.watch: The procurement complaints; the Minerals Security Partnership and EU raw-materials diplomacy in Africa.

items.title: Economy — 2026-11-19 14:30
headlines: IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 calls the Hormuz crisis “the largest energy supply shock in history” and warns importers not to swap one dependency for another
Update: the EU delays its methane rules for oil, gas and coal importers by two years after months of US pressure
Congress moves to stop Microsoft selling OpenAI models to ByteDance, while Washington weighs forcing firms to disclose their use of Chinese AI
South Korea becomes the fourth country to export more than $1 trillion a year, after the US, China and Germany

articles.headline: IEA World Energy Outlook 2026 calls the Hormuz crisis “the largest energy supply shock in history” and warns importers not to swap one dependency for another
articles.summary:
**The International Energy Agency published its World Energy Outlook 2026 on 19 November, with Executive Director Fatih Birol presenting it live at 11:00 CET.**

The report says the Middle East conflict and the disruption of shipping through the Strait of Hormuz have produced the largest energy supply shock in history and that the crisis is likely to leave lasting marks, putting energy security and affordability at the centre of policy. It sees three common responses across countries: diversification of supplies, routes, fuels and technology supply chains; a stronger preference for domestic resources; and faster electrification. Birol’s warning is directly relevant to Europe: “In pursuit of greater energy security, countries must take care not to replace one dependency with another.” If the conflict is clearly resolved, the IEA expects a delayed wave of LNG supply to create a buyer’s market for oil and gas.

**Sources:** [IEA press release](https://www.iea.org/news/as-an-unprecedented-shock-reshapes-the-energy-world-its-duration-will-determine-the-scale-of-the-change), [@IEA](https://x.com/i/status/2123321628050292938), [@IEA](https://x.com/i/status/2123302784510439646), [@Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123358155128119652), [@AJEnglish](https://x.com/i/status/2123328392770523461), [@France24_en](https://x.com/i/status/2123285533954916455)
articles.why: The IEA’s caution describes Europe’s own trajectory since 2022: dependence on Russian pipeline gas has largely been replaced by dependence on US LNG, the theme of the P-TEC agreements covered on 18 November. The report’s winners from a pivot to domestic energy are renewables, led by solar PV, nuclear and efficiency; all can be built inside the EU, but only with a common industrial and financing effort that no single EU member state can carry alone. The same crisis that strains European industry with high gas prices is also an argument for the European energy union CEAFE defends.
articles.watch: WEO chapters on LNG supply and European gas balances; the OECD Economic Outlook on 4 December (announced by @OECD, https://x.com/i/status/2123385841284243615). Earlier coverage: IEA gas-storage warning (3 Nov) and extreme-weather shipping report (18 Nov 20:30). **Not yet reposted by @F_CEAFE (internal note).**

articles.headline: Update: the EU delays its methane rules for oil, gas and coal importers by two years after months of US pressure
articles.summary:
**Overnight on 18–19 November the Council of the EU and the European Parliament reached a provisional agreement to postpone the methane regulation’s obligations for importers of crude oil, natural gas and coal.**

Monitoring, reporting and verification obligations for importers will apply from 1 January 2029 instead of 1 January 2027, and methane-intensity reporting for importers and EU producers from 5 August 2030 instead of 5 August 2028. The two-year delay is longer than the one year proposed by the Commission and backed by EU governments; Parliament had sought three. POLITICO reports the deal came “after months of lobbying by the U.S. and fossil fuel companies”, and that a proposal to keep the rules in place for Russian imports was dropped.

Background: the pressure is not new; in November 2024 Biden administration officials already asked the EU in a letter to align its methane rules with US ones to ease LNG flows (Reuters), as CEAFE reported at the time.

**Sources:** [Council of the EU](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/19/methane-regulation-eu-agrees-targeted-amendment-to-safeguard-security-of-supply/), [POLITICO Europe](https://www.politico.eu/article/eu-extends-delay-of-key-methane-rules-to-two-years-after-us-pressure/), [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/19/eu-pushes-methane-rules-back-two-years-in-win-for-oil-and-gas-industry), [Anadolu Agency](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/europe/eu-reaches-provisional-deal-to-delay-methane-rules-for-fossil-fuel-importers-by-2-years/4130192), [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123343056015409304), [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/1856839118690390442)
articles.why: On 18 November (20:30 edition) we reported US ambassador Andrew Puzder asking the EU to change its own climate, due-diligence and methane laws under the Turnberry trade deal. One day later Brussels has yielded on methane, the rule that mattered most to US LNG exporters, Europe’s largest supplier. Europe adapts its legislation to its supplier’s demands while the US keeps its own tariffs on European steel and aluminium. Here, once more, a lack of reciprocity is presented as pragmatism.
articles.watch: Parliament and Council endorsement votes; whether the US now targets CBAM and the CSDDD next. **ALERT (economic coercion, not yet posted by @F_CEAFE; internal):** EU legislation softened after US pressure.

articles.headline: Congress moves to stop Microsoft selling OpenAI models to ByteDance, while Washington weighs forcing firms to disclose their use of Chinese AI
articles.summary:
**The House Select Committee on China asked Microsoft on 18 November for a bipartisan briefing on reported talks to let ByteDance use OpenAI models through the Azure cloud, a deal The Information put at about $500 million.**

Chairman John Moolenaar said “Microsoft should not sell AI tools to ByteDance” and that it was unacceptable for a company with Pentagon contracts to “arm” ByteDance. Microsoft said it enforces its terms of service and does not comment on confidential customer negotiations; it is also reportedly pursuing similar deals with Alibaba. Separately, Reuters reported that the Trump administration is weighing a rule forcing US firms to disclose their use of Chinese AI models. China’s Global Times (Chinese state media) quoted Xiang Ligang, president of the Beijing Institute of Intelligent Era Industry, saying the plan politicises commercial decisions and would push firms towards costlier models and weaken US competitiveness.

**Sources:** [Select Committee on China](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/press-releases/moolenaar-microsoft-should-not-sell-ai-to-bytedance), [CNA](https://www.channelnewsasia.com/world/us-microsoft-bytedance-openai-access-6563751), [Global Times](https://www.globaltimes.cn/page/202611/1374619.shtml), [Reuters via Investing.com](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exclusivetrump-administration-weighs-forcing-us-firms-to-disclose-chinese-ai-use-5035455), [The Straits Times](https://www.straitstimes.com/business/alibaba-megaspeed-financing-link-traced-via-spore-malaysia-units-allegedly-to-buy-nvidia-servers), [MITI](https://www.miti.gov.my/miti/resources/Speech/MEDIA_STATEMENT_13112026.pdf), [US DOJ](https://www.justice.gov/opa/pr/joint-statement-department-commerce-and-department-justice-megaspeed-investigation), [US DOJ](https://x.com/i/status/2123358289425797405), [US DOJ](https://x.com/i/status/2123332380517949795), [@clashreport](https://x.com/i/status/2123274021458301375)
articles.why: The US control net now covers not only chips and remote access to data centres (the BIS rule of 16 November, which reaches EU data centres) but also cloud services and even which AI models a company may use. Europe has no comparable leverage: it hosts US clouds and US models, and its firms will be expected to follow the same disclosure logic. A European sovereign cloud and AI stack is the only way to decide such questions in Europe.
articles.watch: Microsoft’s briefing; any formal disclosure rule; MOFCOM/MFA reaction. Earlier coverage: BIS remote-access rule (16–17 Nov), USCC report (18 Nov 20:30), Nvidia/Blackwell (19 Nov 07:30).

articles.headline: South Korea becomes the fourth country to export more than $1 trillion a year, after the US, China and Germany
articles.summary:
**South Korea’s cumulative exports for 2026 crossed $1 trillion at 14:09 Seoul time on 19 November, the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Resources announced.**

It is the first new member of the club in 19 years, after the United States and Germany (2006) and China (2007). Semiconductors drove the record: chip exports nearly tripled to $397.7 billion in January–October, 42.7% of the total, as AI data-centre demand lifted memory prices and shipments. The ministry expects $1.17 trillion for the full year, about 65% above 2025’s $709.3 billion, and warned of protectionism in the US and the EU and of dependence on chip prices. President Lee Jae-myung celebrated the milestone on X; @F_CEAFE reposted it.

**Sources:** [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261119003900320), [Yonhap](https://en.yna.co.kr/view/AEN20261118005700320), [The Korea Herald](https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10942838), [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123374514805338133), [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2123316572349452661)
articles.why: Germany is the only EU member state in the trillion-dollar export club, and its model of cheap energy and exports to China is under strain. South Korea reached the mark by owning a key link of the AI supply chain (memory chips). Europe has the scale to do the same in strategic technologies only as a Union; the figures show how far ahead the leaders already are.
articles.watch: Add to the rankings file if a national export ranking is published; chip-price trajectory into 2027.

headlines: Update: Berlin drops its opposition to UniCredit’s takeover of Commerzbank, opening the way to one of the largest cross-border bank mergers in the euro area
Trump says Nvidia’s Blackwell chips could be sold to China “in two to three years” and plays down the Huang affair before his talks with Xi
Anthropic prices the largest IPO in history: $81.3 billion in one day, about what all European start-ups raise in a year
Orlen reopens LNG talks with QatarEnergy days after cancelling a contract, while it buys about 90% of its LNG from the United States
The EU authorises signature of its trade and investment agreements with Indonesia, Southeast Asia’s largest economy
