articles.headline: Update: Moscow confirms Putin's Shenzhen trip as Trump leaves for Asia and says he "may" meet Kim Jong Un
articles.summary:
**Russia's Foreign Ministry announced that President Putin will pay a working visit to China on 18–19 November, attend the APEC summit in Shenzhen and take part in a planned trilateral meeting with the leaders of China and the US, then visit Tajikistan on 19–20 November (official Russian source).**

Departing the White House, Donald Trump said: "we're also going to meet with President Putin, and we may meet with Kim Jong Un also", adding that Kim's presence was "up to President Xi" (Reuters, Yonhap). Senior US officials told ABC News that denuclearisation will be the focus of the trilateral, that they expect no concrete agreement, and that Trump and Putin will not meet one-on-one; ABC reports Ukraine is not meant to be discussed in the trilateral, while AP reports Trump said he plans to raise the war. Before China, Trump stops in Manila for a Quad meeting, a trade deal with Thailand and the ASEAN summits. North Korea has publicly said it has no intention of meeting the US president at this time (Reuters).
articles.why: Nuclear arms control, the Iran war and, possibly, Ukraine will be discussed by Washington, Beijing and Moscow in a room with no European present, three days after 40 European states declared in Dublin that no decision on Europe's security can be taken without Europeans. Only a Union speaking and acting as one has the weight to be invited to such a table.
articles.watch: Whether Xi invites Kim; whether Ukraine enters the trilateral agenda; any European reaction before Thursday.

articles.headline: Pax Silica: the US signs a tech-security declaration with nine partners, the UK among them, as Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the Commission line up to join
articles.summary:
**On 15 November in San Francisco, the United States and nine Pax Silica participants (Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the UAE and the United Kingdom) signed the "San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity", convened by Under Secretary of State Jacob Helberg (State Department).**

It states that "economic security is fundamental to national security", sets a common understanding of the sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure behind "Super Intelligence" supply chains, from materials and know-how to ports, networks and energy, and creates five working groups to deliver results within six months. Reuters describes Pax Silica as a US push for allies' joint projects and export controls to cut reliance on "adversaries" in critical minerals, AI models and chips, in the context of the rivalry with China. The FT, cited by Reuters, reports that Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission are set to sign next week.
articles.why: This is the US double standard in plain text: Washington defines economic security as national security and organises others' supply chains and export controls around its own lead, while asking Europe not to protect its own markets. The UK has already signed alone, and three Member States are set to sign one by one alongside the Commission. Europe's leverage (ASML, materials, its market) only counts if it negotiates as one, sets its own conditions and asks for reciprocity.
articles.watch: The exact terms Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the Commission sign next week; China's response (MOFCOM/MFA): none found yet.

articles.headline: Update: EU lists 140 more targets over Russia's war, including its largest set yet against disinformation and cyberattacks
articles.summary:
**After the Foreign Affairs Council, High Representative Kaja Kallas said ministers approved 140 new listings targeting "Russian refineries, banks, e-commerce, and companies in the Gulf and East Asia" that support the shadow fleet, including "the largest set of listings to date" against those behind Russia's cyber and disinformation attacks; the 22nd sanctions package will be presented "in the coming days" (EEAS).**

The Council's FIMI and cyber decision covers 30 individuals and two entities: the Moscow-based Social Design Agency and 24 of its staff, propagandists including RT International's Chay Bowes, and the pro-Russian hacker group NoName057(16) for DDoS attacks on critical infrastructure and election-related targets (Council; Kyiv Independent). The EEAS says nearly 50 Russian banks were added to the more than 100 banks and financial institutions already cut off. Ministers also called for tighter visa policies and for keeping Russian athletes out of sports events held in the EU.

**Response:** Chay Bowes said the "authoritarian EU" had sanctioned him with "no hearing, no evidence" and that he would fight it. @F_CEAFE reposted his statement and a post by Max Blumenthal citing former MEP Clare Daly, who argues the listing freezes his accounts and bans travel without due process. No official Russian reaction yet; MFA spokeswoman Zakharova briefs on Friday 20 November.
articles.why: Sanctions are the EU's main collective instrument and today showed it can act fast and at scale. Listing a journalist, however, puts the Union's credibility on free expression at stake: the evidence behind each listing must be public and open to challenge before the EU Court.
articles.watch: The 22nd package; Moscow's countermeasures; any legal challenge by Bowes.

articles.headline: China's defence minister in Italy: first visit in more than 18 years, and a Chinese delegation aboard an Italian navy ship
articles.summary:
**Italian Defence Minister Guido Crosetto received his Chinese counterpart, Admiral Dong Jun, calling it "particularly significant, the first by a Chinese defence minister to Italy in over 18 years"; they agreed to follow up the understandings reached by their leaders, strengthen dialogue "including between the armed forces" and contribute to regional and global security (Italian MoD).**

China's MoD says the two sides agreed to "push the deepening of military relations" (Chinese MoD, state source). Italian press reports Dong Jun will meet Italian Navy leaders on Tuesday aboard the logistics ship Atlante in Brindisi, in a closed, two-hour programme that may include the arsenal (Quotidiano di Puglia, Corriere).
articles.why: A Member State opening military-to-military channels with China on its own, days before Washington, Moscow and Beijing meet without Europe, shows the pull of national bilateralism. Contacts with China are legitimate, but they carry weight only when they follow a common EU line; otherwise Beijing can play capitals against each other, just as Washington does.
articles.watch: Any statement after the Brindisi visit; Rome's coordination with EU partners.

articles.headline: Le Pen tells Ukraine's ambassador France would stop new financial aid to Kyiv if she is elected
articles.summary:
**Marine Le Pen told Ukraine's ambassador in Paris that, if elected president in 2027, France's public finances would no longer allow financial aid to Ukraine (Le Monde, Le Figaro, AFP).**

According to the reports, she would keep equipment donations, humanitarian aid and diplomatic support, and honour existing commitments, including the EU's €90bn loan. The same day Barrot, citing the Dublin declaration of 40 European states, said "no one can dictate" Ukraine's security choices (Anadolu), and Germany's Foreign Minister (@AussenMinDE) said in Brussels that "no decision on Europe without Europe… We do not need a new security architecture, but respect for existing principles".
articles.why: Europe now carries Ukraine's financing almost alone (see the 13:30 brief, item 1). A national veto on that effort by a future French government would weaken the whole Union's leverage at the negotiating table; common, EU-level instruments are what protect Ukraine's support from changes in national politics.
articles.watch: Reaction from Kyiv and other French parties.

articles.headline: Enlargement Forum: Costa expects Moldova's last two accession clusters to open by year-end
articles.summary:
**European Council President António Costa said he was "confident that the two remaining accession clusters will be opened by the end of the year" for Moldova, and discussed Moldova's security "in light of the recent surge in drone incursions and hybrid attacks"; Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said Moldova "already today participates in European defence projects" and discussed its gradual integration into the European defence architecture.**

Costa called enlargement "the best geopolitical investment in Europe's peace, security, democracy, stability and prosperity". Reuters reports diplomats are privately cautious about Kyiv's path, saying elections in key Member States could make progress harder. At the FAC, Ministers also backed moving ahead with an EU–Syria Association Agreement; Kallas said "a stable Syria is in Europe's interest" (EEAS).
articles.why: Enlargement extends the Union's weight and its security perimeter eastwards; bringing Moldova into common defence projects is the kind of integration that makes a larger Union stronger.

France's secret "Volia" mission: French soldiers have been working inside Ukraine since at least summer 2026, RFI reports

Iran: Tehran blames an Israeli "disinformation machine" for France's fridge-hack attribution and US assassination-plot claims

articles.headline: Update: EU foreign ministers answer Russia's "maximum demands" with their own, approve €8bn for Kyiv and 113 new listings
articles.summary:
**At today's Foreign Affairs Council in Brussels, High Representative Kaja Kallas said the ministers would work on "the substance" after leaders fixed the E5 + EU negotiating format on Friday, setting out "maximum demands" of their own "to reply to the maximum demands that Russia is still presenting".**

She said Russia's 2021 list of demands "was a pretext for war" and the same list, enlarged, is now "a pretext for keeping the war going", and that a ceasefire must come before "talks about anything else" (EEAS transcript). Euronews reports Russia is again demanding that NATO roll its military presence back to 1997 positions. The Council approved the largest single payment yet under the Ukraine Facility, nearly €8bn (Council press release; Zelenskyy thanked von der Leyen), and Ireland's presidency said ministers would adopt 113 new sanctions designations, including Russians blamed for cyberattacks and sabotage. The FT reports, in an exclusive reposted by @F_CEAFE, that the Commission will offer to cover almost two-thirds of Ukraine's estimated €70bn financing gap for next year, in a proposal due to member states on Wednesday. Poland's Radosław Sikorski noted that "the United States stopped funding aid to Ukraine in January last year… It is Europe that is supporting Ukraine". Ukraine's FM Andrii Sybiha told the Council that trilateral talks "have resumed after a nine-month pause" and that "Europe will play a new role in the peace process".

**Russia's side:** President Putin, in a message published by the Russian MFA (official Russian source), said Russia "firmly rejects all manifestations of neocolonialism, including the use of force & sanctions to exert pressure". No Russian official reaction to today's listings yet; watch MFA spokeswoman Zakharova's briefing.
articles.why: Sikorski's line is the key fact: Europe now carries Ukraine's financing alone, yet it sits at the table only as an ad hoc E5 + EU group, with the High Representative working "on the substance" behind it. The money and the sanctions are European; the decision on the format should be too. A single EU negotiating voice, backed by the €70bn financing plan, would turn Europe's weight into leverage.
articles.watch: FAC press conference this afternoon; the Commission's €70bn financing proposal (Wednesday); the extraordinary European Council on financing on 26–27 Nov; NATO foreign ministers on 2 Dec.

articles.headline: Update: Beijing confirms the first-ever Xi–Putin–Trump summit in Shenzhen on 19 November
articles.summary:
**China's Foreign Ministry formally announced that Xi Jinping will hold a China–Russia–U.S. summit with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of APEC, on Thursday 19 November (MFA; The Hindu).**

Spokeswoman Mao Ning said it will be "the first ever face-to-face meeting between the Chinese, Russian and U.S. heads of state" and that the leaders will discuss "safeguarding world peace" and "strategic stability in major-country relations"; @F_CEAFE reposted both her post and Global Times' version. A Global Times editorial (Chinese state media) calls the summit proof of "high recognition of China's image as a stable and responsible major country" and a rebuttal of the idea that great powers are "destined for confrontation". Reuters reports that tighter US curbs on Chinese access to advanced AI chips will likely overshadow the Trump–Xi talks, though AI-safety cooperation is possible. Al Jazeera notes Washington wants China in a new nuclear arms-control treaty with Russia, which Beijing resists because of its much smaller arsenal. Yonhap's experts expect the North Korean nuclear issue to feature little.
articles.why: The three powers will discuss "world peace" and strategic stability, Ukraine included, with no European at the table. EUISS's Alice Ekman (in Le Monde) says Beijing wants to use APEC to "accelerate the restructuring of global governance and marginalise Western countries". A Europe that speaks with 27 voices is easy to leave out; this is the clearest case yet for a single EU foreign and security policy voice.
articles.watch: Summit readouts on Ukraine, Iran, Taiwan and chips; any reference to Europe; Chinese and Russian readouts compared with the White House's.

articles.headline: France's secret "Volia" mission: French soldiers have been working inside Ukraine since at least summer 2026, RFI reports
articles.summary:
**An RFI investigation published this morning says small teams of French soldiers have been operating in Ukraine since at least the summer of 2026 under a highly confidential structure called "Volia", led by a French general.**

Their task, according to RFI's sources, is not combat but training Ukrainian troops and maintaining French-supplied equipment (Caesar guns, Mirage 2000 jets, precision missiles). The officially acknowledged "Gerfaut" training detachment in Poland (part of EUMAM-Ukraine, extended to 15 Nov 2028) is said to serve as a cover and gateway; soldiers are reportedly told to say they are going to Poland. An AFP source confirmed small contingents are deployed for training and maintenance. RFI says Parliament was not informed, although Article 35 of the Constitution requires it for any deployment of conventional forces abroad; Senate defence committee chair Cédric Perrin called informing Parliament "a constitutional obligation" (JDD, quoting RFI). @F_CEAFE reposted Florian Philippot's post calling it a "state lie unmasked".

**Russia's side:** No official Russian reaction to the RFI report was found at the time of writing. Moscow has previously said any foreign troops in Ukraine would be "legitimate targets" (Russian MFA, January 2026, reported by CNN). Watch the Kremlin and MFA briefings.
articles.why: If confirmed, Volia shows a European state already doing in Ukraine what the Coalition of the Willing has only discussed: keeping European weapons working where they are used. It also shows the cost of doing it nationally and in secret: no democratic mandate, no common EU framework, and a fresh pretext for Russian escalation. Europe's support for Ukraine is stronger and more legitimate when it is common, declared and parliamentary.
articles.watch: Élysée / Armed Forces Ministry response; parliamentary questions; Russian reaction; any similar reports on other European states.

articles.headline: UK–EU summit on Friday: food and carbon deals and a defence commitment, as Burnham says Brexit cost more than it gained
articles.summary:
**Britain and the EU will meet in Brussels on 20 November for the second EU–UK summit, with António Costa and Ursula von der Leyen hosting Prime Minister Andy Burnham (EEAS).**

Reuters reports the sides will sign deals on food and link carbon markets and make a commitment on defence, while a youth-mobility scheme and tuition fees remain disputed and the full package could take another six months. Burnham is expected to say tonight that the UK "has lost more than it gained" from a "needlessly hard Brexit" (BBC). The UK will have a "voice" but no vote on EU food rules, and the deal is calculated to add 0.4% to UK GDP (BBC, citing minister Hamish Falconer). London also wants a signal on whether its car industry can join the "Made in Europe" scheme (Reuters). Finland's President Alexander Stubb said "leaving the EU is a bad thing, both politically and economically… Brexit has proven that to be true", while keeping "all options open" with the UK (via @ClashReport).
articles.why: Ten years on, the UK is rediscovering what CEAFE argues: a mid-sized European state alone is a rule-taker. A defence and security partnership with London strengthens Europe, but the EU should insist that UK participation in "Made in Europe" and SAFE-type programmes means European, not US-controlled, supply chains (Trident, F-35 and Palantir are all US dependencies for Britain).
articles.watch: Burnham's Lord Mayor's Banquet speech tonight; summit declaration on Friday; "Made in Europe" and SAFE access for UK firms.

articles.headline: Iran: Tehran blames an Israeli "disinformation machine" for France's fridge-hack attribution and US assassination-plot claims
articles.summary:
**Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said that "from the so-called 'refrigerator cases' in France to allegations that Iran is plotting to assassinate U.S. officials" there is "a coordinated malign narrative campaign orchestrated by Israel's disinformation machine", designed to portray Iran "as an enemy of ordinary people" (post reposted by @F_CEAFE and by Iran's MFA, which added that Iran has no "need to resort to terror").**

France had attributed the 11–12 October cyberattacks on refrigeration systems at about 700 retail sites to Shahid Kaveh, an IRGC-affiliated cyber unit (Iran International). In parallel, @F_CEAFE reposted a report (via @HormuzLetter, citing Ynet) that Mossad chief Roman Gofman briefed Israel's security cabinet on possible military action against Iran after returning from Washington. US Treasury Secretary Bessent said Iranian officials "cannot fly abroad as isolation tightens", and Parliament Speaker Ghalibaf said Iran "does not care whether the U.S. wants war or talks" (both via ClashReport articles). Pakistan hosted the 30th ECO Council of Ministers in Islamabad with Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi present.
articles.why: France's attribution makes Iran's hybrid campaign a direct EU security issue, not only a US–Israel matter. Iran's denial is a claim from an official state source and does not refute France's evidence; Europe's answer should be common (EU cyber-sanctions regime) rather than national.
articles.watch: Any French or EU response to Tehran's denial; Israeli cabinet decisions; US–Iran escalation (Conflicts section).

articles.headline: Update: ASEAN and China reach "substantial completion" of the South China Sea code, but no final text
articles.summary:
**Correcting the picture from the morning brief: at the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, Philippine Foreign Secretary Theresa Lazaro announced the "substantial completion" of negotiations on the ASEAN–China Code of Conduct, with provisional agreement on "about 80 percent" of the paragraphs, up from about 50% at the start of the year.**

She stressed "there's no conclusion yet": geographic scope, terms of reference and whether the code is legally binding are still open, and the text passes to Singapore's chairmanship in 2027. The parties did agree that the 2002 Declaration (DOC) is the code's foundation and that it will uphold UNCLOS. Around it, ASEAN held summits with China (Premier Li Qiang, who praised free trade "in the face of global trade restrictions"), the UN (Secretary-General Guterres said Myanmar's "human suffering has reached epic proportions"), Australia, South Korea (President Lee Jae Myung), and Japan's PM Takaichi and India's PM Modi arrived in Manila. Greece marked the anniversary of UNCLOS as "the only basis for the peaceful resolution of disputes".
articles.why: The South China Sea carries a large share of EU trade. The EU is not a party, but its interest is the same as ASEAN's: rules over force, under UNCLOS. A non-binding code would leave the door open to coercion. Europe's credibility in the region depends on acting as one trading and naval power, not as members sending ships on Washington's request.
articles.watch: Chairman's statement; East Asia Summit; Trump's arrival in the region before Shenzhen.

items.title: World — 2026-11-16 07:30
headlines: Ukraine peace talks: Europe's "E5 + EU" team takes shape as Russia tests whether it gets a seat
Xi to host Putin and Trump in Shenzhen on 19 November, with Europe absent
Gaza: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK say 150,000 tents are held at the border
Rubio: "Stop quoting laws to men with swords", and the ICC drops US troops from its Afghanistan probe
Asia: ASEAN and China fail to close the South China Sea code, Canada concludes an FTA with ASEAN

articles.headline: Ukraine peace talks: Europe's "E5 + EU" team takes shape as Russia tests whether it gets a seat
articles.summary:
**European leaders meeting in Dublin on 13 November named Europe's team for any Russia–Ukraine talks.**

It is made up of the E5 of the Coalition of the Willing (France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK, at national-security-adviser level) plus the European Commission and the European Council, "in full coordination with NATO" (António Costa, as reported by Agence Europe, Euronews and Kyiv Independent). On the evening of 15 November Ursula von der Leyen said she had discussed the peace talks with Finland's President Alexander Stubb, and that "Europe will closely engage in this process through the E5 + EU format", while keeping "maximum support for Ukraine and maximum pressure on Russia". Former Commissioner Thierry Breton objected that leaders had named "7 representatives" for the talks "in place of the one provided for by the treaties". A Reuters podcast post says Zelenskyy has stated that US negotiators floated the idea of Kyiv ceding Donbas in return for NATO membership. UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting answered that "Russia is in no position to dictate policy" (Sky News) and said Britain's nuclear deterrent is "not up for negotiation" as HMS Vengeance came home from what the Daily Mail called a record-length patrol. EU foreign ministers meet in Brussels today (16 Nov) with Ukrainian FM Andrii Sybiha. According to Ireland's foreign ministry, the meeting will adopt 113 new sanctions listings.

**Russia's side:** TASS reported von der Leyen's statement as "European countries are seeking a role" in the talks. It also gave space to a US op-ed (The American Conservative) arguing that "Russia has, in fact, won". The Kremlin had earlier said it first wanted to understand Europe's "real intentions" (AFP, quoted by Kyiv Post). @F_CEAFE reposted a post mocking the line "Russia must have no seat at the table" as "European diplomacy in the age of incompetent warmongers" (a quote of Estonian MP @markomihkelson).
articles.why: Europe is finally at the table, but as an ad hoc group of five capitals (one of them, the UK, outside the EU) plus two institutions, with the High Representative left out. Breton's point is CEAFE's: the treaties already provide a single EU voice. A continent of 27 split into national envoys is easier to divide, and harder for Washington or Moscow to take seriously. Streeting's "not up for negotiation" deterrent rests on US-supplied Trident II D5 missiles, a reminder that Europe's ultimate security guarantee is still not fully sovereign.
articles.watch: FAC conclusions and the 113 listings today; whether Moscow accepts European negotiators; the 26–27 Nov summit on Ukraine financing and frozen Russian assets (Belgium's position).

articles.headline: Xi to host Putin and Trump in Shenzhen on 19 November, with Europe absent
articles.summary:
**China's foreign ministry announced that President Xi Jinping will hold a "China-Russia-U.S.**

Summit" with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on 19 November, alongside the APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting (18–19 Nov). Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov confirmed it to TASS. Xinhua and Global Times (Chinese state media) frame APEC around "openness, innovation, and cooperation". Reuters says Ukraine, trade and AI will hang over the meeting. Bloomberg says Trump arrives "politically weakened at home, yet perhaps even more eager to flex his power abroad". @F_CEAFE reposted the Chinese MFA announcement. Canada's Mark Carney will meet Xi on Tuesday and said Canada "has other partners for auto manufacturing" if Washington does not want an integrated North American supply chain (Bloomberg).
articles.why: The three powers whose choices decide the war in Ukraine, global trade rules and AI will meet without any European present, just days after the EU finally named its negotiating team. The lesson for CEAFE: only a Union that acts as one actor, with its own defence, technology and trade weight, gets invited to tables like this. Canada's open hedging with China is the kind of collective leverage the EU rarely uses with Washington.
articles.watch: whether Ukraine terms are discussed over Europe's head; any US–China trade or export-control deal (chips, rare earths) that EU firms would then have to follow.

articles.headline: Gaza: Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK say 150,000 tents are held at the border
articles.summary:
**On 15 November the foreign ministers of Australia, Canada, Italy and the UK urged Israel's government to "stop the delays now and allow immediate, rapid and unimpeded humanitarian access throughout Gaza".**

They said "150,000 tents and other vital supplies are being held at the border" as winter floods hit, asked for dual-use items for early recovery to be let in, and called on all parties to implement the Comprehensive Plan for Gaza. The EU issued its own statement on 14 November urging Israel to reopen all crossings (Al Jazeera). Ireland's Helen McEntee will press the FAC today to "intensify pressure" on Israel. Haaretz reports that Israel's own figures show aid deliveries fell far short of its commitments. Israel's MFA amplified an Israeli diplomat's UN speech calling UNRWA "the arsonist" and criticised the Palestinian Authority. Inside Israel, Haaretz reports coalition talks between Netanyahu's camp and Gadi Eisenkot's bloc. @F_CEAFE reposted Eisenkot's post calling Netanyahu's conduct a direct threat to Israeli democracy.
articles.why: Italy is the only EU member among the four signatories. The EU again speaks through separate national statements and a Council text, not one policy with consequences. Europe is Israel's first trading partner, so its leverage is real but unused.
articles.watch: FAC language on Israel; whether crossings open; Israeli coalition outcome.

articles.headline: Rubio: "Stop quoting laws to men with swords", and the ICC drops US troops from its Afghanistan probe
articles.summary:
**In a keynote at the Federalist Society on 13 November, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said that "for this global elite, international law is not a neutral body of rules… it is an instrument".**

He defended the US sanctions on the International Criminal Court and warned that if the court tries to enforce "paper decrees" on Americans, the answer will be Pompey's: "Stop quoting laws to men with swords" (transcript, Reuters, AFP). The State Department's X account then amplified friendly coverage from Breitbart, Daily Caller and American Greatness. Iran's FM Abbas Araghchi replied that the Roman general behind that phrase died "beheaded after fleeing the battlefield". Separately, ICC judges are closing the parts of the Afghanistan investigation that could have looked at US troops, to focus only on the Taliban (Defense News). Reuters says the US sanctions on the ICC take effect in April unless the court's supporters reach an agreement with Washington.
articles.why: The ICC sits in The Hague and is funded mainly by European states. Washington's message is that law binds others, not the US, while it asks Europe to follow its sanctions on third countries. This is the double standard CEAFE highlights. Europe has a legal tool (the EU Blocking Statute) and the economic weight to protect institutions it hosts; whether it uses them before April is a test of strategic autonomy.
articles.watch: EU/Dutch response to the April sanctions deadline.

articles.headline: Asia: ASEAN and China fail to close the South China Sea code, Canada concludes an FTA with ASEAN
articles.summary:
**At the 49th ASEAN Summit in Manila, ASEAN and China failed to conclude the South China Sea code of conduct despite tentative agreement on about 80% of the draft.**

The Philippine FM Theresa Lazaro said key issues remain, including whether the code is legally binding (Al Jazeera). The 29th ASEAN–China Summit was held with Premier Li Qiang. Canada announced the substantial conclusion of a free trade agreement with ASEAN, a market of "nearly 700 million people" (Carney). Bloomberg says leaders came to Manila seeking trade links "as a hedge against the rising US protectionism". Taiwan's defence ministry reported 4 PLA aircraft sorties, 7 PLAN vessels and 3 official ships around Taiwan; all 4 sorties crossed the median line. Hundreds of protesters against the Middle East conflict and Trump's expected visit clashed with police in Manila (Reuters).
articles.why: Middle powers (Canada, ASEAN, India) are diversifying away from US trade pressure. The EU, the world's largest trading bloc, should be leading this, not following.

headlines: US envoys float a Donbas-for-NATO probe as Europe forms an E5 and funding splits appear
Trump, Xi and Putin plan a first trilateral meeting in Shenzhen
Eighteen states condemn the Nasser Hospital strike as the EU and Israel clash over winter aid
ASEAN leaders meet in Manila; Canada says it has concluded FTA talks
Greece rejects the “pseudo-state” in Cyprus on the 43rd anniversary of its declaration
FAS estimates Israel’s nuclear stockpile at about 90 warheads, with delivery-system upgrades

articles.headline: US envoys float a Donbas-for-NATO probe as Europe forms an E5 and funding splits appear
articles.summary:
After meeting US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy told reporters that American negotiators had for the first time asked whether Ukraine would withdraw from parts of the Donbas that Russia does not fully control, in exchange for NATO membership. He said Ukraine would not give up land or recognise occupied territory as Russian, but that if Washington and other NATO partners offered a concrete package of security guarantees, a strong army and funded reconstruction, he would put the question to Ukrainian society. The White House had not confirmed the remarks; a US official told the BBC that “many ideas continue to be discussed.” Kushner wrote that he and Witkoff remained in close consultation with Russia, Ukraine and European partners, with the focus on facilitating direct engagement. France 24 reported that the meetings with Putin and Zelenskyy took place on Thursday after two days of talks in Abu Dhabi that ended without a breakthrough, but with agreement that European countries would join future talks.

In Dublin, after the ninth European Political Community summit and an informal European Council, Prime Minister Donald Tusk said leaders had broadly backed an “E5” format — Poland, Italy, the United Kingdom, France and Germany, plus EU institution leaders — to coordinate Europe’s role in talks. He said European Council President António Costa should present a common European position, and that Poland’s representative would be Deputy Foreign Minister Robert Kupiecki. Tusk also told NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte that, for now, Poland would not contribute additional funds to the PURL initiative (European money for US weapons for Ukraine), citing a high budget deficit and already very large national defence spending. Defence Industry Europe reported that Warsaw had previously contributed $100 million to PURL in a December 2025 package with Norway and Germany. Slovak Prime Minister Robert Fico, in a post amplified by @F_CEAFE, rejected “war loans” and said Slovakia would support peace talks and humanitarian aid but “not a single cent for weapons.” President Emmanuel Macron, in a 14 November address, said 42 countries had approved a French-initiated declaration of principles for Europe’s security, warned against “rationing” Ukraine’s means, and pointed to a Coalition of the Willing follow-up in Berlin on Thursday 19 November. Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, rejected any “new security order” for Europe, saying Russia keeps violating the existing one and that, at this stage, the most Moscow could negotiate was a fair ceasefire along the current line of contact, not spheres of influence.
articles.why: The shape of any settlement — territory, NATO membership and who sits at the table — is being negotiated in formats that can include or sideline Europeans. Poland’s pause on PURL and Slovakia’s refusal of further military financing expose strain in the very mechanisms created after the United States stopped supplying weapons free of charge, just as US mediators want Europeans in the next round.
articles.watch: Concrete security-guarantee language, if any, after further Witkoff/Kushner contacts; whether other allies fill a PURL gap; the Berlin Coalition of the Willing meeting on 19 November; and Europe’s line if Russia again tables demands to roll NATO’s posture back.

articles.headline: Trump, Xi and Putin plan a first trilateral meeting in Shenzhen
articles.summary:
The White House and Russian officials have confirmed that Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin intend to meet on the sidelines of the APEC summit in Shenzhen, with the gathering expected on 19 November and the summit itself on 18–19 November. White House assistant press secretary Olivia Wales said the discussion would, “among other topics,” address “the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world.” Reporting indicates the agenda is also expected to include the US–Israel war with Iran and residual US–China trade tensions; US officials have said Ukraine is unlikely to be raised there because a separate Witkoff–Kushner track is under way and “China is not really a part of that track.”

New START lapsed in February. Trump has previously rejected a simple Russian extension and called for a new agreement that would also involve China; Beijing has said it would be “neither fair, reasonable nor realistic” to join trilateral nuclear disarmament talks at this stage. A senior US official told Reuters that the nuclear discussion would open the conversation but that “we do not expect to get any kind of agreement.” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called the meeting “extremely significant” but said any understandings could not be imposed on other nations. Some Russian politicians have evoked a “new Yalta”; Ukraine’s foreign minister Andrii Sybiha dismissed the idea, saying that “to put forward ideas of this magnitude, you first need to win a world war.”
articles.why: A US–China–Russia meeting from which Ukraine and European leaders are absent, with nuclear arms and Iran on the table and Ukraine officially off it, is a test of whether Europe can still shape outcomes that directly affect its security.
articles.watch: The 19 November readout, or a cancellation; whether Ukraine or European security architecture appears despite the US briefing; and China’s line on New START-like constraints.

articles.headline: Eighteen states condemn the Nasser Hospital strike as the EU and Israel clash over winter aid
articles.summary:
In a joint statement dated 14 November 2026 and circulated by Qatar’s foreign ministry and others, the foreign ministers of 18 Arab and Islamic states condemned “in the strongest terms” an Israeli airstrike on the Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis, which they said caused casualties among patients and medical personnel, in violation of international humanitarian law. The signatories were Türkiye, Algeria, Djibouti, Egypt, Indonesia, Jordan, Kuwait, Lebanon, Libya, Mauritania, Oman, Pakistan, Palestine, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Somalia, Sudan and the United Arab Emirates. They also condemned continued Israeli attacks on civilians, including strikes on tents and other shelters, saying these undermined the ceasefire and were inconsistent with President Trump’s Comprehensive Plan, and called on Israel to implement its obligations under the Sharm El-Sheikh Agreement, that plan and UN Security Council Resolution 2803 (2025).

The same day, High Representative Kaja Kallas, speaking on behalf of the European Union, said severe flooding and winter conditions in Gaza were aggravating an already grave humanitarian situation and urged Israel to allow immediate, unimpeded access and to reopen all Gaza border crossings. The official EU text also called the Nasser Hospital airstrike “deeply alarming,” recalled that aid should not be diverted by armed groups, reaffirmed the two-state solution, and called for full implementation of Resolution 2803, including the permanent decommissioning of weapons from Hamas and other non-state armed groups and the full withdrawal of Israeli forces from Gaza. Israel’s Foreign Ministry rejected the EU statement as “completely unbalanced,” said it rewarded Hamas’s refusal to disarm, and stated that “more than 93,000 tents and over 8,600 trucks carrying winter supplies and essential equipment have entered Gaza.” A @DropSiteNews claim, reposted by @F_CEAFE, that 150,000 tents were being blocked at the border was not independently verified in the list briefs and sits in tension with Israel’s figure. Separately, the IDF said it had killed Samir Mahmoud Hassan Abu Younis, commander of Hamas’s Rafah Brigade, in a strike in southern Gaza.
articles.why: The EU is publicly at odds with Israel — and with a US-backed “Board of Peace” mechanism — over humanitarian access, while military operations against Hamas commanders continue during a fragile, contested ceasefire. A new regional spiral would again draw in European diplomacy, naval deployments and domestic politics.
articles.watch: Whether crossings reopen and shelter materials are allowed in; casualty figures and any Israeli or WHO account of the Nasser strike; and whether the Board of Peace or the United States presses on access.

articles.headline: ASEAN leaders meet in Manila; Canada says it has concluded FTA talks
articles.summary:
ASEAN leaders gathered in Manila on 15 November 2026 for the 49th ASEAN Summit and related meetings, under the chairmanship of Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. The opening included the ceremonial unveiling of an updated ASEAN emblem and flag — described as the first amendment to the emblem — and the handover of the ASEAN Digital Economic Framework Agreement (DEFA) from Marcos to Secretary-General Kao Kim Hourn. On Myanmar, ASEAN said leaders expressed deep concern over the conflicts and humanitarian situation, encouraged “substantive progress” in implementing the Five-Point Consensus, and underscored the need to “calibrate” ASEAN’s engagement with Myanmar “based on developments on the ground.”

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said in Manila that Canada had “just wrapped up negotiations on two major free trade agreements — with the Philippines and with ASEAN.” On the margins he announced, with President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, an initial Canadian contribution of up to C$560 million over four years to Brazil’s Tropical Forest Forever Facility; Carney’s post said “half a billion dollars.” Official Canadian statements also recorded a discussion of defence cooperation under a Canada–Brazil Defence Cooperation Agreement. @F_CEAFE reposted Global Times reporting that Australia and the Philippines had signed a new defence pact amid South China Sea tensions; that item was Chinese state-media commentary and was not independently confirmed from official Australian or Philippine texts in the briefs.
articles.why: The Manila summit is a snapshot of Indo-Pacific alignment — trade, digital rules, Myanmar and South China Sea security — among partners the EU and European states are also courting.
articles.watch: Publication of the FTA texts or official joint statements; official Australian and Philippine texts of any new defence pact; and ASEAN’s full Leaders’ Review on Myanmar.

articles.headline: Greece rejects the “pseudo-state” in Cyprus on the 43rd anniversary of its declaration
articles.summary:
Greece’s Foreign Ministry marked 15 November 2026 as the 43rd anniversary of what it called “the illegal unilateral declaration of the pseudo-state in Cyprus,” in “flagrant violation” of the UN Charter and international law, and recalled UN Security Council Resolutions 541 (1983) and 550 (1984). Athens “categorically rejects the fait accompli of the Turkish invasion and occupation,” called on all states to respect the sovereignty, independence and territorial integrity of the Republic of Cyprus, and restated its commitment — “in full coordination with the Republic of Cyprus” — to a comprehensive settlement based on a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation with political equality, a single international personality, single sovereignty and single citizenship, in line with UNSC resolutions and the European acquis. Türkiye’s Presidency Directorate of Communications, by contrast, issued remarks “wholeheartedly” celebrating the 43rd anniversary of the proclamation of the Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus as “a symbol of the Turkish Cypriot people’s struggle for freedom.” On the same day, several Turkish defence-industry firms on CEAFE’s RoW list posted ceremonial congratulations; those messages announced no new capability or contract (see also the Defence Industry section only by this cross-reference).

On 14 November, Greek Foreign Minister Giorgos Gerapetritis separately briefed parliamentary party leaders on developments concerning the Greece–Cyprus electricity interconnection.
articles.why: Cyprus remains a live EU–Türkiye fault line. Anniversary diplomacy, and any tension around the Greece–Cyprus interconnector, can affect Eastern Mediterranean energy projects, sanctions debates and the broader EU–Türkiye agenda.
articles.watch: Any formal Turkish or TRNC replies; progress or incidents around the interconnector; the next step in the UN Personal Envoy’s process.

articles.headline: FAS estimates Israel’s nuclear stockpile at about 90 warheads, with delivery-system upgrades
articles.summary:
Hans M. Kristensen and Mackenzie Knight-Boyle’s Nuclear Notebook for the *Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists* (10 November 2026) estimates Israel’s stockpile at roughly 90 single-stage, boosted fission warheads — the same size as the previous notebook edition from 2021. The authors, of the Federation of American Scientists’ Nuclear Information Project, say satellite imagery shows significant construction at several key sites and that aircraft and submarines are being upgraded. They place the force across a triad of aircraft (F-16s, possibly F-15I, and F-35I “Adir”), land-based Jericho ballistic missiles (about 25–50 road-mobile launchers at Sdot Micha, with Jericho III reportedly exceeding 4,000 km — enough, they write, to reach all of Iran, Pakistan, Europe and western Russia), and possibly sea-launched cruise missiles from six German-built Dolphin-class submarines, with three next-generation Dakar-class boats contracted in 2022 for delivery from the early 2030s. Israel continues its policy of nuclear ambiguity; the estimate is an open-source assessment, not an official disclosure.

The authors caution that rumours of several hundred warheads are likely exaggerated. They cite an International Panel on Fissile Materials estimate of 800–1,000 kg of plutonium as of the beginning of 2025, theoretically enough for 160–250 weapons if all were converted — which they do not assume. Dimona is described as nearing the end of its design life, with officials indicating an intent to keep it running until 2040, and as the site of the largest construction project in decades since 2021; 2026 imagery shows a new circular structure of similar diameter to the existing reactor, but the authors say there is no indication yet that it is a reactor.
articles.why: A published open-source assessment that Jericho III’s reported range includes Europe, ongoing force modernisation (including German-built submarines), and the wider Middle East crisis all affect European security, non-proliferation diplomacy and crisis management.
articles.watch: Any official Israeli or US response; further imagery of the Dimona construction; and Dakar-class submarine milestones.

Presupuesto de la UE 2028-2034: Costa propone 1,78 billones de euros, 204.000 millones menos que la Comisión y un 232 % más para defensa

articles.headline: Washington restringe en un memorando secreto los lazos militares con Canadá, y Ottawa firma un acuerdo naval con Alemania y Noruega
articles.summary:
**Según publicó el viernes el Washington Post citando a varios funcionarios, el secretario de Defensa de EE. UU., Pete Hegseth, hizo circular la semana pasada un memorando clasificado que impone «nuevas restricciones» a la relación de defensa con Canadá.**

Uno de esos funcionarios dio por hecho que Ottawa lo verá como «una bofetada». El portavoz del Pentágono, Sean Parnell, aseguró que la directriz «no afecta a la cooperación en inteligencia de defensa, al mando binacional NORAD ni a la cooperación en la OTAN», y que el Pentágono quiere que sus relaciones con Canadá «sirvan a objetivos de defensa concretos de EE. UU.» (Globe and Mail; Xinhua, medio estatal chino). La cúpula militar canadiense se enteró por la prensa, y Ottawa dice no haber recibido ninguna comunicación al respecto. Los programas de intercambio militar podrían ser uno de los afectados (Globe and Mail). En su rueda de prensa del viernes, Trump afirmó que Canadá se siente «envalentonada» y que Washington no puede permitir que siga así (Anadolu, AP).

**Contexto:** Esa misma noche, el Departamento de Defensa Nacional de Canadá anunció un memorando de entendimiento con Alemania y Noruega sobre cooperación en material naval, «para desarrollar, adquirir y mantener equipos y sistemas de defensa naval» (@NationalDefence). Los tres países ya habían abierto con TKMS una fase conjunta de planificación del submarino Type 212CD (TKMS). Ese mismo día, el ministro David McGuinty inauguró el 18.º Foro Internacional de Seguridad de Halifax (@NationalDefence). El Globe relaciona el roce con la decisión de Ottawa de aplazar la compra del F-35 estadounidense y con la guerra comercial. En mayo, Washington ya había suspendido la Junta Permanente Conjunta de Defensa.

**Fuentes:** [de pago; titular y entradilla](https://www.washingtonpost.com/national-security/2026/11/20/secret-hegseth-memo-restricts-us-canada-defense-relationship/), [de pago; titular y entradilla](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/world/us-politics/article-no-change-to-canada-us-defence-co-operation-military-sources-say-amid/), [de pago; titular y entradilla](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/americas/us-defense-chief-imposed-new-limits-on-military-ties-with-canada-report/4132656), [de pago; titular y entradilla](https://english.news.cn/northamerica/20261121/7ad991f2ec8e4b07ba3189f791c3a574/c.html), [@washingtonpost](https://x.com/i/status/2123978459625992241), [@washingtonpost](https://x.com/i/status/2123902538265006236), [Halifax](https://x.com/i/status/2123884359614706005), [TKMS](https://www.tkmsgroup.com/news/article/launch-of-trilateral-cooperation-germany-norway-canada-and-tkms-begin-planning-phase-for-the-212cd-program), [TKMS](https://x.com/i/status/2123897564143734877)
articles.why: Un aliado de la OTAN que aparca un caza estadounidense y opta por un submarino europeo recibe un castigo de Washington. Es el riesgo de dependencia y de *kill switch* del que advierte el CEAFE, ya en la práctica. Que Canadá elija un diseño germano-noruego demuestra que la industria europea puede ser el socio alternativo de los aliados, siempre que Europa ofrezca una cadena de suministro completa y soberana.
articles.watch: Si trasciende el contenido del memorando (intercambios, adiestramiento, adquisiciones); la respuesta canadiense en Halifax; los próximos pasos del 212CD y una posible incorporación de Canadá a instrumentos europeos como SAFE.

articles.headline: Presupuesto de la UE 2028-2034: Costa propone 1,78 billones de euros, 204.000 millones menos que la Comisión y un 232 % más para defensa
articles.summary:
**El presidente del Consejo Europeo, António Costa, presentó el sábado una nueva «caja de negociación» para el marco financiero 2028-2034 (Consilium).**

Según Rapporteur y Politico, fija los compromisos en 1,78 billones de euros: 204.000 millones (un 10,2 %) menos que la propuesta de casi 2 billones que la Comisión presentó en julio de 2025. Costa afirma que, frente al presupuesto vigente 2021-2027, la defensa crece un 232 %, la competitividad un 120 %, los fondos para migración y fronteras se duplican, la acción exterior sube un 23 % y Horizonte Europa un 57 %. Las contribuciones nacionales pasarían de media del 0,80 % al 0,82 % de la RNB. Cinco nuevos recursos propios (ingresos digitales de las grandes empresas, CBAM, residuos electrónicos no reciclados, tabaco y ETS) aportarían, junto con los actuales, unos 60.000 millones al año. Frente al plan de la Comisión, la competitividad pierde 95.000 millones (un 16 %) y la acción exterior 45.000 millones (un 21 %), y por primera vez se recorta la cohesión (Rapporteur, Politico).

**Contexto:** La presidencia francesa rechazó el texto de inmediato: lo considera «muy decepcionante» y «no es base para un acuerdo», sobre todo por las ayudas a la renta agraria (franceinfo). Por parte del PPE, su negociador Siegfried Mureșan lo calificó de «inaceptable para el Parlamento Europeo» (Politico). Los líderes celebran una cumbre extraordinaria la semana próxima, y Costa aspira a cerrar el acuerdo en el Consejo Europeo que arranca el 17 de diciembre.

**Fuentes:** [consilium.europa.eu](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/21/multiannual-financial-framework-president-costa-s-proposal/), [rapporteur.com](https://www.rapporteur.com/news/costa-proposes-e204-billion-cut-to-eu-budget/), [politico.eu](https://www.politico.eu/article/costa-cuts-proposed-eu-budget-by-44billion-euros/), [franceinfo.fr](https://www.franceinfo.fr/monde/europe/sommet-de-l-ue/le-president-du-conseil-europeen-propose-un-budget-de-l-ue-en-baisse-de-204-milliards-d-euros-aussitot-rejete-par-la-france_8293637.html), [@eucopresident](https://x.com/i/status/2124083354823725327), [@business](https://x.com/i/status/2124103074931261778)
articles.why: Por primera vez, el presupuesto de la UE se articula en torno a la defensa. Pero un aumento del 232 % parte de una base pequeña, y el recorte en competitividad, donde están las líneas de industria de defensa e I+D, golpea precisamente los instrumentos que permitirían a Europa dotarse de capacidades propias. Un presupuesto común menor deja el gasto en defensa en manos nacionales, y ese dinero acaba con demasiada frecuencia en sistemas no europeos.
articles.watch: La división entre frugales y el grupo de la cohesión en la cumbre de la semana próxima; qué parte del capítulo de defensa irá a compras europeas conjuntas (herramientas tipo EDIP/SAFE) y no a sobres nacionales.

articles.headline: Actualización: Europa cierra filas tras el complot de asesinato en Dinamarca; Macron habla de la «agresividad nueva» de Rusia
articles.summary:
**Ursula von der Leyen condenó el sábado «el intento de asesinato contra un ciudadano estadounidense-ucraniano en Dinamarca, orquestado por los servicios de inteligencia rusos.**

Ha sido un ataque en suelo de la UE. Y es inaceptable» (@vonderleyen). António Costa expresó la «plena solidaridad» de la UE con Mette Frederiksen (@eucopresident). En una declaración que @F_CEAFE reposteó, Emmanuel Macron afirmó que varios socios y aliados europeos habían sufrido en 24 horas «incidentes graves que denotan una agresividad nueva por parte de Rusia». Se solidarizó con Polonia, respaldó a Copenhague y calificó la estrategia rusa de «apuesta irresponsable» (@EmmanuelMacron; France 24, Le Parisien). El portavoz de la OTAN habló de «otra señal de la disposición de Rusia a poner en riesgo la seguridad en territorio aliado» (@NATOpress). Países Bajos, Noruega y el Reino Unido se pronunciaron en el mismo sentido. @F_CEAFE citó la declaración de Frederiksen: «La primera ministra danesa atribuye a Rusia un intento de asesinato de un ciudadano estadounidense-ucraniano en suelo danés».

**Contexto:** Sigue a la edición de las 20:30 y al Kh-101 caído en Polonia (14:30, tema 1). **Respuesta rusa:** en las publicaciones del Ministerio de Exteriores ruso leídas en este periodo no aparece reacción oficial a las acusaciones danesas. El ministerio protestó, en cambio, porque Rumanía negó visados a deportistas rusos menores de edad, y su embajada en Varsovia denunció el derribo previsto de un monumento soviético en Olsztyn (reposteado por @F_CEAFE).

**Fuentes:** [@vonderleyen](https://x.com/i/status/2124059842029531346), [@eucopresident](https://x.com/i/status/2123860656109559883), [@EmmanuelMacron](https://x.com/i/status/2123865506499252318), [@EmmanuelMacron](https://x.com/i/status/2123918493418721547), [@EmmanuelMacron](https://www.france24.com/fr/info-en-continu/20261120-macron-d%C3%A9nonce-un-agenda-agressif-de-la-russie-sur-le-territoire-europ%C3%A9en-un-pari-irresponsable), [@NATOpress](https://x.com/i/status/2123850200553042257), [primer ministro neerlandés](https://x.com/i/status/2123867744151986383), [Noruega](https://x.com/i/status/2123863606676865138), [Noruega](https://x.com/i/status/2123878345620476187), [cita de @F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/2123845911012938029), [Exteriores ruso sobre Rumanía](https://x.com/i/status/2124071933558026305), [Exteriores ruso sobre Rumanía](https://x.com/i/status/2123919216101212591), [Euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2124109099512275245)
articles.why: Por primera vez, la presidenta de la Comisión califica una operación de la inteligencia rusa de «ataque en suelo de la UE». Eso plantea una respuesta común de la UE (sanciones a agentes de inteligencia y límites a los viajes de ciudadanos rusos, como proponen Dinamarca y Polonia) en lugar de 27 expulsiones nacionales.
articles.watch: Las propuestas en el próximo Consejo de Asuntos Exteriores; una eventual réplica del Ministerio de Exteriores ruso o de su embajada a Copenhague.

articles.headline: La UE e Indonesia firman sus acuerdos de comercio e inversión tras diez años de negociación
articles.summary:
**Ursula von der Leyen lo anunció el sábado: «Tras diez años de negociaciones, lo hemos conseguido…**

Hemos firmado el Acuerdo de Asociación Económica Integral UE-Indonesia… que conecta a 730 millones de personas» (@vonderleyen). Firmaron el comisario de Comercio, Maroš Šefčovič, y el ministro de Comercio, Budi Santoso; el Acuerdo de Protección de Inversiones lo suscribió el ministro Airlangga Hartarto (CNBC Indonesia). Según el Consejo, cuando se aplique por completo se liberalizará hasta el 98,5 % de las líneas arancelarias y el 96 % de los aranceles indonesios desaparecerá en cinco años, con un ahorro de unos 600 millones de euros anuales en derechos. Los aranceles indonesios de hasta el 50 % a los coches europeos desaparecerán en cinco años y quedarán protegidas 221 indicaciones geográficas de la UE. El arroz, el azúcar y el etanol quedan excluidos, y el acuerdo incluye cooperación en energía y materias primas. El comercio bilateral ronda los 30.000 millones de dólares anuales (Airlangga).

**Contexto:** El Consejo autorizó la firma y la aplicación provisional el 18 de noviembre. Falta la aprobación del Parlamento Europeo. Ambas partes quieren aplicar el acuerdo de forma provisional a comienzos de 2027, cuando Indonesia salga del SPG de la UE (Consejo, CNBC Indonesia).

**Fuentes:** [@vonderleyen](https://x.com/i/status/2124111154100228461), [@vonderleyen](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/18/eu-indonesia-council-greenlights-signature-of-landmark-trade-and-investment-agreements/), [@vonderleyen](https://www.cnbcindonesia.com/news/20261121085713-4-787157/ieu-cepa-cepa-diteken-hari-ini-menko-airlangga-matangkan-implementasi), [@EU_Commission](https://x.com/i/status/2124050184212803956)
articles.why: Es un acuerdo comercial negociado a 27, con «450 millones de personas detrás», como recordó la Comisión esa misma mañana. Contrasta con el bilateralismo de «compradnos el 100 %» del tema 4. El acceso al níquel y a otras materias primas indonesias es un activo para la cadena de suministro europea de baterías y defensa.
articles.watch: La votación de aprobación en el Parlamento Europeo; cómo se aplica en la práctica el capítulo de materias primas; las reacciones de China y EE. UU.

articles.headline: ONU: bloqueo en la elección del próximo secretario general, con el veto de Reino Unido, Francia y China a la candidata emiratí; acuerdo para redactar normas sobre «robots asesinos» antes de 2028
articles.summary:
**En el noveno sondeo informal del Consejo de Seguridad, celebrado el viernes, la emiratí Lana Nusseibeh volvió a obtener siete votos de «apoyo», seis de «desaliento» y dos «sin opinión».**

Según Middle East Eye, tres de los votos de «desaliento» fueron de Reino Unido, Francia y China; el Guardian sostiene que Londres y París se opusieron por los presuntos vínculos de EAU con atrocidades en Sudán, algo que EAU niega. La favorita, Rebeca Grynspan (Costa Rica), logró diez votos de «apoyo», pero también dos de «desaliento» de miembros permanentes, que se atribuyen a Rusia y EE. UU. Rafael Grossi (Argentina) sumó tres de «desaliento» de miembros permanentes (Middle East Eye, Al-Monitor). Con más de 100 días, es la elección más larga de la historia de la ONU, y el mandato de Guterres termina el 31 de diciembre (Guardian). El embajador estadounidense Mike Waltz dice que Washington quiere un secretario general del hemisferio occidental (Al-Monitor). En Ginebra, la 7.ª Conferencia de Examen de la Convención sobre Ciertas Armas Convencionales (CCW) acordó, entre 128 partes, «elaborar» antes de 2028 un instrumento sobre sistemas de armas autónomas letales, sin comprometerse a un tratado jurídicamente vinculante (AFP, AP, Al Jazeera).

**Fuentes:** [middleeasteye.net](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/uk-france-and-china-vote-against-uaes-lana-nusseibeh-un), [theguardian.com](https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/20/uk-france-veto-uae-choice-lana-nusseibeh-next-un-secretary-general), [al-monitor.com](https://www.al-monitor.com/originals/2026/11/us-seeks-un-leader-western-hemisphere-says-waltz-amid-gridlock), [securitycouncilreport.org](https://www.securitycouncilreport.org/whatsinblue/2026/11/ninth-security-council-straw-poll-on-un-secretary-general-candidates.php), [@clashreport](https://x.com/i/status/2124106761330180332), [@clashreport](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/21/nations-agree-to-draft-rules-for-killer-robots-at-arms-control-summit), [@Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124106843068764211), [@UN_News_Centre / @UNGeneva](https://x.com/i/status/2124100655312941310)
articles.why: Francia y el Reino Unido usan aquí sus asientos permanentes con una línea distinta de la de Washington. En armas autónomas, la lentitud del consenso significa que serán las normas y la industria europeas, y no un tratado, las que decidan antes qué es aceptable en los campos de batalla de Europa.
articles.watch: El próximo sondeo; si surge un candidato de consenso antes del 31 de diciembre.

articles.headline: Irán: Araghchi da por descartado el memorando de Islamabad mientras Washington endurece la «Operación Economic Outcast»
articles.summary:
**El ministro iraní de Exteriores, Abbas Araghchi, afirmó que Teherán no aceptará un acuerdo «solo para salir del bloqueo actual» y que cualquier pacto debe impedir que se reanude la guerra (Al Jazeera, reposteado por @F_CEAFE).**

Según las crónicas de sus declaraciones, el memorando de entendimiento de Islamabad con Washington «ya no está sobre la mesa». Unos 400 kg de uranio enriquecido al 60 % «no saldrán» de Irán, aunque Teherán está abierto a una fórmula negociada dentro de un paquete más amplio (Al Jazeera; IRNA, medio estatal iraní). Trump dijo que Irán quiere un acuerdo, pero no en condiciones que Washington acepte (Reuters; Xinhua, medio estatal chino). El viernes, el Tesoro de EE. UU. sancionó a cuatro iraníes dentro de la «Operación Economic Outcast», entre ellos «fideicomisarios» del petróleo. Según Bessent, Irán «no tiene petróleo en el agua» fuera del bloqueo estadounidense (Tesoro/OFAC; reposteado por @F_CEAFE). IRNA lo califica de «campaña hostil». Las fuerzas iraníes aseguran haber derribado un MQ-9 estadounidense sobre el estrecho de Ormuz (Al Jazeera).
