articles.headline: Update: Russia hits Kyiv's bridges in mass missile and drone strike after Putin vows revenge for Crimean Bridge
articles.summary:
**Russia launched a large-scale missile and drone attack on Ukraine overnight into 20 November.**

In Kyiv, three employees of the city water utility were killed and about 15 people injured, and Mayor Vitali Klitschko reported that three bridges and critical infrastructure were damaged (https://x.com/i/status/2123652405220818965, https://x.com/i/status/2123643824824107089). Local reporting names the Podilsko-Voskresenskyi, Darnytskyi and Southern bridges across the Dnipro, with power, heat and water outages (Kyiv Independent, hromadske). Explosions were also heard in Lviv and Ivano-Frankivsk in western Ukraine shortly before 07:00 local time (https://x.com/i/status/2123643826539475177). The attack followed a day of Russian jet-drone raids on Kyiv and Putin's warning, delivered from China, that Russia's “response will be much more painful” after Ukraine's repeated strikes on the Crimean Bridge (quote relayed, https://x.com/i/status/2123505071464026290; original not checked this run). Russia's Defence Ministry (state source) claims it struck port infrastructure in the Odessa region, vessels “used in the interests of the AFU”, and defence-industry, energy and transport targets in Kyiv and five regions (TASS, t.me/s/tassagency_en). Earlier, EU High Representative Kaja Kallas said the EU would summon Russia's envoy over damage to European and other diplomatic premises in Kyiv (https://x.com/i/status/2123498192293490699).

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123652405220818965), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123643824824107089), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123643826539475177), [kyivindependent.com](https://kyivindependent.com/russia-launches-mass-missile-attack-against-ukraine-after-putin-vows-revenge/), [telegraph.co.uk](https://www.telegraph.co.uk/world-news/2026/11/20/russia-strikes-ukraine-kyiv-bridges/), [t.me](https://t.me/s/mod_russia_en), [t.me](https://t.me/s/tassagency_en)
articles.why: Striking bridges in a European capital is a deliberate escalation in the action–reaction cycle with Ukraine's deep strikes, and it lands while Europeans are funding Ukraine's 2026–27 needs almost alone. Damage to EU diplomatic premises makes the attacks a direct matter for the Union.
articles.watch: Final casualty toll and how long the bridges stay closed; Ukraine's air-defence figures; whether Kyiv answers with new deep strikes; the EU summons of the Russian envoy.

articles.headline: Ukrainian drones hit Russia's Dorogobuzh nitrate plant
articles.summary:
**Ukrainian attack drones struck the Dorogobuzh Nitrate Plant in Russia's Smolensk region on the evening of 19 November, according to @OSINTtechnical, which describes it as a major producer of nitrogen compounds used in explosives manufacturing and shared geolocated video (https://x.com/i/status/2123571745797841393).**

The Kyiv Independent reported that Ukrainian drones “reportedly” struck a Russian chemical plant (https://x.com/i/status/2123615348054188112). Defense News reports that Ukraine plans to double drone supplies and triple deep strikes with European support, despite Washington asking it to prioritise front-line defence (defensenews.com, Europe section).

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123571745797841393), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123615348054188112), [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/)
articles.why: Ukraine's long-range campaign against Russia's explosives supply chain is increasingly European-backed; it is also the trigger Moscow cites for its strikes on Kyiv (topic 1).
articles.watch: Official Ukrainian General Staff confirmation and damage assessment; Russian MoD claims of interceptions.

articles.headline: Yemen war: government forces battle the Houthis in Marib and Al-Jawf; Houthis claim new strikes on Riyadh and Jubail after the PIF Tower hit
articles.summary:
**The Yemen war goes on: the army of Yemen's Saudi-backed government says that, under Operation 'Dawn of Yemen', its forces are fighting the Houthi militia in northern Marib and south-eastern Al-Jawf with warplanes, drones and rockets, and has released footage of the combat ([@YemenAFMediaeng](https://x.com/i/status/2123479167794606091)); the Houthis, for their part, attacked government (PLC) positions in Raghwan, Marib (@war_noir).**

The war has now reached Saudi Arabia's financial heart: on 19 November a Houthi attack damaged several floors of the Public Investment Fund (PIF) Tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District, with no injuries reported by Saudi Civil Defence.

Yemen's Ansarallah (Houthis) said they targeted Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District twice on 19 November, the Sadara petrochemical complex in Jubail, Khamis Mushait air base and Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport (statement relayed by @MenchOsint, https://x.com/i/status/2123485617078095979). The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi drones heading for southern Saudi Arabia (https://x.com/i/status/2123597462405583248). Al-Masirah (Houthi-run) reported two Saudi airstrikes on Sanaa, including a warehouse hit for a second time (relayed by Tasnim, Iranian state-aligned). Egypt condemned the Houthi attacks on civilian and economic facilities in Riyadh (https://x.com/i/status/2123626804221239344).

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123485617078095979), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123597462405583248), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123626804221239344), [t.me](https://t.me/s/Tasnimnews_en)
articles.why: The Saudi–Houthi war is spreading to the Gulf's economic centres and energy plants, close to the Red Sea and Hormuz routes that carry Europe's trade and energy.
articles.watch: Damage confirmation at Jubail; further alerts over Riyadh; any Houthi move against Red Sea shipping.

articles.headline: Update: US widens Iran blockade to ship-to-ship transfers; Mossad chief pressed for new campaign; Iran weighs tanker “swarm”
articles.summary:
**The US has expanded its blockade of Iranian ports to include any ship that receives cargo by ship-to-ship transfer from a vessel loaded in Iran, according to a Joint Maritime Information Center advisory reported by USNI News (https://x.com/i/status/2123520682445398206).**

Since the blockade was reinstated in July, after the Iran–US memorandum of understanding failed, US ships have redirected about 150 vessels and disabled five (CENTCOM, 11 Nov). USNI counts 16 attacks on commercial shipping so far in November and 34 in October, the highest since the war began on 27 February; the IMO counts 25 seafarer deaths. The Wall Street Journal reported that Mossad chief Roman Goffman urged the Trump administration during a visit to Washington last week to launch a new multi-day air campaign against Iran (via Iran International, https://x.com/i/status/2123606354296508926). Israel's N12 says Tehran is considering a breakout attempt with loaded tankers (unconfirmed, https://x.com/i/status/2123493602399514661). Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said US allegations about Iranian biological or chemical weapons are a pretext for invasion, comparing them with Colin Powell's 2003 UN presentation (relayed by TASS, Russian state media). Iranian lawmaker Esmail Kowsari called on regional countries to push the United States out of the region (https://x.com/i/status/2123649834443845915).

**Sources:** [news.usni.org](https://news.usni.org/2026/11/19/u-s-expands-iranian-blockade-as-ship-attacks-continue), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123606354296508926), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123493602399514661), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123649834443845915), [t.me](https://t.me/s/tassagency_en)
articles.why: A wider blockade and talk of a new Israeli–US campaign keep Gulf energy flows at risk and raise the chance of new shocks to European fuel prices, while Europe has little say in the escalation.
articles.watch: Any Iranian tanker convoy towards the blockade line; US decisions on new strikes; UKMTO/JMIC incident reports.

articles.headline: Update: Iran war drains US munitions — GAO and CSIS warn
articles.summary:
**A Government Accountability Office study warns that “DoD does not have an overarching plan that links munitions production and funding to requirements”, and that the war on Iran is adding pressure to stockpiles (Defense News, https://x.com/i/status/2123492968522768473; Al Jazeera, https://x.com/i/status/2123608705459712098).**

A new CSIS report says the Iran war has strained US missile stocks, raising concerns about readiness for a possible conflict with China (https://x.com/i/status/2123528248634032617). A Pentagon nominee told senators the Iran war has cost the US over $48 billion in munitions, equipment replacement and operating expenses (relayed, https://x.com/i/status/2123520480715931711).

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123492968522768473), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123608705459712098), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123528248634032617), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123520480715931711)
articles.why: US munitions shortages compete directly with European orders and Ukraine's PURL deliveries. They show why Europe needs its own production capacity, built together, as no single member state can do it alone.
articles.watch: Reconciliation and appropriations figures for munitions; delivery delays to European customers.

articles.headline: European deterrence: first France–Sweden nuclear exercise
articles.summary:
**France and Sweden held their first joint nuclear-deterrence exercise; the defence ministries said it involved no actual nuclear weapons and was not aimed at any country (Defense News).**

An OSINT analyst found the French A330 MRTT tanker that supported the exercise, callsign TOTAL95, taking off from Istres nuclear air base on 16 November (https://x.com/i/status/2123516914379227166).

**Sources:** [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123516914379227166)
articles.why: French nuclear cooperation with a Nordic partner is a concrete step towards a European dimension of deterrence, built jointly rather than state by state.
articles.watch: Further European partners joining French deterrence exercises.

articles.headline: Putin vows “much more painful” retaliation for the Crimean Bridge strike, rules out an energy ceasefire
articles.summary:
**At his press conference closing the China visit, Putin said Russia's response to Ukraine's Neptune strike on the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge “will be much more painful than what Kyiv did to the Crimean Bridge”; the Kremlin's own channel quotes him: “The Crimean Bridge will be rebuilt…**

It all comes down to retaliation. And there will be retaliation.” He said Russia will protect drivers on the land route to Crimea (the “Novorossiya Highway”) while the bridge is repaired. Putin also said he had discussed a possible ceasefire in several areas with the Security Council, but after the bridge strike Russia will not negotiate any form of energy ceasefire (@ClashReport, @FaytuksNetwork). He added that Russia has invited EU representatives to Moscow to discuss security for Ukraine, Russia and Europe. A Western satellite image circulating on X shows the damaged road arch of the bridge (unverified).

**Sources:** [posts 8459–8464](https://t.me/s/news_kremlin_eng), [posts 8459–8464](https://x.com/i/status/2123413441989820688), [posts 8459–8464](https://x.com/i/status/2123413895725359512), [posts 8459–8464](https://x.com/i/status/2123461732756529484), [posts 8459–8464](https://x.com/i/status/2123464416108712094), [posts 8459–8464](https://t.me/s/tassagency_en)
articles.why: An announced reprisal raises the risk of a heavy Russian strike on Ukraine's energy grid as winter starts, precisely while the Coalition of the Willing meets (topic 2); the Moscow invitation is an attempt to split the EU from Kyiv.
articles.watch: Size and targets of the next Russian combined strike; repair timeline; EU reply to the Moscow invitation.

articles.headline: Russian drone damages the Dutch Embassy in Kyiv during hours-long daytime attack
articles.summary:
**A Russian drone struck or crashed in the courtyard of the Dutch Embassy in Kyiv on 19 November, damaging cars, a security post and the building's windows; it is unclear whether the area was targeted or the drone was shot down (Kyiv Independent, OSINTtechnical).**

Kyiv authorities report one man, 26, killed and four injured in the hours-long daytime drone attack, and a three-storey building hit in broad daylight. Russia's MoD (state source) claims daytime UAV strikes on port infrastructure and vessels “used in the interests of the AFU”.

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123402819344486736), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123419655846953333), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123430773130948913), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123454157583434191), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123419424174542977), [t.me](https://t.me/s/mod_russia_en)
articles.why: An EU member's embassy was hit days after Moscow's diplomatic attack on the Netherlands over Dutch firm Destinus and the Crimean Bridge strike (07:30 edition); watch for a Dutch and EU response.
articles.watch: Dutch government reaction; summoning of the Russian ambassador.

articles.headline: Update: Houthi strike on Riyadh's PIF Tower confirmed; Saudi Arabia “will not tolerate” attacks; GCC and Kuwait condemn
articles.summary:
**Saudi Civil Defence said a Houthi attack damaged several floors of a tower in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District and nearby buildings, with no injuries; the 80-storey Public Investment Fund Tower houses the $900 billion sovereign wealth fund (@ClashReport).**

Saudi Arabia's Foreign Ministry said it “will not tolerate” attacks on its territory. The GCC called it a dangerous escalation; Kuwait condemned Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia with ballistic and cruise missiles and drones. New alerts were sounded over Riyadh in the afternoon (Early warning).

**Sources:** [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123441993011376635), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123448848656023643), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123434361320034717), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123470449220661454), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123472072399634674), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123430570466128321)
articles.why: Houthi strikes on Gulf financial centres widen the Iran war's economic front and raise risks for Red Sea and Gulf shipping and energy supplies to Europe.
articles.watch: Saudi-led coalition retaliation in Yemen; further launches at Riyadh, Jizan and Abha.

articles.headline: Update: Iran — IRGC says blockade must end before any nuclear talks; oil-export breakout signals; Bloomberg: US strikes more likely
articles.summary:
**IRGC spokesman Hossein Mohebbi said Iran will not allow the US-imposed blockade to continue and will not discuss its nuclear programme until the Strait of Hormuz issue is resolved (Al Jazeera); IRNA (state agency) quotes the IRGC claiming a significant upgrade of air defences, and Iranian accounts relay a claim that missile range has risen to 4,500 km (unverified).**

The IRGC-affiliated Sabereen News says Iran is considering resuming oil exports despite the blockade, after TankerTrackers said Iran appears to be preparing to ship oil again. Bloomberg reports Western officials see an increased likelihood of renewed large-scale US strikes on Iran; Tasnim relays Trump telling Israel's Channel 12 there is “no rush” and “we'll see what happens after the new year begins”. At the IAEA Board, Iran's envoy Reza Najafi warned that information gathered at Iranian sites “will certainly be used for further attacks” and Iran rejected “unrestricted inspections under threat”.

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123438653946958109), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123474871707406629), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123395922306764992), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123478390283837780), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123432897206002124), [t.me](https://t.me/s/Irna_en), [t.me](https://t.me/s/Tasnimnews_en)
articles.why: A blockade-running attempt could trigger the next US–Iran clash at Hormuz; the E3 are directly involved at the IAEA Board.
articles.watch: Movement of Iranian tankers through Hormuz; IAEA Board resolution; US force posture.

articles.headline: Military movements: NATO surge over the Black Sea, Russian naval convoy in the Mediterranean, Turkish Black Sea base plan
articles.summary:
**Beyond the Early warning items, ItaMilRadar describes today's NATO air activity over the Black Sea as the heaviest in some time, combining drones, AWACS, tankers, SIGINT aircraft and fighters.**

In the Mediterranean, the frigate *Admiral Golovko* and the tanker *Yelnya* are being tracked moving east. A post relayed on the list says the Turkish Naval Forces plan a new Black Sea base, with 5,000 personnel to arrive in Rize for training and 500 apartments to be built (not checked against an official Turkish source). Russian Tu-95 bombers flew through Taiwan's ADIZ for the second time in three days.

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123477288088195346), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123451401766424649), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123456878071947753), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123425763932180760)
articles.why: NATO surveillance over the Black Sea coincides with Putin's retaliation threat and the Kerch strikes; the Russian presence in the Mediterranean touches Italy and Spain's area of interest.
articles.watch: Whether the Russian convoy heads for Tartus or Libya; Turkish MoD confirmation.

articles.headline: Defense News: Ukraine plans to double drone supplies and triple deep strikes, with European backing
articles.summary:
**Defense News reports Ukraine is pressing ahead with its long-range strike campaign with support from European partners, despite Washington asking Kyiv to prioritise front-line defence and mid-range strikes; Kyiv plans to double drone supplies and triple deep strikes.**

This is the new item in the defensenews.com Europe section this window.

**Sources:** [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/2026/11/19/ukraine-plans-to-double-drone-supplies-triple-deep-strikes/), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123407258813960409)
articles.why: European funding of Ukraine's deep-strike capacity (e.g. Destinus) is now a point of friction with Washington and a stated reason for Moscow's threats.
articles.watch: US reaction; European financing for long-range drones.

articles.headline: Update: Crimean Bridge rail span hit by Neptune missiles, Ukraine confirms; train traffic halted
articles.summary:
**Ukraine's Defence Ministry and General Staff confirmed that Navy Neptune coastal missile systems struck the railway section of the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge during the night of 19 November, with hits near the arch and on the tracks; all train traffic has been halted while damage is assessed.**

Kyiv Independent notes this comes less than two days after the previous strike. Ukraine's MoD framed it with the line “This train terminates here” / “Please vacate Crimea”.

**Sources:** [General Staff](https://x.com/i/status/2123370976901521851), [General Staff](https://x.com/i/status/2123377280835535131), [General Staff](https://x.com/i/status/2123376932628660411)
articles.why: The bridge is the main logistics link to Crimea; repeated strikes, together with Ukraine's deep strikes into Russia, are the backdrop to the US–Europe rift in Berlin (topic 3).
articles.watch: Russian MoD response and repair timeline; satellite imagery of the span.

articles.headline: Russia's overnight attack: 98 drones and Onyx missiles; daytime drone raid on Kyiv
articles.summary:
**Russian attacks killed 4 and injured 36 across Ukraine over the past day, including two children, per Kyiv Independent; Russian forces launched Onyx anti-ship missiles and 98 drones (Shahed-type, Gerbera and Parodiya decoys) overnight.**

Kyiv had a sixth air-raid alert of the day during a daytime drone attack, with roof fires in the Podilskyi and Desnianskyi districts; a strike on a residential building in Izium injured 12. Russia's MoD (state source) claims strikes on Ukrainian power and port infrastructure and on ships supporting Ukraine's forces; the Kursk governor says a Ukrainian attack injured 11 in Kursk (TASS, state agency, claim).

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123360600260567055), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123369123262746782), [t.me](https://t.me/s/mod_russia_en), [t.me](https://t.me/s/tassagency_en)
articles.why: The air-defence gap is the first of Zelensky's four priorities in Berlin today.
articles.watch: Whether the large bomber raid forecast for 18–19 November materialises tonight.

articles.headline: Update: Hormuz tanker war escalates — two more supertankers hit; Iran sets IAEA conditions
articles.summary:
**After the Army Navy's claim of three tankers hit by mines, the IRGC Navy says two more “violating” supertankers exploded near the southern coast of the Strait, alleging they were escorted by US fighters and surveillance drones while using a “prohibited route” (IRNA/IRGC claims).**

A drone strike on a tanker off Shinas (Oman) is also reported but unconfirmed. Tehran urged regional states to deny the US their territory for attacks, and IRNA reports that Iran, China and Russia set conditions for resuming IAEA verification (an end to hostile acts, among others).

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123356637708636173), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123363545140035709), [t.me](https://t.me/s/Irna_en), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123301910115680316)
articles.why: Energy supply and shipping insurance; Trump said today the US and China share an interest in keeping energy flowing through Hormuz.
articles.watch: UKMTO advisories (page unreadable without JS); ship names and flags; IAEA Board of Governors.

articles.headline: Space as a battlefield: MBDA and Atmos study orbital deep-strike; Italian space sigint by 2028
articles.summary:
**Defense News reports that MBDA and German start-up Atmos Space Cargo are teaming up to study deploying deep-strike weapons from Earth orbit using re-entry vehicles.**

Aviation Week reports that Italian sigint specialist VirtuaLabs aims to have the first of a space-based signals-intelligence constellation operational in 2028. In the US, Ursa Major and Avio USA won a joint Raytheon contract for a new Tomahawk solid-rocket booster, and Lockheed Martin tested the warhead of its low-cost PAC-3 ACE interceptor against Group 3 drones.

**Sources:** [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/2026/11/19/mbda-and-german-startup-atmos-team-up-to-study-space-based-strike-weapons/), [aviationweek.com](https://aviationweek.com/space/satellites/virtualabs-readies-sigint-satellites-2028-operations), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123388062814064786), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123377201328357565)
articles.why: A European industrial path to space-based strike and space ISR (positive intra-European capability), while Italian firms also feed US munitions chains (Avio USA).
articles.watch: Whether the MBDA study is tied to the European Long-Range Strike Approach (ELSA); counter-space implications.

articles.headline: Update: Houthi strike damages Riyadh's tallest tower; Saudis warn against filming impacts
articles.summary:
**The WSJ reports a projectile struck the tallest tower in Riyadh on Thursday, damaging multiple floors of a building that houses the sovereign-wealth fund (via @MenchOsint).**

New early-warning alerts were issued for Abha after launches from Yemen, and the Saudi government released an ad warning citizens not to film impacts or air-defence activity.

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123374353391796560), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123348386552135932), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123373971638768110)
articles.why: The Yemen front is now hitting Gulf financial centres; Red Sea and Gulf shipping risk.
articles.watch: Coalition retaliation in Saada; WSJ original (not checked this run).

articles.headline: Update: Israeli tanks east of Nuseirat in central Gaza
articles.summary:
**Israeli tanks moved east of the Nuseirat refugee camp, with witnesses reporting heavy shelling, gunfire and airstrikes, as the Israeli military said it had launched an operation in a Hamas-controlled area; strikes killed at least three people (France 24).**

**Sources:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123385967474004354)
articles.watch: Whether the central Gaza offensive, coordinated with the US, widens further.

articles.headline: Update: Trump weighs new strikes on Iran as Israel presses for a four- to seven-day air campaign
articles.summary:
**Trump is considering another round of major strikes on Iran, with Israel pushing for a four- to seven-day air campaign and warning that Iran is rebuilding its missile and drone arsenals, The New York Times reports (as relayed by @ClashReport and @KingstonAReif); Gulf leaders are urging restraint.**

Reuters reports that Israel's spy chief lobbied for joint strikes during a visit to Washington. Trump called the memorandum of understanding that JD Vance negotiated with Iran “a waste of time”, said he would wage the war again, and that talks continue but he wants a “lasting” deal (Al Jazeera, @atrupar). He also claimed Iran is “looking at gas” and biological weapons and threatened to “wipe them out” if a dirty-bomb attack happened, while saying Washington residents need not worry. US intelligence director Jay Clayton told lawmakers Iranian threats to Americans have “increased substantially” (Reuters), while Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there is no imminent dirty-bomb threat (Anadolu).

**Sources:** [NYT via @ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123252866982752289), [NYT via @ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123271548987474370), [@KingstonAReif](https://x.com/i/status/2123252413695967338), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123161868072042593), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123223482032922922), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2123246014513741880), [@atrupar](https://x.com/i/status/2123217195870076992), [Anadolu](https://x.com/i/status/2123130368215662668), [@HormuzLetter](https://x.com/i/status/2123176962990424523)
articles.why: A new US–Israeli air campaign would hit Gulf energy flows again, and Europe would bear the cost without having any say in the decision.
articles.watch: Any White House decision after Shenzhen; Iranian reaction (IRNA, Tasnim); tanker movements.

articles.headline: Update: Three tankers on fire after hitting mines east of Hormuz; Iran says it struck US Patriot batteries in Kuwait
articles.summary:
**Iran's army says three oil tankers caught fire after hitting naval mines east of the Strait of Hormuz (Al Jazeera); UKMTO issued warning 212-26 the same evening (as quoted by @MenchOsint; the UKMTO page was not readable).**

Iran says its forces struck US Patriot air-defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms in Kuwait in “self-defence”; Kuwait condemned the attacks as a violation of its sovereignty (Anadolu). Tasnim (Iranian state agency) mocks Trump's “imaginary control” over the Strait, saying ships hit mines or projectiles there “multiple times a day”. Iraq has reopened its oil pipeline to Turkey to bypass the disruption (Euronews).

**Sources:** [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2123158454747681034), [Al Jazeera](https://aje.news/bfbnk1), [@MenchOsint citing UKMTO](https://x.com/i/status/2123182951705739735), [Anadolu](https://x.com/i/status/2123178183411294680), [Tasnim](https://t.me/s/Tasnimnews_en), [Euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2123118075369111592), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123122776341131600)
articles.why: The Americas can shield themselves from Hormuz; Europe cannot. Mines in the shipping lanes keep raising the cost of the Gulf energy Europe relies on.
articles.watch: Names and flags of the mined tankers; CENTCOM comment on the Kuwait claim.

articles.headline: Update: Ukraine hits the Crimean Bridge again; rail span reportedly struck and rail traffic suspended
articles.summary:
**Ukrainian forces hit the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge again just after midnight local time on 19 November, less than two days after the 17 November strike collapsed an entire section of it, Russian-installed Crimea head Sergey Aksyonov confirmed (Kyiv Independent).**

OSINT accounts report drones and cruise missiles scored multiple hits on the remaining rail span and that rail traffic was suspended (@Osinttechnical); the Kyiv Independent could not verify the damage. Ukraine reportedly used domestically built airborne relays (“flying modems”) to guide the 17 November strike without Starlink (@ClashReport, citing a report). The Russian embassy in the Netherlands asked whether The Hague is “openly joining the conflict” after the Dutch firm Destinus said its missiles were used against the bridge. France 24 has fact-checked fake damage videos circulating after the attack.

**Sources:** [Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/ukrainian-forces-once-more-hit-russias-crimean-bridge-days-after-devastating-strike/), [@Osinttechnical](https://x.com/i/status/2123224949082968296), [CNN](https://x.com/i/status/2123220150132330692), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123137386590900526), [@MilitarySummary on the Russian embassy](https://x.com/i/status/2123104358623592651), [France 24](https://x.com/i/status/2123172509088628903)
articles.why: A European-made missile helped cut Russia's main land link to Crimea. That is what European industry can do once it gets the orders, and it explains why Moscow is now going after the Netherlands.
articles.watch: Russian MoD statement and satellite imagery of the rail span; Russian retaliation against Kyiv's bridges (The Economist reports seven ballistic missile strikes on two Kyiv bridges, via @MilitarySummary).

articles.headline: Musk says Starlink will not serve offensive strikes as NATO launches STARLIFT for military satellite launches
articles.summary:
**Elon Musk said Zelensky has asked to use Starlink's commercial satellites for offensive military actions and SpaceX has declined “from the beginning of this conflict”; he said Starlink is a civilian system and offensive drone strikes need the military Starshield, denied ever turning Starlink off, and, asked about Zelensky's claim that Starshield was slowed down, said “Zelensky is not always truthful” (interview clips via @ClashReport).**

He also said “if we were to turn off Starlink, the entire Ukrainian front would collapse”. Separately, NATO formally launched STARLIFT at NATO EDGE 26 in Izmir, an initiative to secure slots on commercial rockets for military satellites, including short-notice launches, through a network of spaceports in the Alliance and South Korea (NATO). Ten NATO members finance it through NSPA: Belgium, Canada, Finland, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway, Sweden, Türkiye and the UK, plus South Korea; France, Spain, Luxembourg, Hungary and the US are not among the funders (NATO, SpaceQ).

**Sources:** [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123267369997074712), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123271234012197139), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123266243734175882), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2123264819704823930), [NATO](https://www.nato.int/en/news-and-events/articles/news/2026/11/17/natos-multinational-space-initiative-starlift-begins), [Anadolu](https://www.aa.com.tr/en/world/nato-launches-multinational-initiative-to-secure-military-satellite-launches/4129426), [SpaceQ](https://spaceq.ca/nato-starlift-begins/)
articles.why: The owner of a foreign private network says he decides which military uses Ukraine may make of it, and that the front depends on him. This is the kill-switch risk in its purest form, and it shows why Europe needs IRIS² and its own launchers. STARLIFT pools demand, but without France and Spain among its funders, it is no substitute for a single EU space policy.
articles.watch: Kyiv's response to Musk; CSIS Space Strategic Dialogue on 19 November (spacecraft threat discrimination).

articles.headline: Update: Houthis fire at Riyadh and Jizan; coalition reports damage in Riyadh and strikes Saada
articles.summary:
**Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed cruise-missile strikes on Riyadh airport and the King Abdullah Financial District, several ballistic missiles at a “vital site” in Jizan and a drone at Khamis Mushait air base (as relayed by @MenchOsint).**

The Saudi-led coalition says a Houthi missile threat toward Riyadh caused damage (Reuters) and that it destroyed a ballistic-missile launch platform in Saada (Al Jazeera). Al Masirah (Houthi) says Saudi warplanes bombed the Sahar area of Saada (via Tasnim, Iranian state agency).

**Sources:** [@MenchOsint citing @Yah_Saree](https://x.com/i/status/2123150991608414350), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123257580298416585), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2123209953553055931), [Tasnim](https://t.me/s/Tasnimnews_en)
articles.why: Missile fire at the Saudi capital's airport and financial district shows the Yemen war widening at the same time as Hormuz, with both chokepoints on Europe's route to Asia and the Gulf now under threat.
articles.watch: Saudi statement on the damage in Riyadh; flight disruptions.

articles.headline: Update: Israel's central Gaza offensive goes on for days, coordinated with the US; Katz vows indefinite occupation
articles.summary:
**Israel coordinated its offensive in central Gaza with the US and expects it to last several days, Israeli Army Radio reports (Anadolu); forces have advanced beyond the ceasefire's “yellow line” and taken sections of Salah al-Din Road (Al Jazeera).**

UN humanitarian officials say Palestinians are fleeing Deir al-Balah (Xinhua). Defence Minister Israel Katz vowed to occupy Gaza, Lebanon and Syria indefinitely and threatened to expand the occupied territory if fighting escalates (Al Jazeera). Palestinian Islamic Jihad and Hezbollah called the operation a “flagrant violation” of the ceasefire. In southern Lebanon, Israeli excavators demolished homes in Zawtar al-Sharqiye (Al Jazeera).

**Sources:** [Anadolu](https://x.com/i/status/2123231092089950471), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2123125335428641003), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2123127851176346018), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2123122818179080254), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2123136747060236553), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2123176518247485514)
articles.why: A fourth active front, next to Iran, Yemen and Lebanon, pushes the EU's southern neighbourhood further towards permanent war. Europe is the Palestinians' largest donor, yet it has no seat on the US-led Board of Peace.
articles.watch: Reactions from Egypt and Qatar (mediators) and from the EU High Representative.

articles.headline: Update: US Navy stretches destroyer tours to hold the Iran blockade as Hormuz insurance reaches $64m a transit
articles.summary:
The US Navy is extending destroyer deployments from six to at least 11 months to sustain the naval blockade of Iran, which needs 17 destroyers, Acting Navy Secretary Hung Cao told sailors' families (MS NOW, via Clash Report). At his Senate confirmation hearing he said insuring a single commercial ship through the Strait of Hormuz now costs $64 million, against $54,000 a year ago (Al Jazeera); the 20:30 edition of 17 November had reported this figure only as an unconfirmed post. Clarksons Research counts 47 VLCCs damaged in attacks across the wider Middle East since March, six of them in the first half of November. CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper met IDF Chief of Staff Eyal Zamir and Mossad chief Roman Gofman in Israel on 18 November, and Reuters reports that the Mossad chief lobbied in Washington for joint strikes on Iran. CENTCOM says no US personnel were injured in Iranian attacks this week, contradicting OSINT claims about Ali Al Salem (Kuwait).

**Sources:** MS NOW via Clash Report ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123063066203959768)), [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/18/us-official-says-hormuz-insurance-hits-64m-is-the-strait-really-open), Reuters ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123099153991438735)), Clarksons Research via @Schizointel ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123088217679249564)), CENTCOM via @DefenceGeek ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123112880447111281)).
articles.why: Gulf oil exports have reportedly fallen by almost half in two weeks, so Europe's energy bill is tied to a war it does not steer. A blockade that needs 17 US destroyers is also US naval mass that is not in the Atlantic or the Mediterranean.
articles.watch: Pentagon confirmation of the tour extensions; JMIC guidance on ship-to-ship transfers; further tanker strikes (NAVIG8 MESSI reported hit).

articles.headline: Ukraine strikes a bridge in occupied Luhansk and hits Krasnodar refineries again
articles.summary:
Ukraine's General Staff says it struck a bridge near Stanytsia Luhanska in occupied Luhansk Oblast, used by Russian forces to move ammunition, fuel and equipment, and damaged three Russian military aircraft (Kyiv Independent). Ukraine's Defence Ministry said its strikes again hit two key refineries in Krasnodar Krai. Russia's Defence Ministry said it shot down 51 Ukrainian drones over Krasnodar Krai and the Sea of Azov in 12 hours (Russian claim). After the Kerch strike, OSINT accounts say Crimean rail traffic stops at Kerch and the Armyansk and Tokmak lines are out of service (unverified). A Ukrainian officer told The Times that Ukraine guided its missiles onto the Crimean Bridge with its own communications system, not Starlink or Starshield.

**Sources:** Kyiv Independent ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123074194300699093)), @DefenceU ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123105022720290971)), Russian MoD via @MilitarySummary ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123108854548373837)), The Times via Clash Report ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123030962925621721)).
articles.why: Ukraine is running this campaign with its own guidance links rather than US satellite services. The strikes push the war up a level just as the talks begin; CEAFE's line is that escalation weakens Ukraine, Russia and the EU alike.
articles.watch: Satellite imagery of the bridge and refineries; Russian retaliation (see next story).

articles.headline: Update: Russian strikes kill at least five across Ukraine and hit a Kyiv high-rise
articles.summary:
Russian air attacks across Ukraine killed at least five people, according to Ukrainian authorities (Al Jazeera). In Kyiv, drones injured three people and hit a 28-storey residential building, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said. OSINT accounts say a jet-powered Geran drone hit a hangar at Hostomel holding the An-124 UR-82009 (unverified). This follows the 13:30 edition's report on Odesa: Russia's Defence Ministry says the ship it hit was carrying "military-purpose cargo" to Odesa, without naming it. OSINT trackers claim Russia is preparing a large strike with Tu-160 and Tu-95MS bombers (unconfirmed).

**Sources:** [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/11/18/russian-attacks-on-ukraine-kill-at-least-five-people), [Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/russia-attacks-kyiv-with-drones-injures-3-hits-28-story-residential-building/), Russian Defence Ministry (state source), @AMK_Mapping_, @MilitarySummary ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123098815465144373)).
articles.why: Attacks on shipping to Odesa threaten Black Sea trade routes, a day after the LPG carrier GAS HUSKY sank in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone.
articles.watch: A possible large missile raid overnight; the identity of the cargo ship.

articles.headline: Update: Saudi Arabia prepares for a Yemen war lasting into 2027
articles.summary:
Saudi Arabia expects its campaign against Yemen's Houthis to run well into 2027, Reuters reports, citing two Western officials, despite setbacks and Houthi attacks on Saudi cities, including Aramco's Riyadh headquarters. Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed 87 Saudi air strikes in 24 hours on Sanaa and other provinces, using F-15 and Typhoon aircraft (Houthi claim, not verified). France 24 analyses why the Houthis may besiege Aden rather than storm it.

**Sources:** Reuters ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123106527343001734)), Clash Report ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123060740579790908)), @Yah_Saree ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123102966521397448)), France 24 ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123085489553166427)).
articles.why: A longer Yemen war keeps the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb at risk at the same time as Hormuz: the two chokepoints of Europe's trade with Asia and its Gulf energy. The Typhoon is a European-built fighter (Eurofighter: Airbus, BAE Systems, Leonardo).
articles.watch: Houthi pressure on Aden; more missile fire at Riyadh.

articles.headline: Israel launches its first major ground push in central Gaza since the October 2025 ceasefire
articles.summary:
The Israeli military said its forces and the Shin Bet launched an intensive operation in central Gaza, west of the "yellow line". Analysts say tanks and armoured bulldozers crossed the line around Nuseirat and Al-Bureij, the first major ground offensive since October 2025. Al Jazeera reported an Israeli air strike in central Gaza that killed one person. Palestinian Islamic Jihad and the Houthi-run Yemeni foreign ministry say the operation violates the ceasefire and the Sharm el-Sheikh agreement (IRNA and Tasnim, Iranian state agencies).

**Sources:** @mazzenilsson ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123046776059916636)), Al Jazeera ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123030543604306113)), IRNA, Tasnim.
articles.why: A collapse of the Gaza ceasefire would add a front to the Iran and Yemen wars and strain the EU's Middle East policy.
articles.watch: An official Israeli statement on the scope; reaction from the mediators (Egypt, Qatar, US).

articles.headline: China launches a second Type 095 nuclear attack submarine, according to an OSINT account
articles.summary:
The OSINT account @PLA_MilitaryUpd says China has launched a second Type 095 nuclear attack submarine, citing Janes, and counts five Type 095/09X boats launched this year. The claim has not been independently verified.

**Sources:** @PLA_MilitaryUpd ([post](https://x.com/i/status/2123020881412890741)).
articles.why: China's naval build-up shapes how much US naval power remains available for Europe.
articles.watch: Janes' confirmation and imagery.

items.title: Conflicts — 2026-11-18 13:30
headlines: Update: Hormuz shipping attacks mount as Gulf states condemn Iran's strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain
Poland reportedly foiled a Russian false-flag plot on the Kaliningrad border
Russia strikes central Odesa and claims hits on Izmail port and a cargo ship
Germany backs Ukrainian findings of Russian chemical weapons use and seeks accountability at the OPCW
Update: Houthis fire a cruise missile at Riyadh and threaten Aden
Ukraine's drones hit Krasnodar refineries as Russia reports record interceptions

articles.headline: Update: Hormuz shipping attacks mount as Gulf states condemn Iran's strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain
articles.summary:
New since the 07:30 edition: ADNOC said one of its vessels was attacked crossing the Strait of Hormuz, injuring 11 crew with one missing, and UKMTO logged a delayed report of a tanker hit by a projectile 13 nm north of Khasab. Kuwait, the GCC Secretary-General, Qatar and the UAE condemned Iran's drone attacks, while Iran's army chief warned of a response “without geographical restrictions” and Tehran claimed it shot down a US MQ-9. Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi dismissed CNN and New York Times reports of an Iranian “dirty bomb” plot against Washington as “rubbish” (IRNA); France 24 reports Trump said the reports are being taken seriously, while Rubio earlier said he saw no imminent threat to the capital (Reuters).

**Key facts.** 11 injured, 1 missing on the ADNOC ship (Al Jazeera); incident 13 nm N of Khasab (UKMTO via Tasnim); Gulf bourses mostly fell (Reuters, https://x.com/i/status/2122983198401482978); a US court sentenced Pakistani businessman Asif Merchant to more than 27 years over a plot he said was directed by Iran's Revolutionary Guard (Anadolu); Qatar's PM said diplomatic efforts for an Iran–US agreement continue (IRNA). The US Navy chief was criticised at a hearing over the Iran war and its toll on sailors (Reuters headline; article returned 401). An IISS Strategic Dossier argues Hormuz cannot easily be reopened by military means against Iran's asymmetric threats (@IISS_org).

**Sources:** [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2122954637150236892) ([2](https://x.com/i/status/2122950475049812314), [3](https://x.com/i/status/2122970567481659743), [4](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2026/11/18/iran-war-live-kuwait-says-intercepting-hostile-drone-attacks)), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2122929041288372363) ([2](https://x.com/i/status/2122937895962984821), [3](https://x.com/i/status/2122921491587010836)), [France 24](https://x.com/i/status/2122993594604650782), [Anadolu](https://x.com/i/status/2122978367372984748), [IRNA (Iranian state agency)](https://t.me/s/Irna_en), [Tasnim (Iranian state agency)](https://t.me/s/Tasnimnews_en), [@IISS_org](https://x.com/i/status/2122961521739259966)
articles.why: European energy prices and shipping insurance depend on a strait where, according to Atlantic Council analyst Elisabeth Braw, US naval escorts cannot protect every vessel. Europe has no naval or diplomatic role of its own in the escalation; Qatar, not the EU, is the mediator Tehran cites.
articles.watch: Names of the struck ships and casualty figures; US confirmation or denial of the MQ-9 loss and of casualties at Ali Al Salem; whether Hormuz is raised at the Shenzhen trilateral.

articles.headline: Poland reportedly foiled a Russian false-flag plot on the Kaliningrad border
articles.summary:
Polish daily Rzeczpospolita, citing senior security sources, reports that Russian intelligence planned a sabotage operation on Polish territory near Kaliningrad in late October or early November, possibly a border crossing and a staged attack, to be blamed on Ukraine with mass casualties. One source compared it to the 1939 Gleiwitz provocation; the stated aim was to halt aid to Kyiv. Warnings came from allied services and Polish analysts, and were also passed to Lithuania, Latvia and Estonia. Tomasz Siemoniak, Poland's minister coordinating the special services, confirmed extra measures “because we considered the threat real” but would not confirm details and cautioned that undisclosed assessments are not established facts.

**Key facts.** About 180 police from prevention units, counter-terrorism teams, extra Border Guard and Internal Security Agency officers, and GROM, NIL and AGAT special forces deployed to Warmia-Masuria (Rzeczpospolita via Hromadske, Ukrainska Pravda, Polsat). On 3 November Prime Minister Donald Tusk reported “suspicious movement” on the Kaliningrad border (Meduza). No evidence has been published by Polish authorities; list members @mazzenilsson and @GeromanAT called the report unproven.

**Sources:** [Hromadske](https://hromadske.ua/en/europa/274576-poland-thwarted-suspected-russian-false-flag-plot-to-blame-ukraine-for-deadly-attack-report-says), [Meduza](https://meduza.io/en/news/2026/11/18/russia-planned-false-flag-operation-with-mass-casualties-on-polish-territory-rzeczpospolita-reports), [Ukrainska Pravda](https://www.pravda.com.ua/eng/news/2026/11/18/8063407/), [Onet](https://wiadomosci.onet.pl/kraj/rosyjska-prowokacja-na-granicy-z-polska-dziennikarze-ujawniaja-kulisy-operacji/j448987), [Polsat News](https://www.polsatnews.pl/wiadomosc/2026-11-18/rosja-chciala-przeprowadzic-dywersje-w-polsce-miala-przypominac-prowokacje-gliwicka/), [@InsiderGeo](https://x.com/i/status/2122980716698869763), [@mazzenilsson](https://x.com/i/status/2122997817312440792)
articles.why: A staged incident on an EU and NATO border is the kind of provocation that could drag Europe into the war. It also shows that Poland and the Baltic states relied on allied intelligence warnings: a case for pooled European intelligence and border protection rather than 27 separate systems.
articles.watch: Any official Polish or Baltic statement with evidence; Russian MFA reaction (none on its Telegram channel at time of writing).

articles.headline: Russia strikes central Odesa and claims hits on Izmail port and a cargo ship
articles.summary:
Russia repeatedly struck central Odesa on 18 November, killing 4 and injuring 9 according to the Kyiv Independent's updated count. Ukraine's Air Force said Russia launched 141 long-range attack drones overnight, 73 of them jet-powered, and Russian attacks killed 5 and injured 15 across Ukraine over the past day, including a strike on a market in Zlatopil (Kharkiv Oblast) that injured at least 11. Russia's Defence Ministry said its drones hit port facilities in Izmail used for military cargo and, at sea, a dry-cargo ship it says carried dual-use cargo to the port of Yuzhny (Russian state source, claim).

**Key facts.** 141 drones incl. 73 jet-powered (Ukrainian Air Force via Kyiv Independent); 4 killed, 9 injured in Odesa; Zlatopil hit for the second time in seven days. Russian MoD: Izmail port infrastructure and a dry-cargo ship bound for Yuzhny hit (name not given).

**Sources:** [Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/russian-strikes-central-odesa-kills-3-injures-7/) ([2](https://kyivindependent.com/russian-attacks-kill-5-injure-15-across-ukraine-over-past-day-as-russia-continues-energy-assault/), [3](https://x.com/i/status/2122992024999592181)), [Russian Ministry of Defence (Russian state source)](https://t.me/s/mod_russia_en)
articles.why: Izmail sits on the Danube opposite Romania, and the Odesa ports are Ukraine's link to EU markets; with GAS HUSKY sunk in Bulgaria's EEZ (07:30 edition), the maritime war is moving closer to EU waters. CEAFE's line: these are reasons for a pan-European negotiated peace involving Ukraine, Russia and the EU, not for further escalation.
articles.watch: Identity and flag of the ship Russia says it hit; Romanian reaction to strikes on Izmail.

articles.headline: Germany backs Ukrainian findings of Russian chemical weapons use and seeks accountability at the OPCW
articles.summary:
Germany's Foreign Ministry accused Russia of “grave breaches of the Chemical Weapons Convention” and said Moscow must be held accountable at the OPCW. A 76-page Ukrainian investigation, carried out with OPCW technical assistance, concludes that a drone dropped an RG-Vo grenade containing CS gas into a Ukrainian trench near Illinka on 20 September 2024, and that this was part of an organised system of manufacture, supply and use. Ukraine says it has documented 14,009 cases; Russia denies using chemical weapons and accuses Ukraine of doing so.

**Key facts.** Incident 20 September 2024 near Illinka (Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant area); OPCW circulated the report to States Parties this week; New Zealand also said it was “deeply concerned” (RNZ).

**Sources:** [Anadolu (Turkish state agency)](https://aa.com.tr/en/europe/germany-accuses-russia-of-using-prohibited-chemicals-against-ukraine/4128823) ([2](https://x.com/i/status/2123000780739273167)), [UPI](https://www.upi.com/Top_News/World-News/2026/11/18/ukraine-Russia-chemical-weapons/8141794983599/), [RNZ](https://www.rnz.co.nz/news/politics/2660780/deeply-concerned-peters-reacts-to-russia-s-chemical-weapons-attacks)
articles.why: Chemical-weapons attribution is one of the few legal tools Europe can use collectively; the OPCW's annual conference next week gives the EU a chance to speak with one voice.
articles.watch: Attribution vote at the OPCW conference; Russian MFA response.

articles.headline: Update: Houthis fire a cruise missile at Riyadh and threaten Aden
articles.summary:
New since the 07:30 edition: the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed a Houthi cruise missile launched toward the Riyadh region (coalition spokesman Turki al-Maliki via Anadolu). Reuters reports Houthi forces are threatening Aden after capturing territory along Yemen's Red Sea coast, raising concerns for the Saudi-backed government and for shipping through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait. Al Jazeera details how the Houthis raise funds for the war through rallies and donations of cash and weapons.

**Sources:** [Anadolu (Turkish state agency)](https://x.com/i/status/2122982750042898856) ([2](https://x.com/i/status/2122932955651756408)), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2122926524680622252), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2122958857945399309), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2122976418149650589)
articles.why: With Hormuz contested, the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb are Europe's other energy and trade artery; Houthi control of more of the coast puts the EU's naval operation Aspides and Suez traffic at greater risk.
articles.watch: Fighting around Aden; UKMTO advisories for the southern Red Sea.

articles.headline: Ukraine's drones hit Krasnodar refineries as Russia reports record interceptions
articles.summary:
Two oil refineries in Krasnodar Krai's Seversky district, Ilsky and Afipsky, were reportedly targeted in an overnight Ukrainian drone attack on 17–18 November (Kyiv Independent). Russia's Defence Ministry said it intercepted 184 Ukrainian fixed-wing drones overnight over Belgorod, Rostov, Krasnodar, Crimea and the Sea of Azov, and 310 over the past day; Krasnodar officials reported four people injured and fires at two industrial sites (TASS). Ukrainian MP Fyodor Venislavsky said, citing Ukrainian intelligence, that Russia is testing a Geran-6 drone with speeds of up to 1,000 km/h (via @MilitarySummary).

**Key facts.** 184 drones claimed overnight and 310 over 24 hours (Russian MoD, state source); refineries repeatedly targeted before (Kyiv Independent). Reuters describes Ukraine's “Operation Vivaldi” combining ground robots, drones and jamming to repel Russian assaults.

**Sources:** [Kyiv Independent](https://x.com/i/status/2122917678767824980), [TASS (Russian state agency)](https://t.me/s/tassagency_en), [@MilitarySummary via @GeromanAT](https://x.com/i/status/2122971269188448396), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2122959240381759927)
articles.why: The tit-for-tat energy war keeps oil prices volatile and raises the risk of escalation. CEAFE's line: report the strikes neutrally and push for a pan-European ceasefire framework rather than more long-range weapons.
articles.watch: Damage at Ilsky/Afipsky (satellite imagery); any confirmation of a Geran-6 in combat.

Pentagon criticises Ukraine's deep strikes, and Germany and the UK push back
LPG carrier GAS HUSKY sinks in Bulgaria's EEZ after drone attack
UK hands US Army officer held for alleged spying for Russia to US military

articles.headline: Update: Iran widens attacks to Kuwait and Bahrain as US strikes Qeshm
articles.summary:
**Iran's army said it launched drones at US drone and missile installations at Kuwait's Ali al-Salem Air Base, according to IRNA, after Kuwait reported its air defences engaging hostile drones.**

Bahrain's Defence Force accused Iran of ongoing attacks and said air defences intercepted several Iranian aerial attacks before an all-clear. An OSINT timeline (@FaytuksNetwork) lists Iranian attacks on Bahrain at 07:00Z, a US strike on Qeshm around 13:00Z, Iran on Kuwait at 21:40Z and on Bahrain again at 23:10Z on 17 November. A US official described the Qeshm strikes as a response to Iranian aggression; Iranian media say they caused no infrastructure damage. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Iran poses no “imminent threat” to the US and dismissed a report of a possible dirty-bomb plot; Iran's government, via IRNA, called the “dirty bomb” story a fabricated pretext for aggression.

**Sources:** [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2122910107323482308), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2122892640869871910), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2122848296947364347), [Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2122844735685750957), [Anadolu](https://x.com/i/status/2122869901652341066), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2122869969654272465), [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2122875004190683166), [t.me](https://t.me/s/Irna_en), [@FaytuksNetwork](https://x.com/i/status/2122844168468967668), [@ClashReport](https://x.com/i/status/2122827840584380447), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2122831937685291330)
articles.why: The war around Hormuz keeps tanker traffic and energy prices hostage, and Europe is again a bystander: the escalation is managed between Washington and Tehran, with the EU absent from both the fighting and the bargaining.
articles.watch: Kuwaiti and US damage reports from Ali al-Salem; whether Iran keeps striking several Gulf states a day; any Hormuz item at the Trump–Xi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen.

articles.headline: Update: Destinus (Netherlands) says its Ruta missiles hit the Kerch bridge
articles.summary:
**Destinus, a Dutch-headquartered start-up, said Ukraine fired nine of its Ruta Block 1 cruise missiles at the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge and that seven hit it.**

Its president, Oleksandr Danyliuk, told Reuters they were the only foreign-made weapons used in the strike, alongside the company's Da Vinci (“Lord”) deep-strike drones; Ukraine's FP-5 Flamingo missiles by Fire Point were also used (@sentdefender, video of three Flamingo launches). New footage shows the main road span collapsing after a missile impact (@OSINTtechnical). OSINT accounts also report the destruction of the Mius River road bridge on the R-280 highway, which cuts the safer coastal route between Rostov and the occupied south, and list most road and rail links into Crimea as cut or damaged, with ferries still running (@Schizointel).

**Sources:** [Reuters via Euronext](https://live.euronext.com/en/financial-news/european-made-ruta-missiles-only-foreign-weapons-used-ukraines-crimean-bridge-strike), [Defence Blog](https://defence-blog.com/destinus-says-seven-ruta-missiles-hit-putins-bridge/), [@sentdefender](https://x.com/i/status/2122816640228155627), [@sentdefender](https://x.com/i/status/2122806225482252400), [@OSINTtechnical](https://x.com/i/status/2122862620479049891), [@Schizointel](https://x.com/i/status/2122791371237150728), [@Schizointel](https://x.com/i/status/2122774966597030168), [@FaytuksNetwork citing The Guardian and The Times](https://x.com/i/status/2122858362006294721), [Destinus newsroom](https://www.destinus.com/press/news)
articles.why: It is a rare operational role for a European-made long-range weapon in this war: a system designed and produced in Europe (Destinus' newsroom presents Ruta B1 as “the production system behind 1,750 missiles”), not dependent on US export permission. CEAFE's line on the war remains a negotiated, pan-European peace with Ukraine, Russia and the EU at the table; the strike also raises the risk of Russian retaliation against European firms.
articles.watch: Russian MoD/MFA reaction naming Destinus or the Netherlands (none found on their Telegram channels at time of writing); repairs and ferry capacity to Crimea.

articles.headline: Pentagon criticises Ukraine's deep strikes, and Germany and the UK push back
articles.summary:
**At the Ukraine Defense Contact Group in NATO headquarters on 17 November, US Under Secretary of War for Policy Elbridge Colby said Ukraine's deep strikes “have not been effective in driving an end to the war” nor in blunting Russia's advances, and warned that strikes on commercial targets such as Wildberries warehouses could stiffen Russian resolve (Reuters, via Kyiv Independent).**

German Defence Minister Boris Pistorius called that criticism “quite a stupid thing”, and UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting said the strikes had weakened Russian capabilities, bought time and saved lives. Colby said Western aid should prioritise front-line defence and medium-range strike. Separately, the Kyiv Independent reports a draft under which the European Commission would propose an extra €45 billion in loans to Ukraine in 2027.

**Sources:** [Kyiv Independent](https://kyivindependent.com/germany-uk-push-back-after-us-criticizes-ukraines-deep-strikes-into-russia/), [Kyiv Independent](https://x.com/i/status/2122872453303349675), [Euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2122847868117717192), [Swedish government via @camille_grand](https://x.com/i/status/2122826657010680137), [Anadolu](https://x.com/i/status/2122853560677220411)
articles.why: The US has stopped directly funding new weapons for Ukraine, leaving Europeans and Canada to pay, including for American-made systems, while Washington now tells Kyiv how to fight. Europe carries the cost without setting the strategy, a clear case for the EU acting as one — and, in CEAFE's view, for putting that weight behind a European-led peace process rather than open-ended escalation.
articles.watch: Commission proposal text; Ukraine talks scheduled for 19 November and the European negotiating group (France, Germany, Italy, Poland, UK, EU and NATO officials, with Kallas and the Baltic states left out, per Euronews).

articles.headline: LPG carrier GAS HUSKY sinks in Bulgaria's EEZ after drone attack
articles.summary:
**The Liberian-flagged LPG carrier GAS HUSKY (IMO 9507764), managed by Greece-based Stealth Maritime, was struck around 23:45 local time on 16 November in Bulgaria's Exclusive Economic Zone while carrying LPG from Alexandria (Egypt) to Midia (Romania).**

“We believe four drones hit us,” the master said, adding the bridge and engine room were hit. All 19 Filipino crew were rescued by a Bulgarian Air Force Cougar helicopter after an Su-25 spotted their life raft; two had minor injuries. BTA reports the tanker later sank, and AP says it is the second merchant ship to sink off Bulgaria's coast in two days.

**Sources:** [Maritime.bg](https://www.maritime.bg/158410/), [BTA](https://www.bta.bg/en/news/bulgaria/1248291-lpg-tanker-gas-husky-sinks-near-bulgarian-coast-all-19-crew-members-rescued), [AP](https://apnews.com/article/bulgaria-romania-black-sea-gas-tanker-gas-husky-3265b6f9e84eb28b349dceb3223fd37f), [Euronews](https://x.com/i/status/2122858066777649261), [@sentdefender](https://x.com/i/status/2122759781354213756)
articles.why: Attacks are now sinking ships inside an EU and NATO member's EEZ on routes to Romanian ports. Maritime.bg reports the ship vanished from radar around midnight but the emergency beacon fired only at 08:02, and Varna's governor asked why nothing was done for eight hours, which exposes gaps in Black Sea surveillance and rescue.
articles.watch: Bulgarian investigation and attribution; NATO/EU maritime response in the western Black Sea; insurance on Romanian-bound cargoes.

articles.headline: UK hands US Army officer held for alleged spying for Russia to US military
articles.summary:
**The UK handed a US Army officer to the US military in an espionage probe (Reuters).**

Defense News identifies him as Lt. Col. Brandon Carroll Tyner, arrested earlier this week in the UK for reportedly assisting Russian intelligence.

**Sources:** [Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2122910227796214245), [Defense News Europe section](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/)
articles.why: A Russian intelligence case on British soil is being handled by US military justice, a reminder of how far the UK's security is entwined with, and deferential to, the US.
articles.watch: Charges and the information allegedly passed; any Russian comment.

articles.headline: Taiwan seeks a 300-satellite constellation, citing Starlink throttling in Ukraine
articles.summary:
**Taiwan's space agency TASA is in early talks with “like-minded partners” on a constellation of more than 300 communications satellites, citing the throttling of SpaceX's Starlink service in Ukraine (Aviation Week).**

Ukrainian reporting relayed by OSINT accounts says restrictions on Starshield terminals have continued for days, and The Guardian and The Times say Ukraine bypassed them for the Kerch strike with drone relays.

**Sources:** [Aviation Week](https://aviationweek.com/space/satellites/citing-starlink-problems-taiwan-pushes-300-sat-multinational-network), [Aviation Week](https://x.com/i/status/2122789122473336843), [@FaytuksNetwork](https://x.com/i/status/2122858362006294721)
articles.why: It shows the kill-switch risk of relying on a single US private provider for military communications, the argument for Europe's own IRIS² constellation and sovereign satellite communications.
articles.watch: Which partners join; Europe's IRIS² timeline.

headlines: Update: Kerch bridge road span collapses; Zelensky says it ended a seven-phase operation
France's secret “Volia” military mission in Ukraine; Moscow calls French troops “legitimate targets”
Russian drones over Moldova and Hungary's rail halt: the war spills onto Europe's borders

articles.headline: Update: Kerch bridge road span collapses; Zelensky says it ended a seven-phase operation
articles.summary:
**New since the 07:30 edition: images at dawn showed a whole section of the road part of the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge had collapsed.**

The Kyiv Independent reports it was hit by a Ukrainian Flamingo cruise missile overnight on 17 November, the final part of what President Zelensky called a seven-phase operation over “several weeks” using Flamingo and Neptune missiles and Ukrainian long-range drones. OSINT mapping estimates the fallen roadway at about 270 m. Russia's Transport Ministry suspended road and rail traffic; by midday rail traffic had resumed on one track and a passenger-only ferry was running. Russia answered with a large overnight missile and drone attack: Russia's MoD claims it hit drone plants in Kyiv (Techno-Links, Ukrplastic), the Yuzhny and Severny road bridges in Kyiv and the Motor Sich and Ivchenko-Progress engine plants in Zaporizhzhia (Russian state source). OSINT accounts counted about 30 missiles and about 300 Geran-2 drones, many aimed at western Ukraine. Nuclear safety regulators from 38 countries warned the risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is rising this winter because of attacks on the power grid (Reuters).
articles.why: Ukraine destroyed Russia's most protected target with Ukrainian-made missiles, without needing anyone's permission to use them. ItaMilRadar notes the cut also blocks Russian naval movement between the Caspian and the Black Sea. Europe should keep funding Ukrainian production of such weapons.
articles.watch: Russian repair timeline for the road span; whether Kyiv's bridges reopen (partial traffic resumed on the Southern Bridge); 7:30 edition story linked: “Update: Kerch bridge hit again; Salavat petrochemical fire”.

articles.headline: France's secret “Volia” military mission in Ukraine; Moscow calls French troops “legitimate targets”
articles.summary:
**Radio France Internationale reported that French troops have been working in Ukraine in non-combat roles since at least summer 2026, maintaining French equipment (Caesar howitzers, Mirage 2000 jets, precision missiles) and training Ukrainian soldiers.**

The mission, called Volia, is led by a French general and deployed under the cover of the Gerfaut training mission in Poland; France Télévisions says several dozen soldiers are involved and that parliament has not been informed (Defense News, citing RFI). Le Monde was told by a source that small French contingents rotate in Ukraine for training and repairs. Russia's Foreign Ministry said it was aware of French troops in Ukraine and called it “direct participation” in the war (Euronews). The Russian Embassy in France said France had “de facto become embroiled” in the conflict and that foreign contingents would be “legitimate targets” (Russian MFA Telegram, state source). Separately, troops from an 11-nation force led by the UK and France tested drone defences in Poland to prepare to support Ukraine after a ceasefire (Reuters).
articles.why: The French mission shows how European weapons need European people on the ground to keep them working. It also tests whether Europe will stand together behind a member state threatened by Moscow. A European framework would make such missions less exposed than one country acting alone.
articles.watch: Paris's official response; French parliamentary questions; any Russian strike on sites linked to foreign personnel.

articles.headline: Russian drones over Moldova and Hungary's rail halt: the war spills onto Europe's borders
articles.summary:
**Moldova closed its airspace on 17 November after its Defence Minister said 7 drones entered between 15:45 and 18:10 local time; police received calls about explosions in several districts and bomb-disposal teams were sent out.**

A Gerbera-type drone was filmed over Chișinău. Earlier, Hungary suspended rail traffic with Ukraine for 17–18 November after a Russian drone struck near Mukachevo station, about 300 m from a train with a Hungarian crew. In the Black Sea, an OSINT tally counts six Russian attacks on ships in Romanian and Bulgarian waters since 13 November, as NATO ISR flights (a US P-8A and a French ALSR Vador out of Constanța) patrol the area.
articles.why: Russian drones are now hitting or crossing the borders of an EU candidate (Moldova) and touching EU members' transport (Hungary) and waters (Romania, Bulgaria). No single small state can defend its skies alone; a common European air-defence and drone-wall effort is the answer.
articles.watch: Moldovan statement on the drones' origin and debris; Romanian and NATO response at sea.

articles.headline: Update: US strikes near Qeshm, more Iranian mine hits on tankers, and “dirty bomb” claims
articles.summary:
**New since 07:30: Iranian state agencies (Mehr, Fars) reported US strikes and explosions near Qeshm on 17 November, and Russia's MFA confirmed “hits” on Qeshm and Bahrain, calling on “above all the US” to stop (Russian state source).**

Iran's Navy said a third tanker of the day hit a mine east of Hormuz; the IRGC Navy said a supertanker and an LPG carrier caught fire after hitting mines (IRNA). The IRGC says it shot down an 18th US MQ-1, and Iran's Army says it destroyed a US LUCAS drone (Iranian claims). The IRGC also warned Bahrain over “hostile actions”. In Washington, Trump said the US is looking into a reported Iranian “dirty bomb” threat against the capital (CBS via @FaytuksNetwork) and warned Iran would “pay a price”. Foreign Minister Araghchi called the chemical-weapon and “missile bases under dams” reports “RUBBISH”, and Speaker Ghalibaf called them war propaganda (IRNA). Czech Prime Minister Babiš said Europe must cooperate closely with Israel against Iran's missiles (Euronews).
articles.why: Every day of mine and drone attacks keeps energy prices and shipping insurance high for Europe, which has no naval force of its own able to secure Hormuz. Europe pays the costs of a US–Iran war it did not decide.
articles.watch: CENTCOM confirmation of the Qeshm strikes; UKMTO notices on the new tanker hits. 07:30 story linked: “Update: Hormuz tanker attacks”.

articles.headline: Update: Yemen — Houthis close in on Aden and claim drone strikes on Saudi pipeline
articles.summary:
**France 24 reports, citing military and government sources, that Houthi forces are getting closer to Aden, seat of the internationally recognised government, which has stepped up security in the port city.**

Saudi aircraft carried out four strikes on northern Sanaa (@ILRedAlert via @GeromanAT). Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed drone attacks on Pumping Stations No. 8 and No. 9 of Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline west of Riyadh (via Tasnim, Iranian state agency); Saudi Arabia has not confirmed. Off Al Mukalla, UKMTO reported an attempted boarding of a cargo ship by an armed skiff, repelled by warning shots.
articles.why: A Houthi push on Aden and attacks on Saudi oil infrastructure threaten the Bab al-Mandab and Red Sea route to Suez, which is vital for European trade, while EU naval mission Aspides is small.
articles.watch: Front line north of Aden; Saudi Aramco statement on the pipeline.

articles.headline: Update: Putin in Shenzhen as Kremlin says Trump–Putin–Xi meeting is agreed; Stubb wants Europe at the table
articles.summary:
**Putin arrived in Shenzhen for the APEC leaders' meeting on 18–19 November (CGTN, Chinese state media).**

Kremlin spokesman Peskov said “everything is agreed” for a Putin–Trump–Xi meeting on the sidelines (TASS, Russian state agency); Trump, now in the Philippines, said he would also like a bilateral meeting with Putin (@MilitarySummary via @GeromanAT). Finnish President Alexander Stubb urged European leaders to talk to Putin directly, calling Europe's reliance on US-led talks “irresponsible” and warning of a Yalta-style division of Europe (Kyiv Independent, @ClashReport). Breaking Defense reports that Russia reportedly wants Finland to leave NATO as part of a Ukraine deal. Trump, speaking about the wars, said “25,000 lives a month are lost” (@ClashReport, @atrupar).
articles.why: A deal on Europe's security could be shaped by Washington, Moscow and Beijing with no European present. A demand that Finland leave NATO shows what is at stake. Only a united EU voice has the weight to be heard.
articles.watch: Outcome of the trilateral meeting; talks of 19 November. 07:30 story linked: “Update: Ukraine talks 19 Nov, Kallas rejected, E5+EU”.

headlines: Update: Zelensky hails an "unprecedented operation" against the Crimean Bridge; OSINT mappers say the Sea of Azov is cut off
Update: Iran's IRGC claims a drone strike on a US radar in Bahrain, as Qatar says mediation continues
Regulators from 38 countries warn of a growing risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine this winter

articles.headline: Update: Zelensky hails an "unprecedented operation" against the Crimean Bridge; OSINT mappers say the Sea of Azov is cut off
articles.summary:
**President Zelensky thanked Ukraine's Security Service (SBU), the Defence Forces and Ukraine's weapons manufacturers on 17 November for "an unprecedented operation in response to" Russian strikes on Ukraine's infrastructure, a reference to the overnight attack on the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge covered in the 07:30 edition.**

The OSINT account AMK Mapping wrote that, besides destroying the roadway section and stopping vehicle traffic, debris from the collapsed span has blocked ships from passing through the channel below, "effectively cutting off the Sea of Azov" and its ports. CEAFE has not been able to verify that claim independently. Russia struck Kyiv's North and South bridges late on Monday, as reported in the 07:30 edition.
articles.why: If confirmed, the closure of the Kerch Strait would hit Russia's logistics to Crimea and the Azov ports, while peace talks continue and Moscow has still not accepted the European negotiating team.
articles.watch: Official Russian statements or satellite imagery on the state of the channel, and any Russian retaliation against Ukrainian infrastructure.

articles.headline: Update: Iran's IRGC claims a drone strike on a US radar in Bahrain, as Qatar says mediation continues
articles.summary:
**Iran's Revolutionary Guard (IRGC) said it carried out a drone attack on the morning of 17 November against a US radar system at Isa Air Base in Bahrain, Al Jazeera reported, and Reuters reported that Iran had attacked a US military radar in Bahrain with drones.**

Qatar's foreign ministry spokesman Majed al-Ansari said mediation to end what Al Jazeera calls the "US-Israel war on Iran" is still under way, and that a meeting with Iranian officials would take place within hours. The 07:30 edition covered the tanker attacks in Hormuz and the arrival of a third US carrier.
articles.why: A strike on a US installation in a Gulf state widens the war's geography to the bases that also protect European shipping and energy supplies. Europe is a bystander in the mediation, which runs through Qatar.
articles.watch: Any US response, damage reports from Bahrain and the outcome of the Qatari meeting with Iranian officials.

articles.headline: Regulators from 38 countries warn of a growing risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine this winter
articles.summary:
**Nuclear safety regulators representing 38 countries said on 17 November that the risk of a nuclear accident in Ukraine is increasing this winter, and urged Russia to stop its attacks on the country's power infrastructure, Reuters reported.**

Nuclear plants depend on stable grid power for cooling and safety systems, which is why regulators link the risk to strikes on the power network.
articles.why: A nuclear accident in Ukraine would directly affect EU territory. It is a reminder that Ukraine's security is European security.
articles.watch: Statements by the IAEA and any new strikes on Ukraine's substations and power plants.

articles.headline: Komyshuvakha: search ends with 72 dead, one of the deadliest strikes of the war
articles.summary:
**Ukraine's Foreign Ministry said on 17 November that search and rescue operations in Komyshuvakha, in the Zaporizhzhia region, are complete.**

It said the Russian strike on the settlement on 2 November was one of the deadliest attacks of the full-scale war, killing 72 people, among them rescuers, police officers and school and administrative staff.
articles.why: The toll comes as Europeans try to secure a role in the peace talks; any settlement will have to address accountability for strikes on civilians.
articles.watch: International reactions and any investigation by the International Criminal Court or the UN.
