articles.headline: Update: Ukraine hits the Kerch bridge again overnight as part of its largest drone campaign of the war
articles.summary:
**Ukraine struck the Crimean (Kerch) Bridge for the second time in less than 24 hours.**

Sergey Aksyonov, the Russian-installed head of Crimea, said on Telegram at about 01:34 local time on 17 November that “the enemy attacked the Crimean Bridge again” and that traffic was suspended (relayed by TASS, Russian state agency). OSINT accounts reported more than 15 strikes in the evening, several waves after midnight and intense Russian air-defence fire; a Faytuks Network clip appears to show structural movement of the span. The damage from the new strikes is not yet known: TWZ says it is unclear, while satellite imagery after the first strike on 16 November showed a deformed road arch, reportedly tilted about 4.9 degrees, and damaged roadway in at least two places. The Kremlin called the earlier damage “minor”. Overnight, Ukrainian drones also hit the Gazprom Neftekhim Salavat petrochemical complex in Bashkortostan, deep inside Russia, causing a fire (Kyiv Independent).
articles.why: The bridge is Russia's main road and rail link to occupied Crimea and its southern front. A lasting cut would weaken the forces that threaten Black Sea shipping off Romania and Bulgaria. Ukraine is doing this mostly with its own long-range drones, which shows the value of European funding for Ukrainian-made strike weapons over waiting for US permission.
articles.watch: Daylight imagery of the span and rail section; Russian MoD figures on drones downed; whether Russia shuts the Kerch–Yenikale shipping channel. Earlier coverage: 13:30 and 20:30 editions of 16 November.

articles.headline: Russia hits Kyiv's North and South bridges with ballistic missiles
articles.summary:
**Late on 16 November, Russian ballistic missiles struck Kyiv's Northern and Southern bridges over the Dnipro, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said, damaging critical infrastructure and cutting water and heating in parts of the city.**

Explosions were also reported in Kharkiv, Zaporizhzhia (six strikes, an industrial site hit), Dnipro, Cherkasy, Smila (three injured) and Pavlohrad, and further blasts were heard in Kyiv on the morning of 17 November (Kyiv Independent, Kyiv Post, BBC, France 24/Reuters). Zelensky had warned hours earlier of imminent strikes and of “extremely dangerous” North Korean missile development; a senior Ukrainian official told the FT the missiles used may have come from North Korea. ISW assessed on 14 November that strikes on Kyiv's bridges may aim to split the capital's power grid along the Dnipro.
articles.why: Kyiv's three million residents depend on eight Dnipro bridges, and Russia is now targeting them as winter starts. Ukraine's air defence relies heavily on scarce US interceptors; the IMF now puts Ukraine's funding gap at $32–34 billion in 2027 (TASS, citing the IMF review). Europe is paying for most of it. A new €1.71 billion tranche of the EU's Ukraine Support Loan, with about 40% for European-made items according to Ukraine's MoD, shows the right direction: European money for European air defence and ammunition.
articles.watch: Damage assessment of the bridges; any confirmation of North Korean missiles; EU air-defence deliveries. Linked action–reaction: the Kyiv strikes and the Kerch strikes came within the same hour.

articles.headline: Update: Hormuz tanker attacks continue as Iran sets terms and a third US carrier arrives
articles.summary:
**UKMTO confirmed a second tanker attack on 16 November (warning 208-26, 7 NM north of Khasab, 19:00 UTC): the vessel was disabled with an engine-room fire and its crew is safe.**

That follows the 05:58 UTC projectile strike covered at 13:30. Iran's Navy claims a fourth tanker in 24 hours struck a mine after entering a “restricted route” with its navigation systems off; UKMTO has not confirmed the link or the cause. Army spokesman Brig. Gen. Mohammad Akraminia said the strait “will only be reopened by accepting Iran's conditions” (IRNA, Iranian state media). Foreign Minister Araghchi travelled from Islamabad to Muscat for talks with Oman's Badr Al-Busaidi on navigation in Hormuz, after regional support for Tehran's proposed two-day ceasefire (Al Jazeera, Tasnim). In Washington, CNN reported US intelligence that Iran is developing preliminary plans to target senior officials with a dirty bomb or chemical weapon; officials stressed the plotting appears preliminary. Vice President Vance said the war will not become a “10 or 15 year commitment”, and a Reuters/Ipsos poll puts US support for the war at 31%.
articles.why: Europe pays for the Hormuz crisis through energy prices and inflation (Euronews reports Japan's economy stalled because of it) but has no seat at the table. The UK's Andy Burnham says London supports mediators seeking a deal to end the US-Israel war on Iran and reopen the strait. The EU as a bloc has no comparable role, while Oman, Pakistan and China act as intermediaries; China's UN envoy called the attack on Iranian nuclear sites illegal (Tasnim).
articles.watch: Identity and flag of the tankers; Oman mediation outcome; US response to the MQM-170 and MQ-1 claims. Earlier coverage: all three 16 November editions.

articles.headline: Russian aircraft violate Japanese airspace and probe Korea's and Taiwan's air zones before APEC
articles.summary:
**Japan says two suspected Russian aircraft entered its airspace northwest of Okinoshima, Fukuoka, for about three minutes each between 04:07 and 04:12 on 17 November, the first such violation since September 2024.**

Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara called it “completely unacceptable” and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi promised close watch of Russian military movements. The aircraft continued through the Tsushima Strait and between Yonaguni and Taiwan; Taiwan's MND tracked two Russian military aircraft through its ADIZ, and South Korea scrambled fighters after Russian aircraft entered the KADIZ. Relations between Tokyo and Moscow have soured after a Japanese journalist's arrest and the seizure of Japan Tobacco's Russian assets, and the flight came on the eve of Putin's visit to China for APEC (18–19 November; Russian MFA).
articles.why: Russia is showing it can pressure US allies in Asia at the same time as it attacks Ukraine and harasses NATO's Black Sea flank. For Europe, the lesson is that the US must spread its forces across several theatres. Only a European defence able to act alone can guarantee Europe's own security.
articles.watch: Aircraft type (Japan has not yet published it); any Russian explanation; a possible Takaichi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen.

articles.headline: Update: Saudi air campaign over Sanaa as the Houthis claim Bab al-Mandab
articles.summary:
**Houthi-run Saba reported Saudi airstrikes on residential areas of Sanaa on the morning of 17 November, after strikes reported on 16 November in Sanaa (Bani al-Harith: one child killed, 11 wounded), Saada (a migrants' shelter), Taiz and Lahj.**

These figures come from the Sanaa authorities and cannot be verified independently. Al Jazeera reports the Houthis now claim control of the Bab al-Mandab Strait, while Saudi-backed southern forces, the Giants Brigades and Nation's Shield announced a “redeployment” from Dhubab airport toward Khor Umayra and Lahj to protect Aden. Iranian state media present it as a Saudi defeat with “100 km liberated” (Tasnim). Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree earlier claimed Saudi F-15 and Typhoon jets fly the raids from Khamis Mushait and Taif.
articles.why: Bab al-Mandab carries Europe's trade with Asia through Suez. Losing its Yemeni coast to the Houthis would put EU Aspides ships and Djibouti-based forces next to a hostile shore. If Saree's claim is right, European-built Typhoons are part of the Saudi campaign, which raises export-control and reputational questions for the Eurofighter partners (Germany, the UK, Italy and Spain).
articles.watch: Saudi or coalition statement on the Sanaa strikes; Aspides posture; shipping notices for Bab al-Mandab. Earlier coverage: 16 November, 07:30, 13:30 and 20:30.

articles.headline: Update: Russian sea drones sink a grain ship off Bulgaria as the Black Sea campaign reaches NATO waters
articles.summary:
**The Somali-flagged bulk carrier BETUL 8 capsized off Bulgaria on 16 November after, according to its crew, being hit by two naval drones.**

It was carrying 3,000 tonnes of wheat from Romania to Egypt. All 12 crew members were rescued by Bulgarian, Romanian and Turkish units (AP/Reuters, via @FaytuksNetwork; first photographs by Maritime bg). Ship-tracking analysts note that the vessel appears to have been hit by the same unidentified naval drone type that struck the container ship CONTSHIP JET on 28 October, assessed by maritime security firm Ambrey as a variant of the Russian Murena-300S. The OSINT account @Schizointel now counts four commercial ships hit by drones in Romanian territorial waters and one sunk in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone since 13 November. Romania has issued a navigation-danger warning off the Danube Delta and sent Navy EOD divers to two drifting drones spotted by a French Atlantique 2 patrol aircraft.
articles.why: Russian drones are now sinking civilian ships inside or next to the waters of two EU and NATO members. Bulgaria and Romania depend on allied patrol aircraft (here French) to see the threat, which shows both the value of European pooling and how thin the Union's own maritime surveillance in the Black Sea is. The NATO and EU ministers meeting in Brussels on 17–18 November will have to answer it.
articles.watch: Bucharest's and Sofia's requests at the Brussels ministerials; whether Russia's MoD claims the strike (it claimed a ship bound for Chornomorsk this morning).

articles.headline: Update: Iran claims a third tanker hit and a US drone downed, and threatens US and Israeli officials' homes
articles.summary:
**Iran's Navy said on 16 November that a third “rogue” oil tanker, sailing an unauthorised route east of the Strait of Hormuz with its navigation systems off, had caught fire after striking a naval mine, the third in 24 hours (IRNA, Iranian state media).**

Iran's Army separately said it shot down a US Army MQ-1 drone over the strait, and state broadcaster IRIB aired footage (via @MenchOsint). Air defences were activated over Isfahan, according to the semi-official Mehr agency. Iran's General Staff warned Trump and Netanyahu that, because civilian residential areas had been targeted, Iran would “begin bombing the homes of American and Israeli officials and politicians in the region” (quoted via the list; primary text not yet located). In Washington, Trump answered a 60 Minutes report on Iranian strikes on US bases by saying, as quoted on X, that of about 9,000 Iranian drones only two got through, and of 2,000 ballistic missiles only one (video clip; transcript not checked). Diplomatically, Lavrov and Araghchi spoke by phone (Russian MFA and IRNA), while Araghchi attended the ECO ministerial in Islamabad and met Pakistan's army chief, Field Marshal Asim Munir.
articles.why: Every claimed mine strike raises Gulf shipping and insurance costs for Europe's energy imports, and Europe has no seat in the US–Iran escalation or in the Pakistan channel. Only one of the three tanker strikes is independently confirmed (UKMTO 207-26), so Iranian claims must be read as claims.
articles.watch: UKMTO confirmation of the second and third tankers; any US statement on the MQ-1; whether the General Staff threat is followed by action.

articles.headline: Update: Saudi king replaces the Yemen war commander after losses near Bab al-Mandab
articles.summary:
**A royal order published on 16 November moved Lt Gen Fahd bin Hamad al-Salman, commander of the Saudi-led Joint Forces in Yemen since late August 2024, to adviser to the defence minister, and tasked the Chief of General Staff, Gen Fayyad bin Hamed al-Ruwaili, with commanding the Joint Forces in addition to his post (Saudi royal order, quoted via @MenchOsint).**

The change follows days of Houthi gains in Lahj and around the Bab al-Mandab strait. Tasnim (Iranian state-affiliated) claims Houthi-held areas have grown to 15,000 km² and speaks of a 90-kilometre buffer zone around Bab al-Mandab; pro-Houthi accounts claim the whole strait coast and a stretch of the Gulf of Aden coast. These figures are not independently confirmed.
articles.why: Riyadh is putting its top officer in charge because the Bab al-Mandab, the southern gate of the Suez route to European ports, is at stake. A Houthi-held strait coast would make the EU's Aspides mission's task much harder.
articles.watch: Whether the new command brings a Saudi counter-offensive or talks; any attack on shipping in the strait.

articles.headline: Europe's place at the Ukraine talks: EU money for EU-made weapons, Kallas sidelined, Moscow sets conditions
articles.summary:
**The European Commission has transferred €1.76 billion to Ukraine to buy missiles and drones, and none of it may be spent on US Patriot interceptors because all weapons in this tranche must be produced in the EU or Ukraine (Commission spokesperson Balazs Ujvari, via TASS).**

Politico reports that High Representative Kaja Kallas has been left out of the EU negotiating team, as talks are being run by national security advisers rather than foreign ministers (relayed on the list). Kremlin aide Yury Ushakov said the Russia–US–Ukraine talks will continue in Abu Dhabi with no date set, that widening the format “has not been agreed with Russia”, and that EU participation will arise only once Moscow gets “constructive proposals” from Europe (TASS, Russian state media). US NATO ambassador Matthew Whitaker said envoys Witkoff and Kushner are working on terms both sides could accept, and Trump told reporters Putin “could be a lot tougher” on Ukraine. Trump said denuclearisation, Iran, Ukraine and trade will be on the agenda of the Trump–Xi–Putin meeting in Shenzhen.
articles.why: The “buy European” condition on the €1.76 billion is exactly the kind of choice that builds Europe's own industry and avoids dependence on US approval. At the same time, Europe is still negotiating for a seat at a table set by Washington, Moscow and Beijing.
articles.watch: Shenzhen summit on 19 November; the EU team's composition.

articles.headline: US embassies across Europe issue terror warning for holiday season
articles.summary:
**US embassies in Europe warned American citizens that terrorists, including lone actors, may attack holiday markets, transport hubs and places of worship “with little or no warning” (relayed on the list and by Tasnim).**

The alert does not name a specific threat. Separately, Lithuania has submitted a proposal package to the US for a permanent US military base, and its defence minister said talks would be lengthy (Tasnim; to be confirmed with Lithuanian sources).
articles.why: A US-wide alert across Europe, issued during a war with Iran that has threatened retaliation against US officials, concerns European security services directly; European governments have issued no matching alert in the material read.
articles.watch: Any national alerts in EU states; Vilnius' official statement on the base request.

articles.headline: Asia-Pacific movements: Chinese naval presence near Japan, US HIMARS in the Pacific, US–Russia oppose autonomous-weapons talks
articles.summary:
**Defense News reports that a large Chinese flotilla mixing coast-guard vessels and navy warships may have been aimed at Japan, and that China has normalised its naval presence near Japan since the 2025 political spat.**

Japan's Joint Staff reported a PLA Y-9 intelligence aircraft flying out-and-back over the East China Sea on 16 November, and the Maritime Self-Defense Force spotted the Type 052D destroyer Qiqihar (121) and a Type 903 replenishment ship heading north about 60 km west of Kume Island (via @TaiwanMonitor). The US Army's 25th Infantry Division fired HIMARS rockets at Kwajalein Atoll on 13 November (DVIDS). Military Times reports that the US and Russia look set to oppose launching negotiations on binding rules for autonomous weapons at a global meeting.
articles.why: US attention and assets are pulled toward the Pacific while Europe faces Russia alone in the Black Sea. The US–Russia stance on autonomous weapons leaves the EU to lead any rule-making alone.
articles.watch: Trump's Asia trip (Philippines 17 November, China 19 November).

articles.headline: Ukraine hits the Crimean Bridge and sends one of the largest drone barrages of the war toward Moscow
articles.summary:
**Ukraine struck the bridge linking Russia and occupied Crimea across the Kerch Strait overnight on 15–16 November, Crimea's Russian-installed head Sergei Aksyonov said on Telegram.**

Road traffic was restricted “until approximately midday” and an operational headquarters was set up in Kerch. The Russian Transport Ministry said repairs were under way, that it was considering alternating one-way traffic, that rail services were running normally and that preliminary reports showed no injuries. Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov spoke of “minor damage”. Kyiv Post, citing a bridge information channel, said traffic stopped at about 02:22 Moscow time and that four passenger trains were delayed. Pro-Kremlin channel Mash reported about 2,000 cars queuing (via Politico).

The bridge strike came in a mass drone raid. Russia's Defence Ministry claimed 1,336 fixed-wing drones were intercepted overnight over 17 regions, Crimea and the Black and Azov seas, and 2,049 drones plus four “Flamingo” long-range cruise missiles in 24 hours. Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said about 600 drones flew toward the capital region between 17:00 on Sunday and 08:00 on Monday, 191 of them near Moscow. Regional officials reported injuries in Krasnodar (six people) and at an oil depot and gas station in Azov, Rostov (three). All of these are Russian official claims and were not independently verified. Peskov said air defence was working “very effectively” but that “no system can provide 100% protection in the face of such massive strikes”. He added that Moscow “will not give the Kiev regime a break to heal its wounds” and wants a lasting peace, not a short truce. Russian Ombudswoman Yana Lantratova said a prisoner exchange is being prepared (TASS).
articles.why: Ukraine's long-range drones, increasingly built at home and with European money, can now strike Russia's most symbolic logistics link while talks happen without Europe in the room. This is the kind of sovereign strike capability (see ELSA, topic 5) that Europe itself still lacks at scale.
articles.watch: The Russian Transport Ministry's damage report, the Ukrainian General Staff's claim, and Russia's retaliation pattern against Ukrainian energy and Black Sea ports.

articles.headline: Update: Iran war, UKMTO confirms a tanker hit in Hormuz, Iran claims a captured US drone, and Araghchi rallies ECO
articles.summary:
**New since 07:30: UKMTO confirmed an attack for the first time in this run of claims.**

Warning 207-26 says a tanker sailing outbound through the Strait of Hormuz was struck by an “unknown projectile” at 05:58 UTC, causing an engine-room fire, with all crew accounted for. Iran's Army Navy, via IRNA (Iranian state media), said another “violating” tanker caught fire and stopped after hitting a naval mine in a “prohibited zone” east of the strait. It warned that ships which switch off tracking or enter unauthorised zones “face serious risks” and that owners are responsible for the consequences. IRNA repeated that Iran closed the strait after alleged US violations of the “Islamabad MoU”. The IRGC Navy separately claimed it brought down a US MQM-170 target/surveillance drone intact by electronic warfare south of Qeshm Island, its fourth such claim (Fars via @IranObserver0, Al Jazeera). There was no US response.

On the diplomatic side, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi told the ECO foreign ministers in Islamabad that Iran's strikes are “directed exclusively at the targets and military bases of the aggressors” and not at neighbouring peoples or governments. He said ECO members welcomed Iran's “two-day proposal” to end the war (IRNA). Al Jazeera reported Tehran's claim that it has at least six months of essential food reserves despite the US “sea-and-land blockade”. Trump shared a message saying “May God protect our troops” as USS Theodore Roosevelt joined two other US carriers in the region (Al Jazeera). @F_CEAFE reposted an @HormuzLetter report that Mossad chief Roman Gofman briefed Netanyahu and the security cabinet on possible military action against Iran after meetings with CIA Director Ratcliffe and envoy Witkoff. The meetings were reported by the Times of Israel (via @FaytuksNetwork); the cabinet briefing is unconfirmed.
articles.why: A confirmed projectile strike on an outbound tanker undercuts the calm that oil markets had priced in (Brent around $95 in this morning's brief). European importers and shipowners carry the risk, while European navies have no say in the US-run escort and blockade.
articles.watch: The vessel's identity and flag, CENTCOM comment on the drone claim, any Israeli cabinet decision, and the Shenzhen summit's Iran item on 19 November.

articles.headline: Russia's offer to sign separate non-aggression pacts with NATO members, while Europe fields a seven-member peace team
articles.summary:
**Al Jazeera's analysis today revisits the proposal made on 11 November by Alexei Drobinin, head of the Russian Foreign Ministry's policy planning department: bilateral “non-aggression” agreements with individual NATO member states, which would receive “additional individual security guarantees” from Russia.**

Reported terms include pledges not to provide territory, transit routes or industrial capacity for military action against the other party (Kyiv Post citing Reuters, Verkkouutiset). Former Russian diplomat Boris Bondarev told Al Jazeera that “NATO will collapse, and European nations will be face to face with Russia”. Euronews reports that Moscow is again demanding that NATO roll back its presence in Europe to its 1997 positions. EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said that in 2021 Russia's list of demands was “a clear pretext for war” and that the same demands now are “a pretext for keeping the war going” (video via @clashreport). Peskov said European statements show an “unwillingness to contribute” to the peace process (TASS). Latvia's PM Andris Kulbergs told Euronews that Russia “is losing in Ukraine” and is in no position to set terms.

Europe's answer is still plural. After the Dublin summit, leaders chose a seven-member team (France, Germany, the UK, Italy, Poland, the EU institutions and NATO) instead of a single envoy, leaving Kallas out (Euronews, Politico). Reuters also reports that the US and Russia will oppose talks on limiting autonomous weapons.
articles.why: Separate pacts are a textbook divide-and-rule offer. They work only if Europe stays a collection of states rather than a single security actor. A seven-member delegation is better than none, but it confirms the problem: no Member State, nor a small group of them, carries the weight of a united EU with a common defence.
articles.watch: The Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin on 19 November (Zelenskyy's deadline on European representation), and whether any NATO capital engages with Drobinin's offer.

articles.headline: Update: Estonia sabotage case, the Kremlin "categorically" rejects the accusation and Tallinn weighs an open-ended border closure
articles.summary:
**Russia's response to Estonia's version (07:30 edition, topic 4) has now come.**

Peskov said Estonia and other European countries are “baselessly accusing Russia of sabotage” and that Moscow “categorically” rejects this. He added that Estonia is building a “wall” with Russia, and “history shows that walls bring nothing good to their builders” (TASS, Russian state agency). TASS, citing Delfi, reports that PM Kristen Michal now wants the border closed indefinitely and says the border guard is ready for a possible “migration attack”. Breaking Defense also covered the attempted attack on Threod Systems. A European intelligence officer told journalist Holger Roonemaa that FSB officers are questioning travellers entering Russia from Europe about their knowledge of and contacts in military industries (via @RALee85). This is a single-source report.
articles.why: The attack was aimed at a drone maker that supplies Ukraine. Russia's flat denial and border threats make it a test of whether the EU treats sabotage on one member's defence industry as an attack on the common industrial base.
articles.watch: The Estonian government's decision on the duration of the closure, and any Latvian or Finnish response.

articles.headline: Europe's own firepower: 155 mm output up fivefold, ELSA moves to delivery, and Sweden eyes a French cruise missile
articles.summary:
**IISS says NATO Europe's 155 mm ammunition production capacity has grown fivefold since 2022 and will more than double again by 2030 if current plans are realised, although order backlogs have grown faster than production.**

A separate IISS Missile Dialogue Initiative paper (Matthew Bint) says the European Long-Range Strike Approach (ELSA) has moved from requirement planning to implementation, and that “timely delivery is now the challenge”. Sweden's navy chief told La Tribune he is “interested” in the MBDA MdCN naval cruise missile for the Naval Group FDI frigates that Sweden is considering. Spain's Indra unveiled its Prisma-S fully digital AESA naval radar at Euronaval 2026. By contrast, the UK will test the US YFQ-48A “Talon Blue” autonomous jet from a Queen Elizabeth-class carrier in 2027 (Navy Recognition), while Tekever's AR5 drone has completed trials aboard HMS Queen Elizabeth (Defence Post).
articles.why: Swedish interest in a French frigate armed with a French missile, Spanish radars and European long-range strike are the intra-European procurement that builds sovereign capability, jobs and R&D. ELSA's delivery problem and the UK's choice of a US drone for its carriers show how quickly that gap is filled from outside when Europe is slow.
articles.watch: The Swedish frigate decision, and ELSA milestones at the EU and NATO defence ministers' meetings on 17–18 November.

articles.headline: Update: Yemen, the Houthis say their Lahj push aims at a Bab al-Mandab "buffer zone" as fighting moves toward Aden
articles.summary:
**New since 07:30: Reuters carried Houthi video said to show clashes with pro-government troops in Lahj province.**

Pro-Houthi trackers report advances around Khor Omaira, Ras al-Ara and Al-Madaribah; this is unverified. Mohammed Al-Bukhaiti, a member of the Ansarullah political bureau, told Tasnim (Iranian state-affiliated) that “the objective of this military operation in Lahj Province is to ensure the security of Bab el-Mandeb” through a buffer zone, after what he called Saudi attempts to retake the strait. France 24 repeats that the Houthis are about 60 km from Aden.
articles.why: The Houthis now openly say the Lahj offensive is about holding the Bab al-Mandab chokepoint. That directly shapes Suez traffic to European ports and the environment for the EU's Aspides naval mission.
articles.watch: Whether the front stops at the Lahj coastal districts or moves on Al-Anad and Aden, and the Saudi air response.

headlines: Iran war: a third US carrier arrives, US strikes are reported but unconfirmed, and the IRGC claims more tanker fires in Hormuz
Yemen: government forces leave Bab al-Mandab and the Houthis move to about 60 km from Aden
Black Sea: four ships hit in Romanian waters in three days, and Bucharest asks NATO for help
Estonia blames GRU for sabotage at drone maker Threod and will close the Russian border on 1 December

articles.headline: Iran war: a third US carrier arrives, US strikes are reported but unconfirmed, and the IRGC claims more tanker fires in Hormuz
articles.summary:
**The United States now has three carrier strike groups in the Middle East after USS Theodore Roosevelt entered CENTCOM's area on 15 November, a US official told the NYT, Axios and Al Jazeera.**

This follows two IRGC drone attacks on Bahrain in three days. CENTCOM said US forces shot down the first two drones with no damage, and Bahrain said it intercepted the second wave. Late on 15 November, OSINT accounts (@HormuzReport, relayed by @F_CEAFE) reported fresh US airstrikes on Iranian missile launchers at Bandar Lengeh and Sirik. Fact-checkers and wire searches found no official US or Iranian confirmation by the time of writing. On 12 November IRNA had reported an “enemy” strike on Sirik without naming the attacker. IRNA's Telegram channel posted that “Iran will not leave any strike unanswered”, and Tasnim reported that Iran's army had found the wreckage of an “Orbiter 4” surveillance drone in western Iran.

At sea, the IRGC Navy, via Tasnim (Iranian state-affiliated), claimed that two more tankers on what it calls an “illegal southern route… under the direct guidance of US officers” hit naval mines and exploded. It called this the sixth tanker to “catch fire and sink” since the previous day and warned shipowners that the route is “lined with mines”. OSINT accounts said the Greek-owned tanker AMETHYST crossed with its AIS on, and the IRGC said a tanker caught fire at about 19:00 UTC. Neither claim was confirmed by UKMTO or the operator in this run. Tasnim also relayed a UKMTO report of a security incident 430 nautical miles east of Socotra. Markets, however, read the strait as functioning: Reuters reported Brent near $95 a barrel, with shipments through Hormuz approaching pre-war levels and the IEA forecasting a Q4 supply surplus of 1.7 million barrels a day.

On the diplomatic and political side, Parliament Speaker Mohammad-Baqer Qalibaf said Tehran “will not accept a prolonged state of neither war nor peace” and demanded that the US accept Iran's seven-point plan. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi arrived in Islamabad for the ECO ministerial (IRNA) and will go on to Oman (CGTN). Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmail Baghaei rejected Germany's demand that Iran stop enriching uranium (Al Jazeera, reposted by @F_CEAFE). The IRGC also clashed with the Kurdish group PJAK near the Iraqi border; PJAK said one fighter was killed (AP). @F_CEAFE reposted a 60 Minutes analysis saying Iran has hit at least 31 US military and diplomatic sites since the war began.
articles.why: Europe gets oil, LNG and shipping costs from a war it is not running, and its only roles are diplomatic statements such as Berlin's enrichment demand and individual naval contributions. Three US carriers set against a handful of European statements show the gap between Europe's exposure and its ability to influence events.
articles.watch: Any CENTCOM statement on Bandar Lengeh and Sirik, and the IRGC response against Gulf bases. Watch UKMTO and JMIC for confirmation of the tanker claims, Araghchi's talks in Muscat, and the Iran item on the 19 November Shenzhen agenda.

articles.headline: Yemen: government forces leave Bab al-Mandab and the Houthis move to about 60 km from Aden
articles.summary:
**The Saudi-backed Southern Armed Forces announced on 15 November that they were redeploying “from Dhubab Airport and the Bab el-Mandeb area” to make securing Aden the priority.**

Reuters called it the apparent end of a six-week counteroffensive to retake the coast at the mouth of the Red Sea, which the Houthis seized in September. Government and military sources told AFP that the Houthis took the Al-Maqatirah and Al-Madaribah districts in Lahj and were at the Al-Kharaz camp, about 60 km from Aden. A government source told Xinhua (Chinese state media) that “the offensive has failed, and there is no clear plan for what comes next.” Xinhua's sources blamed the poor performance of the Giants Brigades and the rift between Riyadh and the Southern Transitional Council. Government forces have dug in around Aden with sandbags and tunnels.

The Houthis also escalated against Saudi Arabia. Military spokesman Yahya Saree claimed two ballistic missiles at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport and the King Abdullah Financial District, drones at pumping stations 5 and 6 on the East–West pipeline, and six ballistic missiles at coalition forces in Lahj. These are Houthi claims. The coalition said it intercepted a drone over the Medina region, and Reuters reported that Gulf stock markets fell. Saree said Saudi aircraft carried out 75 air strikes in 24 hours. The ICRC confirmed that the Houthis unilaterally released 600 detainees in Sanaa, outside the Stockholm agreement. The US Embassy warned Americans in Bahrain about possible attacks by the Iranian-backed Houthis.
articles.why: If the Houthis hold both shores of the Bab al-Mandab chokepoint, Suez traffic to European ports stays hostage, and the EU's own Red Sea mission (EUNAVFOR Aspides) faces a harder environment. The reported daily presence of a British tanker supporting the Saudi air campaign is a European military involvement with little parliamentary visibility.
articles.watch: Whether the Houthis push on Aden or stop to consolidate, Saudi air and diplomatic moves, any Houthi statement on shipping through the strait (they say they will target only Saudi vessels), and Aspides posture.

articles.headline: Black Sea: four ships hit in Romanian waters in three days, and Bucharest asks NATO for help
articles.summary:
**Drones hit the Greek-flagged tanker Evia Petrol V (21:10 local time, 14 November, about 4 nautical miles south-east of the Sulina canal), the bulk carrier Marsol (21:45, about 5 nautical miles south-east) and the product tanker Ali Najafov (near midnight, St Kitts and Nevis flag), all inside Romanian territorial waters.**

The general cargo ship Larissa 1 had been hit on 13 November. Crews put out the fires and nobody was hurt (Romanian MoD, Reuters). Prime Minister Luca Niculescu called the attacks “unacceptable” and a violation of international law, and blamed the “deteriorating security situation caused by Russia's ongoing war against Ukraine” without naming the attacker. Defence Minister Ștefan-Radu Oprea said he would ask allies in Brussels for surveillance aircraft and counter-drone equipment, and that Thales would deliver Gap Filler radars early. Reuters notes that Russia denies targeting Ukraine's neighbours. The Russian MoD's Telegram said on 15 November that it had struck “port infrastructure facilities, and vessels used in the interests of the AFU”. Maritime Executive reports that Russia has claimed attacks on 15 Ukraine-linked ships in the past week.
articles.why: These are strikes inside the territorial waters of an EU and NATO member, on the Danube–Black Sea route Ukraine uses for exports. They test whether Europeans can defend their own sea lanes. A French aircraft and Thales radars are a European answer, but Europe still has no common maritime surveillance and counter-drone capability for the Black Sea.
articles.watch: The NATO and EU defence ministers' meetings in Brussels on 17–18 November, any attribution by Bucharest, and Bulgarian and Turkish positions.

articles.headline: Estonia blames GRU for sabotage at drone maker Threod and will close the Russian border on 1 December
articles.summary:
**Estonia's version: in the early hours of Saturday 14 November, intruders tried to break into drone maker Threod Systems in Viimsi, near Tallinn, to set the building on fire and cause an explosion.**

Security staff and police stopped them. Eight residents of Latvia were detained, and five have been remanded (Prosecutor General Astrid Asi). The Internal Security Service (KAPO) says the attack was commissioned by Russia's GRU military intelligence. Prime Minister Kristen Michal called it “part of Russia's broader hybrid war against Europe”. Foreign Minister Margus Tsahkna announced that all road crossings with Russia (Narva, Luhamaa, Koidula) will close from 1 December, and said he would push for more pressure on Russia at the EU Foreign Affairs Council on Monday. Milrem Robotics was targeted in a similar way in August.

Russia's response: Foreign Ministry spokeswoman Maria Zakharova told TASS that Moscow “will verify all this to see if it's true”, but that if Estonia really closes the border it would be “yet another bout of aggressive and unbridled Russophobia” (reported by AFP and Delfi from TASS). Russia did not address the GRU accusation itself. Nothing on it had appeared on the MFA's Telegram channel when it was checked.
articles.why: European defence makers that supply Ukraine are being targeted on EU soil, and this is now the second Estonian drone or robotics firm. Protecting the industrial base and coordinating the response (Finland, Latvia and Lithuania were informed) is a common European task, not just a national one.
articles.watch: The FAC decisions on 16 November, a formal Russian MFA statement, the investigation's findings on how the cell was recruited, and whether Latvia or Finland take similar steps.

articles.headline: Ukraine: Kyiv claims refinery damage and Russian losses, Moscow presses Kherson and the front, and the satellite dependency debate widens
articles.summary:
**Zelenskyy said Ukraine has “disabled more than 55% of Russia's oil refining capacity” (via @ClashReport, reposted by @F_CEAFE) and that Russia had more than 50,000 killed and wounded in October.**

Both are Ukrainian claims and were not independently verified. The General Staff said it struck the Akhtubinsk airfield (929th State Flight Test Center) in Astrakhan and a drone launch site in Oryol (Kyiv Independent). The Institute for the Study of War said overnight strikes on 14–15 November on petrochemical, military-industrial and missile production sites advanced Ukraine's counterforce campaign. The Russian MoD said its forces advanced on several axes and shot down more than 50 fixed-wing drones over Zaporizhzhia. A Russian MFA envoy accused Ukrainian forces of attacking evacuating civilians near Kupiansk. These are official Russian claims. OSINT accounts reported repeated glide-bomb strikes on the bridge to Korabelnyi Island in Kherson.

On dependencies: after Zelenskyy's complaint that Starshield speed caps hamper interceptor drones (see the 15 November brief), a Ukrainian brigade commander, Kyrylo Veres (K-2 Brigade), warned that if Russia deploys its planned 347-satellite “Rassvet” constellation, it would be “the end for us”. That quote was relayed by @HavryshkoMarta and has not yet been checked against the primary interview. Zelenskyy also announced a review of the coalitions supporting Ukraine, to see “which ones are truly fulfilling their tasks and which remain empty shells”.
articles.why: Ukraine's air defence depends on a US company's satellite service whose limits Kyiv cannot control, while Russia builds its own constellation. This is the case for Europe's IRIS² and sovereign milsatcom, and for not repeating the dependency in European forces.
articles.watch: Confirmation of Russian refinery outages from Russian or industry data, any SpaceX or US move on Starshield caps, and Rassvet launch dates.

items.title: Conflicts — 2026-11-15
headlines: Iran strikes at Bahrain again; a tanker is attacked approaching Hormuz
Russia intensifies strikes on Ukrainian energy; Kyiv hits Nizhnekamsk; Starshield limits remain
EU Operation IRINI boards suspected Russian shadow-fleet tanker MV MIDAG
Europe is told to prepare for a prolonged hybrid campaign; a device is made safe in Dublin
Canada and the UK discuss PAC-3 missiles, F-16 ammunition and deep-strike support for Ukraine

articles.headline: Iran strikes at Bahrain again; a tanker is attacked approaching Hormuz
articles.summary:
Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on Sunday, 15 November, that it had launched six drones at a US air-defence radar at Bahrain’s Al-Riffa (Riffa) helicopter base, the second such claim in three days. Bahrain’s defence force said its air defences intercepted and destroyed the incoming attacks “before they could achieve their objectives.” The interior ministry issued nationwide shelter alerts, the first since September. There was no immediate US or Bahraini confirmation that the radar itself was hit. A Friday attempt was denied as a hit by US Central Command, which said it shot down two one-way attack drones with no injuries or damage. Saudi Arabia’s foreign ministry condemned the Iranian air attacks “in the strongest terms” and pledged full solidarity with Manama; Bahrain’s foreign ministry held Iran “fully responsible.” The episode sits in the broader, months-long US–Israel war with Iran, in which Tehran asserts that the Strait of Hormuz is closed. US Central Command said on 14 November that US Air Force F-16s were patrolling regional waters and that “more than 1.7 billion barrels of crude oil have been shipped through the Strait of Hormuz by Gulf partners with US protection” (the period was not specified in the post).

Separately, UK Maritime Trade Operations issued Warning 205-26 after Indian shipping authorities reported an attack on a tanker transiting the Arabian Gulf eastbound before entering the Strait of Hormuz. The crew were accounted for and safe; damage and any environmental impact were unknown. UKMTO marked the incident near Khasab, Oman. IRGC and some OSINT accounts also claimed that two oil tankers struck naval mines south of the strait; those additional claims were not confirmed in the UKMTO warning.

A related front in Yemen remained active in official and factional posts. Houthi spokesman Yahya Saree claimed that at dawn on 15 November his forces shot down a Saudi CH-4 drone over Al-Jawf and that Saudi F-15s had carried out 72 air raids in 24 hours; the anti-Houthi “Yemen Army Media” account said Marib air defences intercepted Houthi drones. These are competing combat claims and were not independently verified in the briefs.
articles.why: Roughly a fifth of the world’s oil and gas usually transits Hormuz. Continued attacks on Gulf bases and shipping keep energy prices volatile, raise insurance and freight costs, and complicate any diplomatic off-ramp. The Yemen track is part of the same regional war system and of European Red Sea risk.
articles.watch: A US CENTCOM or Bahraini damage assessment on Sunday’s raid; any second UKMTO update on the tanker (identity, flag, pollution); whether IRGC mine claims are corroborated by maritime authorities; Hormuz transit in the coming days.

articles.headline: Russia intensifies strikes on Ukrainian energy; Kyiv hits Nizhnekamsk; Starshield limits remain
articles.summary:
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said that in the past week alone Russia had used more than 2,300 attack drones, 1,590 aerial bombs and 15 missiles of various types against Ukraine. Overnight into Sunday, he said, Russia targeted energy infrastructure in Zaporizhzhia, Sumy, Odesa, Zhytomyr and Kirovohrad regions, and hit railway infrastructure in Dnipro, Kharkiv and Zaporizhzhia, with strikes also reported in Donetsk and Kyiv regions and 16 people injured. DTEK said an energy facility hit in Odesa left 41,000 households without electricity, according to Al Jazeera. Zelenskyy argued that many Shahed strikes on substations succeed because speed restrictions on Starshield terminals along the front and in occupied territory remain in place, causing interceptor drones to lose contact at 161 km/h (100 mph) and fail to catch jet-powered Shaheds. SpaceX has denied a policy change, calling the issue technical; Zelenskyy has said Ukraine does not accept that explanation.

In the other direction, Ukraine’s General Staff said its forces struck the Sibur-owned Nizhnekamskneftekhim petrochemical complex — more than 1,000 km from the Ukrainian border — and the only primary distillation unit (ELOU-AVT-7) at the Nizhnekamsk (TAIF-NK) oil refinery during the night of 14–15 November, and also the Monolit aviation plant in Trubchevsk, Bryansk Oblast. Fire Point, the Ukrainian drone maker, said Ukrainian forces used its FP-1 drones against Nizhnekamskneftekhim. Nizhnekamsk’s mayor reported a “massive and prolonged” drone attack that damaged industrial-zone facilities and a residential building. AFP, citing regional authorities, reported three people wounded and a fire at the petrochemical site; later reports cited local officials as saying six people were injured. Russia’s defence ministry said it had shot down 533 Ukrainian drones overnight across a dozen regions and Crimea. AFP said it had not authenticated social-media footage of the fire. On a related industrial note, Fire Point also published company figures on the scale of Ukrainian deep strikes and video of an earlier (around 10 November) attack on a Russian drone base in occupied Donetsk; those company tallies were not independently audited.
articles.why: Winter energy attacks raise the risk of a new refugee and reconstruction burden and keep pressure on European air-defence stocks and financing. A dispute over US-controlled satellite connectivity goes to Ukraine’s ability to defend critical infrastructure — and to whether Europe can help close the gap without depending on a US commercial constraint.
articles.watch: Whether SpaceX or the US government lifts or explains the Starshield cap; confirmed production impact at Nizhnekamskneftekhim and TAIF-NK; the scale of the next Russian energy strike package.

articles.headline: EU Operation IRINI boards suspected Russian shadow-fleet tanker MV MIDAG
articles.summary:
On 15 November, EU High Representative Kaja Kallas said that forces from EUNAVFOR MED IRINI had boarded a suspected Russian shadow-fleet tanker in the Mediterranean on 13 November. The boarding, under Article 110 of the UN Convention on the Law of the Sea (flag verification), confirmed that MV MIDAG was sailing under a false flag. Kallas said the EU would “keep disrupting Russia’s shadow fleet at sea and through diplomatic means,” and that EU foreign ministers were due on Monday, 16 November, to approve new Russia sanctions listings, including on banks, buyers and companies supporting the shadow fleet. Kallas did not announce a detention.

Operation IRINI said the boarding took place in the central Mediterranean in line with its mandate, which was renewed in October through 31 March 2029 and now includes helping to constrain the shadow fleet. Italian reporting said two warships and an Italian helicopter took part. MarineTraffic and press accounts described MIDAG as a crude-oil tanker of about 241 metres and more than 106,000 dwt, displayed as flying the flag of Zimbabwe. Similar flag-verification boardings were reported earlier of MV Sun and MV Toa Payoh. Open-source reporting cited in the EU brief (The Insider, not an official EU source) said the tanker was not detained and continued west; that vessel-history point is attributed to that reporting, not to the EU statement.
articles.why: The shadow fleet is a principal channel for sanctioned Russian oil revenues that finance the war, and a safety and environmental risk in European waters. Boardings that only confirm a false flag, without a seizure, show both the reach and the limits of the current mandate. Monday’s listings are a test of whether the EU can move from documentation to disruption.
articles.watch: The 16 November Foreign Affairs Council listings; any detention, diversion or flag-state follow-up on MIDAG; further IRINI boardings.

articles.headline: Europe is told to prepare for a prolonged hybrid campaign; a device is made safe in Dublin
articles.summary:
An Atlantic Council UkraineAlert essay circulated on the Defense News list (dated 10 November, posted 14 November) argued that Europe has seen a surge in suspected Russian hybrid incidents — bomb threats against airports in Rome, Copenhagen, Prague, Warsaw and Lisbon and against media organisations, plus cyberattacks on supermarket frozen-food systems — designed to stay below the threshold of open conflict and hard to attribute. The author pointed to the attempted bombing of Leipzig Airport in August 2026 as a watershed, and concluded that “Europe should prepare for a prolonged campaign of hybrid hostilities that poses a threat to civilian infrastructure of all kinds.” A Foreign Policy essay of 12 November made a similar argument: adversaries are testing how much violence Europe will absorb, and “fear” is Russia’s cheapest hybrid weapon. Official confirmation of Kremlin direction is in most of the cited cases still lacking.

In that context, Irish police and the Defence Forces’ EOD team on 13 November made safe a “crude but viable” explosive device at an office building on Merrion Square North in Dublin — near, but not at, the National Gallery of Ireland, where the taoiseach had hosted EU leaders at dinner the previous evening during the European Political Community summit and informal EU meeting. Sources told *The Journal* the device resembled a firework attached to a can of flammable liquid. No attribution to a state actor has been announced.
articles.why: Whether or not the Dublin device is eventually linked to a foreign campaign, the political effect of scares around an EU leaders’ gathering sits squarely in the pattern European services are already investigating. Attribution difficulties are themselves part of the challenge for NATO and EU deterrence.
articles.watch: The outcome of the Garda investigation; any European or NATO attribution of the early-November airport threats; further incidents around critical civilian infrastructure.

articles.headline: Canada and the UK discuss PAC-3 missiles, F-16 ammunition and deep-strike support for Ukraine
articles.summary:
Ukraine’s defence minister, Evgeniy Khmara, spoke with Canada’s minister of national defence, David McGuinty, about air defence, F-16 support and long-range capabilities, the Ukrainian Defence Ministry said (readout dated 14 November 2026). Khmara thanked Canada for contributing to the procurement of PAC-3 missiles for Patriot batteries through the JUMPSTART mechanism, and called 20 mm cannon ammunition for F-16s a “critical resource,” saying “the lion’s share of jet-powered drones are destroyed by our F-16s,” and asked that the next delivery be sped up. The ministers also discussed deep-strike support and procuring Ukrainian drones. Figures for Canada’s PAC-3 contribution were not stated in the ministry text.

Ahead of the Ramstein-format Ukraine Defense Contact Group, Khmara and UK Defence Secretary Wes Streeting discussed the next aid package, aircraft munitions, faster deliveries against jet-powered drones, and possible joint defence ventures; Khmara thanked the UK for a recent transfer of Lightweight Multirole Missiles (LMM). Poland’s pause on further PURL funding for US weapons, and the wider financing debate, are covered in Current Affairs.
articles.why: PAC-3, Patriot and the F-16 fleet sit at the centre of Ukraine’s air-defence effort. Canadian financing via JUMPSTART and UK munitions transfers are concrete allied channels into that pipeline; ammunition shortages for F-16 guns directly affect the cheaper end of the counter-drone fight, just as interceptor stocks are under strain.
articles.watch: Timelines for the next 20 mm shipment and any public JUMPSTART/PAC-3 quantities; the next Ramstein-format package.

articles.headline: Drones alcanzan un carguero ruso rumbo a Kaliningrado en el golfo de Finlandia
articles.summary:
**Rusia afirma que dos drones alcanzaron un carguero que navegaba de San Petersburgo al enclave de Kaliningrado en aguas neutrales del golfo de Finlandia, a unas 3 millas náuticas de aguas rusas, la mañana del 21 de noviembre.**

El gobernador de la región de Leningrado, Alexandr Drozdenko, dijo que se estaba evacuando a la tripulación y evaluando los daños. Publicaciones que citan a Reuters y a la radiotelevisión estonia ERR identifican el buque como *Sparta II*, sancionado por EE. UU. y vinculado al transporte de carga militar, y aseguran que se incendió y derivó hacia aguas finlandesas. Las Fuerzas de Defensa de Finlandia ya habían restringido una zona frente a Kotka por posibles operaciones de interceptación de drones. Durante la noche se informó de decenas de drones ucranianos rumbo a San Petersburgo y a la terminal de Ust-Luga.

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2124086216408621332), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124087362682572876), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124096777443754416), [· Bloomberg](https://x.com/i/status/2124111866599280922), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124072896545108415), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123954268688261373)
articles.why: Es un ataque contra el enlace marítimo de Rusia con Kaliningrado, dentro del Báltico y al borde de aguas finlandesas y estonias. Pone a prueba cómo gestionarían los Estados bálticos de la UE incidentes, restos o buques a la deriva en sus propias aguas, y muestra de nuevo que la seguridad europea depende de una guerra que Europa no controla.
articles.watch: Declaraciones del Gobierno y la Guardia de Fronteras finlandeses; posible reivindicación ucraniana; escoltas rusas al tráfico hacia Kaliningrado; reacción de Estonia y la OTAN.

articles.headline: Actualización: otros dos petroleros alcanzados en Ormuz e Irán afirma haber derribado nuevos drones de EE. UU.
articles.summary:
**La UKMTO informó de dos petroleros alcanzados en el estrecho de Ormuz a primera hora del 21 de noviembre, y unas imágenes mostraron un petrolero en llamas cerca de la costa omaní.**

La Armada de la Guardia Revolucionaria iraní afirmó que el ejército estadounidense, con aviones cisterna, cazas F-16, F/A-18 y F-35, aviones de patrulla P-8, helicópteros y drones MQ, intentó escoltar petroleros a través del estrecho, y dijo haber derribado un MQ-9 y después un MQ-1 sobre Qeshm, con lo que eleva sus cifras a 58 MQ-9 y 19 MQ-1. Son afirmaciones iraníes no confirmadas por fuentes estadounidenses.

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2124063507024888053), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124064660043276793), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124082823854186811), [· Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2124085991480955377), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124087784889610511)
articles.why: Los precios de la energía y los seguros marítimos europeos dependen de Ormuz; las marinas y navieras europeas quedan expuestas a una escalada que se decide en Washington y Teherán.

articles.headline: Actualización: los hutíes atacan una central eléctrica saudí y apuntan a Riad; la coalición bombardea Yemen
articles.summary:
**Los hutíes atacaron el complejo eléctrico saudí de Shuqaiq, en Jizán, el 20 de noviembre; un vídeo muestra humo en dos puntos y un incendio en la central.**

Esa misma noche la coalición liderada por Arabia Saudí afirmó haber interceptado tres misiles balísticos lanzados contra Riad tras repetidas alertas. Reuters informa de ataques de la coalición contra un puerto yemení mientras los hutíes advertían a las aerolíneas que evitaran el reino, y de que las divididas fuerzas gubernamentales de Adén se preparan para una ofensiva hutí. La televisión hutí al-Masirah afirmó que al menos 41 personas murieron en bombardeos atribuidos a Arabia Saudí en 24 horas (afirmación hutí, difundida por la cadena estatal china CGTN).

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123848504292573207), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123854662457524632), [· Al Jazeera](https://x.com/i/status/2124008274496565659), [· Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124067829645258804), [· Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123899273821528506), [· Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123942001548595661), [· Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2124027530281685349)
articles.why: Una guerra entre Arabia Saudí y los hutíes amenaza, junto con Ormuz, las rutas energéticas del mar Rojo y el Golfo de las que depende el comercio europeo.

articles.headline: Alerta por drones en Sigonella, un día después del cierre del aeropuerto de Génova
articles.summary:
**Una presunta intrusión de drones activó la alerta en la base aeronaval de Sigonella (Sicilia) la noche del 20 de noviembre, con instrucciones de precaución al personal estadounidense.**

ItaMilRadar describe una semana excepcionalmente intensa en la base: misiones de vigilancia sobre el mar Negro, el tránsito de una flotilla naval rusa al sur de Sicilia y el despliegue de dos P-8 Poseidon británicos. El incidente se produjo unas 24 horas después de que la actividad de drones obligara a suspender las operaciones del aeropuerto de Génova.

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123874728808944018), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124080477984190590), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123907642670158106)
articles.why: Las incursiones de drones sobre bases y aeropuertos europeos se extienden del norte de Europa a Italia; Sigonella acoge vuelos de inteligencia italianos, estadounidenses y de la OTAN sobre el mar Negro y Oriente Próximo.

articles.headline: Doble ataque ruso contra Kryvyi Rih; Zelenski dice que el puente de Crimea «no seguirá en pie»
articles.summary:
**Un ataque ruso con misiles balísticos contra Kryvyi Rih la noche del 20 de noviembre mató a un niño de 7 años y a una sanitaria de 20 y dejó 42 heridos, después 47, en lo que el Kyiv Independent describe como un doble ataque contra los equipos de rescate.**

En la noche del 21, Rusia lanzó tres misiles balísticos y 148 drones (87 de ellos a reacción), según la Fuerza Aérea ucraniana; al menos 2 muertos y 83 heridos en todo el país. Zelenski dijo que Putin debe entender que el puente de Crimea «no seguirá en pie».

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123892487429431398), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2124067724733133079), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123945727638356467), [· AFP](https://x.com/i/status/2123929392527347859)
articles.why: La guerra de Ucrania sigue escalando en paralelo a unas conversaciones entre EE. UU. y Rusia de las que Europa está ausente.

articles.headline: Actualización: el ISW afirma que Rusia lanzó deliberadamente misiles y drones al espacio aéreo polaco
articles.summary:
**El Institute for the Study of War concluye que las fuerzas rusas lanzaron intencionadamente misiles y drones al espacio aéreo polaco durante sus ataques contra Ucrania el 20 de noviembre.**

El ejército polaco investiga las incursiones; según Al Jazeera, Varsovia denunció tres violaciones de su espacio aéreo durante la noche, que el primer ministro Donald Tusk calificó de «provocación». Una publicación afirma que dos cazas suecos JAS Gripen no lograron interceptar misiles y un dron sobre Polonia (fuente única, no verificada).

articles.headline: Irán: CBS dice que EE. UU. e Israel sopesan un nuevo ataque; Tasnim habla de un ataque estadounidense en Qeshm; Trump rechaza la postura de Teherán
articles.summary:
****Resumen:** CBS News informó de que Israel y EE. UU. estudian lanzar a corto plazo un nuevo ataque contra Irán; Netanyahu prefiere una operación conjunta y Trump no se ha decidido (https://x.com/i/status/2123779266731241612; https://x.com/i/status/2123760164574781688).**

La agencia estatal iraní Tasnim afirmó que EE. UU. atacó con un misil las afueras de la isla de Qeshm; más tarde, el vicegobernador de Hormozgán lo atribuyó a la destrucción de munición estadounidense sin explotar (fuentes estatales; véase Alerta temprana). Trump dijo que Irán «quiere un acuerdo que para mí no es aceptable», aunque sigue queriendo «un acuerdo de verdad» (https://x.com/i/status/2123831860299985193), y llamó a la guerra «un pequeño movimiento militar» (@ClashReport, https://x.com/i/status/2123831612563701852). El embajador israelí en Washington, Yechiel Leiter, dijo que las tropas estadounidenses volverán a casa «cuando Irán sea derrotado» (https://x.com/i/status/2123812362402632018).
articles.why: Una nueva escalada volvería a golpear el tráfico por Ormuz y los precios de la energía, con un segundo petrolero alcanzado cerca de Jasab esta semana.
articles.watch: Declaración oficial de EE. UU. sobre Qeshm; avisos del UKMTO; despliegue estadounidense (salida de F-35C frente a refuerzos).

articles.headline: Actualización: la coalición saudí ataca el puerto de Hodeida, Saná y centrales eléctricas; los hutíes dicen haber alcanzado la central de Shuqaiq y el puerto de Jizán
articles.summary:
****Resumen:** La coalición liderada por Arabia Saudí anunció una «operación especial» contra objetivos hutíes: atacó instalaciones del puerto de Hodeida que, según ella, servían para introducir armas y misiles balísticos, y emplazamientos de misiles y drones en Saná (@sentdefender, https://x.com/i/status/2123783553720725783; Al Jazeera, https://x.com/i/status/2123777486571856035, https://x.com/i/status/2123783668917567504).**

Un vídeo mostró humo negro sobre Hodeida (https://x.com/i/status/2123786496301797507). Arabia Saudí atacó también las centrales de Saada y Moca (https://x.com/i/status/2123756693003624804). Sonaron alertas en Jizán tras lanzamientos de misiles desde Yemen (https://x.com/i/status/2123761888446103792); un portavoz saudí dijo que cayó «metralla» en la zona de Shuqaiq, y los hutíes (Ansarolá) afirmaron haber atacado la central de Al Shuqaiq y el puerto de Jizán en represalia (https://x.com/i/status/2123801618709663968, https://x.com/i/status/2123832101040472485).
articles.why: Una guerra abierta entre Arabia Saudí y los hutíes en torno a los puertos del mar Rojo vuelve a amenazar la ruta de Suez del comercio europeo. Lo que dicen los hutíes son afirmaciones suyas.
articles.watch: Daños en Shuqaiq y Jizán; amenazas hutíes contra el distrito financiero Rey Abdalá de Riad; avisos a la navegación.

articles.headline: Ataques de Ucrania: lanzadores de misiles rusos alcanzados; se extienden las restricciones a la venta de combustible en Rusia
articles.summary:
****Resumen:** Kiev afirma que sus fuerzas alcanzaron tres lanzadores de misiles balísticos rusos y un sistema antiaéreo de cañones y misiles, y que destruyeron uno de los lanzadores (Kyiv Independent, https://x.com/i/status/2123799788080525772).**

Reuters informa de que más regiones rusas limitan la venta de combustible porque los ataques ucranianos con drones reducen la producción de las refinerías (https://x.com/i/status/2123793544515125726), y de que los ataques al puente de Crimea tensan la logística rusa (https://x.com/i/status/2123757030284382244). Según Defense News, Ucrania prevé duplicar el suministro de drones y triplicar los ataques en profundidad con apoyo de socios europeos, pese a que Washington le pide priorizar la defensa del frente (sección Europa de defensenews.com).
articles.why: La campaña ucraniana de ataques en profundidad depende cada vez más del apoyo europeo, un terreno en el que las decisiones europeas se apartan de las preferencias de EE. UU.

articles.headline: El misil intercontinental ruso RS-28 Sarmat podría haber entrado en servicio, según el IISS
articles.summary:
****Resumen:** Un análisis del IISS (Missile Dialogue Initiative, Matthew Bint) señala que las imágenes por satélite indican que el ICBM nuclear RS-28 Sarmat podría haber empezado a entrar en servicio en las Fuerzas de Misiles Estratégicos, y que podrían realizarse más pruebas de vuelo para disipar las dudas sobre su fiabilidad (https://x.com/i/status/2123753731523018978).**

Antecedentes (archivo CEAFE): @F_CEAFE sigue el Sarmat desde diciembre de 2019 (planes de ojivas hipersónicas de nueva generación) y marzo de 2020, cuando Rusia completó la modernización de sus instalaciones de producción en serie (TASS).

**Fuentes:** [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/1206565634970140673), [@F_CEAFE](https://x.com/i/status/1243610476203950081)
articles.why: El equilibrio estratégico se mueve mientras se habla de conversaciones de «desnuclearización» entre EE. UU. y Rusia, en las que Europa no tiene asiento más allá de las disuasiones francesa y británica (véase el ejercicio Francia-Suecia, edición de las 08:30).

articles.headline: Actualización: el ataque ruso deja al menos 8 muertos en Ucrania y alcanza la mayor subestación de Europa y embajadas de la UE
articles.summary:
**Al Jazeera eleva a ocho los muertos del ataque aéreo ruso nocturno en toda Ucrania, con los puentes y las infraestructuras de Kiev como objetivo (https://x.com/i/status/2123745672440500685); AFP informa de seis muertos en Kiev (https://x.com/i/status/2123730578977526025).**

El Kyiv Independent dice que los ataques alcanzaron una subestación de 750 kV en el oeste de Ucrania, que describe como la mayor de Europa, citando a un responsable energético anónimo (https://x.com/i/status/2123699240249528355). AFP señala daños en una catedral histórica y en las embajadas de Austria y Países Bajos (https://x.com/i/status/2123724036328874143). Se informó de la destrucción de la estación ferroviaria de Sknyliv, en Leópolis (https://x.com/i/status/2123704034229985731), y hubo cortes de luz de emergencia en las regiones de Leópolis, Transcarpatia e Ivano-Frankivsk. El Ministerio de Defensa ruso (fuente estatal) afirma haber alcanzado puentes de carretera y ferrocarril usados para mover armamento en Kiev y la región de Odesa (t.me/s/mod_russia_en). El canciller alemán Friedrich Merz dijo que «Rusia no ganará esta guerra» y que Alemania es hoy el mayor apoyo de Ucrania (https://x.com/i/status/2123736715038699781, https://x.com/i/status/2123739689249079435).

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123745672440500685), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123730578977526025), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123699240249528355), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123724036328874143), [t.me](https://t.me/s/mod_russia_en)
articles.why: Dos embajadas de la UE alcanzadas y ataques a nudos de la red cerca de las fronteras de la UE llevan los efectos de la guerra directamente a la Unión, justo al empezar el invierno y cuando los europeos asumen la mayor parte del coste del apoyo a Ucrania.
articles.watch: Cifras oficiales de la Fuerza Aérea ucraniana; duración de los cortes de luz; respuesta de la UE a los daños en las embajadas.

articles.headline: Ucrania ataca una estación del oleoducto Druzhba en Tartaristán y la unidad de drones «Rubicón» en Kursk
articles.summary:
**El Estado Mayor ucraniano confirmó un ataque contra la estación de bombeo de Kaleykino, cerca de Almetievsk (Tartaristán), un nudo clave del oleoducto Druzhba a más de 1.000 km del frente (Kyiv Independent, https://x.com/i/status/2123749715938296187).**

Las fuerzas ucranianas también atacaron una base del Centro Rubicón de Tecnologías No Tripuladas Avanzadas, núcleo de la nueva rama rusa de Sistemas No Tripulados, en la región de Kursk (https://x.com/i/status/2123735020393136270). Reuters afirma que la destrucción parcial del puente de Crimea refuerza la campaña de Kiev para cortar las líneas de suministro rusas al sur de Ucrania (https://x.com/i/status/2123695365387866116). Defense News informa de que Ucrania prevé duplicar el suministro de drones y triplicar los ataques en profundidad con apoyo europeo.

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123749715938296187), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123735020393136270), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123695365387866116), [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/)
articles.why: Druzhba sigue abasteciendo a Hungría y Eslovaquia, de modo que estos ataques afectan directamente a la política energética de la UE. La campaña en profundidad es la acción a la que Moscú dice responder.
articles.watch: Posibles interrupciones del flujo de Druzhba hacia Hungría y Eslovaquia y la reacción de sus gobiernos.

articles.headline: Actualización: la coalición saudí ordena evacuar el puerto de Hodeida; los hutíes amenazan puertos y centrales saudíes
articles.summary:
**La coalición liderada por Arabia Saudí pidió a los civiles evacuar el puerto de Hodeida, el principal de Yemen en el mar Rojo, en manos hutíes (Al Jazeera, https://x.com/i/status/2123733381657526577).**

El portavoz hutí Yahya Saree advirtió de que un ataque al puerto provocaría ataques contra los puertos saudíes del mar Rojo, incluido Yeda (https://x.com/i/status/2123746174788043226, https://x.com/i/status/2123744828919881971). Los hutíes dijeron que la central de Shuqaiq sería atacada «en las próximas horas» en represalia por los ataques a centrales de Saada y Moca, y señalaron como objetivo el distrito financiero Rey Abdalá de Riad (Iran International, https://x.com/i/status/2123749318486024242, https://x.com/i/status/2123749993702191360). Fuerzas hutíes atacaron además posiciones gubernamentales en Raghwan (Marib) (https://x.com/i/status/2123725771697008857).

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123733381657526577), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123746174788043226), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123749318486024242), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123749993702191360)
articles.why: Una batalla por Hodeida y ataques a puertos saudíes del mar Rojo golpearían la ruta de Suez, por la que pasa buena parte del comercio europeo con Asia, sumándose al bloqueo de Ormuz.
articles.watch: Ataques de la coalición sobre Hodeida; ataques hutíes contra Yeda, Shuqaiq o Riad; avisos de UKMTO para el mar Rojo.

articles.headline: Actualización: la Guardia Revolucionaria habla de una «confrontación final»; memorando estadounidense sobre el bloqueo; Israel mejora David's Sling
articles.summary:
**El comandante de la Guardia Revolucionaria, Ahmad Vahidi, afirmó: «Entramos en la confrontación final con el imperialismo global» y prometió venganza por asesinatos recientes (https://x.com/i/status/2123717994668855549, https://x.com/i/status/2123728544782000616); dijo que Irán podría revisar su doctrina militar al ser preguntado por ampliar el alcance de sus misiles (https://x.com/i/status/2123704250454663241).**

El imán interino de la oración del viernes en Teherán dijo que las fuerzas armadas tienen orden de actuar «sin límites en un momento determinado» (https://x.com/i/status/2123731327849803837), y el comandante de Jatam al Anbiya advirtió de una respuesta contundente a cualquier ataque contra las presas iraníes (https://x.com/i/status/2123698973269545414). El ministro de Exteriores, Abás Araqchí, dijo que Irán hará todo lo posible por exportar petróleo y seguir negociando (https://x.com/i/status/2123707712001224783). Al Jazeera revela que un memorando interno de la Administración Marítima de EE. UU. reconoce el impacto del bloqueo en el transporte comercial (https://x.com/i/status/2123686402139275515). Según Bloomberg, Israel ha mejorado David's Sling para interceptar más tipos de misiles balísticos iraníes con menor coste: cada interceptor Stunner cuesta alrededor de 1 millón de dólares, frente a 3 millones del Arrow 3 y más de 4 millones del PAC-3; Irán conservaría al menos 1.700 misiles balísticos (difundido en https://x.com/i/status/2123718061861519405).

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123717994668855549), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123704250454663241), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123731327849803837), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123686402139275515), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123718061861519405)
articles.why: La retórica iraní sobre un «momento determinado», el bloqueo ampliado y las amenazas hutíes apuntan a una posible nueva fase de la guerra de Irán, con efectos directos en los precios de la energía en Europa (Lufthansa cita el choque energético al recortar 1.000 empleos, https://x.com/i/status/2123743182991102302).
articles.watch: Decisiones de EE. UU. sobre nuevos ataques; movimientos de petroleros iraníes hacia la línea del bloqueo.

articles.headline: Actualización: fuerzas iraquíes entran en Jurf al Sajar, bastión de Kataib Hezbolá
articles.summary:
**En virtud del acuerdo de compromiso conocido esta mañana, fuerzas federales iraquíes entraron en Jurf al Sajar (provincia de Babilonia), en manos de Kataib Hezbolá —el principal aliado miliciano de Irán en Irak— desde hace más de una década (Reuters, Iran International, https://x.com/i/status/2123702785631719781, https://x.com/i/status/2123723728215330991).**

El primer ministro Ali al Zaidi pidió contención a las tropas, al afirmar que no se enfrentan a ningún enemigo (https://x.com/i/status/2123744582835777717).

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123702785631719781), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123723728215330991), [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123744582835777717)
