articles.headline: Germany's record €139bn 2027 defence budget clears committee, with 16 new Airbus A400Ms
articles.summary:
**The Bundestag budget committee approved Germany's 2027 defence budget and the Bundeswehr special-fund plan in an overnight session ending on 13 November: more than €139bn in total, of which about €109.7bn is the regular defence budget, €31.4bn more than in 2026.**

The amendments allow the purchase of 16 new Airbus A400M airlifters in tactical configuration (self-protection, DIRCM, Link 16) to replace the 16 earliest German A400Ms, which are configured only for logistics in permissive airspace; the older aircraft could be sold to partners. The budget also adds more frigates, more communications satellites and funding for a space-based sensor network, according to Aviation Week. The full Bundestag votes from 24 to 27 November and the Bundesrat on 18 December; no price has been given for the aircraft.
articles.why: This is the kind of purchase CEAFE wants: a European aircraft, built by a multinational European programme (final assembly in Seville, Spain), bought by Europe's largest defence budget. It also gives the A400M line new work as its backlog shrinks (139 of 178 delivered by March, per AFP via defence-blog). One caveat: Germany's existing tactical A400Ms use the Israeli Elbit J-MUSIC DIRCM; a European self-protection suite would keep the whole value chain in Europe.
articles.watch: Bundestag plenary vote (24–27 Nov); contract with Airbus and its value; which partner buys the 16 older aircraft.

articles.headline: Morocco reported close to French Scorpène submarines, with Rafale F4s and A330 MRTTs also in talks
articles.summary:
**Moroccan and Spanish outlets reported on 16 November that Rabat is in the final phase of buying Scorpène submarines from Naval Group, citing a French National Assembly foreign-affairs committee report (October 2025) that said Morocco was "in the final phase of an agreement" for the boats.**

El Español says the deal covers two submarines, after Rabat set aside offers from Germany, Russia, Portugal and Greece, and includes technology transfer and a maintenance facility in Casablanca; Médias24 says the signature could come during King Mohammed VI's visit to Paris. A post reposted by @F_CEAFE describes a wider package: 12–18 Dassault Rafale F4s, 2–3 Scorpènes, up to four Airbus A330 MRTT tankers and Airbus H125/H145 helicopters. None of this is officially confirmed by Paris, Rabat, Dassault or Naval Group; the Rafale talks were first reported in July 2026 (deliveries 2030–31 mentioned).
articles.why: A package of this size would be one of Europe's biggest export wins of the year, all of it European (French and Airbus) hardware in a market where the US F-16 and other non-European suppliers compete. For Spain it would be a significant change on its southern flank: a first Moroccan submarine force operating around the Strait of Gibraltar.
articles.watch: Date of the royal visit to Paris and any signature; reaction in Spain and Algeria.

articles.headline: Italy will build its own naval missile launcher for the MBDA Stratus LO cruise missile
articles.summary:
**Italy's 2026–2028 multi-year defence plan (Documento Programmatico Pluriennale, sent to Parliament on 10 November and published on 15 November) formalises the development of a national vertical launch system, the "lanciatore polivalente nazionale", for the new FREMM EVO frigates and the future DDX destroyers.**

It must fire the Stratus LO, the stealthy land-attack and anti-ship cruise missile that MBDA is developing for France, the UK and Italy; Rivista Italiana Difesa reports an eight-cell module with cells larger than the French SYLVER's, able to fire the Aster 30 and later the Aquila anti-hypersonic interceptor. The deep-strike programme keeps its €260m total but brings funding forward (€71.2m in 2026, €170.2m in 2027). The plan also funds two FREMM EVO frigates from Orizzonte Sistemi Navali (Fincantieri–Leonardo). No manufacturer is named for the launcher.
articles.why: Stratus LO is a genuine three-nation European missile, and putting it on Italian ships instead of buying US Mk 41 launchers and Tomahawks keeps the strike capability sovereign. But a new Italian launcher next to the French SYLVER is another national duplicate inside Europe; a joint Franco-Italian launcher would give MBDA's missiles one common home.
articles.watch: Choice of launcher maker (likely Leonardo or MBDA Italia); the DPP's other lines, including GCAP (see Italy's GCAP spending, 16 Nov 07:30 brief).

articles.headline: UK defends its use of SpaceX's Starshield as Europe debates dependence on Musk
articles.summary:
**UK defence minister Luke Pollard told Parliament that "Starlink is not used for UK military operations" but that the Ministry of Defence does use SpaceX's military Starshield service, alongside military and commercial satcom, to provide "operational resilience through diversity".**

In answers published on 16 November he said the MoD has "a substantial number" of Starshield terminals but would not give the figure or list their uses, citing national security. The questions came from Liberal Democrat MPs after restrictions were placed on Ukraine's access to SpaceX services.
articles.why: The UK, Europe's leading military space power alongside France, now depends in part on a US private company whose service to Ukraine has been restricted. That is the kill-switch risk CEAFE warns about, applied to communications. European alternatives exist or are being built: Eutelsat OneWeb, the UK's own Skynet, and the EU's IRIS² constellation.
articles.watch: Ukraine's Starshield restrictions (Conflicts section); IRIS² timetable.

articles.headline: US Senate proposes a $1.1 trillion defence bill, with $47bn for munitions and $9.4bn for Golden Dome
articles.summary:
**Senate Appropriations Republicans released a $1.072 trillion fiscal 2027 defence bill on 16 November (military construction excluded), short of the $1.5 trillion the administration wants.**

They moved nearly $69bn of the White House's stalled $350bn reconciliation request into regular appropriations: $9.4bn for Golden Dome missile defence, $3bn for the new Defense Autonomous Warfare Group and $47.2bn for munitions, $40.6bn of it for multiyear deals such as AMRAAM, PAC-3 MSE and PrSM. Appropriators add 25 F-35s (five A, five B, 15 C; +$4.1bn). The bill also has $750m for the Ukraine Security Assistance Initiative, about $175m for the Baltic Security Initiative and about $1bn for a First Island Chain initiative (Philippines, Taiwan). Separately, the Pentagon failed its ninth annual audit and now aims for a clean opinion by 2028.
articles.why: US munitions multiyear contracts (PAC-3 MSE, AMRAAM) fund the same production lines Europeans queue for, so US orders come first. With $750m for Ukraine and $175m for the Baltics, the US contribution to Europe's security is now small next to the EU's own: the Commission paid €1.71bn to Ukraine on 16 November alone.
articles.watch: House–Senate negotiation before 11 Dec; fate of the $350bn reconciliation package.

articles.headline: Update: Vulcan failure tightens the US launch squeeze; Europe's space week opens in Bremen
articles.summary:
**Breaking Defense reports that the Vulcan failure of 15 November is likely to ground the rocket for months, leaving SpaceX's Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy as the only US rockets certified for critical national-security payloads while Blue Origin's New Glenn remains grounded; six Vulcan missions were already moved to SpaceX by 1 October.**

If the BE-4 engine is involved, New Glenn is also affected. SpaceX stopped taking commercial Falcon orders for after 2028. Meanwhile Arianespace promoted the next Ariane 64 launch for Amazon Leo (VA271/LE-04), and Space Tech Expo Europe opens in Bremen today (17–19 November), with ESA's SME office present. US firms are there too: Redwire is showing its Hammerhead LEO platform built in Kruibeke, Belgium, by its Belgian subsidiary (the former QinetiQ Space).
articles.why: A US launch shortage makes Ariane 6 more valuable, even to American customers like Amazon. Europe should make sure its launch capacity serves European sovereign missions first and keeps growing, rather than filling US gaps.
articles.watch: ULA's failure investigation; VA271 launch date; EU SST webinar on space surveillance on 19 Nov (https://x.com/i/status/2122396785444602251).

articles.headline: RoW and arms sales: Thailand to rerun its Hanwha frigate tender; Malaysia looks beyond NATO suppliers
articles.summary:
**Thailand: an appeals committee reportedly ordered the Royal Thai Navy to cancel and restart its 17bn-baht frigate tender, in which South Korea's Hanwha Ocean had been selected with a 16.73bn-baht offer, after an appeal by the Thai Frigate Building Consortium.**

- **Thailand:** an appeals committee reportedly ordered the Royal Thai Navy to cancel and restart its 17bn-baht frigate tender, in which South Korea's Hanwha Ocean had been selected with a 16.73bn-baht offer, after an appeal by the Thai Frigate Building Consortium. The Navy is reviewing the order; a new tender could take about six months. https://x.com/i/status/2122503283445207367 ; https://www.nationthailand.com/news/politics/40073585 ; https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/3355814/navy-reviews-call-to-scrap-frigate-tender

- **Malaysia:** Macron is in Kuala Lumpur seeking a strategic partnership including defence; Malaysia's defence minister questioned Western suppliers' reliability after Norway revoked an export licence for missiles for its navy. Full story in Economy. https://www.france24.com/en/asia-pacific/20261117-macron-malaysia-france-defence-rare-earths-trade-energy

articles.headline: Italy says it backs a fast German entry into the GCAP fighter
articles.summary:
**Italy's defence ministry issued an unusually long statement on 16 November denying a Financial Times report that Defence Minister Guido Crosetto had opposed giving Germany partner status in GCAP, the Italy–UK–Japan sixth-generation fighter.**

Rome says it proposed observer status for Germany only as an "immediate, Program information-sharing enabler towards subsequent full membership", to speed up German entry without delaying the programme's timetable. Berlin is considering joining after its talks with France on the rival FCAS jet collapsed. The three partners awarded a £4.6bn ($6.1bn) development contract to their national champions in July; Italy has spent €875m on development this year. Canada already has observer status.
articles.why: With FCAS stalled, GCAP is becoming the main European home for a next-generation fighter, and German entry would bring two of the EU's three largest defence budgets into one programme. That is positive for European scale. But GCAP is not an EU programme: it has a non-EU lead (UK) and a non-European partner (Japan), and it leaves France on a separate path. Two parallel European fighters would repeat the Eurofighter–Rafale split that CEAFE regards as a cost Europe can no longer afford.
articles.watch: Germany's decision on GCAP, and any French reaction on the future of FCAS. Related: Italy's GCAP budget increase (07:30 brief, topic 3).

articles.headline: EU pays €1.71bn more for Ukraine's drones, ammunition and air defence; 40% goes to EU manufacturers
articles.summary:
**The Commission disbursed €1.71bn to Ukraine on 16 November under the €90bn Ukraine Support Loan, the eighth payment from its defence component.**

The money will buy drones, ammunition and air-defence systems, including early-warning radars and missiles, from Ukrainian and European manufacturers; about 40% will fund contracts with firms established in the EU. The Commission says €23.6bn of EU support remains available for the rest of 2026, including about €19.2bn from the loan (€10.2bn for Ukraine's defence industrial capacity, €9.0bn budget support). Commissioner Andrius Kubilius said he told Ukrainian PM Koretskyi about the payment and that both sides will keep working on the EU–Ukraine Defence Pact and on integrating their industries. Separately, Kubilius received Moldova's President Maia Sandu in Brussels, saying Moldova already takes part in European defence projects and will be integrated gradually into the European defence architecture.
articles.why: EU money is buying weapons from Ukrainian and EU firms rather than through US Foreign Military Sales. This is the European preference CEAFE supports, and it strengthens a Ukrainian industry that the EU plans to integrate into its own.
articles.watch: The next USL defence tranches and the share going to EU firms; progress on the EU–Ukraine Defence Pact.

articles.headline: Pentagon deputy secretary steered Lockheed and RTX to his Goldman banker during missile megadeals, Bloomberg reports
articles.summary:
**According to Bloomberg (16 Nov, sources not named), US Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg suggested that Lockheed Martin and RTX hire Jim Donovan, a Goldman Sachs banker who worked for years with Feinberg and his former firm Cerberus, while the companies negotiated multibillion-dollar contracts with the Pentagon.**

Both companies hired him. Donovan advised on Lockheed's $59bn agreement to triple Patriot interceptor production over seven years and its plans to sell a record number of F-35s, and on two RTX missile contracts worth more than $45bn. Some executives reportedly felt pressure from Pentagon officials. Goldman reviewed the concerns internally and capped its fees, but allowed Donovan to keep working. Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell called the claims "completely false". Democrats, who are about to take control of Congress, plan to scrutinise the Pentagon's contracts for conflicts of interest.
articles.why: These are the deals that set price and delivery for the Patriot interceptors that European governments are queuing to buy. They are negotiated in Washington, under US political rules and pressures over which Europe has no say. It is one more argument for European production of the equivalent capability (SAMP/T NG, IRIS-T SLM), whose terms Europeans set themselves.
articles.watch: Congressional inquiries in the new Congress; any review of the Lockheed and RTX frameworks.

articles.headline: Update: the Patriot interceptor ramp-up gets a $1.6bn second-source rocket-motor order
articles.summary:
**Northrop Grumman announced on 16 November a $1.6bn multi-year order for solid rocket motors and ignition safety devices for Lockheed Martin's PAC-3 MSE interceptor.**

Built at Allegany Ballistics Laboratory (West Virginia), the motors make Northrop a second source alongside incumbent L3Harris. The order is part of the $3bn+ framework agreements of August 2026 and supports Lockheed's January 2026 framework to lift PAC-3 MSE output from about 600 to about 2,000 a year over seven years. Quantities and delivery rates were not disclosed.
articles.why: This follows the 07:30 Bruegel analysis on Europe's Patriot dependence. The US is fixing its own supply bottleneck in the propulsion stage. European buyers of PAC-3 depend on that supply chain and its priorities ("U.S. and allied forces", US first).
articles.watch: Patriot dependence thread ([2026-11-16_0730.md](2026-11-16_0730.md), topic 1).

articles.headline: Korean missiles made in Poland: Hanwha–WB breaks ground on a CGR-080 plant
articles.summary:
**WB Group publicised the groundbreaking (4 November) of the Hanwha WB Advanced System (HWBAS) plant in Gorzów Wielkopolski, a 51:49 joint venture between Hanwha Aerospace and WB Electronics.**

It will make CGR-080 guided rockets for Poland's Homar-K (K239 Chunmoo) launchers under multi-year contracts signed in December 2025. Test batches are due in 2029 and series production around 2029/2030, with "several thousand missiles per year" according to a WB spokesperson quoted by Janes. The project includes technology transfer, MRO capability, more than 60 buildings and over 250 jobs. WB says the plant could supply Chunmoo users worldwide, "with a particular focus on the European market".
articles.why: Local production and technology transfer are better than buying off the shelf. But the design authority and the majority stake stay Korean, and the plant aims to sell Korean rockets to other Europeans. Through the 51:49 structure, that would bring a non-European missile into Europe's supply chain. The European alternative for long-range rocket artillery is France's sovereign FLP-T programme, and Poland's own industry could have been the partner in a European programme.
articles.watch: Whether other European Chunmoo/Homar-K customers emerge; Poland's balance between Korean, US and European suppliers.

articles.headline: Sovereign military software: Europe looks for Palantir alternatives
articles.summary:
**Reuters (Berlin, 16 Nov) reports that European defence ministries are trying to reduce their dependence on Palantir's Maven Smart System, and that a growing number of European firms are competing for the business.**

Germany has a shortlist of a handful of solutions that does not include Palantir; a person familiar with it said they would not match Palantir but would be "good enough", keep data sovereign and reach about 80% of requirements within a year. France's procurement agency (DGA) is building a sovereign platform, **Arcadia**, with several suppliers: contracts by year-end and a field version by mid-2027 (deputy head Alexandre Lahousse). The Netherlands uses some Palantir software but wants a European alternative within two years; procurement minister Derk Boswijk said European AI know-how is "very fragmented". Helsing unveiled **Clarity** on 11 November ("developed and built in Europe, under European control", running on customer-owned infrastructure) and offers an initial version to the Bundeswehr's Lithuania brigade within months. Systematic (Denmark, SitaWare), Thales, Safran and Comand AI are also competing. Palantir says its NATO system has no "kill switch"; NATO's SACEUR, Gen. Grynkewich, praised Maven this summer. @F_CEAFE posted the story this morning.

**Note for the compiler:** the Economía 13:30 brief also carries this story (its topic 5). Suggested primary section: Defence Industry, with a cross-reference in Economy.
articles.why: This is the kill-switch and data-sovereignty argument applied to the software layer that now decides targeting. Reuters links the concern to the Starlink speed restrictions that hampered Ukraine's drone interception last month. The weak point is Boswijk's: Germany, France and the Netherlands are each building a national answer. A single European platform (EDF/EDIP funding, a common procurement through EDA or OCCAR) would give European firms the scale Palantir has in the US market, where Pentagon software must be American-controlled.
articles.watch: DGA Arcadia awards (by end-2026); the German shortlist decision; whether the Netherlands joins a German or French solution.

articles.headline: ICEYE unveils Gen5: an 11 cm, ITAR-free European radar satellite
articles.summary:
**Finland's ICEYE announced its fifth-generation SAR satellite on 16 November, "the sharpest commercially built" according to the company.**

For government customers it images with 1,800 MHz bandwidth and resolution as fine as 11 cm (subject to ITU compliance); all customers get 1,200 MHz and 16 cm. Image window separation is cut by more than 30%, imaging time per orbit is twice that of earlier ICEYE satellites, and an on-board AI processor will allow screening and tip-and-cue in orbit. ICEYE says new customers can have a "fully sovereign Gen5 system, free of ITAR restrictions, operational within 12 months of signing", including ground segment and training. It describes itself as "natively European, founded in Finland", with over 1,500 employees. Bloomberg covered the launch.
articles.why: A European firm is now selling a sovereign, ITAR-free military surveillance constellation, exactly the capability CEAFE argues Europe should buy from itself rather than from US providers. ICEYE satellites are also the target of Russian proximity operations (Kosmos 2612 near ICEYE-X36 in October; sibling satellites drifting towards ICEYE-X37, per the Conflictos log in shared/space.md), which shows how central they have become to European and Ukrainian intelligence.
articles.watch: first Gen5 launch date and launcher (European or US); government customers.

articles.headline: Türkiye: ASELSAN signs €1.28bn with ROKETSAN for missile seekers and data links
articles.summary:
**ASELSAN told Borsa Istanbul's disclosure platform (KAP) on 16 November that it signed contracts worth **€1,281,101,744** with ROKETSAN for the supply of missile data-link and seeker-head systems.**

ROKETSAN accounted for 5.6% of ASELSAN's net sales and 7.3% of its trade receivables in the latest statements. The filing gives no delivery schedule, number of contracts or missile programmes. It follows a €1.234bn ASELSAN–ROKETSAN contract for air-defence subcomponents disclosed on 23 September 2026 (icwwm.com). The same morning ROKETSAN promoted its long-range KARA ATMACA cruise missile and ASELSAN its TOLUN glide-bomb family.
articles.why: Türkiye keeps the most valuable parts of a missile (the seeker and the data link) inside its own industry, in two large contracts within two months. Europe has the equivalent firms (MBDA, Diehl, Thales, Leonardo, Kongsberg, Saab), but many European air-defence buyers still import complete US systems. Türkiye's model of national champions supplying each other is a benchmark for European vertical integration at EU scale.
articles.watch: which programmes (HİSAR/SİPER air defence, ATMACA, ÇAKIR, TAYFUN) the seekers are for.

articles.headline: European tech sovereignty: TeQuantS quantum links and a Nordic-Baltic AI gigafactory bid
articles.summary:
**Thales Alenia Space (Thales 67%, Leonardo 33%) signed two contract amendments with ESA as prime of TeQuantS, under ESA's ARTES programme with CNES support.**

- **Thales Alenia Space** (Thales 67%, Leonardo 33%) signed two contract amendments with ESA as prime of **TeQuantS**, under ESA's ARTES programme with CNES support. The new phase sets up a quantum laboratory at CNES to test an entangled-photon source, satellite–ground time synchronisation and ground photon detection, towards the **QINSAT** satellite, which will demonstrate entangled-photon transmission between space and Earth. Partners include Airbus Defence and Space, AUREA Technology, Bertin, OGS Technologies, SIGMAWORKS and two French labs. The release cites government users exchanging information "in a resilient and sovereign manner".

- **Nokia** leads **AI Gigafactory Northern** with Nscale, Telia, Verda and Skeleton: a federated AI infrastructure across Finland, Estonia, Latvia and Sweden combining compute, sovereign cloud, connectivity and decarbonised energy, to bid in the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking's AI Gigafactory tender.
articles.why: Both are positive examples of the line: European primes, start-ups and labs working together under ESA and EU programmes on technologies (quantum-secure links, sovereign AI compute) that the defence sector will depend on. CEAFE's caution from the SABRE case applies: ESA/EU-funded IP should carry ownership-retention clauses so it stays in Europe.

articles.headline: Update: Vulcan failure traced to the Centaur upper stage, Space Force decision on national-security launches pending
articles.summary:
**New since the 07:30 brief: reporting now places the anomaly in the **Centaur V upper stage near the end of its burn**, with the solid boosters (redesigned nozzles) and the BE-4 first stage performing normally (DW; Spaceflight Now; Behind the Black).**

ULA and the customer are investigating. The Space Force had paused Vulcan national-security missions after the February nozzle failure and wanted data from this flight before deciding; that decision is now further away (Spaceflight Now, DW). Reuters and DW stress it was ULA's first outright failure since 2006. (See 07:30 brief, topic 6.)
articles.why: With Vulcan and New Glenn both grounded, Amazon's 24 Ariane 6 launches and Europe's own institutional missions depend on Ariane 6 cadence; a reliable European launcher is a commercial and strategic asset while US alternatives other than SpaceX falter.

articles.headline: Industry round-up: Poland's GLADIUS in service, Airbus helicopters for the Marine Nationale, L3Harris under FAA scrutiny
articles.summary:
**WB Group (Poland): its GLADIUS reconnaissance-strike system (loitering munitions with its own reconnaissance and command chain) is becoming routine in the 14th Suwałki Anti-Tank Regiment of the 16th Mechanised Division, according to the company.**

- **WB Group (Poland):** its GLADIUS reconnaissance-strike system (loitering munitions with its own reconnaissance and command chain) is becoming routine in the 14th Suwałki Anti-Tank Regiment of the 16th Mechanised Division, according to the company. A Polish-built system in front-line Polish service on NATO's eastern border.

- **Airbus Helicopters** marked the French Navy's 400th anniversary, flying alongside the Marine Nationale (European platform in European service).

- **L3Harris (US):** the FAA is investigating whether a router installed by contractor L3Harris during copper-to-fibre work in El Dorado, Arkansas, flooded the air-traffic-control network and triggered last week's nationwide ground stop; about 60–69 similar routers had broadcasting disabled while tests continue (USA Today, 14 Nov; ABC News). Not covered in earlier briefs.

- **Elbit Systems (Israel)** is marketing its space electro-optics at Space Tech Expo (company post). Israeli space optics competes with European suppliers for European EO satellites.

articles.headline: Bruegel: Europe's bet on US technology for air superiority "is unravelling"
articles.summary:
**A Bruegel analysis published on 10 November (Burilkov, Ospital, Wolff), flagged on the European list by @AresGroup_EU, says that relying on the US industrial base for air and missile defence has become "a major strategic liability".**

European countries ordered 1,519 Patriot missiles between February 2022 and the end of 2025, against 1,026 in the previous seven years. Europe accounted for 84% of Patriots ordered worldwide in 2022–2025. PAC-3 MSE deliveries rose from 385 (2023) to 620 (2025), but the backlog reached 4,300 missiles in May 2026, at least 35% of them for Europe. At current rates that is close to seven years of production. The US also told Europeans in early 2026 to expect further delays because of the Iran war. Patriots make up 67% of Europe's long-range air-defence launchers (182 of 304, using IISS data). France and Italy, which operate the European SAMP/T (Aster 30, Eurosam), have no Patriot orders.
articles.why: This is CEAFE's argument in figures. Buying American was meant to secure availability and US commitment. Instead it created a technological path dependency and a seven-year queue controlled by another country's priorities. Bruegel concludes that, had Europe invested decisively in home-grown alternatives in 2022, "it would have made a major difference already by now". It calls for long-term order books for SAMP/T and the new 10-nation **Freyja** system (a prototype is possible by mid-2027). Germany, with 70 Patriot launchers, is the biggest exposed operator. The European alternative already exists but lacks orders.
articles.watch: Freyja prototype timeline and funding (EDF/SAFE). German decisions on further Patriot or IRIS-T SLM/SAMP/T purchases. Bruegel recommends lobbying the US Congress elected in November 2026 for timely deliveries.

articles.headline: GLOBSEC: 71% of Europeans back an EU army
articles.summary:
**POLITICO (13 Nov) reports GLOBSEC's 2026 Trends survey of 14 countries (11 EU member states, Ukraine, the UK and the US).**

It finds that 71% of respondents want the EU to have its own army, rising to 82% in Romania, 78% in Lithuania and 75% in France. The figures are 70% in Poland and Bulgaria and 69% in Germany. In the EU countries surveyed, 78% back developing the bloc's own defence capabilities alongside NATO, and 77% in NATO countries would vote to stay in the Alliance. More than a third of European respondents now see the United States as a security threat. That share is around half in Germany, France and Britain, and Germany is the only country where a majority holds that view. Commissioner Andrius Kubilius shared the story on the list: "Europeans want 'more Europe' and 'stronger Europe' inside of NATO".
articles.why: Public opinion is ahead of governments. A European army, and the European industrial base needed to equip it, has majority support even in member states usually wary of integration. This gives political cover to European-preference rules in EDIP/SAFE procurement.
articles.watch: The full GLOBSEC Trends 2026 report. Whether the Commission's defence-union proposals cite it.

articles.headline: Italy raises GCAP spending to €875m while cutting army vehicle funds (Defense News)
articles.summary:
**Defense News (Tom Kington, 13 Nov) reports from Italy's delayed 2026 defence budget, sent to parliament this week.**

Italy spent **€875m on GCAP** in 2026, against €625m in 2025 and a €275m forecast, and plans €696m in 2027. Spending on the Lynx/Panther programme with Rheinmetall (1,050 Lynx, 272 Panther, a €23bn deal) plus Ariete upgrades fell to €177m, against a €425m forecast. It is due to rise to €872m in 2027. Italy's F-35 programme (115 aircraft) cost €782m this year, below the €961m forecast. Programme outlays add up to about €12.8bn, up €307m.
articles.why: Money is shifting towards a sovereign sixth-generation fighter built by European and allied industry (Leonardo, BAE Systems, with Japan) and away from the US F-35 line. That is positive for European R&D and jobs. Defense News notes that Germany is reportedly considering joining GCAP after the collapse of FCAS with France. That would bring the leading European economy into a programme that also includes Japan, and leave France outside. For CEAFE's line, Europe still has two rival fighter efforts and no single European programme. Italy's and Germany's choices will decide whether consolidation happens.
articles.watch: A German decision on GCAP (observer status first, as Italy proposed; see the 15 Nov brief). Parliamentary approval of the Italian budget.

articles.headline: Intra-European industrial moves: WB Group enters Germany, Diehl adds a shell line, Spain authorises PEM
articles.summary:
**WB Group (Poland) opens WB Germany.**

- **WB Group (Poland) opens WB Germany.** On 10 November, Poland's largest private defence group launched WB GERMANY in Berlin, with its office opposite the Defence Ministry according to Handelsblatt. It also announced its first German acquisition, Regensburg drone-propulsion maker Smoto, which Handelsblatt says will produce motors for WB drones. WB cites the Polish-German defence cooperation agreement of June and Bundeswehr trials in September in which WARMATE loitering munitions scored a 100% hit rate (company claim). DW adds that WB plans to deepen partnerships with Volkswagen and Rheinmetall MAN Military Vehicles.

- **Diehl Metall and Diehl Defence** posted highlights from the inauguration of a new production line for DiNa 155mm artillery shell bodies in Röthenbach (no capacity figure given in the post).

- **Spain:** the defence industry association TEDAE welcomed the Council of Ministers' authorisation of the Special Modernisation Programmes (PEM) on 13 November. It says they give multi-year budget certainty, skilled jobs and "sovereign industrial capacities" for Spain and Europe. The note gives no amounts.

- **UK–Norway:** the UK will buy three Norwegian P1118-design vessels as motherships for uncrewed mine-hunting systems (£90m). The first is due in 2031, with an option for three more. The deal was confirmed by Wes Streeting and Tore O. Sandvik in Oslo on 12 November, just before this window (GOV.UK; Breaking Defense).

- **EDA** ran its first operational experimentation campaign outside the EU, in Switzerland, testing drones and ground robots for urban resupply and casualty evacuation with Swiss and EU companies.
articles.why: These are the positive cases in the editorial line: cross-border European capital and production (a Polish group buying German suppliers), European ammunition capacity, and national programmes framed as European autonomy. As Handelsblatt notes, production in Germany is seen as the price of access to Bundeswehr money. Europe is applying a "local content" logic among its own members, which is healthy when it keeps the work inside Europe.
articles.watch: PEM amounts and programmes (BOE / Council of Ministers note). WB Germany's further acquisitions.

articles.headline: US firms court European buyers: Gambit in Bavaria, V-BAT for Greece via NATO, F-16 marketing, Redwire in Riga
articles.summary:
**General Atomics hosted Bavarian Minister-President Markus Söder at GA AeroTec Systems in Oberpfaffenhofen to promote its Gambit collaborative combat aircraft for the Luftwaffe.**

- **General Atomics** hosted Bavarian Minister-President Markus Söder at GA AeroTec Systems in Oberpfaffenhofen to promote its **Gambit** collaborative combat aircraft for the Luftwaffe. GA proposes "sovereign German and European mission systems" and possible integration or production in Bavaria, depending on orders (GA-ATS release; defence-industry.eu).

- **Shield AI:** NSPA ordered more **V-BAT** VTOL drones for the Hellenic Army and Navy (release of 11 Nov; quantity and value undisclosed). Greece approved 10 more on 23 July. First deliveries are due in January 2027 (Janes). Shield has opened an Athens office and signed an MoU with GEK TERNA on X-BAT.

- **Lockheed Martin Europe** ran F-16 posts ("Strengthening Europe's defense") and reposted Belgian F-16 drone-intercept scrambles from Lithuania. LM also promoted ATACMS and **PAC-3 ACE** (warhead tests against Class 3 drones, first flight planned next year).

- **Redwire** welcomed the US ambassador to its Riga facility, which the US Embassy calls "a leading supplier of uncrewed aircraft systems in the Baltic region".
articles.why: US primes are using local assembly and "sovereign mission systems" to win European budgets. Final design authority, export control (ITAR) and software stay in the US. Every Gambit or V-BAT order is one fewer for European alternatives, such as Airbus's and Helsing's uncrewed combat aircraft projects, or Schiebel's Austrian-built Camcopter S-100 VTOL drone for maritime ISR. Contrast with US rules: a European firm that wants Pentagon work must set up a US subsidiary under FOCI mitigation, with a US-citizen board, and its products then fall under ITAR. Greece buying through NSPA does not change who controls the technology.
articles.watch: A Luftwaffe CCA decision. Greek V-BAT deliveries in January 2027.

articles.headline: Space: Vulcan's first failure, Starship's first ship catch, and Europe's launcher gap
articles.summary:
**ULA Vulcan failed on 15 November.**

- **ULA Vulcan failed on 15 November.** The first Vulcan flight for Amazon Leo (LV-01, 40 satellites) suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes into flight, during the Centaur V burn, and the payload was lost. It was ULA's first outright mission failure since 2006 and Vulcan's first flight in nine months, after solid-booster nozzle problems (ULA; Spaceflight Now; Reuters). Amazon has 38 Vulcan launches booked, plus 24 on New Glenn (grounded since a May pad explosion), **24 on Ariane 6** and 13 on Falcon 9 (Spaceflight Now).

- **Starship Flight 15** (launched 13 Nov, 22:47 UTC) deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites. On 14 November, after about 22.5 hours in orbit, Ship 42 was caught by the launch tower for the first time. The Super Heavy booster diverted to splash down offshore and did not return as planned (SpaceX; The Verge; Spaceflight Now).

- **Rocket Lab's 100th Electron** (14 Nov, for Japan's iQPS) came after a HASTE launch for the US Space Force's **VICTUS HAZE** tactically responsive mission, 21 h 55 min apart. Rocket Lab says VICTUS HAZE lifted off 16 h 42 min after the Space Force call.

- **Europe:** Avio's CEO said the third Vega C launch of 2026 (six Thales Alenia Space IRIDE satellites for Italy) is slipping "very close to Christmas Day" because of late satellites. Avio now targets four, then five launches a year (European Spaceflight). ESA and ArianeGroup said October's Prometheus tests were not connected to the long-delayed Themis hop. Commissioner Kubilius toured Italian space industry (Leonardo, Thales Alenia Space, Telespazio, ALTEC, Argotec) on his "#EULaunchTour": "Increased satellite production requires European solutions for access to space."
articles.why: The US is moving towards fully reusable heavy lift (SpaceX: 127 launches and about 1,787 t to orbit so far in 2026, per Flight Atlas; see shared/launches.md), while Europe has flown 6 Ariane 6/Vega C missions. Vulcan's grounding and New Glenn's shows that Amazon's 24 Ariane 6 launches are a strategic commercial anchor for Europe. Reliable Ariane 6 cadence and reusable European launchers (Themis, the European Launcher Challenge) are a sovereignty issue, as both Kubilius and the German Space Command panel with ICEYE, Isar and OHB stressed ("responsive space").
articles.watch: The Vulcan failure investigation and its effect on US national-security launches (NSSL). The next Ariane 6 launch for Amazon Leo. The Vega C launch date.

headlines: Italy says it supports Germany joining GCAP, proposing observer status first
SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage; Rocket Lab’s Electron reaches 100 launches
ASELSAN’s EJDERHA system said to disable 51 drones at once; CEO says serial production has begun

articles.headline: Italy says it supports Germany joining GCAP, proposing observer status first
articles.summary:
Italy’s government said on Saturday, 14 November, that it fully supports Germany’s participation in the Global Combat Air Programme (GCAP) and called a *Financial Times* report that Rome had sought to block Berlin “entirely misleading.” In a defence ministry statement, Italy said it had proposed that Germany first join as an observer, to ease information-sharing and speed a later path to full membership without putting the programme’s timetable at risk, and that it had restated that position at the latest GCAP videoconference of the three partner nations. GCAP is the UK–Italy–Japan effort, led industrially by BAE Systems, Leonardo and Mitsubishi Heavy Industries, to field a next-generation fighter around 2035. Canada became GCAP’s first observer in July 2026, according to subsequent reporting.

The Japan Times, reporting on 15 November, noted that German defence minister Boris Pistorius had said earlier this month he expects a decision by the end of March on whether to join GCAP, after Berlin abandoned the Future Combat Air System (FCAS) New Generation Fighter project with France earlier in 2026. Subsequent reporting (The Telegraph, Aviacionline) said a German official had described observer-only status as “unacceptable” because Berlin wants a full workshare, including for Airbus Defence and Space. Berlin is also reported to be weighing a possible alternative partnership with Sweden and Spain (Airbus and Saab). The original Reuters article linked from @F_CEAFE could not be fetched in the briefs (HTTP 401); the same official line was taken from Il Sole 24 Ore, Arab News and The Japan Times.
articles.why: After the collapse of Franco-German FCAS, GCAP is the main live path to a European-involved sixth-generation fighter, albeit one anchored in a UK–Japan industrial axis as well as Italy. How Germany enters — or whether it builds a separate project with Sweden and Spain — will shape industrial workshare, timelines, and Europe’s long-term air-combat autonomy, in contrast to further reliance on the US F-35.
articles.watch: Germany’s formal response to observer status; any UK and Japanese comments; Pistorius’s end-of-March decision; whether France, Sweden and Spain outline an alternative combat-air path.

articles.headline: SpaceX catches a Starship upper stage; Rocket Lab’s Electron reaches 100 launches
articles.summary:
On 14 November, SpaceX caught the upper stage of Starship Flight 15 in the mechanical arms of the Starbase, Texas, launch tower — the first catch of a Starship upper stage after an orbital flight, about 22.5 hours after liftoff from Pad 2 on 13 November. SpaceX said the ship completed a nominal ascent, deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites (with contact made on all of them), and, after more than 20 hours on orbit, executed a deorbit burn and a landing flip on three Raptor engines into the tower’s arms. The Super Heavy booster did not return to the tower: SpaceX said a boostback burn ended early because of low fuel mass, guidance aborted the catch to an offshore landing zone, and after a landing-burn hover the flight-termination system was triggered. CNBC, reporting the same flight, said the booster exploded before hitting the water in the Gulf of Mexico.

Separately, Rocket Lab announced that Electron’s 100th launch — “The Mountain God Rises,” at 18:30 on 14 November from Launch Complex 1 in Māhia, New Zealand — successfully deployed iQPS’s YAMATSUMI-II synthetic-aperture radar satellite to a 575 km low-Earth orbit. Rocket Lab said Electron has reached 100 launches faster than any other commercially developed rocket. Year-to-date orbital launch figures compiled in CEAFE’s `shared/launches.md` as of 15 November 2026 (including the failed ULA Vulcan / Amazon Leo LV-01 of that day), according to Flight Atlas 2026 statistics, put the United States at 157 attempts (~1,893 t to orbit), of which SpaceX accounted for 127 attempts (~1,787 t); China at 81 attempts (~255 t); and Europe’s Ariane 6 and Vega C together at 6 attempts (Ariane 6: 4, Vega C: 2; ~60 t). Counts differ slightly between trackers.
articles.why: A successful orbital catch of a Starship-class upper stage, even with a failed booster recovery, is a step-change in reusable heavy-lift cadence that Europe does not yet match, with direct implications for transatlantic launch dependence and constellation deployment. Electron’s 100th flight underscores a responsive small-launch market in which European operators also compete. The year-to-date gap in mass to orbit remains very large.
articles.watch: SpaceX’s investigation of the early boostback; the next attempt at a dual booster-and-ship catch; European launcher and institutional reactions; Neutron as Rocket Lab’s medium-lift follow-on.

articles.headline: ASELSAN’s EJDERHA system said to disable 51 drones at once; CEO says serial production has begun
articles.summary: ASELSAN and its CEO, Ahmet Akyol, on 15 November publicised a demonstration of EJDERHA, a high-power electromagnetic (HPEM) counter-UAV system, held at the company’s Gölbek firing and test centre to mark ASELSAN’s 51st anniversary. In a written company statement quoted by Anadolu Agency, ASELSAN said the system first disabled two different cable-controlled drones at a range of about 1,000 metres, then, in a second phase, simultaneously disabled 51 drones launched together, in seconds and without missiles or munitions. Akyol called it the first system in the world to down 51 drones with a single command without a missile or munition, placed EJDERHA in the drone-defence layer of Türkiye’s ÇELİKKUBBE (“Steel Dome”) air-defence architecture, and said the system has entered serial production. ASELSAN gave no production volumes, delivery timetable or recipient units. ADDR Magazine, repeating the company line, noted that a demonstration does not guarantee the same effect under all operational conditions.
articles.why: Cheap massed drones have exposed the cost and magazine-depth limits of missile-based air defence in Ukraine and the Middle East. A fielded Turkish HPEM effector would add a non-NATO, munition-free layer that European forces and industry will be compared against.
articles.watch: Official delivery or inventory announcements; production quantities and recipient units; any export interest; independent technical commentary on the “world first” and serial-production claims.

articles.headline: China flight-tests a large unmanned cargo aircraft and a 10-tonne electric airliner
articles.summary:
On 14 November, Air White Whale’s W5000 — described by the company and Chinese state media as the world’s largest unmanned cargo aircraft — completed a roughly 30-minute technical verification flight at Otog Front Banner Oljoq Airport in Ordos, Inner Mongolia. CGTN and Global Times, citing the company, reported a maximum take-off weight of 10.8 tonnes, a 5-tonne payload, a 5.8-tonne empty weight, a 2,600 km range and more than 65 m³ of cargo volume, with all 220,000 components said to be domestically produced. The company reported 835 letters of intent and a target of commercial service by the end of 2027; airworthiness certification is still under way. “World’s largest” is the company’s and state-media characterisation, by payload, and was not independently verified in the briefs. CGTN and Global Times are Chinese state media; their claims are reported as such.

The same day, COMAC’s CE-25A, its first electric commercial aircraft, made its first crewed “intelligent” flight in Binzhou, Shandong, carrying two pilots and a flight-test engineer (16 minutes 38 seconds airborne, 60.4 km), after a first unmanned flight on 2 February 2026. Xinhua, citing COMAC, said the 19-seat aircraft has a 10-tonne maximum take-off weight, a 300 km/h cruise at 2,400 m and a 400 km range, with distributed electric ducted-fan propulsion; partners include CATL and Shanghai Jiao Tong University. China’s civil aviation authority has accepted a type-certificate application.
articles.why: A large indigenous unmanned cargo aircraft and a battery-electric regional airliner are markers of Chinese aerospace and dual-use industrial autonomy — relevant benchmarks for European UAV, cargo-drone, electric-aircraft and battery efforts, and for export-control and certification debates.
articles.watch: W5000 airworthiness progress toward end-2027 service; whether the 835 letters of intent convert to firm orders; CE-25A type certification; any European or EASA reaction to large unmanned cargo types.

articles.headline: France and India hold their first DRDO–DGA Joint Steering Group
articles.summary: Naval Group India reposted an Indian Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) statement on the first Joint Steering Group meeting between DRDO and France’s Direction générale de l’armement (DGA). According to DRDO, the meeting was held in France on 13–16 October 2026 to deepen defence research and development cooperation, following a Technical Arrangement between India and France signed in New Delhi on 20 November 2025. Talks covered aero engines, wind-tunnel testing, naval technologies, defence innovation and academic cooperation. A follow-up review was held on 13 November 2026 at DRDO Bhawan in New Delhi, co-chaired by Dr Chandrika Kaushik, director general (Production Coordination & Services Interaction), DRDO, and Brigadier General Mickael Le Cam, DGA director for Asia-Pacific.
articles.why: France is using the DGA–DRDO channel, and companies such as Naval Group, to lock in long-term co-development with India in engines, naval systems and testing infrastructure. That is part of Europe’s effort to build extra-European defence-industrial partnerships that can share cost and open markets — while also placing French industry in a competitive field that includes other European and non-European suppliers.
articles.watch: A joint communiqué with project-level detail (engine or naval demonstrators, wind-tunnel access, academic calls); any Naval Group follow-up on drones, propulsion and underwater systems.

articles.headline: US Army releases footage of a high-energy laser in use on the southern border
articles.summary: AeroVironment reposted, in this window, a clip described as freshly published US Defense Department footage of a high-energy laser operated on the US–Mexico border by soldiers of 2nd Battalion, 327th Infantry Regiment, 101st Airborne Division, assigned to Joint Task Force–Southern Border. Independent coverage of the same unit and system identifies it as the Army Multi-Purpose High Energy Laser (AMP-HEL), a vehicle-mounted 20 kW counter-drone weapon based on AeroVironment’s LOCUST laser, used in a 2 November 2026 training exercise near Fort Hancock, Texas, under Operation Ardent Vanguard. US Northern Command has previously said AMP-HEL had downed 11 cartel-linked drones by early September, after first combat use on the border in late August; those figures are official US claims. An FAA safety assessment concluded in April, after a February airspace incident near El Paso, that the systems do not increase risk to the flying public, according to Defence Blog.
articles.why: Cheap, magazine-deep directed-energy counter-UAS is directly relevant to Ukraine and to NATO’s eastern flank, where interceptor stocks are under strain. Operational use of a fielded US 20 kW laser, even in a homeland-border role, is a data point on reliability and industrial maturity, against which European programmes such as the UK’s DragonFire will be compared.
articles.watch: Any new official engagement figures; whether AMP-HEL or LOCUST variants are offered to European or Ukrainian customers; progress of European directed-energy programmes.

articles.headline: Auterion y la ucraniana SkyFall crearán una empresa conjunta de drones con fábrica en Alemania
articles.summary:
**Auterion y SkyFall anunciaron el 20 de noviembre su intención de crear «Skyfall x Auterion» para fabricar drones en gran volumen en una nueva planta en Alemania, con financiación alemana y la posibilidad de suministrar a la Bundeswehr.**

Ya han entregado juntas más de 50.000 drones de ataque Shrike a Ucrania. La producción empieza con el Shrike FPV con aviónica y AuterionOS.

**Fuentes:** [auterion.com](https://auterion.com/auterion-and-skyfall-intend-to-form-a-joint-venture-to-build-drones-for-ukraine-in-germany/), [·](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/autonomy-firm-auterion-to-launch-joint-venture-with-ukrainian-drone-maker-skyfall/)
articles.why: Dinero y suelo europeos, pero la capa de software autónomo es de Auterion, que opera desde EE. UU. La cuestión es quién controla el software y sus licencias de exportación.

articles.headline: Marruecos destina 366 M€ a crear una industria nacional de defensa antes de 2035
articles.summary:
**Marruecos asigna 4.000 millones de dírhams (unos 366 M€) del Fondo Hassan II a su hoja de ruta industrial de defensa.**

Para 2035 quiere crear unos 50.000 empleos, fabricar en el país el 40 % de su equipo militar y de seguridad y obtener más del 65 % de los ingresos del sector con exportaciones. Prioriza drones, sistemas terrestres y navales, electrónica, ciberdefensa e IA, con zonas industriales en Benguerir y Benslimane (Gabinete Real; Euronews).

**Fuentes:** [maroc.ma](https://maroc.ma/en/news/statement-royal-office-12), [·](https://www.euronews.com/2026/11/20/morocco-commits-366-million-to-build-a-national-defence-industry-by-2035)
articles.why: Un mercado y socio en el flanco sur, donde empresas francesas y españolas compiten con proveedores estadounidenses, israelíes y turcos.

articles.headline: La USAF abre un contrato de propulsión de 16.100 M$ a 58 empresas, entre ellas Rolls-Royce y Safran
articles.summary:
**La Fuerza Aérea seleccionó a 58 empresas para un contrato marco de «propulsión avanzada» con un techo de 16.100 M$ hasta 2041 (Breaking Defense).**

Entre ellas, Boeing, GE Aerospace, Honeywell, Lockheed Martin, Northrop Grumman, RTX, Rolls-Royce, Safran y Hermeus. El techo no es gasto garantizado.

**Fuentes:** [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/air-force-issues-massive-16b-contract-for-engine-work-to-dozens-of-companies/)
articles.why: Los fabricantes europeos acceden al mercado estadounidense a través de filiales sometidas a las normas de control de EE. UU. (FOCI, ITAR). No existe un marco europeo recíproco de esta escala.

articles.headline: Los ministros de Defensa de la UE respaldan una declaración sobre seguridad de suministro
articles.summary:
**En el Comité Director de la Agencia Europea de Defensa, los ministros respaldaron una declaración conjunta para reforzar la seguridad de suministro de cara a Defence Readiness 2030 (EDA, 21 nov.).**

**Fuentes:** [eda.europa.eu](https://www.eda.europa.eu/what-we-do/all-activities/activities-search/security-of-supply)
articles.why: La dependencia de componentes no europeos se convierte en un riesgo operativo. Solo la acción conjunta europea tiene la escala necesaria.

articles.headline: La danesa GomSpace gana 8 M€ para satélites lunares de Blue Origin
articles.summary:
**GomSpace obtuvo un contrato de 8 M€ (segunda fase) para desarrollar dos satélites de prospección de recursos lunares para un cliente que llama «una empresa espacial líder de Norteamérica»; European Spaceflight lo identifica como Blue Origin.**

En enero de 2026 recibió un primer contrato de 2,9 M€.

**Fuentes:** [europeanspaceflight.com](https://europeanspaceflight.com/denmarks-gomspace-secures-e8m-contract-for-blue-origin-moon-mission/)
articles.why: Conocimiento europeo al servicio de un programa lunar estadounidense, sin un programa lunar europeo comparable que lo retenga.

articles.headline: Francia encarga 50.000 proyectiles de 155 mm a KNDS y triplica una planta
articles.summary:
**La DGA ha encargado 50.000 proyectiles de 155 mm a KNDS, con entregas previstas en 2029 y 2030.**

El pedido va acompañado de una inversión conjunta del Estado y KNDS France para triplicar la capacidad de la planta de La Chapelle-Saint-Ursin (Cher), con tres nuevas unidades de producción (KNDS, 20 nov.). Según la DGA, la producción francesa ha pasado de 30.000 a 60.000 proyectiles al año desde 2022 y aumentará de forma progresiva hasta 150.000 al año en 2029 (DGA en X, 20 nov.).

**Fuentes:** [nota de prensa, 20 nov., vía](https://knds.com), [nota de prensa, 20 nov., vía](https://urlr.me/4GPYvx)
articles.why: Es demanda europea que va a un grupo franco-alemán. El suministro soberano de munición es la lección más clara de la guerra de Ucrania. Ahora bien, la escala solo cuadra si los pedidos europeos se agrupan: de lo contrario, cada línea nacional seguirá siendo pequeña frente a la producción estadounidense.

articles.headline: BAE Systems abre la primera fábrica totalmente automatizada de munición de gran calibre del Reino Unido
articles.summary:
**BAE Systems afirma haber abierto en Glascoed (sur de Gales) la primera fábrica totalmente automatizada de munición de gran calibre del Reino Unido.**

Según la empresa, la inversión de 180 millones de libras en robótica y vehículos autónomos permite multiplicar por 16 la capacidad de proyectiles de 155 mm para el Reino Unido y sus aliados de la OTAN (BAE Systems en X, 20 nov.; el enlace a la nota no estaba accesible).

**Fuentes:** [baes.co](https://baes.co/NRVc5108qlh)
articles.why: Junto con el pedido francés, muestra que Europa reconstruye su capacidad en casa en lugar de comprar fuera. El Reino Unido no forma parte de la UE, así que su posible participación en la demanda financiada por SAFE será la prueba de una base europea de munición más amplia.

articles.headline: Dos drones alemanes de ataque superan las pruebas de fuego real; primeras entregas este año
articles.summary:
**Dos variantes alemanas de drones de ataque de un solo uso superaron este mes las pruebas de fuego real, según la oficina de adquisiciones de la Bundeswehr.**

Así queda despejado el camino para las primeras entregas y la formación de tropas antes de fin de año (Defense News, 20 nov.; solo titular y resumen).

**Fuentes:** [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/)
articles.why: Son municiones merodeadoras de proveedores alemanes en lugar de sistemas estadounidenses como el Switchblade. Es un paso nacional, y el beneficio llegará si estos programas se abren a otros compradores europeos.

articles.headline: La sueca Nordic Air Defence lanza el interceptor K200 contra los drones a reacción Geran-3a
articles.summary:
**La start-up sueca Nordic Air Defence ha presentado el K200, un interceptor autónomo de drones que sucede al Kreuger 100XR y está diseñado para derribar drones de ataque a reacción, entre ellos el Geran-3a ruso.**

La empresa ha abierto una oficina con personal en Ucrania, donde las pruebas orientarán el desarrollo (Breaking Defense, 20 nov.).

**Fuentes:** [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/swedens-nordic-air-defence-launches-k200-drone-interceptor-pushes-toward-ukraine-tests/)
articles.why: Los interceptores europeos baratos son la respuesta a gastar misiles caros contra drones baratos, y probarlos en Ucrania acelera el aprendizaje. La noticia coincide con el día en que Polonia informó de que dos misiles y un dron rusos violaron su espacio aéreo durante la noche (Reuters, 20 nov.).

articles.headline: Actualización: Baykar empieza a entregar el Kizilelma a las Fuerzas Armadas turcas
articles.summary:
**Baykar ha empezado a entregar sus drones a reacción Kizilelma a las Fuerzas Armadas turcas, lo que permite a este miembro de la OTAN empezar a usar aviones no tripulados en combate aire-aire (Bloomberg, 20 nov.; Baykar en X: «del primer diseño a la primera entrega»).**

Sigue a la noticia del 19 nov. sobre su entrada en servicio.
articles.why: Turquía despliega un dron de combate antes de que exista ningún caza no tripulado europeo. Baykar es además dueña de Piaggio Aerospace en Italia, por lo que también actúa dentro de la base industrial europea.

articles.headline: El De Grasse, tercer submarino nuclear de ataque de la clase Suffren, entra en servicio activo
articles.summary: **El jefe de la Marina francesa, el almirante Cluzel, declaró el 20 de noviembre la admisión en servicio activo del submarino nuclear de ataque De Grasse, construido por Naval Group (Marine Nationale, compartido por Naval Group).**
articles.why: Demuestra una capacidad europea de submarinos nucleares totalmente soberana. En la UE solo la tiene Francia; en Europa, también el Reino Unido.

articles.headline: MBDA Deutschland y ATMOS estudiarán ataques de precisión desde el espacio
articles.summary:
**La empresa emergente alemana de logística espacial ATMOS Space Cargo ha firmado un acuerdo de cooperación con MBDA Deutschland para explorar una capacidad de ataque de precisión contra objetivos terrestres desde el espacio, mediante vehículos de reentrada (SpaceNews, 19 nov.; Defense News).**

Según Andrew Parsonson (SpaceNews), es una iniciativa de la industria, no la respuesta a un programa gubernamental, que apuesta a que los Estados buscarán estas capacidades en los próximos años.

**Fuentes:** [spacenews.com](https://spacenews.com/atmos-and-mbda-to-explore-space-based-precision-strike-system/), [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/)
articles.why: Un fabricante europeo de misiles y una empresa emergente europea entran en una capacidad hasta hace poco tabú sin esperar a un marco liderado por EE. UU. Es una iniciativa intraeuropea; que los Gobiernos la financien o no mostrará si Europa quiere opciones soberanas o deja el terreno a EE. UU. y China.

articles.headline: Un ministro británico propone que EE. UU. construya en su territorio una fragata de diseño británico
articles.summary:
**En una tribuna en Breaking Defense (18 nov.), Luke Pollard, ministro británico de Preparación e Industria de Defensa, defiende que la Marina de EE. UU. adquiera un diseño británico de fragata y lo produzca en Estados Unidos, en plena reconstrucción de su base naval.**

**Fuentes:** [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/britain-has-the-frigate-the-us-needs-and-americans-should-build-it-uk-minister/)
articles.why: Enlaza con el tema de las 08:30 sobre un astillero de construcción extranjera en suelo estadounidense: los diseños europeos son bienvenidos en EE. UU. solo si el trabajo, el empleo y los astilleros se trasladan allí, mientras Washington se opone a la preferencia europea en el mercado europeo. La asimetría (normas de contenido nacional, ITAR) va en una sola dirección.

articles.headline: Países Bajos aspira a un crecimiento del 40 % y 15.000 M€ de facturación en defensa en 2030
articles.summary:
**Defense News informa (20 nov.) de un plan neerlandés para la industria de defensa que apunta a un crecimiento del 40 % y 15.000 millones de euros de ingresos en 2030 (solo titular y resumen; artículo no leído antes del plazo).**

**Fuentes:** [defensenews.com](https://www.defensenews.com/global/europe/)
articles.why: Los planes nacionales suman capacidad, pero ningún Estado miembro tiene por sí solo el tamaño de los grandes grupos estadounidenses; el valor está en integrarlos en programas europeos conjuntos (Países Bajos se unió esta semana al programa de blindados CAVS).

articles.headline: Europa sigue buscando un papel «indispensable» en el Artemis revisado
articles.summary:
**Casi ocho meses después de que la NASA cambiara a fondo Artemis, Europa aún intenta adaptarse y seguir siendo «indispensable», según SpaceNews desde Bremen (20 nov.).**

La ESA estudia mejorar o ampliar el Módulo de Servicio Europeo para que Orion pueda entrar en órbita lunar baja.

**Fuentes:** [spacenews.com](https://spacenews.com/europe-seeks-indispensable-new-roles-in-artemis/)
articles.why: El lugar de Europa en la exploración lunar depende de decisiones estadounidenses que no controla. Artemis es un bloque liderado por EE. UU.; Europa debería mantener abiertas opciones con otros socios en lugar de atar su futuro espacial a los planes cambiantes de un solo aliado.

articles.headline: La ESA elige Plasma Observatory; Kongsberg suministrará transpondedores para LISA
articles.summary:
**Los Estados miembros de la ESA seleccionaron Plasma Observatory, siete naves coordinadas que estudiarán cómo se transmite la energía solar a través del escudo magnético terrestre, como próxima misión de clase media (ESA, 19 nov.).**

Kongsberg (Noruega) firmó con Antwerp Space (Bélgica) el suministro de transpondedores de espacio profundo en banda X para LISA, la tercera misión de clase grande de la ESA; importe no revelado.

**Fuentes:** [esa.int](https://esa.int/articles/seven-spacecraft-observatory-to-study-plasma-universe), [kongsberg.com](https://www.kongsberg.com/news/news-archive/2026/kongsberg-awarded-contract-to-support-esas-lisa-mission-with-deep-space-transponders/)
articles.why: Cadenas de suministro espaciales intraeuropeas, el modelo cooperativo que da escala a Europa.

articles.headline: El carro medio Karpat de FNSS y CSG dispara en Eslovaquia
articles.summary: **La turca FNSS y el grupo checo CSG anuncian que su carro medio CFL-120 KARPAT completó su primera demostración con fuego real en Eslovaquia (FNSS en X, 20 nov.; web de FNSS inaccesible).**
articles.why: Un grupo europeo (CSG) se asocia con un fabricante turco para un mercado centroeuropeo, en lugar de una compra a EE. UU.

articles.headline: China entrega a Kazajistán un avión de transporte militar Y-9E
articles.summary:
**El Ministerio de Defensa de Kazajistán anunció el jueves que un avión de transporte militar chino Y-9E ha llegado a Almaty y se ha incorporado a la flota de la aviación de transporte militar de las Fuerzas Armadas kazajas (Global Times, medio estatal chino).**

Global Times destacó la «tecnología madura» del avión. @F_CEAFE reposteó la publicación. Kazajistán es miembro de la Organización del Tratado de Seguridad Colectiva (OTSC), liderada por Rusia.

**Fuentes:** [@globaltimesnews](https://x.com/i/status/2123752270487810472)
articles.why: China ya no es solo compradora de tecnología occidental y rusa: se está convirtiendo en exportadora de armas y proveedora de seguridad en Asia Central, el patio trasero tradicional de Rusia, y en los mercados donde compite la industria europea. Ese mismo día, legisladores de EE. UU. presionaron para negar la certificación a los aviones fabricados en China (véase Economía).
articles.watch: Nuevas entregas chinas a ejércitos de Asia Central; la reacción de Rusia.

articles.headline: Congresistas de EE. UU. quieren que Airbus pierda contratos de defensa por sus inversiones en China
articles.summary:
**El Comité Selecto sobre China de la Cámara de Representantes publicó el 19 de noviembre un informe que recomienda que EE. UU. no certifique aviones de fabricación china y retire los contratos públicos a las empresas aeroespaciales, Airbus incluida, que no dejen de invertir en la base industrial aeroespacial china (Reuters; comité).**

Según el comité, las empresas occidentales participaron «inadvertidamente» en la estrategia china de fusión civil-militar, y pide endurecer los controles de exportación y las restricciones a la inversión. Señala las líneas de montaje del A320 de Airbus en Tianjin, cuyas alas fabrica Xi'an Aircraft Industry Group, que también construye aviones militares chinos; su presidente, John Moolenaar, ha acusado además al Gobierno francés de controlar lo que Airbus puede revelar (AeroTime). El mismo informe cita a las estadounidenses Honeywell, GE Aerospace y Collins por obtener licencias para transferencias controladas con usuarios militares chinos. Son recomendaciones, no leyes.

**Fuentes:** [chinaselectcommittee.house.gov](https://chinaselectcommittee.house.gov/media/reports/investigation-details-how-western-government-policy-enabled-china-s-rise-in-the-skies), [·](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/exclusiveus-should-not-certify-chinese-aircraft-restrict-investments-in-chinas-aerospace-sector-lawmakers-say-5039601), [·](https://www.aerotime.aero/articles/us-lawmakers-airbus-contracts-china-ties), [· @Reuters](https://x.com/i/status/2123660108504994077)
articles.why: Es presión extraterritorial sobre el gran grupo aeroespacial europeo: un órgano del Congreso propone usar los contratos de defensa de EE. UU. como palanca sobre la estrategia comercial de una empresa europea, mientras proveedores estadounidenses citados en el mismo informe obtuvieron licencias de su propio Gobierno. Europa no tiene una palanca equivalente sobre las empresas estadounidenses, y la dependencia del mercado de defensa de EE. UU. expone a los grandes grupos europeos a la política de Washington.
articles.watch: Si alguna recomendación pasa a la NDAA o a una orden ejecutiva; reacción de Airbus y de París.

articles.headline: España aprueba más de 6.400 millones en préstamos a interés cero para los Programas Especiales de Modernización
articles.summary:
**El Consejo de Ministros aprobó un real decreto que regula préstamos plurianuales a interés cero del Ministerio de Industria para financiar los Programas Especiales de Modernización (PEM).**

La prensa española cifra el paquete en más de 6.400 millones de euros (Europa Press, Infodefensa, El Español, elEconomista); otro medio habla de 6.900 millones, así que la cifra exacta está por confirmar. Entre los beneficiarios figuran Indra, GMV, Airbus, EM&E (Escribano) y el consorcio español del Eurofighter, para sistemas PNT/Galileo, helicópteros, digitalización de la UME, antidrones y modernización de plataformas aéreas.

**Fuentes:** [europapress.es](https://www.europapress.es/economia/noticia-gobierno-financiara-6400-millones-indra-gmv-airbus-eme-consorcio-espanol-eurofighter-20261118124816.html), [·](https://www.infodefensa.com/texto-diario/mostrar/6095764/gobierno-moviliza-6400-millones-prestamos-financiar-programas-defensa-indra-airbus-gmv-escribano), [·](https://www.elespanol.com/observatorio-defensa/20261117/gobierno-aprueba-millones-prestamos-desarrollo-programas-especiales-modernizacion/1003744462301_0.html)
articles.why: Positivo: dinero nacional para programas de fabricación europea (Eurofighter, PNT basado en Galileo, helicópteros de Airbus) en lugar de compras llave en mano fuera de Europa.
articles.watch: El texto en el BOE y el desglose por programa.

articles.headline: Leonardo DRS gana trabajo en el buscador del THAAD y prevé cuadruplicar su producción
articles.summary:
**Leonardo DRS, filial estadounidense participada mayoritariamente por la italiana Leonardo, anunció el 19 de noviembre un contrato de BAE Systems para desarrollar una nueva matriz de plano focal infrarroja para el interceptor THAAD.**

El trabajo se hace en su fundición de Dallas, que amplía para multiplicar por cuatro la producción histórica de buscadores. No se ha dado el importe.

**Fuentes:** [leonardodrs.com](https://www.leonardodrs.com/news/press-releases/leonardo-drs-awarded-contract-to-develop-advanced-next-generation-sensor-for-thaad/), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123525990093615152)
articles.why: Un grupo europeo crece en la cadena de defensa antimisil de EE. UU., pero a través de una filial cotizada en EE. UU. y sujeta a las reglas de control estadounidenses: la tecnología se queda en EE. UU.

articles.headline: El candidato a subsecretario de la Armada propone un astillero extranjero en EE. UU. para fragatas
articles.summary:
**En su audiencia de confirmación en el Senado el 19 de noviembre, William Toti propuso crear en EE. UU. un nuevo astillero «de primer nivel», construido por un constructor extranjero, dedicado a fragatas y grandes buques de superficie (Breaking Defense).**

La construcción en el extranjero enfrenta a la Administración, que quiere encargar fuera algunos buques (el «modelo finlandés»), con el Congreso, que quiere limitarlo.

**Fuentes:** [breakingdefense.com](https://breakingdefense.com/2026/11/toti-pushes-new-foreign-built-shipyard-in-the-us-to-focus-on-frigates-large-surface-combatants/)
articles.why: Los astilleros europeos (Fincantieri ya es dueña de Marinette Marine) y asiáticos son los candidatos; EE. UU. trae capacidad extranjera a su suelo y bajo su control, lo contrario de lo que suele hacer Europa al comprar plataformas terminadas fuera.

articles.headline: Los republicanos del Senado aparcan un suplemento de defensa de 350.000 millones
articles.summary:
**Los republicanos del Senado suspenden su intento de aprobar 350.000 millones de dólares adicionales para gasto militar, ante la falta de impulso para pagar la guerra con Irán antes de perder el control del Congreso en enero (WSJ).**

Al Jazeera informó de que la GAO concluye que el Pentágono carece de un plan global contra la escasez de munición, y Xinhua de que un responsable del Pentágono cifró ante el Congreso el coste de la guerra con Irán en 48.300 millones de dólares a 13 de noviembre, un 27 % más que los 38.000 millones anteriores.

**Fuentes:** [X](https://x.com/i/status/2123582713298817127), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123608705459712098), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123641295411548261)
articles.why: La escasez de munición en EE. UU. retrasa las entregas a clientes europeos de FMS (Patriot, THAAD, GMLRS): un argumento a favor de la capacidad de producción europea.

articles.headline: Actualización: el fallo del Vulcan agrava el cuello de botella de lanzamientos de la Space Force
articles.summary:
**Según Air & Space Forces Magazine, el fallo del Vulcan Centaur de ULA del 15 de noviembre, que destruyó 40 satélites Amazon Leo, estrecha la capacidad de lanzamiento de la Space Force; ULA lo atribuye a un «suministro insuficiente de combustible del vehículo a los motores BE-4».**

New Glenn no vuela desde mayo, lo que deja a SpaceX con un casi monopolio en carga pesada. SpaceX explicó que el propulsor del vuelo 15 de Starship abortó con seguridad la captura y amerizó frente a Starbase.

**Fuentes:** [airandspaceforces.com](https://www.airandspaceforces.com/ula-launch-failure-trouble-space-force/), [·](https://x.com/i/status/2123516375805379040)
articles.why: La concentración en un solo proveedor privado contrasta con la necesidad europea de mantener en vuelo Ariane 6 y Vega C; Ariane 6 lanza satélites Amazon Leo el 23 de noviembre.
